# Contracts (locked in GRO-1961)

Source of truth for types: [`shared/types.ts`](../shared/types.ts). This file is the prose companion.

## Repo layout / scripts

```
package.json          npm workspaces: client, desktop. Root scripts:
                        dev            electron-vite dev (cwd desktop/): builds main + preload, serves the renderer with HMR, launches Electron
                        build          tools/packDrawio.mjs (YAZ-3028 D5: the pinned draw.io into desktop/.cache/drawio), then electron-vite build → desktop/out/{main,preload,renderer,drawio}
                        drawio:pack    tools/packDrawio.mjs alone: verify (size + sha256) and unpack the pinned draw.io v31.5.2, prune it, lay desktop/drawio-overlay over it; idempotent (CI runs it before test)
                        desktop:build  build, then electron-builder --mac → desktop/dist-app (.app + dmg, F1 — see "Packaging"); the root version is injected via extraMetadata
                        typecheck      tsc -p client && tsc -p shared && tsc -p desktop
                        test           vitest run  (FOUR projects: client=jsdom, desktop=node, tools=node, perf=jsdom — client/vitest.perf.config.ts, the budget tripwires kept off the main run's contended pool)
                        e2e            build, then playwright test --config desktop/e2e/playwright.config.ts (G1 — Playwright-Electron smoke suite)
                        e2e:only       the same Playwright suite on the existing desktop/out, no rebuild
                        perf           tools/perf/run.mjs: the local CDP perf harness on the packaged app (A/B with --vs, ABBA order; see tools/perf/README.md). Never in CI
                        perf:budget    tools/perf/measureBudget.mjs: the size and integrity gate on desktop/out + the packaged .app and DMG (run after desktop:build; see "Packaging")
                        perf:budget:ci the same gate on desktop/out alone (--out-only; after build) — what CI runs
client/               The renderer: React 19 + TS, @milkdown/crepe 7.22.x, plus ONE lazily-loaded dependency: `@excalidraw/excalidraw` PINNED to 0.18.1 (YAZ-878 — the module is imported only by `drawings/renderScene.ts`, and only through a dynamic `import()` on the first drawing preview or modal open, so it never enters the main chunk; its stylesheet is a second dynamic import, made by the modal's surface alone, YAZ-879). No scripts of its own — electron-vite (desktop/electron.vite.config.ts) builds it with ./index.html as the entry, and its renderer config `dedupe`s `react`/`react-dom` — 🔒 load-bearing since YAZ-879: npm hoists an OLDER react beside the Excalidraw tree at the repo root, and without the dedupe `<Excalidraw>` mounts against a second React and dies on a null dispatcher. The sidebar chrome is TWO rows since YAZ-847: ROW 1 the tablist (Files · Search · Focus · Favorites, in `SIDEBAR_TABS` order — the three lenses are YAZ-2619's, and Search is a tab of its own and no lens since YAZ-2638 🔒 D2; `DEFAULT_SIDEBAR_LENS` = Files since YAZ-1846 — a new window and a switch to a different vault land on it; the per-window `WindowEntry.sidebarLens` since YAZ-1628, which holds a lens and never Search) — carrying, right-aligned at its end, the ⚡ YAZ-862 expand/collapse-all button: ONE double-chevron acting on the dirs the ACTIVE lens has ON SCREEN (`bodyDirs`), in a single `setAll` dispatch on the one `expanded` set every lens shares (a SESSION bucket since YAZ-1642: shared by every window on the vault, never restored by a launch); it collapses those dirs whenever ANY of them is open and expands them only when none is — on Files with two or more vaults the vault rows fold with them (YAZ-2631 D6 — "The sidebar lenses": Several vaults) — and it is GONE rather than disabled on the Search tab (YAZ-2638 S17: the folds there are the search's own) and whenever the active lens has nothing to unfold, no folder and no vault row — and ROW 2 the search bar (YAZ-801), on the SEARCH TAB ONLY (YAZ-2638 🔒 D2, cases S1–S25 on the issue). THE SEARCH TAB: Search is the second tab, a magnifier (`SearchIcon`, its word in `title` + `aria-label`), so the bar has no magnifier of its own. Files, Focus and Favorites have no bar (S6). This overturns four locked rules on purpose. YAZ-797: search was "never a tab", and the bar was ALWAYS visible, on every lens, loading/error/empty vault included. YAZ-847 🔒 D5: a typed query replaced the body of the ACTIVE tab. YAZ-801: Esc emptied a typed query first, and only the second press gave up focus. YAZ-2630 🔒 D8: the `esc` keycap showed only while a query was typed, and a click cleared the query. WHY: Yasin wants to go back to a search after he leaves it, and he does not search from Focus or from Favorites. THE CARET HAS ONE PATH: ⌘K and a click on the tab both show the tab and put the caret in the bar, with the text that is there selected (S2, S5 — ⌘K's `openSearch` and the tab's click both reach App's `changeLens('search')`, which raises `pendingSearchFocus`: the App handshake above), ALSO when the Search tab already shows (S4). With the sidebar hidden, ⌘K shows the sidebar first (S3). A plain show of the sidebar while it is on the Search tab — hidden, then shown, with no ⌘K — does NOT take the caret: the flag is false at that mount. ESC IN A PAGE (`focusSidebar`, `lib/focusHandoff.ts`): while the Search tab shows it puts the caret in the search bar, empty or not — the bar gets it whenever the bar is on the page; on Files, Focus and Favorites the tree's active row gets it, as before. ESC IN THE BAR goes back to the lens the window last showed, the text STAYS (S12 — `leaveSearch`), and THE CARET GOES INTO THE OPEN PAGE (YAZ-2662 🔒 D9, S56 — `leaveSearch` ends with `focusOpenDocument()`; with no page open no caret moves and nothing is said, S57; this overturns the YAZ-2638 rule "after Esc in the bar the focus is given up"); with the preview panel on show the first Esc closes the panel ONLY and the next one leaves (`searchEsc`, YAZ-2662 S34); it writes nothing when the lens did not change (`changeLens` does not write the lens that is stored already). The `esc` keycap at the bar's right is ALWAYS in the bar, and a click IS the Esc key — `searchEsc` too, so with the panel on show it closes the panel only (YAZ-2662 S58) — and a press on it takes no focus, so the caret is still in the bar after such a click (`.sidebar__search-back`, `aria-label` "Leave search", `title` "Back (Esc)", no Tab stop, `onMouseDown` default-prevented; S13). There is no clear button: to clear, select the text and delete it, and ⌘K selects it (S14). Refused: Esc clears the text (one habit key press would lose the search); a `↩ <query>` keycap in an empty bar that brings the last search back (the tab keeps the search). THE SEARCH STAYS (S10): the text, the folds and the highlight live in `useSidebarSearch`, which stays mounted with the panel, so they stay while a different tab shows. While a different tab shows, the search does no work and scrolls nothing (`useSearchResults(vaults, active ? query : '', pinnedPaths)`: a search that is not on screen ranks nothing); on return to the Search tab the text, the results, the folds and the highlight are back. New typed text gives a new ranking and the search's own folds again (S11). NEVER STORED (S15): `changeLens` writes each tab but Search to the window identity, so `storage.setSidebarLens` and `window.setIdentity` never get `'search'`, the main process did not change, and a window that starts again opens on its last lens. A switch to a different vault lands on Files, and the text is gone (S16, YAZ-1846). Known and accepted: a hidden sidebar unmounts the panel, so the text is lost, as before. THE BODY: with no text it is one line, "Type to search every note and folder.", THE KEYS of the search below it, and no tree (S7; the keys are YAZ-2662 🔒 D10, S59 — `SEARCH_KEYS`, a `dl.sidebar__keys` of seven rows, each key in the keycap of the bar: `↑` `↓` Move · `↵` Open · `⌘↵` Open in a background tab · `⇧↵` Show in Files · `space` Preview a file or open a folder, after ↑ or ↓ · `→` `←` Open or close a folder, after ↑ or ↓ · `esc` Back to the page; with text typed, matches or none, they do not show, S60; and with the bar EMPTY no key of the list is taken — ↓, ↑, →, ←, Space and Enter are left for what stands beside the bar); with text that matches nothing it is "No matches" (S9); with text it is the search TREE (YAZ-2620, overturning the flat-list ruling on YAZ-739 for the sidebar; the shortcut picker keeps the flat `SearchResults` list): the Files tree of the WHOLE vault — with two or more vaults the FOREST, so each match stands under its vault's row, a parent row that is never a match (YAZ-2602 A9) — cut down by `searchTree` to the ranked matches and the folders that lead to them and drawn by the same `Tree` — a matched folder with no match inside keeps all it holds, closed (🔒 D2); the folders that lead to a match are open, and a fold clicked there lasts as long as its query and never reaches the Files tree's stored folds; no shortcut rows, and nothing there creates, renames or drags; a match shows each part that matched bold on the highlight wash (`--mark-bg`) — the whole typed text, else each typed word, else the joined text, `matchRanges` drawn by `search/marked.tsx`, YAZ-3748 D3; the flat `SearchResults` list marks its labels the same way, B3 — and every other row is dim (`Tree`'s optional `marks`, 🔒 D5); the ranking keeps the best `SEARCH_CAP` (50) candidate rows, and a line below the tree says so once it is reached (🔒 D6) — the candidates carry the loaded tree's FOLDERS (🔒 D1–D2, YAZ-1491 — fed from the Sidebar's own `dirs` memo, `folderCandidates` spliced ahead of `searchCandidates` so a folder ranks first within a rank bucket) and its files that are no notes, each matched by its file name (YAZ-2620 🔒 D3 — `fileCandidates` off the `otherFiles` memo, spliced last; a note still never matches on its folder name, the folder itself is one row; rows match and read by TITLE, YAZ-2420 D14 — plus one `basename — Title` row for a note whose file name was given by hand, not the title, an alias, `kebabTitle(title)`, the id or a name that ends with `-<id>` (`ownFileName`, YAZ-3748 B4) — and text that holds a note's or a folder's id shows the pages whose ids it holds FIRST, then the title matches for the same text, no row twice — `searchRows`, D32 and YAZ-2677 🔒 D9. What "holds" means is `holdsId(query)` in `shared/noteId.ts`, which reads the query ONE time and answers null for a text that can hold no id, so a search by title costs nothing more (S78; `searchCandidates.perf.test.ts` measures 10,000 notes): an old ID, or a number ID typed as `YAZ-12`, `yaz-12`, `yaz12` or `yaz 12`, anywhere in the text — a pasted id, a `[[<id>]]` link, a file name, a whole path — with letters that end a longer word not an ID's; letters the note's vault had before (`SearchCandidate.was`, S77); and a BARE number, which is the whole text and finds that number in each vault of the window (S69, S70). An id is held whole or not at all (`12` is not `YAZ-1` or `YAZ-120`). The row of a number ID match is labelled `YAZ-12 — Title`, and the search tree shows that: `useSidebarSearch` hands the tree `TreeMarks.ids` (path → full ID) for each result whose label starts with its ID, and `Tree.tsx` draws `YAZ-12 — ` in front of that row's title (S70 — in a window with two vaults each row has its own letters; a note found by its title, or by an old ID, reads as its title alone). The sidebar draws its results as a tree in tree order (YAZ-2620), and the ID match is the ranking's first row, so it is the one the highlight starts on), Enter on a FILE row opens its page as a tab, while ENTER ON A FOLDER ROW SHOWS THE FOLDER IN FILES (YAZ-2662 🔒 D1, cases S1–S12 on the issue — it overturns S23 of YAZ-2620, "Enter on a folder opens the folder's page as a tab, nothing is revealed"; WHY: the search tree shows only the matches inside a folder, and Yasin could not see all that the folder holds): the Files tab shows, the folders above it — and a closed vault row, S9 — open, the folder opens, its row flashes for 3 seconds and HAS THE KEYBOARD FOCUS, so `↓` then walks into the folder (the arrows of `Tree`, above); no tab opens, the page on show does not change, the text stays in the Search tab (S1, S2), a folder whose page is already open is shown all the same — a folder has no "take me in" — and a row that is gone gets the notice of "Show in sidebar" (S10). ⇧⏎ does the same for ANY row, a file too (🔒 D8, S5, S6), a file with no viewer in the app among them (S8). ⌘ is read FIRST: ⌘⏎, with ⇧ or without (S7), opens a background tab — of a folder's PAGE, as before (S3) — and a file with no viewer in the app opens in its default app on ⏎ and on ⌘⏎. HOW: `activate(row, background, reveal)` — `background` is `metaKey`, `reveal` is `shiftKey`, and the row is the search tree's own node, a match or not (S52) — calls `onRevealInFiles(path, true)`; the reveal request carries it as `SidebarRevealRequest.focus`, and `flashTreeRows(host, path, focus)` puts the focus on the first occurrence of the row, ONE time for each request (`focusedRevealId` — a folder above it that is closed and opened again later flashes the row and moves no focus); the menu's "Show in sidebar" sets no `focus` and moves none (S12). A CLICK is still the tree row's own — it opens a note and folds a folder; since YAZ-3377 D1 a double-click opens nothing on a folder, and its menu's **Open folder page** opens the page (YAZ-2620 🔒 D1; YAZ-2662 S11, R6: the mouse rules of the search tree are the Files tree's) — and the Search tab stays after an open (YAZ-2638 S24) — the search tree is the body of the Search tab ALONE (YAZ-2638 🔒 D2; before, 🔒 D5 of YAZ-847, it replaced the ACTIVE lens tab's body), while the tabs row stays live and a tab switch keeps the query — a conditional render, never a teardown, so every bit of a lens's tree state (data, expansion, pending create/rename, drag) is waiting untouched when that lens shows again — fed by `client/src/search/` (ranking engine YAZ-802, `useSearchResults(vaults, query, pinned)` YAZ-803 — since YAZ-2602 R2 over every vault of the window: one index snapshot per vault, each kept current by its own watcher and kept while its vault stands, the candidates of all of them ranked as ONE list, so the `SEARCH_CAP` counts the matches of every vault together — `searchTree` YAZ-2620; the hook's index feeds are LAZY since YAZ-808: no `index(root)` read and no watch subscription until the first non-empty query, latched on for good after it, because the always-on index feed of each vault is its WikilinkIndexBridge's) and driven entirely from the input, which keeps the focus while the tree is driven from it — it hands the focus on in two places, both on purpose: Esc, to the open page, and ⏎ on a folder or ⇧⏎, to the row in Files —: the highlight starts on the BEST-ranked match — a pinned match when there is one (YAZ-2662 S23) — wherever the tree draws it, and is held by its PATH (🔒 D4, YAZ-2620); ↑/↓ walk the matches ON SCREEN in tree order — the top group from top to bottom, then "Everything else" (YAZ-2662 S22) — never a parent row, but EACH row on show inside a folder that shows all, a match or not (YAZ-2662 S48), stop at both ends and never wrap (the `[[` picker's rule), and a highlight whose row left the screen moves to the next row still drawn; on a NOTE row ⏎ opens it in place, ⌘⏎ in a background tab, a row click opens and ⌘-click background-opens (I3) — the results stay up either way. THE TWO GROUPS (YAZ-2662 🔒 D2–D4, cases S13–S29 on the issue, S19 as its "S19 changed" record has it, with S19A; before, every match was in ONE tree): a PINNED ITEM is a file or a folder that is in the focus list or in the favorites, and the matches that are a pinned item or are inside one are the TOP GROUP, drawn FIRST under the label "Favorites and focus"; a hairline and the label "Everything else" come next, then the other matches (`p.sidebar__group`, the hairline being the border of a label that follows a tree; two `Tree`s off one `searchTreeProps`). The top rows of the top group are the pinned items themselves — no folder above one is drawn, as on the Favorites tab (S14), and with two or more vaults each names its vault (S26) — in the order of `pinnedRoots([...focusNodes, ...favoriteNodes])` (`lib/treeState.ts`): the focus items in the order of the focus list, then the favorites in the order of the Favorites tab; an item that is in both lists shows ONE time, at its place in the focus list (🔒 D3, S17 — Yasin: an overlap "doesn't have to show up twice"), and a pinned item inside a different pinned folder is no top row — it shows inside that folder (S18). A pinned folder whose name matches, with no match inside, is a top row, closed, and keeps all it holds (S13); one that only leads to a match is open, dim and not bold, its match below it (S14); a pinned file that matches is a top row (S15); a pinned item with no match and none inside is not drawn (S16); and a pinned path that is gone from the disk gives no row and no error (S29). "Everything else" is cut from the tree WITHOUT the pinned items that the top group DRAWS (`withoutPaths(tree, <the top group's top rows>)`), so no row shows two times and a folder that led only to pinned matches is not drawn there; a pinned item that the top group does NOT draw stays in its folder, so a matched folder there still opens to all that it holds but what the top group draws (S19, S19A — the first S19 hid every pinned item, and a pinned item with no match was then nowhere in the search). With every match pinned there is the top group and its label, no line and no "Everything else" (S20); with NO pinned match there is no label and no line, and the tab is the one tree of YAZ-2620 (S21). THE RANKING puts each pinned match before each other match, each part in its own order — exact, starts with, contains, a word match, a joined match (YAZ-3748 D2) — and the limit of 50 cuts AFTER that, so it cuts no pinned match while another match shows: 60 other matches and 3 pinned show the 3 and the best 47 (🔒 D4, S24 — `searchTitles(candidates, query, first)` and `searchRows(candidates, query, first)`, the rows that an id finds too, S25: where the text holds an id the ID matches stay FIRST (YAZ-2677 🔒 D9), the pinned ones before the others, and the title matches come after them, the pinned ones before the others, so there an ID match that is not pinned goes before a pinned title match; `first` is the set of the candidate paths at or below a pinned path, `atOrBelow`, built in a memo of `useSearchResults` when the rows or a list changes and NEVER on a keystroke, which pays one scan of the rows, one look in the set for each match and the two cuts of the tree, R1 — the perf smoke `search/searchCandidates.perf.test.ts` has pinned items and keeps its limit of 50 ms for 10 searches, R2; with an empty `first`, the shortcut picker's call, the ranking is `matchLinkCandidates`' own, which did not change, R7). So with new text the highlight starts on the best PINNED match (S23). An add or a remove on a search row — focus or favorites — moves the row between the groups at once, and the Search tab stays (S27); a fold in either group lasts as long as its text (S28). `useSidebarSearch` returns `found` as `{ top, rest, open, order }`: a row is in one group only, so the two share one set of open folders and one order. THE LIST KEYS (YAZ-2662 🔒 D6, D7, cases S30 and S46–S55): Space, `→` and `←` are also text keys — "working log" has a space — so they act on the search tree only AFTER `↑` or `↓` moved the highlight (`picked !== null`); before it Space types a space and the arrows move the caret, and a change of the text gives the three back to the text (S30). A list key with ⌘, ⌥, ⌃ or ⇧, and a list key with nothing to do on the highlight, is NOT taken and stays a text key (`listKey` says whether it took the key). SPACE ON A FOLDER opens it in the search tree with ALL that it holds — `full`, the set of the folders that show all, which `searchTree(tree, hits, full)` reads: a row that is no match is dim, as each row that is no match, and a match keeps its mark; a folder inside it that leads to a match stays as the search drew it, open with its matches, and one that leads to none is the tree's own node, closed (S46, S47) — and `↑` and `↓` then stop on EACH row on show inside it, a match or not, while outside such a folder they stop on matches only (S48). Space again puts that folder, and each folder inside it, back as the search drew it (S49). `→` does what the first Space does, and on a folder that already shows all, or on a file, it is a text key (S50); `←` closes an open folder, and on a closed folder or on a file it is a text key (S51). On a row inside such a folder ⏎, ⌘⏎ and ⇧⏎ do what they do on a match, Space on a file shows the preview panel and Space on a folder opens that folder too (S52). `full` lasts as long as its text: `changeQuery` empties it with the folds (S53). A folder with nothing in it opens to no row and no error (S54). A vault row is never the highlight, so no list key acts on it (S55). A CLICK still folds a folder as before, and `↑` and `↓` do not go into a folder that a click opened until `→` or Space (R6). THE PREVIEW PANEL (YAZ-2662 🔒 D5, cases S31–S45 and S65–S67, rules R3–R5; `search/QuickLook.tsx` + `search/quickLook.css`; Yasin: "an actual panel shows up ... a screen on top of it ... Almost like when you hit space on Mac" — NOT the preview tab of YAZ-2648, which is a tab): after `↑` or `↓`, SPACE ON A FILE shows that file in a panel over the page area — `section.quicklook`, App's, the last child of `.tabstack` and no layer of it, centred, with no backdrop, so the page stays in sight around it. It is no tab and no page: no tab opens, and the tabs, the preview tab, the page on show and the stored window do not change (S31); over the blank tab of ⌘T it shows over the empty page, and the blank tab stays (S45). It TAKES NO FOCUS: the caret stays in the search bar, whose keys drive it — `↑` and `↓` move the highlight and the panel follows `PREVIEW_FOLLOW_MS` (120 ms) after the LAST move, keeping the earlier file until then, so a walk reads no file on its way (S32); on a folder no panel is drawn, at once, Space keeps its meaning for a folder, and the panel shows again on the next file (`parked`, S38); Space again closes it (S33); the first Esc closes it ONLY (S34); a change of the text closes it, and Space is a text key again (S35); ⏎, ⌘⏎ and ⇧⏎ do their own work and close it (S36); a different sidebar tab, or a hidden sidebar, closes it (S37); a click or a right-click on a row of the search tree closes it, the row does its own work, and it stays off until the next Space (S65); and the tab board and a review each close it, and Space shows none meanwhile and none comes back after (`previewShown`, S67). "A panel is on show" is App's `previewPath` ALONE — the Sidebar's `previewPath` / `onPreview` props are its one door — so the keys in the bar and the ✕ on the panel cannot disagree. WHAT IT SHOWS (S39): each kind of file the app shows as a page, by `fileKind` — a NOTE through `editor/useReadOnlyNote.ts`, the read-only render that the hover card of Table and Board uses, below its frontmatter (S42: nothing in it can be edited, it writes nothing, starts no autosave and stores no folds — never `Editor`), read from the DISK by `api.readFile`, ONE read for each stop of the highlight, so a note with a change that is not saved yet can show the saved text (S44), and a read that lands after the highlight moved is dropped (the `Note` is keyed by its path, R3); a text file, an image and a PDF through the read-only viewer of its page (`viewers/`), on the watcher of its vault; a file with no viewer in the app reads "No preview for this file." (S40); a NOTE that is gone, or that the app cannot read, reads `Can't preview "<name>" — it is no longer there`, and nothing else changes (S41 — for a note: a text file, an image or a PDF that cannot be read shows the error line of its own viewer, as its page does, because that error can be a different fault, a PDF that is too large, and the line would then be false — decided in the review of YAZ-2668); and a note with no text below its frontmatter reads "Empty page", as the hover card does. The header holds the file's name as the tree names it and a ✕, "Close preview", and the mouse can scroll the panel (S43); a press on the ✕ takes no focus. A CLICK IN THE PANEL — to select text — puts the keyboard focus on it (`tabIndex={-1}`, no Tab stop), where the search bar's Esc is out of reach: Esc there, and the ✕ with the focus inside the panel, close the panel and put the caret back in the search bar by ⌘K's door, the text selected (S66 — `closePreview` in App; KNOWN LIMIT: a PDF is an `iframe`, so Esc after a click inside the PDF does not reach the panel, and the ✕ still works). The note in the panel wears `.editor-instance` for the editor's stylesheets and is NOT a page: `focusOpenDocument` walks past `.quicklook`, so the caret never goes into it (R4). The panel adds its own code alone: no new dependency, and the main process did not change (R5). A HELD KEY ACTS ONE TIME (YAZ-2662, the "Cases S65 to S67" record on the issue): a held Enter in the bar is ONE Enter — its repeats are taken and do nothing; before, the repeat was the SECOND Enter of YAZ-961, the caret went into the page, and more repeats typed new lines in the note (taken in `searchKeyDown` and not in `resultKeys`, which the shortcut picker shares, R7); a held Space on the highlight acts one time, so the panel does not show and close, and a folder does not open and go back, at the rate of the key, while Space as a text key still repeats; and a held Enter on a ROW of a sidebar tree does nothing (`heldEnter` in `Tree`, above). NOT INCLUDED, on purpose: Ctrl+N and Ctrl+P as ↓ and ↑; a wrap of ↑ and ↓ (locked, YAZ-803); ⌘1 to ⌘9 for the matches; Tab between the groups; a change to the note-shortcut picker, which keeps its flat list and its ranking (R7); and any change to the main process, the IPC, the stored focus list or the stored favorites. THE MENUS: the blank-space context menu is the TREE's, so right-clicking the Search tab's blank space offers nothing, with text or with none ("New note" there would have no target; YAZ-2638 S19) — not even Electron's text menu, which the body's handler default-prevents (YAZ-2050) — while a result ROW opens that row's own tree menu through the same `openMenu` (YAZ-2050, the tree row's `onNodeContextMenu`; the right-click moves the highlight onto a match, and any row wears the selected style while its menu is open): 🔒 D1 it follows the FILES rules, a search row being a disk row — `MenuTargets.lens` pins `'files'` for a row of the Search tab (the active lens otherwise) and every lens rule in the menu path reads it (`startCreate`'s hop to Files) — and since YAZ-2638 🔒 D1 it is the menu of its row in Files PLUS one item, "Show in sidebar", FIRST ("The sidebar lenses": "Show in sidebar" on a row — before, YAZ-2050 🔒 D1 made the two menus the same); 🔒 D2 the items that draw INTO the hidden tree (Rename, New note / dated note / folder / dated folder) first leave the search through `onRevealInFiles` (App flips the lens to Files and issues the same reveal request the tab menu uses; the Files reveal accepts a dir, which opens ITSELF too via the create menu's synthetic-child `expandTo`) — `MenuTargets.leaveSearchTo` names the row, `viaTree` calls `onRevealInFiles` with it, the reveal expands and flashes the row, and the query STAYS in the Search tab (YAZ-2638 S22; before, the reveal cleared it) — and every other item acts in place, on the Search tab (the focus toggle and the favorite toggle among them: an add from a search row changes the list and the Search tab stays, YAZ-2638 S20, S21 — this overturns YAZ-2619 🔒 D3 for the Search tab, where an add showed the Focus tab); "Show in sidebar" on a document tab shows Files, and the text stays too (YAZ-2638 S23); multi-select never reaches this menu (the selection ends when the Search tab shows, YAZ-2638 S18); ⌘-click on a file row opens it in a BACKGROUND TAB of this window (the locked I3 ruling, GRO-2235); the file- and folder-row context menus carry New note / dated note / folder / dated folder ("New note" is born from the target folder's `.template.md`, YAZ-2290 E3; what is typed inline is the note's or the folder's TITLE, free text, and the name on disk is built from it, YAZ-2420 D6, D20 — where the vault does not use IDs it IS the name, YAZ-2523; `EntryKind` is `file` | `dir`; TOMBSTONE: "New base" and its `base` `EntryKind` were deleted with the format in YAZ-844), on a FOLDER row Open (YAZ-2290 D3), "Review this folder" (YAZ-2322) and "Add note shortcut" (YAZ-2290 D2), on a note row the review toggle (YAZ-2322), Rename (files Links E1 GRO-2194, folders E1b GRO-2241 — inline input replacing the row label, prefilled with the TITLE of a note or a folder, whose commit is a title edit (YAZ-2420 D16; where the vault does not use IDs, a rename of its name, YAZ-2523), and with the full name of any other file, Enter commits / Esc-blur cancels; no hotkey v1 — F2 is a polish note), Copy path, Open in ▸ New window (D2, GRO-2168 — context menu only since I3; a flyout leaf since YAZ-1674) — TOMBSTONE: the type-conditional "New ▸ <type>" submenu and "New type…" (`NewTypeDialog`) were deleted with the type system in YAZ-836; Delete (GRO-2272 — opens ConfirmDelete, never deletes directly) and Open in ▸ Reveal in Finder (GRO-2274 — a flyout leaf since YAZ-1674; file rows, folder rows AND blank space, where it targets the vault ROOT — of a window with one vault; with two or more, blank space is no one vault's and each vault's own row carries these, YAZ-2602 S10, S13); the menu is DATA → sections → render since YAZ-1674 (🔒 D8): `menuSections.ts` holds every gating rule as one small function returning a `MenuItem` or null and the pure `buildMenuSections(targets, handlers)`; `ContextMenu` takes `{ x, y, sections, onClose }` and only draws — a `role="group"` per NON-EMPTY section with a CSS rule between adjacent groups, one button per item whose only text child is the bare label (the ⌘X / ⌘C / ⌘V / ⌘⇧C hints are drawn from `data-hint`, so `textContent` and the accessible name stay what four test files pin); menu ORDER is SIX groups (🔒 D7 as amended; YAZ-2249 split Create in two, YAZ-3085 D3 folds it into three parents): [Show in sidebar (one row of Search, Focus or Favorites — YAZ-2638 🔒 D1, D3) · Open · Open N in new tabs · Add to focus / Remove from focus] · [Cut · Copy · Paste · Copy N paths · Copy path] · [New note ▸ (New note · New dated note) · New drawing ▸ (New Excalidraw drawing · New dated Excalidraw drawing │ New draw.io diagram) · New folder ▸ (New folder · New dated folder)] (YAZ-3085 D1–D3: each is a parent WITH a default — a click or Enter runs the first leaf of its flyout, the same function, so the two never disagree; hover or ArrowRight opens the flyout; no leaf, no parent, so blank space under two or more vaults has no create row; the boards since YAZ-3028 D9 — name first, then `createBoard` writes the empty scene or diagram, then its tab opens; Import from shared: `import type { TreeResponse } from '@shared/types'`.

## Supported file capabilities (YAZ-1289, locked; widened by YAZ-3028 D2)

`shared/fileKind.ts` is the one case-insensitive classifier. The final filename suffix decides the kind; when it decides none, the well-known names with no extension are `text` (YAZ-3505: `WELL_KNOWN_TEXT_NAMES` in `shared/types.ts` — `Dockerfile`, `Makefile`, `Procfile`, `Gemfile`, `Jenkinsfile`, `Vagrantfile`, `LICENSE`, `CODEOWNERS`, by exact, case-sensitive base name — and `Dockerfile.<anything>`, `WELL_KNOWN_TEXT_PREFIXES`; so `Dockerfile.md` stays a note and `makefile.bak` stays unsupported); other extensionless names, leading-dot-only names such as `.json`, compound names ending in an unknown suffix such as `data.json.gz`, and every unlisted extension are unsupported. Existing dot-entry and `node_modules` exclusions apply before classification.

| Kind | Extensions | Files view / open | Read | Write / create | Semantic index | Markdown link |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `markdown` | `.md`, `.markdown` | Visible; editable Markdown editor | `readFile`, 10 MiB maximum; preserves the existing Node UTF-8 replacement-character and leading-BOM behavior | Yes: create, edit, autosave, frontmatter and Markdown-only feature writes | Yes: the only `IndexRecord` kind and therefore the only content-search, folder-row, properties, views, aliases and backlinks source | Semantic wikilinks; existing missing-note create-on-click behavior applies |
| `text` | `.txt`, `.log`, `.csv`, `.tsv`, `.json`, `.jsonc`, `.jsonl`, `.ndjson`, `.yaml`, `.yml`, `.toml`, `.ini`, `.cfg`, `.conf`, `.xml`, `.env`, `.properties`, `.lock`, `.js`, `.jsx`, `.mjs`, `.cjs`, `.ts`, `.tsx`, `.py`, `.rb`, `.go`, `.rs`, `.java`, `.kt`, `.kts`, `.c`, `.h`, `.cc`, `.cpp`, `.hpp`, `.cs`, `.swift`, `.php`, `.sh`, `.bash`, `.zsh`, `.fish`, `.ps1`, `.sql`, `.html`, `.htm`, `.css`, `.scss`, `.sass`, `.less`, `.vue`, `.svelte`, `.graphql`, `.gql`, `.mdx`, `.rst`, `.tex`, `.lua`, `.r`, `.dart`, `.scala`, `.hs`, `.clj`, `.pl`, `.proto`, `.diff`, `.patch`, `.gradle`, `.groovy`, `.ml`, `.erl`, `.jl`, `.cmake`, `.fs`, `.elm` (the last 18: YAZ-3450, D4), and the well-known names above (YAZ-3505; this reverses D4's "names with no extension stay out") | Visible; a tab opens the code tab (`CodeEditor`, Monaco, Editor rule 42; YAZ-3448). Quick Look shows the same Monaco, read only (`code/CodePreview.tsx`, lazy; YAZ-3450). Monaco picks colours by extension or file name; `.hs`, `.diff`, `.patch`, `.gradle`, `.groovy`, `.erl`, `.cmake` and `.elm` have no Monaco language and get the app's small tokenizers (`code/monacoLanguages.ts`, YAZ-3479), as do `Makefile` (its own) and `Jenkinsfile` (Groovy); `Dockerfile.<anything>` joins Monaco's `dockerfile` and `Vagrantfile` its `ruby`; `Procfile`, `LICENSE`, `CODEOWNERS` are plain text | `readFile`, 10 MiB maximum; fatal UTF-8 decode, UTF-8 BOM preserved, any malformed UTF-8 or NUL rejected passively | Yes, through `writeFile` only (the code tab, YAZ-3445 D3): main writes the string as given, so the file's line break and BOM stay as read; atomic; `expectedMtime` → `CONFLICT`, nothing written. A code tab's save puts back a file it read and another app deleted, as VS Code does | Never | Navigation-only, explicit extension required; no embeds, headings/blocks, aliases, create-on-click or semantic record |
| `pdf` | `.pdf` | Visible; Chromium's native PDF viewer in a read-only frame | Dedicated `readPdf` returns `Uint8Array`, 50 MiB maximum; never text, base64 or the asset pipe | Never | Never | Navigation-only, explicit extension required; the same no-semantic/no-create rules as text |
| `image` | `.png`, `.jpg`, `.jpeg`, `.gif`, `.webp`, `.avif`, `.bmp` | Visible with its full filename; centered, read-only static canvas viewer | Dedicated exact-path `readImage` returns `Uint8Array` + allowlisted MIME, 50 MiB maximum; never base64, fuzzy lookup or the asset pipe | Never | Never | Navigation-only, explicit extension required; the same no-semantic/no-create rules as text/PDF |
| `drawing` (YAZ-3028 D2) | `.excalidraw` | Visible as a normal row; a tab opens Draw's Excalidraw canvas (`DrawingEditor`) | Dedicated `drawing:load` returns the scene text, its mtime and the pictures it names (from `<vault>/assets/<sha1>.<ext>`, or a legacy scene's own `files`); 200 MiB maximum (`MAX_DRAWING_BYTES`); the outline check (an object with an `elements` array) refuses anything else `IO_ERROR` | Yes, through its own doors only: `drawing:save` (new pictures land in `assets/` first, then the scene with `files: {}`; atomic; `expectedMtime` → `CONFLICT`, nothing written) and `fs:create-board` (born with the empty scene, never over a file). Never `writeFile` / `createFile`. A note embed's modal keeps `writeAsset` (rule 28) | Never: no `IndexRecord`, content search, properties, views or backlinks. Search finds it by name | Navigation-only, explicit extension required; `![[x.excalidraw]]` stays the note embed (rules 27, 28) |
| `diagram` (YAZ-3028 D2) | `.drawio` (`.drawio.svg` and `.drawio.png` stay unsupported / image, as in Draw) | Visible as a normal row with the draw.io icon; a tab opens the bundled draw.io editor (`DrawioEditor`) | Dedicated `diagram:load` returns the XML exactly as on disk and its mtime; 200 MiB maximum; the outline check (a closed `<mxfile>` or `<mxGraphModel>` root) refuses anything else `IO_ERROR` | Yes, through its own doors only: `diagram:save` (plain `<mxfile>` XML; atomic; `expectedMtime` → `CONFLICT`) and `fs:create-board` (born with the empty diagram) | Never | Navigation-only, explicit extension required |
| unsupported | every other suffix, including `.svg` | Hidden from Files and refused by supported-file deep links | Never through `readFile`, `readPdf` or `readImage` | Never through the note mutation boundaries | Never | None |

A board (`drawing` or `diagram`) carries its two dates (Draw's YAZ-1834 D1, YAZ-1802 D7) — a drawing's first key `yaseendraw: { createdAt, updatedAt }`, a diagram's `yaseendraw-created` / `yaseendraw-updated` attributes on `<mxfile>` — stamped by main on every create and save, so Docs and Draw write the same bytes into a shared vault. The tree walk does not read them. A rename never transcodes: `.excalidraw` ↔ `.drawio`, and a board ↔ any other kind, fail `UNSUPPORTED_EXTENSION` before the disk changes.

Every supported text/PDF/image/board target can use the normal tab, background-tab, restore, reveal, delete, open-in-new-window and open-in-VS-Code paths. Rename/move and external-rename repair must preserve what the existing bytes actually encode: Markdown and text retain their same-`FileKind` behavior, PDF stays `.pdf`, images keep the same extension case-insensitively except that `.jpg` and `.jpeg` are equivalent spellings. A rename never transcodes, so `.png` → `.jpg` and every other cross-encoding transition fail before disk mutation. Markdown, drawing and diagram are the creatable kinds, and with text (YAZ-3445 D3) the writable ones (YAZ-3028 D2 changes YAZ-1289's "Markdown remains the only creatable or writable kind"): Markdown through `createFile` / `writeFile` and its feature writes, text through `writeFile` only (never created), a board only through its own doors (`createBoard`, `drawing.save`, `diagram.save`). Markdown remains the only SEMANTIC kind.

Text, PDF and image transport uses one bounded regular-file snapshot: pre-read `fstat`, reject an oversized or non-regular file before allocation, allocate/read at most the initial size plus one byte (never more than the applicable cap plus one), then post-read `fstat`. A size/mtime drift or a byte count inconsistent with the snapshot fails `IO_ERROR` rather than returning mismatched bytes and metadata. Text above 10 MiB and PDF/image above 50 MiB fail `TOO_LARGE`.

PDF rendering uses an `application/pdf` Blob URL over the dedicated bytes. The viewer revokes the owned URL exactly once on replacement, path change and unmount. Electron enables Chromium PDF plugins while retaining `contextIsolation: true`, `sandbox: true`, and `nodeIntegration: false`; there is no PDF.js, annotation/editor layer, custom pagination, base64 conversion or asset-pipe reuse.

Raster rendering gives the dedicated bytes and allowlisted MIME to `createImageBitmap` once, sizes a canvas to the decoded dimensions, paints only the default frame, and immediately closes the bitmap exactly once. Animated GIF/WebP therefore display their static default/first frame; no timer or animation loop exists. Same-path external refresh keeps the last good canvas until replacement paints, while a path change hides old pixels immediately and stale decode completions can never paint. Decode/bridge failures remain passive. SVG is deliberately deferred: it is structured XML that can carry script and external references, so support needs an explicit sanitization and no-network policy rather than entry through this raster boundary.

View-only wikilinks are backed by a lightweight catalog flattened from the Files tree, never by `IndexRecord[]`. The catalog refreshes only for supported-file/directory structural watch events, and reads the tree itself only when no other consumer of the window's one tree feed (`lib/treeFeed.ts`: same-turn calls share a request, later ones share one trailing request, every answer reaches every listener — YAZ-2191) has read it since; content changes reload an already-open viewer without rebuilding semantic state. Resolution uses exact root-relative paths or case-insensitive basenames, with the shallowest path and then deterministic path order winning duplicates; autocomplete emits the shortest unambiguous spelling with the real extension. Recognized explicit-extension targets always take this navigation-only branch—even before the catalog is ready or when the target is missing—so they can never fall through to Markdown creation. Missing/removed targets and view-only heading/block suffixes remain unresolved and produce passive notices. `|display text` changes presentation only. View-only files produce no backlinks, properties, aliases, searchable content, folder-view rows, semantic records or writes; rename-reference repair reads/writes only Markdown source notes using the pre-rename view-only catalog.

A root switch synchronously clears the old navigation resolver, catalog targets and merged picker rows while the new tree is pending. The semantic source object keeps its identity, but an old vault's catalog can never compose with the new vault's semantic snapshot.

## Bridge API (`window.yaseenDocs`, locked in GRO-2153 — Desktop A1)

**The table** (YAZ-2131 🔒 D9, YAZ-2200): every door below is one line of `CONTRACT` in `shared/ipc.ts` — channel, argument and answer types, arity. The preload builds `window.yaseenDocs` from it, main registers `handle(CONTRACT.x.y, fn)` (typed from the table), and `client/src/api.ts` wraps it, so a new door is one table line plus its handler, and a missing or mistyped one fails to compile. The specials stay hand-written in the preload (`SPECIAL`): `watch` (multiplexed by subscription id), `window.onFlush` (the `app:flush` / `app:flushed` handshake) `menu.onCopyAs` / `onPasteAs` (with their `menu:copy-text` / `menu:paste-text-fallback` fallback invokes), `menu.edit` (`menu:edit`, the note menu's rows, YAZ-3653) and `spell.suggestions` (the renderer's own spellchecker, no IPC); `state.setFolds` / `setBaseGroups` send a copy of their key list and `properties.onChange` hands its listener the payload's `properties`, as they always did. `desktop/src/preload/surface.test.ts` pins the whole surface byte for byte; `desktop/src/contract.test.ts` pins that every door is wired exactly once. The renderer reaches main only through `api`, except `clipboardPaste.ts` / `clipboardCopyOut.ts`, which subscribe with optional chaining so they also run outside Electron (`clipboardCopyOut.ts` also calls `menu.edit` for the Copy without folded lines key).

The desktop app has no HTTP server (GRO-2095 D2): the renderer is sandboxed and calls the typed bridge the preload installs; `ipcMain.handle` answers from the main process (GRO-2157 deleted the server and every HTTP path). All paths are absolute POSIX paths; no jail — any absolute path is allowed. Every method rejects with a plain `BridgeError { code, message, path?, mtime? }` (`BridgeErrorCode` in `shared/types.ts`, plus `CONFLICT` which carries the disk mtime); the client's `api.ts` wraps it in `BridgeRequestError` (same fields) so the renderer can `instanceof` it.

| Bridge | Notes |
|---|---|
| `tree(root)` | `TreeResponse` — recursive; every regular file appears (YAZ-1577 D1) carrying its preview `kind` — exact `FileKind` for Markdown/text/PDF/image/drawing (`.excalidraw`)/diagram (`.drawio`, YAZ-3028 D2), `null` for a file with no in-app viewer, which the renderer hands to the OS default app; every dir shows, files or not (GRO-2022); dot-entries, `node_modules` and crash-left atomic-write tmps (`isAtomicTmp`: `<name>.tmp-<12 hex>`, never deleted, YAZ-2179) are skipped; dirs before files, each sorted case-insensitive. Missing / not a dir → `NOT_FOUND` / `NOT_A_DIRECTORY`. ONE walk per root at a time in main (YAZ-2191): a call during a walk joins the single trailing walk queued behind it, so every answer post-dates its call; the sidebar and search read at once on the first structural event after a quiet spell, then coalesce a burst into ONE trailing read 100 ms after its last event (`lib/leadingTrailing.ts`, YAZ-2240); `ready` reads at once |
| `readFile(path)` | `FileResponse` — Markdown or approved view-only text, 10 MiB maximum. Markdown preserves the legacy Node UTF-8 decode behavior; view-only text uses fatal UTF-8 decoding, preserves a UTF-8 BOM, and rejects NUL. PDF, image and unsupported extensions → `UNSUPPORTED_EXTENSION` |
| `readHeads(paths)` | `(FileHead \| null)[]`, in the order asked (YAZ-2648 D6, `desktop/src/main/fs/heads.ts`) — `FileHead { path, mtime, text }`: the top of a note for a page of the tab board. `.md`/`.markdown` regular files only; main reads `HEAD_READ_BYTES` (8192) off the start of the file at most, whatever its size — never the whole file — decodes it leniently (a read that stops inside a character drops that character), takes the frontmatter block off (`splitFrontmatter`; a block still open where the read stops gives `text: ''`) and answers the first `HEAD_CHARS` (600) of the body, never half of a surrogate pair. A path that fails — a deleted file, a folder (one may be named `Notes.md`), a file that is no note, a relative path — answers `null` and never fails the rest; more than 256 paths: the rest are `null`. A root that is not a directory → `NOT_FOUND` before any worker starts |
| `share.status/accounts/setup/onSetupProgress/openCloudflare/get/list/publish/setPermission/stop/setDomain/disconnect/onChanged` | Share links (YAZ-3040, Draw's YAZ-1799; `desktop/src/main/share/`, handlers in `ipc/share.ts`). Main owns Cloudflare, the token and the upload password; the token crosses the bridge exactly once (renderer → main in `share:setup`) and no answer or push carries it or the password. `setup(token, accountId?)` provisions the bucket, the viewer assets, the Worker, the workers.dev address and a test upload, with `ShareSetupProgress` on `share:setup-progress` to the asking window only; `accounts(token)` lists the accounts a key sees (a picker when there are several). `get({ root, path })` / `list(root, check?)` read `<vault>/.yaseendocs/shares.json` (`list` HEADs each link unless `check` is `false`, the sidebar marks' call). `publish({ root, path, content, id? })` is a first share or the always-live re-upload of `id`; `content` is the standalone `.excalidraw` (images embedded) or the `.drawio` XML; over 100 MB is `TOO_LARGE`. `setPermission` flips view-and-download / view-only on the SAME link; `stop` deletes it. `setDomain(hostname \| null)`, `disconnect(root \| null, deleteEverything)`. Errors: `NOT_SET_UP`, `OFFLINE`, `PROVIDER_FAILED`, `TOO_LARGE`, `NOT_FOUND`, `INVALID_CONFIG`, `BAD_REQUEST`. `share:changed` goes to every window on any status or shares.json change |
| `app.home()` | This user's home folder (YAZ-3886 P2; `desktop/src/main/ipc/home.ts`, `os.homedir()`). The Welcome screen asks once when it mounts and shows a recent folder's path under it as `~/…`; until the answer, or if the call fails, the full path shows. Takes no argument and never fails. |
| `app.sound(kind)` | One sound for one gesture that succeeded (YAZ-3267 D15, S54–S57; `desktop/src/main/sounds.ts`). `kind` is `'land'` (items landed: a paste, a drag-move, a Finder drop, an undo or a redo of a move) or `'trash'` (items went to the Trash: Delete, "Remove from vault"). The renderer asks ONCE per gesture, after it succeeded, through `client/src/lib/gestureSound.ts`, and never waits; a move gesture asks in App's `recordMoves`, so the Sidebar asks only for what reaches no move (a Paste of a Copy, a copy in from another disk). Main answers at once; a play that fails is never a failure. `kind` must be exactly the string `'land'` or `'trash'`: anything else (`['land']`, another string, an object) is `BAD_REQUEST` and plays nothing (the YAZ-3248 rulings). Silent off macOS, in the hidden e2e mode, with the fake clipboard, and when "Play user interface sound effects" is off. |
| `update.state/onState/notes/restart` | The updater (YAZ-2976 D2, D6, D7; `desktop/src/main/updater.ts`, handlers in `ipc/update.ts`). Main owns ONE `UpdateState` and pushes each change to every window (`update:state-changed`, S20); a window reads `state()` once on mount. `{ kind: 'idle' }`, or `{ kind, version }` with `downloading` (the `.dmg` is coming), `ready` (checked and staged at `<bundle>.update`), `manual` (a newer version exists but this copy cannot replace itself — Windows, an unpackaged run, a copy under `/Volumes/` or App Translocation, a folder the user cannot write, an ad-hoc build: S13; or a version in `update-refused`, below). The first launch after a swap is `idle` (YAZ-3698 removed `updated` and its "See what's new" pill: the user read the notes in the sheet before the install); `start()` deletes the `<userData>/updated-to` that the swap of 2.8 and older still writes. **The check** is `GET <feed>/latest` (`feed` = `YASEEN_DOCS_UPDATE_FEED`, else `https://api.github.com/repos/yaseenarshad/yaseen-docs-app/releases`) 10 s after `ready`, then every 12 h, and at Yaseen Docs › Check for Updates…; a dev run with no feed never checks on its own (S7); a failed timer check is silent and changes nothing (S3); never two at once, and while `downloading`/`ready` a check answers the state and fetches nothing (S6). `check()` answers as soon as it knows: `downloading` when the download starts, which goes on in the background (its end is a push). A JSON request stops after 30 s, a download after 60 s with no data. A newer tag counts only with no pre-release part (no `-`) and with an asset named `*-arm64.dmg` that has GitHub's `digest` `sha256:<hex>` (S2). The download (S8) replaces `<userData>/updates/` (one update on disk, S11) with `<version>.dmg.part`, hashed as it streams; a wrong sha256 (S9) puts the state back and the next check tries again. A build that fails `codesign --verify --deep --strict -R =<this app's designated requirement>` (S10) is written to `<userData>/update-refused` (`.part`, then a rename), and the state becomes `manual` for that version: `start()` and each check keep that version `manual`, so it never downloads again, and a later version deletes the file and downloads. `start()` on a packaged Mac copy also deletes `<userData>/updates/` and `<bundle>.update` in the background (no launch starts `ready`), and a download waits for that. `notes()` → `ReleaseNotes` = `{ current, releases }` (YAZ-2988 D13), asked only when the "What's new" sheet opens: `current` is this app's version (`app.getVersion()`; the renderer has no other way to know it), and `releases` is every published release from ONE `GET <feed>?per_page=100` (GitHub's largest page; drafts, prereleases and tags with a `-` dropped) as `ReleaseNote[]`, newest first by version, at most 100. The renderer picks the tags (**Latest**, **Your current version**) and the release the sheet opens on (D10, D11). Rejects when GitHub cannot be reached (S18). `restart()`: `manual` → `shell.openExternal('https://github.com/yaseenarshad/yaseen-docs-app/releases/latest')` (D3); `ready` → quit through the quit sequence (every window saves first) and the swap opens the app again (S21); any other state → nothing. The swap is a detached `/bin/sh` (`SWAP_SCRIPT`) started in the quit sequence's `exit`, also on a plain quit (S22, no reopen): it waits for the PID to end, deletes a stale `<app>.old` (and does not swap while one remains), renames `<app>` → `<app>.old` and `<app>.update` → `<app>`, and deletes `<app>.old`; if the new app is not in place, `<app>.old` goes back and the version goes to `update-refused` (S23) |
| `lsp.open/change/close/definition/references/hover` | The code tab's language helpers (YAZ-3454 4B, YAZ-3455 4C; D9, D10; `desktop/src/main/lsp/pool.ts`, handlers in `ipc/lsp.ts`, types in `shared/lsp.ts`, client `client/src/code/languageClient.ts`). `open({ root, path, text })` → `LspOpenResponse { handle, language, projectRoot } \| null` (a `text` over `MAX_FILE_BYTES` in UTF-8, as `fs:read` refuses, is `BAD_REQUEST` here and in `change`; YAZ-3458): null when no helper takes the file (`lspLanguageOf`: `.ts .tsx .js .mjs .cjs .jsx` → TypeScript 7, `.py` → `pyright`; only `text` kinds a tab opens), when it is in no project (TS: no `tsconfig.json` / `jsconfig.json` / `package.json` above it up to the vault, YAZ-3458; the home folder never counts), when the helper is not installed, or while Settings › Code › "Jump across files" (`codeLanguageHelpers`) is off — then no helper starts, and turning it off stops every helper (YAZ-3500). The project of a Python file is the nearest `pyproject.toml` / `setup.py` / `requirements.txt`, else the vault `root`. Each tab gets its own handle, owned by the CALLING window: a handle of another window is ignored, and a window that is destroyed, reloads (`did-start-navigation`, main frame) or loses its renderer closes its handles. `change(handle, text)` is the tab's whole text (the tab debounces it, 300 ms, and sends it at once before a request); `close(handle)`. Tabs on one file share one LSP document (`didOpen` once, `didChange` full text, `didClose` with the last tab). `definition` / `references({ handle, position })` → `LspLocation[] \| null` (`{ path, range }`, 0-based UTF-16 positions; `file://` URIs become paths, other URIs and places inside the helper's own install folder are dropped); `hover` → `LspHover { contents (Markdown), range? } \| null`. **null = no helper answered** (none, still failing to start, crashed twice, a timeout: 30 s, hover 5 s) → the tab uses Monaco's one-file help, no message; `[]` = the helper found nothing. Bad input → `BAD_REQUEST` / `NOT_ABSOLUTE`. **Helpers**: one per project root, started with the project's first `open`, stopped with its last `close`; at most 3 at once over every language, a 4th stops the one used longest ago (its documents stay; its next request starts it again); a helper that ends with no `stop` asked starts again once, with every open document; the quit sequence stops all (`stopAllLanguageServers`) |
| `lsp.helpers/install/cancelInstall`, `lsp.onInstallProgress` | The helpers' download (YAZ-3500; `desktop/src/main/lsp/download.ts`, rule 42a). `helpers()` → `LspHelpersState { ready, installing }`: `ready` = TypeScript 7 and pyright resolve (the downloaded copy of the pinned version, or a dev build's `node_modules` copy), so a switch-on needs no box. `install()` → `LspInstallResult`: `{ ok: true }`, or `{ ok: false, error: 'offline' \| 'http' \| 'mismatch' \| 'unpack' \| 'disk' \| 'unsupported' \| 'cancelled', detail? }` — never a rejection for a failed download. It takes no argument: main picks the pinned packages of `process.platform`/`process.arch` (`lsp/pins.ts`), the npm registry URL and `<userData>/lsp/<name>-<version>/`; it downloads only the missing ones; a second call while one runs joins it. Progress `{ helper, phase: 'download' \| 'unpack', received, total, index, count }` goes to each calling window on `lsp:install-progress`, once per whole percent. `cancelInstall()` stops a download and resolves when its `.partial-` folder is gone. The switch is the renderer's to set after `{ ok: true }` |

Bases (GRO-2097) adds its methods to `CONTRACT` additively (`index(root)` and `readAsset(root, ref)` above), never routes; the drawing embed (YAZ-852) extends the same pipe the same way with `writeAsset(req)`.

Notes
- Folder picking (client, `usePickFolder`): the vault switcher's last row "Open folder…" (the sidebar header, YAZ-1767 D4) and the Welcome screen's Open folder… call `pickFolder()`; `{ path }` → set root + push to recents, `{ cancelled }` or a rejection → nothing. No dialog ever opens by itself — a window with no folder shows the Welcome screen (C2, GRO-2164). One dialog in flight at a time; the trigger buttons are disabled meanwhile. There is no in-app folder browser.
- Main-process writes trigger `change` events on the watcher; the client must ignore events for a path whose mtime equals the mtime it just received from its own `writeFile` (echo suppression).
- Auto-save: client debounces 500 ms after last `markdownUpdated`, also flushes on file switch / the close flush handshake (`window.onFlush` — GRO-2158/2160 — is what guarantees the last save; `beforeunload` is best effort). Only content that differs from the last loaded/saved markdown is saved (Crepe's first serialisation is a normalised rewrite and is never written on its own). Frontmatter-only external changes absorb silently (GRO-2186): an incoming `change` whose BODY matches the last loaded/saved body just replaces the autosave baseline — no reload, no conflict bar — so unsaved body edits and the caret survive a cell edit landing on that note's frontmatter from a folder's view (see "Cell editing"). The same rule covers a save that loses that race (YAZ-2175): a `CONFLICT` whose re-read shows the body unchanged adopts the new frontmatter and retries ONCE, so the app's own property/comment write never raises the bar; a body that changed still does.
- Desktop tests write right after `ready`: on macOS libuv starts the FSEvents stream asynchronously, so the watcher engine announces `ready` only once a probe watch has heard the stream (YAZ-2192), and walks the tree again then, so nothing that landed in between is missed.

## App state (`yaseendocs.json`, main-owned — GRO-2159, D9)

One user-global JSON file owned by the main process: `app.getPath('userData')/yaseendocs.json` = `~/Library/Application Support/Yaseen Docs/yaseendocs.json` (`app.setName(APP_NAME)` runs before anything reads userData; `--user-data-dir=<dir>` relocates it, which is how the Playwright checks seed state, and so does the `YASEEN_DOCS_USER_DATA_DIR` env var, applied right after the name — `applyUserDataOverride`: trimmed, absent or blank = no override; the two names are `APP_NAME` and `STATE_FILE` in `desktop/src/main/userData.ts`). Renderer web storage is not used at all. The renderer never touches the file: it reads a cache (`storage.ts` in client lib, filled by `storage.init()` before the first render) and writes through the targeted `state.*` mutators; `desktop/src/main/store.ts` owns the file. ONE other process reads it, and only reads: the command line's `yaseendocs vaults` (YAZ-2556 🔒 D2 — "Multi-window": The vault list). It has no Electron to ask, so it finds the folder with `userDataDir(env, platform, home)` (`userData.ts`) — `YASEEN_DOCS_USER_DATA_DIR` when set, by `applyUserDataOverride`'s own rule, else where Electron puts an app of this name: `~/Library/Application Support/Yaseen Docs` on macOS, `%APPDATA%\Yaseen Docs` on Windows — and it does NOT follow a `--user-data-dir` given to the app. Nothing here is ever written into the vault or the markdown. The reverse holds too: a file's "Read only" switch is stored IN the file, never here (YAZ-3076 D1, rule 40).

| Key | Shape | Rules |
|---|---|---|
| `version` | `1` | anything else → the file is treated as corrupt (see below) |
| `settings` | `SettingsState` `{ lineSpacing, blockGap, bulletThreading, threadWidth, threadColor, theme, contentWidth, newNoteLocation, newNoteFolder, confirmDelete, confirmRename, hoverPreview, hoverPreviewIn, commentsOrder, sidebarSort, searchSort, rowDates, sidebarTabs, startupWindows, sectionStep, sectionLines, tableOfContents, tocOnByDefault, tableOfContentsWidth, tocLines, sidebarLines, sidebarLineStyle, sidebarThreadColor, sidebarStickyLevels, sidebarIconSet, sidebarFileIcons, sidebarFolderIcons, sidebarArrowMotion, sidebarRevealActive, sidebarIconColors, sidebarIconRules, canvas, diagramDarkColors, libraryFolder, canvasPanel, noticeLength, noticeUndo, noticeClipboard, noticeLists, gestureSounds, sidebarZoom, appZoom, codeReadOnly, codeWrap, codeMinimap, codeOutlineSort, codeOutlineHidden, codeOutlineLocals, codeLanguageHelpers, vaultOpensOn }` | **Edited in the settings dialog** (YAZ-1679, `client/src/settings/SettingsDialog.tsx`): an Obsidian-style centred modal — ONE PAGE FOR EACH settings section (Appearance · Editor · Code (YAZ-3449) · Excalidraw canvas (YAZ-3037) · Images (YAZ-3038) · Files & Links · Review · Sync; YAZ-2709 D13, ⚡ amending YAZ-1679's one scrolling page) with grouped rows on the right, the section titles down the left as the nav (a click swaps the pane to that section, from its top; the section that shows is the one item with `aria-current="page"`; the dialog always opens on the first, Appearance, and a section that goes away while its page shows — Sync, Review — gives way to the first) under a search box that still looks in every section, and below a nav divider the `standalone` sections, which are reference pages (Hotkeys — a reference, not settings) and swap in the same way — opened by the sidebar-footer cog, `⌘,` or Yaseen Docs › Settings… (`menu:settings`), all three the ONE dialog App mounts. Every page, row and search hit reads from the one registry, `client/src/settings/registry.tsx` (`SETTINGS_SECTIONS`): a setting is declared once — id, label, hint, keywords, render — inside a section's GROUP (a titled sub-heading, optionally hinted, or plain rows), and each row carries `data-setting="<id>"` (the `SettingsState` field name for each field that has a row here — `newNoteFolder` shares `newNoteLocation`'s —, `githubSync` for the per-vault switch, `textFormatting` for Appearance › Text formatting — see "Text formatting" —, `ids` for the vault's IDs switch — "Two kinds of vault": The switch — and `duplicates`, `idLetters` and `oldIds` for the three rows under it, "Note ids"), which is how tests and e2e specs address a row. Search (`searchSettings.ts`) ranks with the `[[` picker's `matchLinkCandidates` over label + hint + keywords + group title + section title, and shows hits under a "Section › Group" breadcrumb. "Settings cog" below means this dialog. THE PAGES FOR ONE VAULT (YAZ-2602 R10, S39) — the Review section, the Sync section and Files & Links › "This vault" (the IDs switch), each marked `vault: true` in the registry — act on the ACTIVE vault, the one that holds the tab in front (with no tab, the window's first), and in a window with two or more vaults each says which: a line "Vault: <name>" under its title (`SettingsCtx.vaultName`, which App hands over only then); with one vault the pages read as they always did. Global: one value for every folder and window; validated field by field on load (`threadWidth` ∈ 1/2/3, `threadColor` `#rrggbb` or null, `theme` ∈ system/light/dark — default `system`, so a pre-K file just gains it; `contentWidth` ∈ narrow/medium/full — default `narrow`, so older files and junk safely preserve the existing 1040px behavior; `newNoteLocation` ∈ root/current/folder — default `current` (YAZ-1643) — and `newNoteFolder` a root-relative path per `isValidNewNoteFolder` (`''` = the vault root; no leading/trailing `/`, and every segment must be one create-on-click would accept — so no empty segment, nothing starting with `.` (which subsumes `.`/`..`), no NUL: GRO-2197, because the panel used to accept `.archive` and then EVERY unresolved-link click failed on the per-segment `validateEntryName`; `shared/types.ts` holds the rule and `sidebar/createEntry.ts` is the sibling that must stay in step) — defaults, so a pre-C2 file just gains them; `confirmDelete` a boolean defaulting **true**; `hoverPreview` a boolean defaulting **true** (Files & Links › **Preview on hover**: a note, drawing or diagram row rested on for 400 ms shows the top of the note or the whole board; off, no dwell starts for either — Draw's YAZ-1800 D2, YAZ-3044 A20, YAZ-3075 D5; since YAZ-3403 it is the master switch of the group Files & Links › **Preview on hover**); `hoverPreviewIn` `Record<HoverPlace, boolean>` (YAZ-3403 D7) is one switch for each place of the hover panel, the rows under the master: `sidebar` (Files, Focus, Favorites, Recents), `search` (the Search tab's results), `newTab` (the new tab page), `tabBoard`, `tabs` (the tab strip), `backlinks` (Linked mentions), `folderViews`, `links` (`[[links]]` in a note) — `HOVER_PLACES` in `shared/types.ts`, each defaulting **true**. A place shows the panel only while the master and its own switch are both on: `hoverOn(settings, place)`, the one check every place reads; the master keeps its own value, so off and on again leaves each place switch as it was. On load `sanitizeHoverPreviewIn` keeps each place that is a boolean and reads a missing or broken one on (a file from before YAZ-3403 has none: every place on); `setSettings` takes only an object with all eight places as booleans (`isHoverPreviewIn`); `commentsOrder` ∈ oldest/newest — default `oldest`, so a pre-1515 file just gains it; it is the settings-cog **Comments** control, `Oldest first` / `Newest first`, the last group of the Appearance page (moved there from Editor by YAZ-2709 D13), and the comment block's own header toggle writes the same field — YAZ-1515; `sectionStep` ∈ 24/30/36 (`SECTION_STEPS`) — default 30 — and `sectionLines` ∈ always/hover (`SECTION_LINES`) — default `always` — so a file from before YAZ-2709 just gains them: Editor › **Section indent** › "Step width" and "Grey lines", which App puts on `.app` as `--section-step-setting` and `data-section-lines` (rule 18a; whether a note is indented is that note's own switch, never a setting); `startupWindows` ∈ all/last/none (`STARTUP_WINDOWS`) — default `last`, so an older file just gains it and a value that is not one of the three reads `last`, YAZ-2589 🔒 D2; `searchSort` `TabSort` (YAZ-3511 D1, D12) is the Search tab's own sort, Best match, Name or Last updated (never Manual; `best` is valid here only), default `DEFAULT_SEARCH_SORT` (Best match), and `rowDates` `Record<SortMenuTab, boolean>` (D10) shows each row's Last updated at its right end, one switch for each of Files, Focus, Favorites and Search, default `DEFAULT_ROW_DATES` (Search only) — both written by the sort menu only (no row in the dialog, D8); a file without them, or with a bad value, reads the default; they travel with the settings folder; while the shown tab's dates, Search's dates or a time filter are on the sidebar keeps the tree's file times live (`useVaultTree`'s `liveTimes`, D2). The Search filters (D13 to D16) are no setting; `selectionToolbar` `{ groups, buttons, hidden }` (YAZ-3806 T5) is the selection toolbar — `groups` each of `TOOLBAR_GROUPS` once, `buttons` each of `TOOLBAR_BUTTONS` once (a group's buttons go in that order; which group a button is in is fixed, `TOOLBAR_LAYOUT`), `hidden` the buttons off the strip — default `DEFAULT_TOOLBAR`; NOT in `LOCAL_SETTINGS`, so it travels; the loader repairs it (`sanitizeToolbarPrefs`: unknown names and duplicates dropped, a missing group or button appended, so a button a later version adds joins the end of its group); the renderer holds it in a Vue ref (`editor/toolbarPrefs.ts`) that Crepe's toolbar `computed` reads, so every open editor's strip follows a change at once (T6). `sidebarTabs` `{ order, hidden, hiddenButtons }` (YAZ-3273 D8) is the sidebar's tab row — `order` each tab of `SIDEBAR_TABS` once, `hidden` the tabs in the ⋯ menu (never `files`), `hiddenButtons` ⊆ sort/fold/more (`SIDEBAR_BUTTONS`) — default `DEFAULT_SIDEBAR_TABS` (the `SIDEBAR_TABS` order, nothing hidden), so an older file just gains it; the loader repairs it (`sanitizeSidebarTabs`: unknown names and duplicates dropped, a missing tab appended, `files` taken out of `hidden`) and `setSettings` takes only an exact one (`isSidebarTabs`); the renderer's rules are `client/src/sidebar/tabRow.ts`; `tableOfContents` ∈ auto/pinned (`TABLE_OF_CONTENTS`) — default `auto`, so an older file just gains it and a value that is not one of the two reads `auto`; it is Editor › **Table of contents** › **Pin default**, `On` (`pinned`) / `Off` (`auto`), and the table of contents’ own **Pin** and **Unpin** buttons write the same field (`pinned` / `auto`) — YAZ-2700 D2, YAZ-3558 D2a; `tocOnByDefault` is a boolean — default `true`; it is Editor › **Table of contents** › **Table of contents default**, `On` / `Off`, the table of contents of each page with no choice of its own in `folders[root].tocSwitches` (a page's choice wins); an older file with `tableOfContents: 'off'` and no `tocOnByDefault` reads `tocOnByDefault: false` and `tableOfContents: 'auto'` (`sanitizeSettings`), and a file that has the field keeps it — YAZ-3558 D2; `tableOfContentsWidth` is a number from 160 to 480 (`TOC_MIN_W`, `TOC_MAX_W`) — default 200, so an older file just gains it and a value outside the limits reads 200, NOT the nearer limit; it has no row in the dialog: the drag edge of the table of contents’ names writes it — YAZ-2752 D1; `tocLines` ∈ hover/always/off (`TOC_LINES`) — default `hover`, so an older file just gains it and a value that is not one of the three reads `hover`; it is Editor › **Table of contents** › **Level lines**, `On hover` / `Always show` / `Never`, which App puts on `.app` as `data-toc-lines`: when the level lines of the table of contents’ names show (rule 35: THE HIERARCHY OF THE NAMES; the tones of the names are not a setting) — YAZ-2762 D5; `sidebarLines` ∈ hover/always/off (`TOC_LINES` again, the same `TocLines` type) — default `hover`, so an older file just gains it and a value that is not one of the three reads `hover`; it is Settings › **Sidebar** › Level lines › **Level lines** (the Sidebar page right after Appearance since YAZ-3440 D7; before it the group "Sidebar level lines" on Appearance, with a row "Show"), `On hover` / `Always show` / `Never` (`TOC_LINES_OPTIONS`), which App puts on `.app` as `data-sidebar-lines`: when the sidebar tree's level lines show. `Tree.tsx` gives each nested level (`ul.tree[role="group"]`, depth > 0) `--tree-depth`, and `app.css` draws that list's grey line below the chevron of the folder that holds it. `hover` shows it while the mouse is over `.sidebar__body` or a tree row has `:focus-visible`, read from two attributes that the sidebar writes on that node through its ref, never through state (`client/src/sidebar/levelLinesHover.ts`, only while `sidebarLines` is `hover`, and only when a value changes): `data-mouse-in` (`mouseenter` / `mouseleave`; not the pointer events, which Chromium ends with `pointerleave` when a drag starts) and `data-key-focus` (`focusin` on a row that is `:focus-visible` sets it, `focusin` on anything else clears it, `focusout` clears it only when the focus leaves the list). THE RULE (bug YAZ-3329): no level-line or thread rule puts `:hover`, `:focus…` or `:has()` on an ancestor of the rows — such a state change makes Chromium restyle, or search, every row below it; `tools/perf/sidebarLinesRecalc.mjs` measures it. With `thread`, CSS draws the bullet-threading path to the row under the mouse: each `li` on the hover path draws its own piece (`::before`), and a folder `li` its coloured chevron (`::after`), so a `:hover` change restyles that `li` alone; a folder in inline rename (`li[data-renaming]`) draws no coloured chevron (bug YAZ-3342). | `tabCanvas` | `TabCanvasState` `{ allWindows: boolean, snap: boolean, cards: CanvasCard[], frames: CanvasFrame[] }` — every field REQUIRED in memory (`frames` too, since the polish: the store's sanitizer always sets it, `[]` for a file from before it) — `CanvasCard` `{ win, path, copy, by: 'folder' \| 'window', x, y }`, `CanvasFrame` `{ win, x, y }` | the tab board's layout (YAZ-3343 🔒 D1, D16, D19, D26; "Multi-window": The tab board). `allWindows` ("Show all windows") and `snap` ("Snap to grid") are ON unless the file says `false`. `cards` holds only the cards the user MOVED, last moved first, one per key (win, path, copy, by) — a tab id never reaches storage — `MAX_CANVAS_CARDS` (500, about 60 KB) at most; `frames` the placed frames, one per window, `MAX_CANVAS_FRAMES` (100) at most; x, y are world px at zoom 1, finite.
