Write semantics: every mutation updates memory, notifies `onChange` listeners synchronously and schedules one debounced (150 ms) atomic write (`<file>.tmp-<rand>` + rename, pretty-printed JSON, parent dir created on demand), skipped when its text equals the last write's — a folder expand / collapse is session-only and changes no byte (YAZ-2198); `flush()` writes at once and `before-quit` holds the quit until it lands (`event.preventDefault()` + `app.exit(0)`), so nothing is lost on ⌘Q. A file that is unparsable, not an object or not `version: 1` is moved to `yaseendocs.json.corrupt-<epoch>` and the defaults are used — the bad file is never overwritten silently. Unknown top-level keys are dropped on load. The read itself is `parseState(text)` (`store.ts`, YAZ-2556 D2): the text as a state sanitized field by field, or `null` for those three cases. The store's `load` is the caller that moves a `null` aside; `yaseendocs vaults`, the other caller, sees exactly the state the app would load, refuses a `null` with `<file> is not a valid app state` (exit 1) and leaves the file where it is for the app to move — and with no file at all it lists no vaults and creates none.

Live broadcast: after any change — from any window, or from main itself (window upserts, and the "last used" bump of `recents` when a vault's window takes focus — YAZ-2555 D5) — every live `BrowserWindow` gets `state:changed` with the whole new state; the preload surfaces it as `state.onChange`, the client cache replaces itself and `storage.subscribe` listeners fire (`App` re-reads global settings and sidebar width). The cache keeps its own `favoritesOrder` list, and its own `focusOrder` list (YAZ-2702 Decision 3), while a broadcast holds the same paths, so what reads an order draws again only when it changed; and `storage.setFavoritesOrder` — a drag on the Favorites tab, or a "Remove from favorites" that takes a path out of the order (R23) — and `storage.setFocusOrder`, its twin for the Focus tab, are the only writes of this window that wake `storage.subscribe` themselves: the cache holds the new order at once and does not wait for main's broadcast (YAZ-2631 R15). Per-window `sidebarCollapsed` — and `sidebarLens` since YAZ-1628 — is read from the boot identity and written optimistically through `window.setIdentity`, so another window's state echo cannot change it.

**The Draw import** (YAZ-3028 D6, YAZ-3041; `desktop/src/main/drawImport.ts`): a one-time copy of Yaseen Draw's data into the gaps. It only reads Draw's files, never writes over a Docs value, and a second run changes nothing, also without its marker. App data (once, on the first launch that finds `app.getPath('appData')/Yaseen Draw/`; off when `YASEEN_DOCS_USER_DATA_DIR` is set or `YASEEN_DOCS_E2E=1`): Draw's `library/` (from Draw's `settings.libraryFolder` when set) → `<userData>/library/`, file by file, only the files Docs lacks; `secrets.json` (mode 0600) and `sharing.json` → `<userData>/`, only when absent; `settings.canvas` field by field and `settings.diagramDarkColors` from `yaseendraw.json`, only where Docs has the default. Never windows, tabs, recents, `thumbs/` or `media-cache/`. Per vault (the first time a vault with `.yaseendraw/` opens): `favorites.json` → union into `.yaseendocs/favorites.json` (Docs order first, then Draw's live entries, `MAX_FAVORITES`; a malformed file on either side → nothing written; `favorites.addFavorites`); `github.json` and `shares.json` → `.yaseendocs/`, only when Docs has none (`vaultConfig.createConfig`, the `createDurable` link claim). The marker is `<userData>/draw-import.json` `{ version: 1, appData?: <ms>, vaults: { [root]: <ms> } }`, per machine, never in a vault.


**The settings folder** (YAZ-3276; `desktop/src/main/settingsFolder.ts`, the rules in `shared/settingsSync.ts`; decisions D1–D7 and every case on the working log YAZ-3277): Settings › General › Settings folder points the settings at a folder that syncs between Macs (Yaseen's is git-synced). Each Mac writes ONLY `settings-<Mac ID>.json` there (`macId()`, YAZ-2677 R13 — never the host name), so a sync tool never has two writers on one file: `{ name: <host name>, savedAt, settings: { …the fields that travel } }`. All `SettingsState` fields travel but `LOCAL_SETTINGS` — `libraryFolder`, `canvasPanel`, `tableOfContentsWidth` (D1). THE NEWEST FILE WINS as a whole (D3): a file of another Mac with a `savedAt` above `settingsSavedAt` goes into the store (`applyFolderSettings` → `mergeFolderSettings`: a value this build can't read, or that the file lacks, keeps THIS Mac's value, never the default — one level down too: an object field such as `canvas` is laid over this Mac's object, `sanitizeSettings` repairs it, and each part that the file lacks or the repair changed keeps this Mac's part (YAZ-3298); local fields are never taken); a tie or an older file changes nothing; the accepted loss — a change on two Macs between two syncs, where the older one goes back. Only names that fit `/^settings-[0-9a-z]{12}\.json$/` count; a file that is not valid JSON or has no `savedAt` is skipped, and the app never moves or deletes another Mac's file. LIVE (D4): one `createWatchedFolder` (depth 0) on the folder; a change starts a read of the OTHER Macs' files (never this Mac's own, so its echo changes nothing), and the store's `state:changed` takes a newer file to every window. A new save on this Mac writes its file 150 ms later (`atomicWrite`), skipped when its text is the last write's; a read writes it too when this Mac is newer than every file (an empty folder, or an edit made while the folder was missing), and never to mirror a file it just took. The first window waits for the first read, at most 500 ms; quit flushes a pending write with the state file. MISSING (D5): a read or a write that fails keeps the settings (the copy in `settings`) and makes `state.settingsFolder()` answer `missing: true`, which the row shows as a red line; edits still move `settingsSavedAt`. The watcher never announces the folder itself, so a folder that comes back with the same files makes no event: while `missing`, ONE timer reads again every 5 s (YAZ-3296), and the first read that works clears `missing` and sends what this Mac changed meanwhile. `setSettingsFolder` answers only after the new folder's first read, so the row's next `settingsFolder()` is that folder's `missing`, not the old one's (YAZ-3297). THE FIRST MOVE (D6): choosing a folder that holds another Mac's file sets `settingsSavedAt` to 0, so the folder wins; an empty folder sets it to now, so this Mac's settings go in; "Reset to default" (`null`) keeps the settings and never deletes this Mac's file.

Per-window identity: main loads each window as `<renderer>?win=<id>` and keeps a `webContents.id → window id` lookup (`desktop/src/main/windows.ts`). `window.identity()` answers `{ id, root, roots, file, tabs, sidebarCollapsed }` from `windows[]` for the calling window (`BAD_REQUEST` for an unregistered sender, `NOT_FOUND` once the entry is gone); `window.setIdentity({ root?, roots?, file?, tabs?, sidebarCollapsed? })` validates and merges into that entry (`id` and `bounds` cannot be changed this way; how `root` and `roots` meet is the bridge table's `setIdentity`). On the client, `storage.getRoot()`, `storage.getRoots()` (YAZ-2602 D1) and `storage.getSidebarCollapsed()` are identity reads; root/file/tab helpers and the sidebar toggle write back through that same targeted identity path. `storage.setRoot(root)` makes the window a window on that ONE vault and resets the tabs and the lens (an in-place switch, S61); `storage.setRoots(roots)` adds or removes a vault and keeps both (D2, D7); neither writes a focus list — the Focus tab follows the vaults of the window, each with the list it keeps in the vault (YAZ-2702 S8, S9); `storage.mirrorRoots(roots)` follows a vault folder that main's store already renamed, with no identity write. The active file is the `lastFile` of the vault that HOLDS it (`rootOfPath`), not of the window's first vault.

## Menus & shortcuts (B3 — GRO-2161)

The menu bar is a pure template (`desktop/src/main/menu.ts`, `buildMenuTemplate(inputs, handlers)`) so structure, accelerators and roles unit-test without Electron; `main/index.ts` applies it (`Menu.buildFromTemplate` + `setApplicationMenu`) and rebuilds it ONLY when `AppState.recents`, the Window menu's vault rows or `settings.hotkeys` actually changed, or a key recorder of Settings › Hotkeys starts or stops (YAZ-3397; see **The keys the user can change** below) (`subscribeMenuRebuild`: `recents` compares by reference — store snapshots reuse untouched sub-objects; the rows — `menuKeyedVaults(state)`, every vault that has a number, in number order, named by its display name else its folder name (the shared `keyedVaults(state.folders)` of `shared/types.ts` since YAZ-2556 — "Multi-window": The vault list) — compare by VALUE, because `state.folders` is a new object on every folder write (a fold, a last file), and that one pass over the folders runs only when `state.folders` IS a new object; YAZ-2555 D3). A second subscription, `subscribeMenuRebuildOnActiveFile` (YAZ-3037), rebuilds when any window's ACTIVE FILE changes, and `app.on('browser-window-focus')` rebuilds on a focus change: the board items below are enabled by the kind of the focused window's active tab (`MenuInputs.activeKind`). So a new, moved or cleared number and a display name set or reset on a numbered vault each rebuild once; a fold, a last-file write, a name on a vault with no number and the same number given again never do; and since `recents` follows focus (YAZ-2555 D5 — "Multi-window": Last used), a switch to another vault's window is a rebuild too. A label that shows a name or a path writes `&` as `&&` (`menuLabel`, YAZ-2555 — the Open Recent rows and the vault rows): Electron reads a single `&` as a mnemonic mark and drops it, so "R&D" would read "RD"; the handler still gets the raw text. Item ids are stable (`menu.file.new-window`, `menu.file.open-recent.<i>`, `menu.window.vault.<n>`, …) so a live check (Playwright) can drive them via `Menu.getApplicationMenu().getMenuItemById(...)`. `buildContextMenuTemplate(params, actions)` is the same idiom for the right-click menu (spell suggestions → Add to Dictionary → cut/copy/paste per `editFlags`; on an `<img>` — `params.mediaType === 'image'`, which Chromium sets only for elements laid out as images, never inline `<svg>`, so sidebar icons keep the text rows — exactly two rows instead: Copy Image through the native `webContents.copyImageAt`, and Reveal in Finder through `revealVaultImage` → `revealItem`, a silent no-op for a non-vault src such as a card cover, YAZ-1666); every window's factory wires it in `main/index.ts` (YAZ-672).

"The focused window" in the table below means `pickMenuTargetWindow` (`menu.ts`, GRO-2197), not a bare `BrowserWindow.getFocusedWindow()`: the focused window when there IS one, else the window focused most recently, else any live window. macOS reports NO focused window whenever the app is not the frontmost application — a detached DevTools window, a native panel, or a programmatic `menuItem.click()` from the e2e harness — and every one of these items used to become a silent no-op in that state (measured: `tabs.spec.ts`'s ⌃Tab step failed 4 runs in 5 under CPU load because the `menu:next-tab` message was never sent at all). A menu item that quietly does nothing is the worst available answer, so the fallback IS the contract. `main/index.ts` tracks the last-focused id from `app.on('browser-window-focus')`; the picker itself is Electron-free and unit-tested.

**The keys the user can change** (YAZ-3397 🔒 D1, D2): the Keys column below is each item's DEFAULT. Since YAZ-3564 every key of the app is a row of `shared/keys/`, and Settings › Hotkeys shows one card per key, each changeable row with a key button. The app-wide commands — New Tab, New Window, New Files Window, Close Tab, Close Window, Switch Vault…, Open Folder…, Search Vault, Settings…, Toggle Sidebar (⌘⇧B, a menu key since YAZ-3564 D10), Copy path (⌘⇧C, renderer-owned), Tab Overview, Next Tab, Previous Tab — are `HOTKEY_COMMANDS` in `shared/hotkeyBindings.ts` (id, label, default accelerator or null, `macStandard` for ⌘T ⌘W ⌘, ⌘O ⌘⇧N), and `SettingsState.hotkeys` (`HotkeyOverrides`) keeps ONLY the user's changes: an id that is not there has its default, `null` is "No key", and a key equal to the default is stored by deleting the entry, so `{}` is every default. It travels with the settings folder (not in `LOCAL_SETTINGS`), as a WHOLE list (`mergeFolderSettings` never merges it by part, so a key one Mac reset does not come back from another). The store's guard is strict at the IPC boundary: known ids, each key null or one the recorder would take (`isUsableKey`: ⌘ or ⌃, or an F-key; never an App-standard key such as ⌘Q), and no two commands on one key (YAZ-3410). `sanitizeHotkeys` drops each bad entry of a stored file, then undoes each clash: of the commands on one key, the change of the one LAST in `HOTKEY_COMMANDS` goes (it gets its default back), again until no two share a key. Every changeable menu item takes its key from `keyFor(id, MenuInputs.hotkeys)` (no `accelerator` at all for null), and `subscribeMenuRebuild` rebuilds when `settings.hotkeys` changes — by reference, then by value, so a settings write that leaves the keys as they were is no rebuild. ⌘⇧C follows through `ownsCopyPathHotkey(event, settings.hotkeys)`, and `ownsWindowChord` matches ⌃ and ⌥ exactly (by the physical key when ⌥ is held; a key that is not a letter — Space, an arrow, ⇧1 — by its physical key too, YAZ-3410) and owns nothing for a null chord. The hints that print one of these keys — the sidebar menu's Copy path, the vault menu's "Open in Files window", the tooltips of the strip's "+" and grid button, the sidebar's search bar and grid button, the settings cog — show the key as it is NOW (`keyHint` / `titleWithKey`), and nothing with "No key". A draw.io diagram clears its own bindings on the menu's keys as they are at `configure` (`menuChords`): a change reaches an open diagram the next time it opens. Everything else in the table — the board items, Paste as plain text, the zoom keys, the hidden `⌘⇧]` / `⌘⇧[` twins, `⌘1`–`⌘9` (they have their own "Set shortcut") and the roles — is built in. **While a key recorder of Settings › Hotkeys listens** (D6), the renderer calls `hotkeys.recording(true)` and main builds the menu with NO key (`MenuInputs.suspendKeys` → `withoutKeys`: an item's `accelerator` goes, a role gets `accelerator: ''`, which Electron reads as none, so ⌘Q, ⌘W, ⌘, reach the page instead of firing — on macOS a menu key fires before the page hears it); `hotkeys.recording(false)`, or a reload, crash or close of that window (`hotkeyRecording.ts`), gives the keys back.

## Share links (YAZ-3040, ported from Draw's YAZ-1799 — Draw's CONTRACTS.md has the full write-up)

A drawing or a diagram can be shared as ONE read-only link anyone can open in a browser. The link is
served from the user's OWN Cloudflare account — one R2 bucket and one small Worker the app sets up —
so nothing goes through anyone else's server. No encryption: the link's random 144-bit id is its
only secret.

* **One account, two apps.** Docs uses Draw's Worker and bucket names (`yaseen-draw-share`,
  `yaseen-draw-shares`, `share/setup.ts`). "Set up sharing" in Docs finds and updates what Draw made
  (never recreates or empties it), and every link made in either app keeps working (YAZ-3028 D1).
  The Worker (`share/worker.js`) is byte-identical to Draw's.
* **Storage.** `<userData>/sharing.json` (account, bucket, Worker, workers.dev address, custom
  domain; app-wide, not a secret), `<userData>/secrets.json` (`cloudflareApiToken`,
  `shareUploadPassword`; plain text, mode 0600, main-only — the secrets door), and
  `<vault>/.yaseendocs/shares.json` (`{ version: 1, shares: { "<vault-relative path>": { id,
  allowDownload, sharedAt, updatedAt } } }`, on the vault's own write chain; sync merges it per
  entry, YAZ-3039).
* **Who assembles.** The renderer (`client/src/share/shareContent.ts`): a drawing as the standalone
  `.excalidraw` Export Drawing writes, read from DISK (an open tab is flushed first); a diagram as
  its saved XML. Main checks the size and uploads.
* **Always live.** Every successful save of a shared board re-uploads it to the same id
  (`client/src/share/liveShare.ts`): after 10 s with no further save, one upload in flight, the last
  save wins. A Version history restore and a sync merge count as saves. Main records each outcome
  in memory; the dialog, the sidebar mark and Settings show one status line. A failure keeps the
  record and the link's last good version; the next save retries.
* **Rename and delete.** An in-app rename or move (any open vault) moves the record with the board,
  beside the Favorites repair in the fs IPC (`share/fsHooks.ts`). An in-app delete stops the share.
* **The UI.** One Share dialog, lazy, opened from a board row's right-click "Share" (top of the
  Delete group, above "Version history") and from File › Share Link ⌘⇧L (the menu item is
  YAZ-3037's; App's `shareActiveBoard` is the callback it calls). Shared boards wear a small link mark in
  the sidebar, every vault's, red when the last update failed or the link is stale. Settings ›
  Sharing is a reference page (Status, Set up sharing, the active tab's vault's shared boards,
  Custom domain, How sharing works, Turn off); the dialog's "Open Settings › Sharing" opens on it.
* **The viewer** is React and the same vendored Excalidraw the app draws with, built by
  `tools/buildShareViewer.mjs`; setup also publishes Excalidraw's fonts and draw.io's viewer files
  from the app's own copies (`readViewerAssets`), so nothing is fetched from a CDN at view time.
* **The demo.** `tools/fakeCloudflare.mjs` fakes the Cloudflare endpoints setup calls and serves the
  real Worker over a disk bucket. The app follows it only through `YASEEN_DOCS_CLOUDFLARE_API` and
  `YASEEN_DOCS_SHARE_ORIGIN`, which `shareEndpoints` honours ONLY in an unpackaged build — a
  shipped app always sends the real token to the real Cloudflare. No test calls the real Cloudflare.

## Multi-window (D3/D6 — GRO-2160/2167/2168/2169)

The window manager (`desktop/src/main/windows.ts`) is Electron-free — `main/index.ts` injects window construction and display geometry as a `WindowHost`, so everything below runs under vitest with fakes.

- **Restore** (YAZ-2589 🔒 D1–D3, with A1, A2 and A6 — ⚡ OVERTURNS 🔒 D3 of GRO-2160, "on launch, one window per `AppState.windows` entry": that rule had no switch, so a launch that asked for ONE vault brought every old window back with it): `manager.restore(which)` runs once, at launch — `main/index.ts`, after every IPC door is registered and before the link queue is flushed — and says which SAVED windows come back. **A launch that asked for something** (🔒 D1) — a `yaseendocs://` link, Finder's Open With, `open -a` (a launcher such as Alfred), waiting in the link queue because macOS hands it over before `ready` — brings back ONLY the saved windows of the vaults it asked for: `index.ts` reads `links.pending()`, finds each request's vault with `manager.rootFor(path, rootOverride)` — a folder is its own vault, trailing slash off; a file belongs to the root `resolveLinkTarget` picks ("Links": Routing — the saved window one of whose VAULTS contains it, the most specific vault whichever place it has in its window (YAZ-2602 A8), else the recent root that contains it, else its parent folder; a `?root=` that contains it names the vault) — and calls `restore(roots)`. **A window is on each vault it shows** (YAZ-2602 🔒 D6, A8): a saved window comes back when ONE of its `roots` is a vault the launch asked for — or, for `last`, is the vault used last — and it comes back whole, with ALL its vaults; so a launch that asks for B brings back the window that shows A and B beside B's own windows, and forgets a window on A alone. A vault with two saved windows gets both; two requests bring back the windows of both vaults; a vault with NO saved window brings back nothing, and no Welcome window opens for it, because the request itself, handled when the queue is flushed right after, opens the vault in a new window, blank (a folder — YAZ-3487 D7), or on the file ("Links": Routing). **A request that cannot open is not a request** (A6): `rootFor` answers `null` for a path that is no folder and is no supported, existing file — the ONE check, `cannotOpen`, that `routeToFile` answers with a notice ("Links": Failure surface) — and a link that does not parse names no path at all; `index.ts` leaves both out of what was asked. One request that can open and one that cannot: only the vault of the good one comes back, and the notice shows there. NO waiting request can open: the launch is a plain launch, and the notice shows in a window that came back — so a dead link in a launcher never costs you your saved windows. **A plain launch** (🔒 D2) follows `settings.startupWindows` ("App state"; Settings › General › When the app starts › Reopen): `all` — every saved window, a saved Welcome window too (the old rule, one switch away); `last`, the DEFAULT — the saved windows of the vault used last, `recents[0]`, which the quit recorded (A1 — Last used, below), so it is the vault you were in, and a saved Welcome window does not come back; `none` — no saved window. **A saved window that does not come back is forgotten** (🔒 D3), as a window you close is: its `windows[]` entry is removed — all of them in ONE store commit, `store.removeWindow(...ids)` — so its tabs, size and place are gone, and its vault later opens in a new window, default size and place, blank (YAZ-3487 D7). `recents` and `folders` are not touched: the vault keeps its last file, its display name and its number, and stays in ⌘O under "Not open". Rejected for this issue: "each vault remembers its windows" (a new saved list, with rules of its own for a renamed or deleted folder). **The Welcome window**: when a plain launch brings back nothing — `none`; `last` with no saved window on that vault, or with an empty `recents`; any value with no saved window at all, a first launch — `restore` opens ONE Welcome window (`openWindow({ root: null, file: null })`), with the list of vaults. A launch that asked for a vault opens none: the request opens the vault. So the app never runs with no window (A2; `linkNotice` holds the last case — "Links": Failure surface). Vault roots compare with the trailing slash off (`stripSlash`), so a window saved on `/v/` belongs to the vault `/v`. Restored bounds are clamped fully inside the display work area they overlap most (fully off-screen → the nearest one; oversized → shrunk to fit) — so a window from an unplugged display always lands somewhere visible — and a clamp that moved a window is saved. Bounds changes (`move`/`resize`) are committed to the state debounced (250 ms per burst — one `state:changed` per drag). Two known limits: macOS can hand a request over AFTER the app decided (S9) — the launch is then a plain launch, and the vault that was asked for opens after it; and on Windows a link at a cold start is not read at all (`argv` is read only in `second-instance`), so the plain rule applies there. Proof: `desktop/src/main/windows.test.ts` ("what a launch brings back", "a request that cannot open is not a request"), `desktop/src/main/index.startup.test.ts` (what `index.ts` asks the manager for), `desktop/src/main/store.test.ts` (`removeWindow`, the setting's guard), `desktop/src/main/linkQueue.test.ts` (`pending`); scenario 8 of `desktop/e2e/scenarios.spec.ts` ("Last vault") is written and has not been run, and a request at a cold start on the real app is by hand (`docs/REGRESSION.md` W5).
- **New window** (GRO-2167; ⚡ YAZ-3343 D35, S59 replaced its copy): `⌘⇧N` / `window.duplicate()` — a window on EVERY vault the caller shows, copied by value (YAZ-2602 S34), with NO tab: no file, no tabs, no page view, the right panel empty, no `name` (D14); the sidebar's shown/hidden and its lens by value; fresh id, bounds cascaded +24 px and clamped at the display edge; it comes to the front. It boots on the blank tab with the caret in the search (`startEmpty`, the flag `duplicateWindow` sets for the new id and `window.identity()` hands over one time), so the sidebar shows its Search tab; the stored lens is unchanged. Its tree starts closed (`startCollapsed`, YAZ-3487 D17: see "Open a vault"). A Welcome window opens another Welcome window. Before YAZ-3343 the copy carried the tabs (GRO-2167) and the page view of the page on show (YAZ-2951 D3, D5); both are gone. "Move to new window" still carries its one tab's page view and name.
- **Move to new window** (YAZ-2933): a tab's right-click menu, on the strip and on the board — `window.popOut(path)`. The new window is the calling window's vaults (every one, by value) and lens with ONE tab, `path`; its sidebar is hidden and its right panel closed and empty; bounds cascaded +24 px and clamped, as Duplicate. The page saves first (`flushRenamedPath`), main opens the window, then the tab closes in the first window as `⌘W` closes it — on the last tab that window stays, empty. The page opens there with its page view (YAZ-2951 D2): read before the save, sent as `popOut(path, { view })`, given to the new window one time. A tab with a display name (YAZ-2949) keeps it in the new window: `popOut(path, { view, name })`, and main stores it as the new window's `tabStrip` (`[{ path, name }]`, YAZ-3057 D3), so the window's boot, a reload and a restart all show it (S12). `popOut` never copies the source window's own strip. A rejected request leaves the tab and says why in a notice. The right panel's page menu has no such item (D6).
- **Move to ▸ <window>** (YAZ-3091 D1–D7): a tab's right-click menu, on the strip and on the board, has "Move to ▸" right after "Duplicate tab" (D3). Its flyout lists the other open windows that show a vault of the page (D2: `storage.getOtherWindows()` from the state cache, filtered by `rootOfPath`, read only while the menu is open), a line, then "Right panel" — the old top-level "Move to right panel" (`movePageToRight`). An empty group is left out; with no group there is no item. Each window row names what that window shows (D7 revised by D8, Yaseen: "the names of the windows are confusing as hell"): no vault, since every listed window shows this one, but the page on show — its tab's display name first — cut at `MOVE_ROW_TITLE_MAX` = 40 characters with "…" (YAZ-3104), then " + N more tabs", where N + 1 is `(tabStrip ?? tabs).length`, copies counted ("Weekly plan + 5 more tabs"); a window with no tab is "Empty window". A row under the pointer or the keyboard calls `window.highlight(to)` (`null` when it is left or goes away, `MenuAction.onPreview`): main pushes `window.onGlow` to that window, which draws a ring at its edge (`.window-glow`) — one lit window per caller, put out when either window closes, and the renderer puts it out after `GLOW_MAX_MS` = 10 s if no "off" comes. A click saves the page (`flushRenamedPath`), calls `window.moveTo(to, path, { view, name })`, and only then closes the tab here, as `⌘W` closes it; App's `sendTabAway` is the one path for this and for Move to new window. The target (`link.onTakeTab` → App's `takeTab`) closes its tab board and adds a NEW kept tab at the end, active, with the display name and the page view — a copy when the page is open there, also under the blank tab (D5); a page in the target's right panel leaves the panel first (one owner). The text cursor and the undo history do not move. When the moved tab was the only tab and the right panel is empty, the source window closes through its real close (`window.closeSelf`, so its flush runs, D6); a right panel with pages, or an open blank tab (YAZ-3105), keeps it open. A refusal (`NOT_FOUND`: the window closed, S19) or a failed save (S20) keeps the tab and shows "Can't move to that window: …". A drag between windows came with YAZ-3637, which reverses D4 (next item); the right panel's page menu has no such item.
- **Drag a tab to another window** (YAZ-3637 D1–D10, cases S1–S16 in the demo record on the working log YAZ-3660): only a tab of the STRIP drags between windows (D8) — no board card, no right-panel page, no sidebar tab row. **The drag** (D1, D7): the strip's HTML5 drag, with the Mac's picture of the tab. `writePageDrag` (`client/src/workspace/pageDrag.ts`) writes the payload `application/x-yaseen-workspace-page` (`PageDrag` `{ path, owner, from, copy }`: `from` is the window id, `copy` the tab's `TabRef.copy`) and a SECOND type, `application/x-yaseen-from-<windowId>.<rootIndex>` (value `'1'`): during a `dragover` Chromium shows another window the type names only. `rootIndex` is the index of the page's vault in the source's roots; `-1` is a page no other window takes (a right-panel page). `foreignDrag(data, self)` reads that type, and answers null for this window's own drag, a drag that is no page drag, and root `-1`. On the drop, when the data is readable, `windowTabOf(data)` answers the strip tab another window sends (`{ from, ref }`), null for a right-panel page. **Another window takes it** (D4, widened in the demo): the WHOLE window, not only its strip. ONE check says whether this window takes a drag: App's `takesDrag(data)` (TabBar's `takesDrag` prop), off the type names alone. Off the strip (and the review bar in its row) the `.app` root catches the drag in the capture phase (`windowDragCapture`), so no editor, sidebar or right panel below sees it, and `windowDrop` takes it at the strip's end — the end as it is when the move goes (`moveTabHere` with no `at`), so a sheet in between cannot leave a stale slot; on the strip TabBar's `foreignTab` / `dropExternal` take it at the slot of the line, and the line goes out when the drag leaves the row. While the drag is over the window it wears the "Move to ▸" ring (`.window-glow`, out `TAKE_GLOW_MS` = 200 ms after the last `dragover`). The drop reads the payload and calls `window.moveTab(from, me, ref, at)`; the source saves the tab, sends it with `window.moveTo(to, path, { view, name, at })` and closes it (`sendTabAway`); the target shows it at the slot and comes to the front (`take(path, false, at)`). A page open there lands as a copy (YAZ-3091 D5); a window the move leaves empty closes (YAZ-3091 D6; D5 here). **A window of another vault** (D6, revised in the demo): `takesDrag` is true in every window but a Files window, when the source's `roots[root]` is in the state cache (`storage.getOtherWindows()`). A page of a vault this window does not show asks first: a `ConfirmSheet` (`#confirm-add-vault-for-tab-text`, "This tab (<name>) is not in this vault. It is in another vault (<vault>), which is not open in this window. Add that vault to move the tab here?", button "Add vault to this window" — the words of YAZ-3609 D21). Add runs `addVault`, then the move; Cancel moves nothing. A Files window takes nothing. **Off every window** (D3, D5): a strip tab's `dragend` with `dropEffect === 'none'` calls `window.tearOff(path, carry, { x: screenX, y: screenY }, alone)` through `sendTabAway` (save first); `alone` = the only tab, no blank tab, an empty right panel. Main answers as the Bridge row says: `'opened'` (a window at the point, sidebar hidden, the tab closes here), `'moved'` (this window moves there, the tab stays), `'none'` (the point is on a window; the tab stays). **This window's own tab** (D8, from the demo): over its own page or sidebar it stops at the root, as does any page drag this window does not take, so the editor draws no drop line; its strip and its right panel take it as before. Another window's right-panel page names no vault (root `-1`); the strip and the right panel tell it apart by `from` on the drop, and it lands nowhere. **What goes along** (D9): what "Move to ▸" carries — the page view and the display name; no Back list, text cursor or undo history. **The strip's line** (D10): see "Tabs" › The line of a drag. **Known limits** (accepted in the demo): macOS slides the tab picture back for about 0.8 s before a drop on empty space reaches the app, and the new window takes about 0.35 s more (dev); an Esc while the pointer is outside every window acts as a drop there. Open (Finding on YAZ-3660): near the edge of two displays `clampBounds` puts the new window wholly on the display it overlaps most, so the tab can land away from the pointer. Proof: `workspace/pageDrag.test.ts`, `tabs/TabBar.test.tsx` ("a tab of ANOTHER window"), `right-panel/RightPanel.test.tsx`, `workspace/useWorkspace.test.tsx` ("YAZ-3637 D4"), `App.test.tsx` ("YAZ-3637 D4", "YAZ-3637 D6"), `desktop/src/main/windows.test.ts` ("a tab torn off its strip"), `ipc/window.test.ts` (`window:tear-off`, `window:move-tab`), `desktop/src/preload/surface.test.ts`; e2e `desktop/e2e/dragTabs.spec.ts`.
- **Open beside** (D2, GRO-2168): a file row's context-menu "Open in new window" → `window.open({ root, file })` — an independent window on the same folder with that file open; from a window that shows several vaults, on the vault that holds the file, ALONE (YAZ-2602 S33). Deep-link routing uses the same `openWindow` path (default bounds, clamped). **The vault switcher** (YAZ-1767, `sidebar/VaultSwitcher.tsx`): the sidebar header's top-left button — bold vault name + the Octicon triangle chevron (D6) — drops, on click or ⌘O, a `ContextMenuSurface` panel hung off the header (`ctx-menu--panel`, D5) — at least the header's width (`minWidth`) and growing to fit its longest name up to 480px, past which a name wraps, so no name is ever cut (YAZ-1974 D7): the filter input first and autofocused (D7), every vault as ONE line — display name, its key badge when it has a number, relative time (YAZ-1974 D2) — the current vault `aria-current` (D3) — "current" being EVERY vault of this window since YAZ-2602 — "Open folder…" last (the folder picker, D4 — it opens beside since YAZ-1914). With two or more vaults in the window the trigger names them (YAZ-2602 S15: `vaultsLabel` — two names joined with " + ", more as the first two then "+ N more"; its `title` lists every path), or, while the window's vaults are EXACTLY a saved workspace (`sameVaults`, the first that matches), shows that workspace's name; a click drops the same panel. **Two groups** (YAZ-2555 🔒 D1; since YAZ-2602 D8 the saved workspaces stand above them under "Workspaces" — Workspaces, below): the vaults that have a window stand FIRST, under a small muted label "Open"; the others follow under "Not open", with a hairline above that label when the first group stands over it. The labels are not rows — never focused, never highlighted, outside the highlight's index space — and a group with no row shows no label. A minimized window's vault is "Open" like any other (no "minimized" mark — the door restores the window), a vault open in two windows is ONE row, each vault of a window that shows several is "Open" (S59), and a Welcome window (root `null`) is no vault. **The rows** (A1) are `storage.listVaults()` — the shared `listVaults` over the state cache, no IPC; the SAME list `yaseendocs vaults` prints (YAZ-2556 🔒 D2 — The vault list, below): the recents PLUS every open vault (`openVaultRoots` — every vault of every window, `windows[].roots`, once, trailing slash off; YAZ-2602 D6) PLUS every vault that has a number (`keyedVaults`), so a numbered vault does not leave the list when it falls out of the 10 recents. The panel then puts them in its two groups: "Open" is the open recents in last-used order, then the open vaults that are not in the recents; "Not open" the other recents in last-used order, then the numbered vaults that are not in the recents, in number order. A row that is not in the recents has an empty time slot (`lastUsed` is `null`; a `VaultRow` is `listVaults`'s `VaultEntry` plus `folder`, the folder's name the filter also matches). **The badge** (🔒 D4): a numbered vault's row wears `⌘<n>` (`<kbd class="vault-switcher__key">` — small, outlined, muted, monospace) after its name, in both groups, ALWAYS — ⌘<n> works with the panel up or down, so nothing is held to see it; the row's grid is name · key · ⓘ · time, the last three each in a named column, so a row with no key keeps its ⓘ and its time where a row with one has them. The rows are read from `storage` on every open, never cached across opens. The path is one hover away (YAZ-1974 D2): an ⓘ before the time shows while its row is hovered (visibility, so nothing shifts; a dead row too) and hovering it draws the WHOLE path — wrapped at each `/`, never truncated — in a `role="tooltip"` portalled to `<body>` with `position: fixed` at the row (below it, or above when there is more room there), so the panel's scroll box never clips it; mouse-only by design; clicking the ⓘ is the row's click. **Display names** (YAZ-1974 D3–D6): `storage.vaultName(root)` (`folders[root].name ?? basename(root)`, live through `useVaultName`) is what the trigger, the OS window title (`windowTitle(vault, file)` takes the NAME), Welcome's recents and "Copy vault name" show, and the SAME rule names the switcher's rows (`listVaults`) and the Window menu's numbered-vault rows (`menuKeyedVaults` — since YAZ-2556 the shared `keyedVaults`, where main had a spelling of its own); File › Open Recent keeps full paths and the Reveal / VS Code "no longer there" notices keep the FOLDER name on purpose. Ranking is `matchLinkCandidates` over each row's display name AND folder name (one candidate per name, the `[[` picker's alias idea — each row once, at its best rank), and the ranked rows are THEN put in the two groups by a stable split (YAZ-2555 A6: the filter keeps the groups and the badges; with no query each group is in last-used order); the highlight starts on the first NON-current row (`defaultHighlight(matches, query, ...roots)` — the first row that is no vault of this window; 🔒 with an EMPTY query it never starts on a workspace row, though those stand above: `⌘O ⏎` is still "the vault you used last", YAZ-2555 wins over YAZ-2602 here) so ⌘O ⏎ jumps to the last-used other vault, an OPEN one first — with two or more vaults open, the open vault used before this one, and "last used" follows focus since D5, so a mouse click or ⌘\` counts (Last used, below); with only this window's vault open, the first "Not open" row; with a typed query, the first row shown, which is the best match among the open vaults when one matches; ↑/↓ clamp, hover moves it, ⏎ activates, **⇧⏎ / ⇧-click open the vault IN this window** — the menu's "Open in this window" (YAZ-1974 D8; on a vault of this workspace window ⏎ and ⇧⏎ — a click too — are "Open by itself" since YAZ-3487 D11; on any other vault it REPLACES all the window's vaults with that one and resets the tabs, YAZ-2602 S61 — to keep them, "Add to this window") — and while ⇧ is held the highlighted row's time slot reads "Open here" in the accent colour (D9; never on the current vault, a dead row or Open folder…); Esc closes on the first press, a second ⌘O closes, and the panel closes when its WINDOW loses focus (`blur`, YAZ-2555 A4: ⌘<n> can take you to another window, and a panel left up behind would show an old list; a row's menu and rename field go with it, the header's stay — so "Reveal in Finder" and "Open in VS Code", which hand focus to another app, close it too). Every other activation goes through `window.openRecent(path)` — raise the vault's open windows (🔒 D9), or with none an EMPTY caller takes the vault, else a new one opens on it blank by default (YAZ-3487 D1, D7, overturning D2; "Its last note", D15); `false` (dead folder, MRU pruned) disables the row with "Folder not found" and keeps the panel open. App's `openVault` is the same door for a vault window's Open Folder… and File › Open Recent (YAZ-1914), the Window menu's ⌘1–⌘9 rows reach it in main (YAZ-2555 D3 — "Menus & shortcuts"), and so does a FOLDER that comes from outside the app (`routeToFile`, YAZ-2556 🔒 D1 — "Links": Routing). **The vault menu** (YAZ-1798): right-clicking the trigger (= the current vault, in a window with ONE vault; with two or more the trigger is several vaults and its right-click is the one item "Save as workspace…" — Workspaces, below) or any live row opens the sidebar's own `ContextMenu` with `buildVaultMenuSections({ path, name, isCurrent, renamed, keyed })` (`sidebar/vaultMenuSections.ts`, pure; `keyed` = `storage.keyedVaults()`, who has which number; `isCurrent` = the vault is one of this window's, YAZ-2602 S8) — another vault gets [Add to this window · Open in this window `⇧⏎`] · [Set display name · Reset to folder name · Set shortcut ▸] · [Copy vault name · Copy path] · [Reveal in Finder · Open in VS Code] · [Remove from recent vaults]; a vault of this window the middle three groups; **"Add to this window"** (YAZ-2602 D2, S8) is App's `addVault` — the blank-space item's own door, Several vaults in one window, below: added → the panel closes; refused → App's notice has said why and the panel stays, the row as it was; "Reset to folder name" only while a display name is set (YAZ-1974 D5 — never labelled "Rename", which renames on disk in the file menu). **"Set shortcut"** (YAZ-2555 🔒 D2) is a parent, last in its group: its flyout lists `⌘1`–`⌘9`, each with a hint — the name of the vault that has that number, `✓ <name>` on this vault's own, "free" on one nobody has — and, in a group of its own and only while this vault has a number, "No shortcut". A number another vault has is offered like a free one: picking it moves it here, no confirm. Picking is `storage.setVaultKey(path, n)` — ONE `state.setFolder(root, { key })`, the cache and the store each taking the number from the vault that had it ("App state": `folders[root]`) — and "No shortcut" is `setVaultKey(path, null)`; the open panel's badges follow at once, the one on the vault that lost the number too, the Window menu gains, renames, moves or drops its row ("Menus & shortcuts"), and the number is there after a relaunch. A row that is listed only for its number and loses it stays until the panel closes; the next open does not list it. "Set display name" turns the name into an inline `TextField` WHERE it was right-clicked — the header or the row, a `<div>` in place of the `<button>` meanwhile — the name selected, the folder name as placeholder: ⏎ or blur saves, Esc cancels, an empty field is the folder name again; the field is the top layer: Esc and click-away end only it (the panel stays), and a mousedown on another row ends it (the blur saves) and swallows that click, so a vault never opens by accident. "Open in this window" is App's `openRoot` (in place — besides Welcome, the ONE deliberate in-place switch since YAZ-1914 made every other open go beside, D8/D11; it lands on Files like any vault switch, YAZ-1846; `false` greys the row like a click's); Reveal / VS Code are the Sidebar's own verbs (any absolute path, `NOT_FOUND` notice); the copies confirm through the sidebar notice; Remove is `storage.removeRecentRoot` with no confirm (the folder is untouched): it drops the row at once and CLEARS the vault's number (YAZ-2555 A2 — `setVaultKey(path, null)`, only when it has one); a vault that still has a window is listed again on the next open, under "Open", with no time and no number (A1). The menu is the top layer while it stands: Esc and click-away close only it, and the filter ignores ↑/↓/⏎/Esc meanwhile. Every right-click swallows Electron's native text menu; a "Folder not found" row gets no menu — the door has pruned its MRU entry; one that has a number keeps it (A3) and is listed again on the next open (A1), where its menu can clear the number. ⌘-click on a sidebar file row is NOT this gesture any more: since I3 (GRO-2235, locked) it opens a background tab in the SAME window — see Tabs below.
- **Several vaults in one window** (YAZ-2602 🔒 D1–D7, rules R1–R12, cases S1–S62 and S73–S80, amended by A1–A9, all on the issue): a window shows one vault or up to `MAX_WINDOW_ROOTS` (8, R7) — `WindowEntry.roots`, `root` the first ("App state": `windows`). With ONE vault everything is as it was before this work: no vault row, the same bridge calls, the same paint (S11, S79 — pinned by `App.test.tsx`, "App with one vault makes the bridge calls it made before"). **One scope per vault** (🔒 D1): each vault of the window stays a FULL vault. App holds one `VaultScope` per vault (`vault/useVaultScope.ts`) and every one stays LOADED. WHY: a note must behave the same in every window — its `[[links]]` and `[[` picker (R1: they stay inside the note's own vault; no link crosses two vaults), its properties, its images, its sync chip, its IDs and its review settings come from the vault that holds it, whichever tab is in front (S30) — and a loaded scope makes a tab switch BETWEEN two vaults cost what a switch inside one costs (S29, S80). Rejected: one loaded vault that follows the active tab (the full index over IPC on each switch, and the hidden tabs on the wrong vault); extra folders in the tree only (links, images and properties off the wrong vault); opening the parent folder (one merged vault). The scopes live in SLOTS (`vault/slots.ts`): `MAX_WINDOW_ROOTS` `useVaultScope` calls on every render, because a scope must exist in the FIRST render — an editor that waited a frame for its vault would change the launch paint — and hooks cannot be called a varying number of times; `assignSlots` gives a new vault the first free slot and a vault KEEPS its slot while it is in the window, through a rename too (`renameSlots`), so nothing of a vault that stays loads again; a slot with no vault is idle — no bridge call, and `useReview` starts no midnight timer for it. `scopeOf(path)` is the scope of the vault that HOLDS the path — the most specific one, `rootOfPath` — and a path in no vault of the window (a pasted `#/abs/path` URL) gets the first vault's (S35); it is ref-backed, so the callbacks under the mounted editors keep their identity. `editorPropsFor(path)` hands each editor — a main tab, a right-panel page, a review's note — the scope's own stable values, so a change in one vault renders no editor of another (`RetainedEditor` is memo), and there is one `WikilinkIndexBridge` per vault, drawn in SLOT order, so a new order of the vaults moves none and no vault reads its index again (YAZ-2631 R22). **Per vault** (the scope): the watcher, the three link sources, the property declarations, GitHub sync, the review settings, its count and its session, the external-rename detector, the answer on IDs and the box that asks, the display name; in the sidebar the tree and its feed, the favorites, the stored open folders (`folders[root].expanded`) and the shortcut rows; in main the one watcher and the one index per root that every window shares, and the per-vault subscriptions (vault config, favorites, properties, sync), which follow `rootsOf` — every vault of every window (S77). **Per window**: `roots` and their order, the tabs and the right panel (absolute paths, of any vault), the lens, the selection, the vault rows the user closed, the one notice — and ONE of each thing that asks for attention: the sync banner of the first vault that has one, the external-rename banner of the first vault that has one (S44), the IDs box of the first vault that must answer (S40), and one review session (S41, S42: a start in one vault closes the session of every other, and it runs with ITS vault's settings and notes whichever tab is in front). **Per machine, for every window**: the Favorites order across vaults (`AppState.favoritesOrder`, YAZ-2631 D1). **The active vault** is the vault that holds the active tab, else the window's first: the window title (R3), the settings pages for one vault (R10, "App state": `settings`) and "last used" (S60). A new note is made in the vault of the row that was clicked, and one made from an unresolved `[[link]]` in the vault that holds the page the link is in, at that vault's "default location for new notes" (R4, S37 — `newNoteFolderFor(sourcePath)`), which for the tab in front is the active vault. **Add a vault** (🔒 D2): two gestures, one door. A right-click on the sidebar's blank space → "Add vault to this window ▸", whose flyout lists the KNOWN vaults that are not in this window, in `storage.listVaults()` order, then "Open folder…" in a section of its own (the system folder picker; a cancel changes nothing, S3); and "Add to this window" in the menu of a `⌘O` row (S8). Both are App's `addVault(folder)`: the folder becomes the window's LAST vault with its row open and goes to the top of the recents (S2), and the tabs and the lens STAY — the list of vaults is the only identity write (`storage.setRoots`), where every other way to change a window's vault resets them. A folder the window cannot take is refused with a notice and nothing changes: one that is in the window → `<name> is already in this window` (S4); one inside a vault of the window → `Can't add <name>: it is inside <vault>`, one that contains a vault of the window → `Can't add <name>: it contains <vault>` (R8, S5 — by path segment, so the vaults of a window never nest and every path has ONE vault); one that is gone on disk → `Can't add <name>: folder not found`, and it leaves the recents (S6); the ninth → `A window holds 8 vaults at most` (R7, S7). The probe is the tree feed's own read (`fetchTree`), so the sidebar's first tree of the new vault is that walk and not a second one; the refusal is asked again after the probe, which waits; any other probe failure still adds, and the sidebar shows the error. A vault that another window shows can be added: both windows then show it (S9). **Remove a vault** (🔒 D7): "Remove from this window" on a vault row is App's `removeVault(root)` — the tabs and the right-panel pages of that vault close as their ✕ closes them (the editor unmounts and its autosave saves the buffer on the way out; NEVER the `retire…` helpers of a delete, which drop the buffer), its rows leave the Focus tab and its focus list stays in the vault, unwritten (YAZ-2702 S9, which overturns A5), the selection clears, and the vaults that stay keep their slots, so nothing of theirs loads again. When the FIRST vault leaves the next one is `root` (S52); the Sidebar mounts again only when the vault it is keyed on left (`sidebarKey` — Reorder the vaults, below). An active tab that was in the vault hands over to its neighbour, and with no tab left the window shows the empty state (S54). Nothing on disk changes — the vault's `favorites.json` neither (S50) — so the item is not `danger` and asks nothing. Rejected: the tabs stay open (a tab with no vault behind it has no links and no properties). The only vault of a window never leaves this way: a window with one vault has no vault row (S51). **A folder that is gone** (R6, S53): a tree read that answers `NOT_FOUND` / `NOT_A_DIRECTORY` for a vault, at launch or during use, is App's `dropVault(root)` — the ONLY vault of the window: the Welcome screen, as before, with no notice; one of several: it leaves as a removed one does, the notice says `<name> is gone: its folder was not found`, and the folder leaves the recents. `store.removePath` never touches `roots` (S49): this probe owns the repair. **A window is on each vault it shows** (🔒 D6 — the rule of YAZ-1767 D9, raise the window and open no copy, kept): the open door `openRecentBeside` — `⌘O`, `⌘1`–`⌘9`, a folder from outside the app — raises every live window that shows the vault, alone or beside others, and opens nothing (S55, S56, S58; rejected: an exact match only, where `⌘O` on B would open a second window on B alone); the exact match is a SEPARATE, explicit door instead — **"Open by itself"** (YAZ-2858 🔒 D1–D4, cases S1–S16 on the issue): `window:open-alone` → `openAlone`, the same body as `openRecentBeside` (`openVault(path, alone)`: the same probe, prune and `noteUsed`) but it raises only a live window whose vaults are exactly this one (`sameVaults`), else an EMPTY caller takes it (YAZ-3487 D1), else it opens a new window on the vault, blank (YAZ-3487 D7) — a workspace window that shows it never counts and never changes, and no saved set changes (S1, S2, S7); it is the first item of the `⌘O` vault menu (hint `⌥⏎`, hidden only on the vault this window shows alone — S9, S10), `⌥⏎` / ⌥-click on a vault row (⌥ wins over ⇧; a workspace row and "Open folder…" ignore it — S13, S14), and a vault row's sidebar menu directly above "Open in ▸" (S15); `resolveLinkTarget` routes a file from outside to the window ONE of whose vaults holds it — the most specific vault wins across windows, a tie keeps the first in `windows[]`, and a `?root=` finds the window that shows that vault (S57) — and answers that vault as the `root`, which is what `rootFor` hands a launch (Restore, above — A8); the `⌘O` panel's "Open" group holds every vault any window shows (S59); "last used" is the window's active vault (Last used, below). **A vault folder renamed elsewhere** (S47, S48): main refuses a rename and a delete of ANY vault root of the calling window; a vault that is a subfolder renamed in ANOTHER window follows — `store.renamePath` moves the entry in `roots`, and on `file:renamed` App mirrors it (`storage.mirrorRoots`, `renameSlots`: the vault keeps its slot and its scope) with no identity write that could clobber the repaired file and tabs. **Files between two vaults** (R11, S45, S46): a drag to a folder or a vault row of a different vault is refused, with the notice `To move between vaults, use cut and paste`; Cut / Copy / Paste between two vaults of one window works as it does between two windows, judged by the vault it lands in. **The other opens are unchanged**: "Open in this window" (`⇧⏎`) replaces ALL the window's vaults with one and resets the tabs (S61); Open Folder… and Open Recent from a window with vaults open beside (S62, YAZ-1914). **Reorder the vaults** (YAZ-2631 🔒 D5, rules R12 and R19–R22, cases S45–S55): a drag of a vault row on the Files tab ("The sidebar lenses": Drag in the tree) is App's `reorderVaults(next)` — ONE identity write, `storage.setRoots`, the vaults in the new order, and `root` follows the first. Each vault keeps its slot and its scope, so no tree, no index and no favorites file is read again, and the tabs, the open folders and the selection stay (S47). The order survives a restart, being the window identity's `roots` (S46); the header's label and a `⌘⇧N` copy follow it (S53, S54); with no stored Favorites order the Favorites tab follows it, and the Focus tab keeps its own order (S55). Where the window's vaults are EXACTLY a saved workspace (`sameVaults` — the order does not count), App then asks `window.saveSet(<its name>)` once, after the identity write, so the workspace takes the new order, keeps its name and its id and moves to the front of the `⌘O` list (S48) — a save that fails is logged (`[reorder-vaults] saveSet failed:`), and the window keeps its order; else only the window changes (S49). THE SIDEBAR'S KEY (R12, R19): `sidebarKey`, the vault that was first when the Sidebar mounted, for as long as that vault is in the window — so a vault that joins, leaves or moves mounts nothing again, the first vault is not always the key, and the Sidebar mounts again only when the key's vault leaves, or on "Open in this window". Rejected: the key on the first vault (a drop at the top mounts the Sidebar again — one tree walk per vault, and a lost selection); a saved workspace that keeps its old order (the next open shows the old order). The `⌘O` request is pinned to that key and not to the first vault (R21): a reorder changes the first vault with no new mount, and the request must not fire again. Known and accepted: with no tab open, the window title and the empty page follow the new first vault. Not included: a keyboard gesture to reorder the vault rows, links between two vaults. The sidebar's half — the vault rows, their menu, Focus, Favorites, search and the Inbox across vaults — is "The sidebar lenses": Several vaults. Proof: `client/src/App.test.tsx` ("App with one vault makes the bridge calls it made before", "App with two vaults keeps one scope per vault", "App adds and removes a vault" — the YAZ-2631 cases of a reorder stand there, and one under "App ⌘O vault switcher"), `client/src/vault/slots.test.ts`, `client/src/lib/storage.test.ts`, `client/src/lib/pageLabel.test.ts` (`useAllPathTitles`, `useFolderPaths`), `client/src/sidebar/Sidebar.test.tsx` ("several vaults in one window"), `desktop/src/main/store.test.ts` ("a window's vault list"), `desktop/src/main/ipc/window.test.ts` ("the vault list"), `desktop/src/main/ipc/fs.test.ts` ("a window that shows several vaults"), `desktop/src/main/windows.test.ts` (the S55–S60 and A8 cases); end to end `desktop/e2e/multiVault.spec.ts` and, for the order of the vault rows, `desktop/e2e/sidebarOrder.spec.ts`, each WRITTEN AND NOT RUN, and the perf scenario `multi-vault` (`tools/perf/README.md`), written and not run — S79 and S80 are measured by hand on an idle machine (`docs/REGRESSION.md` S17).
- **Open a vault: by itself, into an empty window, blank** (YAZ-3487 D1–D7, D11, D15, D17, B1; decisions and cases S1–S30 on the working log YAZ-3488). **The empty-window door** (D1–D3): `window:open-recent`, `window:open-alone` and `window:open-set` pass the caller (`windows.idFor(e.sender)`; a sender that is no window still may ask, as before), and `⌘1`–`⌘9` (`menu.ts` `goToVault`) pass the focused window. When nothing comes to the front (the raise rules of YAZ-1767 D9, YAZ-2602 D6 and YAZ-2858 D1 do not change), an EMPTY caller takes the vault itself — `takeHere` pushes the vault chip's `link:set-roots` (YAZ-3343 D22) and no window opens. Empty = no tab, `file` null and no right-panel item; the blank tab is no tab; a Files window never is (its own rule, YAZ-3357 D12). The renderer's `setRootsHere` keeps a tab that came first (a race of a few ms: then nothing opens). Links, Finder and the CLI name no caller, so they open beside as before. This is the one exception to YAZ-1914's "a vault window never changes vault on a plain gesture": an empty window has nothing to lose. **Open blank** (D7, ⚡ it overturns YAZ-1767 D2 "a new window opens on the vault's remembered last file"): a vault opens with no tab, on the new tab page — `openVault` / `openVaultSet` open `file: null`, `openRoot` resets the tabs to none, and `bootTabs` no longer falls back to `lastFile`. `lastFile` is still written, and since D15 it is read to open a vault only when `settings.vaultOpensOn` is `last` (Settings › General › When a vault opens › Open on › "Its last note"; default `blank`): by main's new windows (`startFile`), `openRoot`, `bootTabs` (not for a window opened empty on purpose) and the empty-window door. A link or a `#/path` still opens its note. **A new window starts closed** (D17): ⌘⇧N, the tab board's "New window" and a new Files window (⌘⇧W) carry main's `startCollapsed` identity flag (`takeStartCollapsed`, one time): `useVaultTree` starts with no open folder and writes nothing back until the user opens or closes a folder there, so the vault keeps its saved open folders (bug YAZ-3513), and with two or more vaults App seeds `closedVaults` with every vault row. A restored window and "Make full window" keep the vault's list. **The `⌘O` keys** (D4, D5, D11): ⏎ / a click on a vault of this workspace window — ⇧ or not — is "Open by itself" (it was a plain open that only raised this window: you are there), and the highlighted row says "Open by itself" (`OPEN_ALONE_TEXT`) on such a vault always, and on any vault while ⌥ is held — never on the vault this window shows alone, a dead row, a workspace row or "Open folder…". **A Files window** (D6): the `⌘O` menu's and the sidebar vault row's "Open by itself" change THAT window (`onOpenHere` / `onOpenVaultHere`), as its keys do. **B1**: the sidebar item on a folder that is gone says "Can't open <name>: folder not found", as `⌘1`–`⌘9` do.
- **Workspaces** (YAZ-2602 🔒 D8, R12, cases S63–S72): a workspace is a saved set of vaults — `AppState.vaultSets` ("App state"), `VaultSet` in the code, because `workspace` already names the tabs code — saved BY HAND and per machine. WHY by hand: the list holds only what the user chose. Rejected: every window with two or more vaults saves itself (half-built sets fill the list); a workspace file on disk (a new file type and a picker). **Save** (S63, S70): with two or more vaults the header trigger's right-click is the ONE item "Save as workspace…" (`SAVE_SET_TEXT`; a window with one vault has no such item — its trigger's right-click is the vault menu). It turns the header's name into the display name's inline `TextField`, holding EVERY vault name joined with " + " (never the trigger's "+ N more"): `⏎` saves the window's vaults under the name — as it stands, or edited (`TextField`'s `commitOnEnter`) — through `window.saveSet`; a blur saves an edit only; `Esc` or an empty field saves nothing. A name that exists REPLACES that workspace (S69 — the one way to update one by hand: a vault that joins or leaves a window never changes a saved workspace; a drag of a vault row in a window that shows exactly the workspace's vaults saves it again through this same door, so the next open has the new order — YAZ-2631 D5, S48); a NEW name while `MAX_VAULT_SETS` (20) are saved is refused with the notice `Remove a workspace first` (R12, S68 — said by the renderer in its own words, because main's `false` does not say which of its reasons it was); a save says `Saved workspace "<name>"`. **The header** (S15): while the window's vaults are exactly a saved workspace, the order aside, the trigger shows that workspace's name. **The list** (S64): the `⌘O` panel shows the workspaces FIRST, last used first, under the label "Workspaces" (`GROUP_WORKSPACES_TEXT` — a label, not a row, like "Open" and "Not open", which follow as before); with none saved the panel is as it was. A row shows the name and, where a vault shows its time, "N vaults"; the filter matches the name with the vaults' own ranking; the workspace this window shows is `aria-current`. The rows are in the highlight's index space, BEFORE the vault rows — `↑` reaches them, and a typed query starts on the top row, a workspace's when one matches — 🔒 but with an EMPTY query the highlight starts where it did before workspaces, on a vault row: `⌘O ⏎` stays "the vault you used last" (YAZ-2555), and a saved workspace never takes that key over. **Open** (S65, S66): activating a row asks main's `window.openSet(id)` → the manager's `openVaultSet`: a live window whose vaults are EXACTLY the set (`sameVaults` — the order does not count) comes to the front; else an EMPTY caller takes them (YAZ-3487 D1), else ONE new window opens on the vaults, in the saved order, blank (YAZ-3487 D7); the workspace becomes the last used. A folder of the set that is gone is left out and the notice names it (`Not found: <name>, …`), and the window that matches is the one that shows the vaults that are LEFT — so a window opened earlier without the missing folder is raised, not doubled; the saved workspace keeps the folder. With NO folder left nothing opens, the row is disabled with "Folders not found" (`SETS_MISSING_TEXT`) and the panel stays, as a vault's dead row does. `⇧` means nothing on a workspace: no "Open here" cue, and `⇧⏎` is `⏎`. **The row's menu** (S67 — `buildVaultSetMenuSections`): [Rename · Remove from workspaces], on a dead row too (the workspace is still saved). "Rename" is the word here — a workspace has one name and no folder behind it — the same inline field, saved through `window.renameSet`; an empty field changes nothing, and a name another workspace has is refused with `Can't rename: a workspace has that name`. "Remove from workspaces" is `window.removeSet`, no confirm: the entry is forgotten and the row leaves at once; the folders are not touched. **Repair** (S71): a vault folder renamed or deleted in the app moves in, or leaves, every workspace, and one with fewer than two vaults left is removed ("App state": `vaultSets`). Not included: a `⌘` number for a workspace; workspaces in `yaseendocs vaults`, in a launcher and on the Welcome screen (S72). Proof: `desktop/src/main/store.test.ts` ("vaultSets"), `desktop/src/main/windows.test.ts` ("openVaultSet"), `desktop/src/main/ipc/window.test.ts` ("saved sets of vaults"), `client/src/sidebar/VaultSwitcher.test.tsx` ("workspaces", "several vaults in one window"), `client/src/sidebar/vaultMenuSections.test.ts`, `client/src/lib/storage.test.ts` (`getVaultSets`), `client/src/views/view/TextField.test.tsx` (`commitOnEnter`); end to end steps 6, 8 and 9 of `desktop/e2e/multiVault.spec.ts`, written and not run.
- **Sessions** (YAZ-3147 🔒 D1–D6, cases S1–S37 on the working log YAZ-3149): a session is a named, saved COPY of a window's tabs — `AppState.sessions` ("App state"), saved BY HAND and per machine. It changes only when it is saved again; it never follows the tabs live (D1). Rejected: a live session (a second write on each tab change, and two windows in one session would fight). **Restore** (D3, S16–S27 — `client/src/workspace/restoreSession.ts`, App's `restoreSavedSession`): main answers the tabs whose file exists and the vaults whose folder exists (`window.restoreSession`, the bridge table). A vault that holds such a tab and that the window does not show joins it through App's `addVault`, one at a time, with its rules (8 vaults at most, no nesting, a gone folder) and without its own notice. Then the tabs that have a vault in the window join the END of the strip in ONE change and ONE identity write — the reducer action `open-stored`, `openStored` on the hook (S27). They open in the saved order, as kept tabs, with their copies and display names (S5, S19). A page that is open — a main tab or a right-panel page — opens no copy (S18, S19). The session's active tab becomes active: its new copy, else the open tab that shows its page; a page of the session in the preview tab becomes a kept tab, so the next sidebar click does not replace it; with no such tab an empty window takes the first new tab, and a window with tabs keeps its own. A tab whose file is gone, or whose vault cannot join, stays closed, and ONE notice counts those tabs: `N tab(s) did not open: the file is gone or its vault can't join` (S20, S22–S24); no notice when every tab opened or was open (S25). Rejected: replace the open tabs (unsaved tabs are lost); always a new window. **Save** (D5, S1–S11 — App's `saveSession(closeAll)`): three gestures, one door. "Save open tabs" on the Sessions tab ("The sidebar lenses"), and two items above "Kill all tabs" in the grid button's right-click menu, in a group of their own: "Save tabs as session" and "Save and close all tabs" — grey with no tab, as "Kill all tabs" is (S4). With no tab App says `No open tabs to save` and asks nothing. Else it asks `window.saveSession('New session')`: main saves the window's own tabs, so the blank tab — in no stored field — is not saved, and the preview tab saves as a kept tab (S9). A refusal changes nothing and says `Can't save: 30 sessions at most` when 30 exist (S7), else `Can't save the tabs`. A save shows the sidebar if it was hidden, switches it to the Sessions tab, and asks for the new row's name field (`sessionNameRequest`): the field opens when main's broadcast puts the row in the list, with "New session" selected (S1, S11). "Save and close all tabs" then closes every tab, the blank tab too, in one change, with no sheet — the tabs are saved (S3) — and only after main answered the id. More than 40 tabs: `Saved the first 40 tabs` (S8); "Save and close all tabs" then closes only those 40 and says `Saved and closed the first 40 tabs. N stay open`, so no tab goes unsaved. "Update with open tabs" is the same door with the session's id (S28): no tab gives the same `No open tabs to save` and changes nothing (S29). Rejected: the Sessions tab only; an item in each tab's menu. Proof: `client/src/workspace/useWorkspace.test.tsx` ("open-stored"), `client/src/workspace/restoreSession.test.ts`, `client/src/tabs/TabBar.test.tsx` ("the grid menu's saves"), `client/src/App.test.tsx` ("App sessions").
- **Last used** (YAZ-2555 🔒 D5): `AppState.recents` is the order the vaults were last USED in, not only opened in. A `focus` on a vault's window bumps that vault to the top of the MRU, stamped with the time of the use (`noteFocused` → `noteUsed` → `store.pushRecent`) — of a window that shows several vaults, its ACTIVE vault (YAZ-2602 S60, A8 — `activeVault(entry)`: the vault that holds its active file, `rootOfPath`, else its first), and the same vault is what the quit and the last window's close record, below — — so a mouse click on a window, ⌘\` and the macOS window list count exactly like ⌘O, and the switcher's highlight starts on the vault used before this one — an open one first, "Open beside" above — however you got here. Three guards: (1) NOT on a window's FIRST focus — a relaunch focuses every restored window in turn, and that must not reorder the list, so `recents` after a relaunch is what the quit left; (2) NOT during a quit (once `flushAllForQuit` has started) — each window destroyed hands focus to the next; (3) NO write when the vault is already `recents[0]` — focus moving between two windows of ONE vault commits nothing, and neither does a focus on a Welcome window (root `null`, not a vault). Roots compare with the trailing slash off (`stripSlash`, `shared/types.ts` — the rule `resolveLinkTarget`, the door and `openVaultRoots` share), so a window on `/v/` and the MRU's `/v` are one row. `openWindow` bumps the vault it opens on through the same `noteUsed`, and that window's first focus then adds nothing — so "Open in new window" and a deep link's new window are a use of their root; `duplicateWindow` does not bump (the copy is on the vault of the window in front), and the open-recent door bumps through the same `noteUsed`, so going to the vault that is already on top (`⌘<n>` for this window's vault, S25) writes nothing. One bump is ONE store commit: one debounced atomic write, one `state:changed` to every window, one menu rebuild ("Menus & shortcuts"). **The quit records the vault in front** (YAZ-2589 A1): guard (1) means `recents[0]` can be BEHIND the window in front — a window that came back at launch and was never left and re-entered has not bumped its vault — so `flushAllForQuit` bumps the vault of the window that had focus last (`focusOrder[0]`) through the same `noteUsed`, as its first step, before guard (2) starts and before any window goes; `runQuitSequence` flushes the store after the windows, so it is on disk. A Welcome window in front records nothing, and a vault already on top writes nothing. When the LAST window closes — which quits (`window-all-closed`) — `closed` records that window's vault the same way; a close while other windows are open records nothing. So at the next launch `recents[0]` is the vault you were in, which is what `startupWindows: 'last'` brings back (Restore, above). The one launch this cannot cover: the first after updating from a version that did not record it — `recents[0]` is then what focus and ⌘O last left. File › Open Recent, Welcome's list, the vault switcher's order and its row times all read this one list. Proof: `desktop/src/main/windows.test.ts` ("last used", and "close" for the last window).
- **The vault list** (YAZ-2556 🔒 D2): `listVaults(state)` (`shared/types.ts`) is every vault the app knows, as `VaultEntry` rows `{ path, name, key, open, lastUsed }` — `name` the display name else the folder's name (`basename`), `key` the number or `null`, `open` whether a window is on it (`openVaultRoots`: a window is on EVERY vault it shows, YAZ-2602 D6; a Welcome window is no vault, `/v/` and `/v` are one; a window read straight off an old state file has no `roots`, and its `root` answers), `lastUsed` its time in the recents (epoch ms) or `null`. ORDER: the recents, last used first; then the open vaults that are not among them, in `windows[]` order; then the numbered vaults that are in neither, in number order. A `folders` entry that is not recent, not open and has no number is no vault and is not listed. ONE list with two readers, so they cannot disagree: the ⌘O panel (`storage.listVaults()`, which then stands the open rows first — Open beside, above) and the command line's `yaseendocs vaults`, which prints the list in THIS order, not the panel's "open first". **`keyedVaults(folders)`** (`shared/types.ts`; `KeyedVault` rows `{ key, path, name }`) is the numbered part on its own — the folders that have a number, in number order, each by its display name else its folder name: the Window menu's rows (`menuKeyedVaults`), the "Set shortcut" flyout (`storage.keyedVaults()`) and `listVaults` all call it, where each had a copy of its own, so the three name and order a numbered vault the same way. **`yaseendocs vaults [--json]`** (`desktop/src/cli/cli.ts` — the door of "Comments"; the one verb that takes no page): without `--json` one line per vault — `<name>  <path>`, then `  ⌘<n>` when it has number n, then `  (open)` when a window is on it — or `no vaults`; with it the rows as a 2-space-indented JSON array, each with its keys in the order above, `[]` for none. It only READS, and only the app's state file — never writes it, never creates it, never moves it aside, and never talks to the app: the file is `yaseendocs.json` in `userDataDir(env, platform, home)` (`desktop/src/main/userData.ts` — the `YASEEN_DOCS_USER_DATA_DIR` override when set, else the folder Electron gives an app of this name; "App state"), read through the store's own `parseState`, so the command sees the state the app would load, field for field. No file (the app never ran) → no vaults, exit 0; a file `parseState` refuses → `<file> is not a valid app state` on stderr, exit 1. So the answer is the same with the app running or not: with the app closed, `open` is a window the app opens again at its start, and with it running a change is in the answer once the store's debounced write has landed (150 ms — atomic, so the command reads the old file or the new one, never half of one). `HELP` says the order, each field and that the command never writes the file. The list is a door for anything outside the app — a script, an agent, a launcher: with the folder door of "Links": Routing, `open -a "Yaseen Docs" <path>` on a row's `path` goes to that vault. A row is listed whether or not its folder is still there (`listVaults` never looks at the disk), and the app holds no launcher's code. Proof: `client/src/lib/storage.test.ts` (`listVaults`; `storage.keyedVaults`), `desktop/src/main/menu.test.ts` (the menu's rows), `client/src/sidebar/VaultSwitcher.test.tsx` (the panel over `storage.listVaults()`), `desktop/src/cli/cli.test.ts` ("vaults": the rows and their order, the plain lines, no file, a damaged file, the override, and that not a byte or the mtime of the file changes — against a state file the real store wrote in a temp folder) and `desktop/src/main/userData.test.ts` (`userDataDir`).

A right-click on ANY card: "Go to tab", then the strip's own `TabMenu` (Move to new window, Duplicate tab, Move to ▸, Show in sidebar, Copy path, Set display name / Reset to page name, Reveal in Finder, Open in VS Code), then "Close tab"; another window runs its own tab action (`window:tab-action` → `link:tab-action`; "Show in sidebar" also raises it). A hover on another window's card lights that tab in its strip (`window:highlight-tab` → `link:highlight-tab`, `boardHighlight.ts`); a hover on its frame, and a "Move to ▸" row, make the real window glow and ring the frame. **A tab to another window** (D13, D20, D38; S40–S43): a single card dropped in another window's frame moves the REAL tab there — this window's card by the "Move to ▸" door (`window:move-to`), another window's by `window:move-tab` (main pushes `link:send-tab` to the source, which saves the tab, sends it with `window:move-to` and closes it). The move from the board is QUIET (`PopOutCarry.background`): the tab arrives as a background tab, the target is not raised, the board stays; the card lands in a free cell inside the target frame (`arrivalIn`). A target that shows no vault of the page refuses: the card slides back and the notice says "Can't move here — that window doesn't have this tab's vault." "Move to ▸" lists only windows with the vault and is quiet from the board (from the strip it still raises). A window whose last tab leaves closes, as with "Move to ▸" (YAZ-3091 D6). **Windows from the board** (D14, D21–D23, D32, D37; S24, S28, S32, S38, S46–S58): a double-click on a frame's LABEL renames the window in place (`TabNameField`; `window:set-name`, cleaned by `cleanVaultName`; empty or the automatic label = no name); the name shows on the frame, in the "Move to ▸" rows and first in the window title ("Client work — Roadmap"). A double-click on a frame's EMPTY area goes to that window's current tab (shows a hidden one, restores a minimized one); on this window's frame it leaves the board onto its active tab. A right-click on a frame: "Open tabs here…", "Tidy up this window" (lines up its cards, the frame stays where it is), "Name window" / "Reset name", "Show window" (hidden windows only, `window:show`), "Close all tabs", "Close window" (`window:close-other`); the two closes are two clicks in the menu, the armed item red at once in both themes. A right-click on empty canvas: "New window" only — never the text menu, and a double-click on empty canvas does nothing. "New window" opens a HIDDEN window on this window's vaults with no tab at the click point (`window:open-behind`, which answers its id; `WindowIdentity.startEmpty`, and `startCollapsed`, YAZ-3487 D17) and opens the app's search for it (`TabSearchPanel`): each pick adds a background tab there, the panel stays, Esc closes it; a pick in no vault of that window says "Can't add here — that window doesn't have this file's vault." While a frame is empty its vault chip ("Choose the vault of this window") switches it to a recent vault (`window:set-roots` → `link:set-roots`). "Move to new window" from a card makes a hidden window beside the source frame, the tab keeping its name and view (`window:pop-out-tab` → `link:pop-out-tab` for another window's card); the source stays open when it is empty. A HIDDEN window shows the first time one of its tabs is opened from the board, its frame is double-clicked, or "Show window"; if no visible window is left, the hidden ones show; a relaunch shows every window. Main keeps the hidden and the minimized sets in memory only (`window:hidden-windows-now`, `window:minimized-windows-now`, pushes `window:hidden-windows`, `window:minimized-windows`; the renderer's copy is `hiddenWindows.ts`). **Kill all tabs** (YAZ-2739; D10, S39): the grid button's menu item closes this window's tabs ("Kill all N tabs? …"); the board's button closes every tab the board is about — with "Show all windows" on, every window's ("Close N tabs in M windows? Your text is saved. The tabs do not come back.", `onKillAll(others)`, each other window closing its own by `window:close-tabs`), whatever the filter shows; an emptied window stays open. **Keys** (S6): the focus stays in the filter box (`combobox` over the `listbox` of cards, `aria-activedescendant`); typing narrows the cards by title and path; the arrows move the highlight (`nearest`), a card off the screen pans into view; Enter opens it.
