A pointer click in the toolbar, the switch too, leaves the keys with the filter box. **Stored** (D1, D14, D16, D19, D26 — "App state": `tabCanvas`, `windows[].name`): the switch, "Snap to grid", the MOVED cards (keyed by window id, path, copy and layout `by`, never by tab id, which never reaches storage) and the placed frames; sent ONCE per drop, switch or tidy (`state:set-tab-canvas`, `applyTabCanvasPatch`), written by the store's atomic, 150 ms debounced write. **Not stored:** the camera, the hidden and minimized sets, the pick, the highlight, the filter, an armed Close. The pages of the right panel (R17) and the blank tab (R19) are not on the board. Not included (D5, D9, D24, D25): the tabs of other apps, "Gather here", a marquee select, a dot grid. Proof: `tabs/board.test.ts`, `tabs/TabOverview.test.tsx` (with "the camera … a pan, a pinch and ⌘-scroll render nothing"), `tabs/TabMenu.test.tsx`, `tabs/TabBar.test.tsx`, `App.test.tsx`, `desktop/src/main/store.test.ts`, `windows.test.ts`, `ipc/window.test.ts`; e2e `desktop/e2e/tabMissionControl.spec.ts` (two windows: the frames, a moved card kept across a reopen and a relaunch, a quiet move to the other window with no raise, a window named by its label) and steps 3b, 4c of `tabs.spec.ts`.
- **The new tab page** (YAZ-2663 🔒 D3, D4, D6 and D7, rules R1 and R5, cases S11–S41 on the issue; `client/src/workspace/StartPage.tsx` + `startPage.css`, `recentlyClosed.ts`; the columns amended by YAZ-3487 D8, D12–D14): what the page area shows under the blank tab and in a window with no tabs — the "empty page" of Tabs, above. It replaced the one line "Select a file from the sidebar.", and `Editor` no longer takes a `null` path. **Mount** (R1): App mounts it in `.tabstack` only while it shows — no mounted tab layer, or the blank tab, and no review — so it reads when it shows, follows while it does, and costs nothing under a page. It reads three things. The records and the names of the vaults come off the app state the window already holds (`storage.getOpens`, `storage.vaultName`, through `useSyncExternalStore` over `storage.subscribe`): each broadcast is a new copy of ALL the state, so the page holds the same list of records until a use, a rename, a delete or a name changed one, and a broadcast of anything else draws nothing. Each vault's favorites are ONE `favorites.get` when the page shows and one more on each `favorites.onChanged` for a vault of the window, put in the order of the Favorites tab (`favoriteOrder` over `favoritesOrder`). The Files tree of each vault comes off the window's one tree feed (`useLatestTrees(roots)` in `lib/pageLabel.ts`, the inner part of `useFolderPaths`), with ONE `fetchTree` for each vault when the page shows, because with the sidebar hidden nothing else reads a new tree. The tree alone says that a path is on the disk and whether it is a file or a folder: a path it does not hold draws no row and no error (S18). The columns are cut in one `useMemo` over those inputs and not on each render (R5): App renders on each broadcast, on each resize of the window and through a drag of the sidebar edge. **Three columns** (`.start__column[data-col]`: `closed`, `recent`, `favorites` — that order since YAZ-3487 D13, "Recently closed" far left; the keys walk them in that order and the way in lands on the first that has rows), each a heading and its rows. **"Recently viewed"** ("Recent" before YAZ-3487 D12; `data-col` stays `recent`): the 8 pages (`START_ROWS`) last on show, the newest first, of every vault of the window, each with how long ago in a few letters (`shortRelativeTime`: "now", "34m", "3h"; as of the last draw: the page has no timer). **"Favorites"**: the first 8 rows of the Favorites tab, files and folders. **"Recently closed"** (YAZ-3487 D8, D10; it replaced "Used a lot, not a favorite yet" of D4, and `suggestFavorites.ts` left): `recentlyClosed(records, openNow)`, one PURE function — the closed notes of every vault of the window (`folders[root].closed`, App state), the newest first, each with its time, less each note a tab shows NOW: this window's (`openTabs`, App's `useMemo` over `tabs`) and the other windows' (`storage.getOtherWindows`, held by its paths, so a broadcast that changes no tab draws nothing, R5). A note opened again, or a tab moved to another window, is thus no row; 8 rows at most, cut after the tree check, so a note that is gone takes no place. It reads the trees and the app state only, so its grey line shows with the trees. An empty column shows one grey line, and only after what it reads has answered: "Pages you open show here.", "No favorites yet. Right-click a file or folder → Add to favorites.", "Notes you close show here." **A row** is a `button.start__row` (`data-path`, `data-col`, `data-row`) with the box and the tokens of a sidebar row — NOT `.tree__row`, by which the sidebar, `focusHandoff.ts` and the e2e specs find the sidebar's rows — and `app.css`'s own `.tree__chevron` (a folder) and `.tree__vault` (the vault's name, with two or more vaults, S20): the name by `pageLabel`, then the folder the row is in (none at the top of its vault). In a row with too little room (YAZ-2740 D2) the folder gives way first, then the vault's name (`.start__row .tree__vault` in `startPage.css`; the sidebar's own tag keeps its width), each down to nothing; the name of the page is cut last, and the time keeps its slot. A click on a file is App's `openCurrent`, so it fills the blank tab as a kept tab; ⌘-click is `openBackground` — of a folder's page too — and the page stays; a click on a folder shows it in Files, open, with the keyboard focus on its row (`showRowInFiles`: the sidebar un-collapses first, then `revealInFiles(path, true)`, S22); a file with no viewer in the app opens in its default app and opens no tab (YAZ-1577 D2). The page is a container (`container-type: inline-size`): where ITS width is 640 px or less — the sidebar and the right panel make it narrow too — the columns stand one below the other (S23). **The row menu** (D6): the page has none. A right-click hands App `onRowMenu(path, x, y)`; App un-collapses the sidebar and sets the Sidebar's `menuRequest` `{ id, path, x, y }` (`SidebarMenuRequest`, the idiom of the reveal request), and the Sidebar opens its OWN row menu at that point through the one builder `openMenuAt(node, x, y, outside)` — `openMenu` is that builder behind a mouse event. A row from outside is a row like a search row: `leaveSearchTo` and `showPath` are its path and `lens` is `files`, so "Show in sidebar" is the first item, and an item that draws into the tree (Rename, New note) shows the row in Files first (S27, S30); it sets no selection and moves no highlight of the search, and its menu is always the menu of ONE row (S32). A row of "Recently closed" asks with `closed: true` (YAZ-3487 D14), and its menu leads with "Remove from Recently closed" · "Clear Recently closed" (`window.forgetClosed`), then the six groups. The Sidebar acts on a request ONE time (`onMenuConsumed`), when it holds the tree and the favorites of the vault of the path — a request that is set when the panel MOUNTS is the right-click with the sidebar hidden (S31) — and a path the tree does not hold opens nothing. "Add to favorites" and "Remove from favorites" reach the page through `favorites.onChanged` (S28, S29). **Keys** (D7): the table under "Keyboard (client)". The way in is the Sidebar's `onLeaveToPage?: () => boolean`, asked by the EMPTY search bar; App answers from `startPageFocus`, a box that the page fills with its door while it shows (`focusRef`, the idiom of `clipboardRef`), so with no page the answer is no. When the page goes while one of its rows has the keyboard focus — Enter on a page that a tab holds already — the caret goes into the page on show in the tab stack (`focusOpenDocument(stack)`), and never into a note of the right panel. **The preview panel** (S39): the search's own (`QuickLook`, YAZ-2662 D5), on a path that is App's and the page's alone — `pagePreviewPath`, handed down as `previewPath` / `onPreview`. App draws `pagePreviewPath ?? previewPath`, the ✕ clears both, and when the search names a file the path of the page goes: the panel draws the file of the last one that asked. On a folder row the preview is parked — no panel — and on a file it follows the keyboard focus `PREVIEW_FOLLOW_MS` (120) after its last move, as the search's does; a row that opens, the way back to the bar and the page that goes close it. A panel is no page on show: it adds no use (S5). **The hover panel** (YAZ-3403 D1, D2, D4): resting the pointer 400 ms on a note or board row opens the sidebar's own hover panel (`PreviewPanel`) beside the row — right of it, or left when there is no room (`besidePlacement`) — through the tab board's `useCardPreview` and `CardPreviewHost` (`client/src/tabs/cardPreview.tsx`), whose dwell lives in a tiny store, so a pointer crossing rows draws no page; a folder, text, PDF or image row opens none, keyboard focus opens none (Space keeps the big panel), and it closes when the pointer leaves, on a click, a right-click, any key, a scroll, the wheel or new rows; it never opens while the Space panel shows, and `hoverOn(settings, 'newTab')` gates it. Proof: `workspace/StartPage.test.tsx`, `desktop/e2e/hoverPreview.spec.ts`, `workspace/recentlyClosed.test.ts`, `App.test.tsx`, `sidebar/Sidebar.test.tsx`; `desktop/e2e/startPage.spec.ts` was written with YAZ-2675 and is not evidence until it has been run once.
- **The Files window** (YAZ-3357 D1–D15, decisions on YAZ-3367; `windows.ts` `openFilesWindow` / `openFromFiles` / `filesWide` / `filesPreview` / `filesToNormal` / `setFilesZoom` (YAZ-3389 D13), `rendererUrl.ts`, `client/src/lib/filesWindow.ts`, `client/src/sidebar/previewPopup.ts`): a window that is ONLY the sidebar — vault switcher, lenses, search, tree, Inbox rows — with no tab strip, editor or right panel (`WindowEntry.kind: 'files'`, D1; title "Files — <vault>", D4). ⌘⇧W (D15), File › New Files Window and the vault menu's "Open in Files window" open one (D5) flush LEFT of the source window, on its top and as tall, as wide as the sidebar (`AppState.sidebarWidth`; 280 with a collapsed sidebar or no source, 280×800 at the default spot), clamped; the source keeps its sidebar, the lens comes from it (D6). A row's doors send ONE `window:open-from-files` each (D2): main picks the most recently FOCUSED live full window that shows the page's vault, else the first, else opens a new full window beside the Files window on that vault (on the page itself for `open`; the push held for its page otherwise). A click previews and brings the target to the front unfocused (`moveTop`), a double click or Enter keeps and focuses, ⌘-click opens a background tab and raises nothing; history, share, review, Inbox (it opens the review, never closes one) and a session focus the target (D7). A Files window is never a target: links (`resolveLinkTarget`'s callers), `raiseWindows` (⌘1–9, Open Recent, the vault sets), `moveTo` / `moveTab` and `storage.getOtherWindows()` ("Move to ▸", the board, Kill all) all leave it out. Its header's "Hide sidebar" is "Show all tabs" (D8): Tabs Mission Control right of the sidebar, always on every window, no switch, no frame of its own, Kill all on the other windows only; main grows the window to `FILES_WINDOW_WIDE_W` (1200, clamped) and back (D3), at once with no macOS animation (D10, `setBounds(…, false)`): the renderer shows the board only once the window IS wide (`afterResize`) and keeps it until the window is narrow again, so the board never lays out in the narrow window and the sidebar never stretches across the wide one — `commitBounds` skips a wide window, so the store keeps the narrow bounds and a restart opens narrow. ⌘T opens a full window (as ⌘⇧N, beside it), ⌘W closes it, Toggle sidebar (⌘⇧B) does nothing; no sessions save from it. The hover and Space preview (D9) float OUTSIDE the window: the page opens one popup `window.open('about:blank', FILES_PREVIEW_FRAME)` — the only popup `windowOpenPolicy.ts` allows, from a Files window only (frameless, transparent, no shadow, unfocusable, hidden) — and main parents it to the Files window, makes it ignore the mouse and shows it inactive beside the window on the row's height (`filesPreviewBounds`: right, or left with no room on that screen). The window's own React tree portals the usual panel into it, with the app's stylesheets copied in: no second index. It is hidden between previews, never closed. Where the popup cannot be made, the panel covers the window's lower 60% (`overlayPlacement`). **Its own origin** (D11): a Files window loads the same bundle from an origin of its own — `app://files/` in the app, `http://[::1]:<port>` in dev (the other windows: `localhost`). `rendererUrl.ts` owns the rule, and the clipboard IPC accepts both origins (`isRendererUrl`). **Its own sidebar zoom** (YAZ-3389 D13, which replaced D11's Chromium zoom): only its list grows; the frame and the footer stay still, and its Chromium zoom is the App size like every window's (YAZ-3432). The zoom menu's − % + and an unclaimed ⌘+ / ⌘− / ⌘0 (View › Zoom) there read and write `WindowEntry.zoom` (a percent, through `window:files-zoom`), never `settings.sidebarZoom`, so each Files window has its own value; full windows share the setting. Every way a Files window opens (⌘⇧W, File › New Files Window, the vault menu) starts it AT its source's sidebar zoom (YAZ-3487 D18, ⚡ it overturns YAZ-3389 D13's one `SIDEBAR_ZOOM_STEPS` step above): a full source's `settings.sidebarZoom` (also with no source), a Files source's own `zoom`; and with every folder closed (`startCollapsed`, D17). The footer order is cog, zoom chip (between its − and +, YAZ-3487 D19), "Files window" chip, update pill. **Vaults in place** (D12): in a Files window the vault switcher's vault row (plain, ⇧ or ⌥) switches THIS window to that vault (`openRoot`); a workspace row takes the workspace's vaults that are still on disk (`openSetHere`, a notice names the gone ones); Open Folder… and File › Open Recent switch it too (`openVault`). The row menu's explicit doors stay ("Open by itself" opens a full window), and ⌘1–⌘9 still go to a full window. **Make full window** (D13): a chip "Files window" beside the cog, in a Files window only. The first click arms it, red "Make full window"; a move off, Esc, a press elsewhere or the window's blur disarm it. The second click is `window:files-to-normal`: main opens a full window where the Files window stands (its narrow bounds when the board made it wide; at least 1200 wide, clamped), on its vaults and lens, on the blank tab (`startEmpty`), and only then closes the Files window by its real close, so the app never quits for it (S44). It is a new window, not a reload: the full window must load from the other origin (D11).
- **Right panel** (YAZ-966): `client/src/workspace/useWorkspace.ts` is the renderer's ONE owner for main tabs, right headers, both session histories, retained mounts, and lifecycle repair. The durable per-window identity is `{ open, width, items, expanded }` beside `{ tabs, file }`; legacy entries gain the default, width is clamped to 320–720 px (440 default), and normalization enforces absolute unique paths plus global-in-window exclusive ownership. Every logical mutation mirrors ONE complete `{ tabs, file, rightPanel }` identity. The panel reuses the full `Editor` and the existing watch/index/properties/sync feeds — of the vault that holds each page, so a page of any vault of the window opens there and uses its own vault (YAZ-2602 S32, `editorPropsFor`); one right header is expanded at most, visited expanded headers retain hidden editor layers, and plain/⌘ link navigation plus Back/Forward stay right-local. Ownership transfers call `carryEditorAcrossPane` before the source unmounts or the identity mirrors, so dirty text crosses without a second editor/cache. Entry gestures are the shared Table/Board `PageContextMenu` (`Open in right panel` LAST since YAZ-1556 — the pane-specific open sits below the page actions every surface shares), ⌥-click or ⌥⏎ on a board card or a table name (YAZ-1557 🔒 D1 — ONE rule in `client/src/lib/openGesture.ts` for both views, mouse and keyboard: plain = current tab (the tab the view stands in: a link inside a page, so `navigate` since YAZ-2648 D3, never the preview tab), ⌘ = background tab (I3), ⌥ = right panel, ⇧/⌃ = nothing, because ⇧ is the selection gesture everywhere; a plain click on a board card no longer opens anything — it SELECTS the card, 🔒 D2 below under "Views" — and neither does one on a table's Name cell, plain text since YAZ-2420 D26, where the rule is its ⌘/⌥-click and Enter; secondary-click, group drag, and preview remain separate), tab/header move commands, and native drag under private MIME `application/x-yaseen-workspace-page`; only validated absolute `{ path, owner: 'main' | 'right' }` payloads enter midpoint/end insertion slots, stale/wrong/external data no-op. The divider previews locally and persists only on commit; below 192 px hides without losing width, while narrow available space derives an overlay without rewriting identity. Rename/delete/root repair covers current paths, retained mounts, expanded choice, and histories; delete retires autosave before workspace removal, rename/transfer carries before remap, and duplicate windows deep-copy identity so later changes are independent. Automated ownership/drag/shell/lifecycle proof lives in `client/src/workspace/*.test.*`, `client/src/right-panel/RightPanel.test.tsx`, `client/src/tabs/TabBar.test.tsx`, `client/src/App.test.tsx`, and the desktop store/window/IPC tests. Since YAZ-2171 one pointed Playwright spec, `desktop/e2e/rightPanel.spec.ts`, pins move-in, resize, hide/show and the relaunch restore; final acceptance still uses the isolated Electron profile and focused demo vault before merge.
- **Single instance** (GRO-2160): `requestSingleInstanceLock` — a second launch quits itself; the first instance gets `second-instance`, routes any `yaseendocs://` URLs in its argv (E1), else focuses a window.
- **Close/quit flush handshake** (GRO-2160): `close` is ALWAYS intercepted — main commits the bounds, sends `app:flush`, the renderer flushes its autosaves (`window.onFlush` listeners: the note editor's own, and App's `flushWindow`, which flushes the outline editor from its live document and then awaits every in-flight `transformFile` frontmatter write, YAZ-2174) and acks `app:flushed`, then main `destroy()`s the window; a hung save can never block close (hard 5 s cap). A user close removes the window's state entry; the LAST window closing quits (`window-all-closed`), and quits — like ⌘Q's flush of every window, all at once under one 5 s cap (YAZ-2198) — keep the entries, so the next launch can bring them back; WHICH of them it brings back is Restore, above (YAZ-2589), and what it does not is forgotten then, at the launch — never at the quit, so nothing unsaved is at risk. A quit also records the vault of the window in front, and the last window's close records that window's vault (YAZ-2589 A1 — Last used, above). ⌘Q is `runQuitSequence` (`main/quitSequence.ts`, YAZ-2174): the windows first, then `allSettled` of the state file, the index cache and the last sync pass, then `app.exit(0)`; a rejected step skips none of the others.
- **Same file in N windows** (GRO-2169 — D6/D9/A4): no dedicated sync channel — the disk-change path IS the sync. A window's save lands on disk → the shared watcher emits `change` to every window → each other window reloads silently when clean, or shows the conflict bar (Reload / Keep mine) when dirty. Echo suppression is per window: each window's own `Autosave` controller holds the mtime from ITS last `writeFile` response and only drops events matching that mtime (client `editor/Editor.tsx` — the one host left since YAZ-844 retired `BaseHost`), so window A's save is never mistaken for window B's echo. Folds are shared per file through the app state (`folders[root].folds`) — last writer wins, applied the next time the file is opened; a live window never adopts ANOTHER window's keys. ⚡ AMENDED by YAZ-1342: a window's OWN silent reload does re-fold, from its LIVE session keys — both fold plugins take `seedCollapsedKeys`, a getter read on every state init rather than a set frozen at mount — so folds on unchanged lines survive an external (AI) edit to the open file and the rebuilt plugin can no longer report an empty set and wipe the persisted keys. ⚡ AMENDED by YAZ-1347: that silent reload is no longer a rebuild — `applyExternalMarkdown` (`editor/external/`) parses the new body, structurally diffs it against the live doc (`diffDocs.ts`) and dispatches ONE `addToHistory: false` transaction stamped `external-edit`, so folds, caret, zoom and scroll ride ProseMirror's position mapping through ANY reword of a collapsed line, and the persisted keys re-derive from the live labels afterwards. The content-hash keys (rule 5) now serve cold start and the fallback only: a whole-document rewrite (one range ≥ 80% of the doc), an unparsable body, or a diff that fails to reproduce the parsed doc exactly falls back to the `setMarkdown` rebuild and its key-based reseed, so no edit ever behaves worse than v0.9.1. Enumeration prefixes (`12) `, `3. `, `X) `) are stripped from key labels (YAZ-1353), so a renumber done while the app is closed keeps cold-start folds too. Zoom is per window and in-memory only, never persisted. ⚡ AMENDED by YAZ-2951 (D1, D4): "Duplicate tab", ⌘⇧N and "Move to new window" START the copy drilled into its source's bullet (the zoom key, `ZoomOptions.startKey`; not found → not drilled in, S7), with the source's live folds, scroll spot and text size — read once, on the action, from the source editor's reader (`lib/pageView.ts`); the start pushes no Back/Forward entry and no ⌘Z level (S21, S22), the copy's folds are not written until it changes one (S10), and nothing of it is stored. ⚡ AMENDED by YAZ-2940 (D3, D4): several editors on one path in ONE window are now valid — a duplicated tab — and those copies sync without the watcher wait: a successful autosave calls `announceTwinSave(path, mtime)` (`lib/twinEditors.ts`), and every editor of that path in the window runs the same `onDiskChange` the watcher drives, so the saver drops it as its own echo, a clean copy reloads as a diff and a dirty copy shows the conflict bar; a switch of the active tab between two copies of one file flushes every editor of that path first (`flushRenamedPath` in `useWorkspace`'s `dispatch`, S22), so the copy you go to shows the text at once; zoom stays per editor, and only the SHOWN copy answers Back/Forward (`.tabstack__layer--hidden` ignores `popstate`, S24). One watcher per folder in main, shared by every window and subscription (`desktop/src/main/fs/watchers.ts`); it closes when the last subscriber leaves.

## Links (E1/E2/E3 — GRO-2171/2172/2173)

- **Format** (E1, locked D7): a note's shareable URL is its `yaseendocs://` file link — path-only, absolute, percent-encoded (`yaseendocs:///Users/me/vault/My%20note.md`), no vault id; an optional `?root=` (also a percent-encoded absolute path) overrides which folder it opens under. `shared/links.ts` (`fileLink`/`parseFileLink`) is the ONE encoding, shared by main's parser and its own `open-file` re-encode (E2); `encodeURI` plus `#` and `?` encoded on top, so either never truncates the path. The path may also name a FOLDER (YAZ-2556 🔒 D1 — Routing, below): the same encoding, a trailing slash allowed and taken off, and a `?root=` on it ignored. No gesture in the app writes a folder link; main's `open-file` re-encode is the one maker. **Draw's links** (YAZ-3028 D7): `yaseendraw://` has the same format, and `parseFileLink` reads it the same way, so a link saved in Yaseen Draw opens the file in Docs through the same routing (`LINK_SCHEMES`, `isAppLink`). Docs never writes one: `fileLink` stays `yaseendocs://`. Draw's Windows drive form (`/C:/…`) is read as a POSIX path, by Docs' rule (D12).
- **Copy link** — TOMBSTONE (YAZ-1554): the sidebar row menu's "Copy link" (E3 GRO-2173, a `yaseendocs://` URL; a `[[wikilink]]` since YAZ-957) was deleted. It sat directly under "Copy path" and the two were easy to confuse, and `[[` already links from inside a note. Everything that existed only for it went with it: `MenuTargets.copyLinkText`, the sidebar's `viewOnlyLinks` prop, and `linkName` on the view-only source and catalog. Main's `yaseendocs://` handler and `shared/links.ts` are untouched.
- **Routing** (E1): a link — clicked anywhere (`open-url`), handed over by Finder's Open With (`open-file`, E2 — the plain path is re-encoded through `fileLink` and rides the same pipeline), or in a second launch's argv — routes identically (`resolveLinkTarget`): (1) the open window ONE of whose vaults contains the file (YAZ-2602 🔒 D6: a window is on each vault it shows — "Multi-window": Several vaults in one window) — the most specific vault wins across every window, a tie keeps the first window in `windows[]`, Welcome windows never match — is focused and opens it as a tab (`link.onOpenFile`); (2) else a new window opens on the most recent recents folder containing it (`?root=` pins the effective root instead when it contains the path); (3) else on the file's parent directory. Either answer says the vault's `root` (`{ kind: 'existing', id, root }` / `{ kind: 'new', root, file }`) — what `rootFor` hands a launch (YAZ-2589 🔒 D1), and where a new window opens when the window it picked is already gone (a mid-close race). **A FOLDER** (YAZ-2556 🔒 D1) is not a file to route: `routeToFile(path, rootOverride)` asks `host.dirExists(path)` FIRST, and a directory that comes from outside the app — a `yaseendocs://` link to it, or `open -a "Yaseen Docs" <folder>`, which arrives as `open-file` and rides the same re-encode — is "Open Folder…" on it. It goes to the ONE open-recent door, `openRecentBeside(stripSlash(path))` ("Multi-window": Open beside): the vault is bumped in the MRU and its windows are raised, a minimized one restored, nothing sent to them; with none, a new window opens on it blank (YAZ-3487 D7; a link names no caller, so no empty window takes it); a folder the app never opened opens as a vault, blank too, and enters the recents. A folder INSIDE an open vault opens as its OWN vault window — the vault that contains it is not raised and is sent nothing (what Open Folder… does on it, YAZ-1914; a path from outside never means the folder's page inside its vault). `resolveLinkTarget` is not asked, so a `?root=` on a folder link is IGNORED. The trailing slash a link keeps (`parseFileLink` does not trim) is taken off before the door, because the door keys the vault's `folders` bucket and its MRU entry by the path it is given: `/v/wiki/` and `/v/wiki` are one vault — one bucket, one recents row, the same last file. The probe is what is on disk, not the name: a directory called `folder.pdf` is a folder. NOT claimed: a folder dropped on the app's Dock icon — the bundle declares no folder document type ("Packaging"), and that case (YAZ-2556 S8) is open. Links queue until the launch has brought its windows back on cold start (`linkQueue.ts` — macOS fires `open-url` before `ready`), and what waits decides WHICH windows those are (YAZ-2589 🔒 D1: only the saved windows of the vaults that were asked for — "Multi-window": Restore). The request then routes exactly as it does hot — a folder too: the door finds that vault's restored window, or opens one — with ONE difference a running app does not have: the windows are still loading, so the push (`link.onOpenFile`, or the notice) is held until the window's page says `link.ready` (A2 — the bridge table), and so is a push to a window that an earlier request in the same launch just opened. With the app running nothing changes: the vault is raised or opened, and no other window is touched. Proof of the folder door: `desktop/src/main/windows.test.ts` ("routeToFile": S1, S2 with and without the slash, S4, S5 with a `?root=`, a folder named like a file); what macOS hands over, and the window coming in front of another app, are by hand (`docs/REGRESSION.md` P6).
- **Failure surface** (E1): an unsupported, missing or non-regular-file target — or an unparsable link — focuses a live window and shows the passive in-window notice (`link.onNotice`), never a dialog: `Can't open <path>: unsupported file type` for a path with no supported kind (asked first), `Can't open <path>: file not found` for a supported name that is no live regular file, `Can't open link: <url>` for a link that does not parse. The first two reasons come from ONE check (`cannotOpen` in `windows.ts`, YAZ-2589 A6), which `rootFor` asks too: at a launch a target that cannot open, like a link that does not parse, asks for no vault, so the launch is a plain launch and the notice shows in a window that came back ("Multi-window": Restore). With NO live window `linkNotice` opens the Welcome window and says it there (A2: the app never runs with no window; not during a quit, which has none on purpose) — since A6 the safety net for one case, a folder that goes away between the launch's check and the open. The notice is a link push, so it waits for the window's page like `link.onOpenFile` (`link.ready`, the bridge table). A FOLDER is no failure since YAZ-2556 D1 — it opens as a vault (Routing, above) — and a folder that is GONE is not a directory any more, so it gets the notice its name earns, in practice "unsupported file type" (S6: unchanged on purpose). WHICH window (`linkNotice`, YAZ-2555 S27): the one that had focus last, else the first live one — restored when minimized. The Window menu's ⌘<n> on a vault whose folder is gone speaks through the same surface (`Can't open <name>: folder not found`), so it says so in the window you are in and raises no other vault's window — that focus would make the other vault "last used" (D5). Every supported Markdown/text/PDF/image file may route through the existing window/new-window pipeline.
- **The Back list** (YAZ-3647 D1–D7, replaces YAZ-721 D1 and YAZ-3609 D10's per-tab stacks): ONE list for each window, `TabsState.history: BackList { steps, index }`, each `Step { id, tab, path, zoom }` (`zoom`: a zoom key or null), renderer- and session-only. `workspaceReducer` wraps every action in `withStep`: when the page in front changed — another tab, another page, another zoom level, whatever did it — a step is added and the Forward steps go; `back` / `forward` only walk it. A step shows in its OWN tab while that tab exists (rule 3 of YAZ-3661 "How it works", YAZ-3675 F1): a tab that shows another page now gets the step's page back in its slot (`replaceSlot`), then the tab takes the step's level (`Tab.zoom`, D2). Another tab of the page (a copy, a bullet's tab) is never touched, so it keeps its level. Only a step whose tab is gone goes to `tabOf` its page, at that tab's own level. After the walk the current step names the tab in front and its level, so an unrelated action (a drag, a rename, a background close) adds no step and keeps Forward. A background tab adds its step when it shows; the blank tab adds none, and the arrows do nothing under it. `close` drops the closed tab's steps (`dropSteps`, D5; two steps that meet become one, with the NEWER step's id, under which a code tab kept its place, YAZ-3675 F2), `delete` drops the page's, `rename` maps them. At most `MAX_STEPS` = 100 (D3). `reset` seeds one step for the active tab. A code tab keeps its place under `step-<stepIdOf(history, tab)>` (YAZ-3458). A QUIET `zoom` (no step) fills the step the tab is on; a quiet change FROM a key (the bullet's text changed, or the bullet is gone) also rewrites that old key in every step of that tab on that page (YAZ-3662 F6), so Back finds the bullet under its new key. The old key and page are `a.from` when the report names them (F6b), else the tab's; the tab takes the new key only while it still shows that page at that key, so a tab that walked to another level keeps it. Keys: Window › Back (⌘⌥←) / Forward (⌘⌥→), `back` / `forward` in `HOTKEY_COMMANDS` (D7), and mouse buttons 4 and 5 (`mouseup` 3 / 4 in App). The right panel keeps its own `rightHistory` (D6). A bullet in a new tab (YAZ-3646 D11): `open-zoom` puts a copy of the tab right after it with `zoom` set, in front (a step) or behind (none until it shows); `zoom: null` is the title crumb's copy, on the whole page (YAZ-3647 E2). **The menus of ← and →** (YAZ-3647 E3): a right-click, or a press held `NAV_HOLD_MS` = 500 (the click that ends it takes no step), lists `nearSteps(history, ∓1)`, at most `MAX_NEAR_STEPS` = 15, the nearest first, in a `ContextMenuSurface`; each row carries its step's id (`NavStep.id`, YAZ-3678 F4) and dispatches `go { id }`, which walks to that step as Back / Forward do (`walkTo`) and adds none; an id that a close or a delete removed while the menu was open does nothing, so a row never goes to another step. Each row is "page › bullet": the bullet's crumb text comes with every `onZoom` and `onOpen` (`label`, the third argument) into App's `zoomLabels` (zoom key → text, memory only; a key IS its text and count, so one text serves every page); a key not in it shows the page alone. The same map gives a zoomed tab's tooltip, "page › bullet" then the path (E4); its label stays the page name (YAZ-3646 D12). A preview tab that a sidebar click moved on (`replaceSlot`) gets its page back on Back the same way, still the preview tab (E7).
- **In-window wiki-link navigation** (Links C, GRO-2192) is RENDERER-LOCAL: clicking a `[[wikilink]]` in the editor drives this window's own tabs API (`navigate` / `openBackground`, Editor rule 23 — `navigate` since YAZ-2648 D3: the sidebar's own open, `openCurrent`, goes to the preview tab now, and a link inside a page keeps the rule it had) — no IPC, no main-process involvement; the manager's `routeToFile` (the Routing bullet above, `windows.ts`) stays the ONLY path that focuses another window or creates one.
- **One link menu** (YAZ-3609 D23, YAZ-3740, `editor/linkMenu.ts`): `linkMenuRows(menu: LinkMenu)` builds the rows every link's right-click shows, in one order, each group under a divider — labels (the page's name, ` (<vault>)` for another vault of the window, then the ID); Open / Open in new tab / Show in sidebar (D5); Copy name and ID (an ID link that is found: `nameAndId`, "AR v2 plan (YAS-466)", the S8 text) or Copy name (the name the pill shows, D2, D3), Copy ID, Copy path, Copy address (a web link's href); Add to / Remove from favorites, Add to / Remove from focus, Open in ▸ (a parent row: New window for a file, VS Code, Default app, a line, Reveal in Finder); Edit link / Remove link (danger). A row the link cannot do is left out (`undefined`); a copy row's text is its grey `hint`. No Copy link: a selected pill and ⌘C copy a working link. `placeRows(path, actions, onNotice, copy?)` gives the place rows (Show in sidebar to Open in) of a target that is there: a folder (no file kind) has no New window. The doors are App's `LinkActions` (`App.tsx` `linkActions`: `showInSidebar`, `listState` / `toggleFavorite` / `toggleFocus` as the tab menu's, and "Open in ▸" from `lib/osVerbs.ts`, the sidebar's and the tab menu's verbs and notices), one stable object in `editorPropsFor`, so every editor — a tab, the right panel, a review — has the full menu (YAZ-3910 A13); an absent door leaves its row out. `copyText(text, what, onNotice, copy?)` is the one copy helper: `Copied <what>` / `Can't copy <what>: <reason>` (`name and ID`, `name`, `ID`, `path`, `address`). `openMenuAt` places the popup (`blockHandleMenu.ts` `renderMenu`) at the pointer and closes it on a row, an outside mousedown, a scroll, Escape and blur; Escape's first press closes an open flyout alone (`closeSubmenu`), and the close clears the flyout's `SWITCH_MS` wait. The flyout (YAZ-3901, `renderParent`) is the sidebar's "Open in ▸": hover opens it, the pointer on another row closes it after `SWITCH_MS`, a click, ArrowRight and Enter open it, ArrowLeft and Escape close it; `renderMenu` leaves an empty group out. `wikilinkMenu.ts` fills the menu for a collapsed `[[link]]` (Open rows through `wikilinkFollower`, the one the click uses; Edit = a selection of the target inside the raw text, with `OPEN_ID_LINK`; Remove = `linkDisplayText`), `markdownLink.ts` for a Markdown link (Edit / Remove through Crepe's link tooltip API). A missing note (S10): (Missing note) (YAS-466), Copy ID, Edit, Remove; an ID of another vault (S23): (INL-4) (ID from the … vault), Copy ID, Edit, Remove. A read-only note drops Edit and Remove.
- **Vault tag** (YAZ-3609 D22, YAZ-3738 D4): a Markdown link pill into a vault of the window other than the note's ends with ` (<name>)` in the muted colour (`MarkdownLinkNav.vaultTag`, App's `VaultLinks.vaultOf` — the name the sidebar shows). It is a widget, `wikilinkPlugin.ts` `vaultSpan` (`.link-pill__vault`, spellcheck off), at the link's end with `side: -1` and the link's mark: drawn before the caret there, so the caret shows after the whole pill, and inside the link's anchor, so a click on it opens the link. No `data-vault`, no `::after`. The same span names the vault of an ID of another vault (S23, rule 23).
- **Paste a path** (YAZ-3609, `editor/pathPaste.ts`): the direct `handlePaste` of `clipboardPaste.ts` turns a pasted plain-text path, or `yaseendocs://` link, of a file or folder of THIS vault into the link the `[[` picker writes for it (`LinkCandidate.insert`, looked up by path in one map per candidate list); a file no tab can show gets a relative Markdown link. It runs before Milkdown's clipboard plugin, which would keep the text. A path is compared with one key: `\` and `/` are one separator, case does not count. A path of another vault open in the window becomes a relative Markdown link (D15), and the `relativeLinks` plugin stores a full vault path that the link box, "Add link…" or a paste SETS relative to the note (D16) — never one an outside edit writes or one the caret types inside (YAZ-3649); `[[links]]` never cross vaults (YAZ-3626 owns that), and nothing converts in code. A resolved `[[link]]` is a pill with its file's sidebar icon: the decoration span of the link's own text carries the icon's attributes and the sidebar's icon CSS draws it on that span's `::before` (`LinkLook`, `sidebar/FileIcon.tsx` `fileIconDecoration`, D13, YAZ-3648, YAZ-3657). A Markdown link into any vault of the window is the same pill, drawn by decorations in `markdownLink.ts` from its path alone (`vaultHref`, D19); the first piece of a link carries the icon (YAZ-3656), and no node or mark view is involved, so the text stays the document's own (YAZ-3655). A click on a Markdown link to a page of a vault in the app's vault list (`storage.listVaults()`) that the window does not show asks, in App's confirm sheet, to add that vault (`addVault`), then opens the page (`VaultLinksContext.askToAdd`, `markdownLink.ts` `elsewhere`, D21). A rest on such a pill previews its page through the `[[link]]` hover (`wikilinkHover.ts` `markdownPath`, D20), and the editor root's `data-pill-hover` hides Crepe's address bar meanwhile. The text right-click menu's "Add link…" (`SPECIAL.menuAddLink` → `menu.onAddLink`) opens Crepe's link box on the selection (D17). The scenario tables (P, K, U, L, B, S, I, W, R, M) are on Linear YAZ-3610.
- **Aliases** (Links E2, GRO-2214): a note's frontmatter `aliases` are extra NAMES it answers to across the whole app — the index carries them (`IndexRecord.aliases`, table below), the ONE resolver consults them LAST (see "Link resolution"), so `[[CAC]]` renders resolved (Editor rule 23) and clicking it opens the aliased page, and the `[[` picker offers the page under each alias, inserting the piped `[[Name|Alias]]` — or, for a note that has an `id`, the plain `[[<id>]]` (rule 24, YAZ-2293). Two consequences pinned elsewhere: alias values are never outgoing `links`, and a rename never rewrites an alias-form link (Rename, below).
- **Note ids** (YAZ-2293, YAZ-2677 — see "Note ids"): a link whose target is a note's frontmatter `id` — `[[YAZ-12]]`, or an old `[[k3m9x2pq7abc]]` — names the NOTE, not its name or its place. The ONE resolver tries the id FIRST (see "Link resolution"), in any case (`[[yaz-12]]`, S17) and by letters the vault had before (`[[OLD-12]]`, `ResolverOptions.letters`, S82), and a target that is the id of NO note falls through to the names, so `[[YAZ-7]]` still opens a note that is only named so (S26); the app WRITES a link that way whenever the note has an id (the `[[` picker, rule 24; a view's link editors, "Cell editing"); the editor, the backlinks snippets and every view show the note's current title in the id's place (rules 23 and 25; "Note ids": What a link reads as); and no rename ever rewrites one (Rename, below). A link written by name keeps working exactly as it did, and a note with no id is still linked by name.
- **Rename** (E1, GRO-2194 — decision E of GRO-2096, LOCKED): an in-app rename updates links AUTOMATICALLY, no prompt (Obsidian's default). ⚡ AMENDED by YAZ-888 for NAME changes only: a changed NAME now asks first, once, in one sheet — the links still ALWAYS update, and a MOVE asks only when it would clear a folder's values (D21 — "Folder settings": Asking first), so everything below is unchanged and runs on confirm ("The page title + rename confirm"). Scope since E1b (GRO-2241): FILE rename and cross-directory move, and FOLDER rename — the extension kind stays unchanged for files; E1b lifted E1's same-parent and files-only guards. Gestures: the sidebar file- OR folder-row context menu's "Rename" → inline input over the row (a NOTE or a FOLDER: prefilled with its TITLE, free text, and the commit is a title edit — YAZ-2420 D16, "The page title + rename confirm" — or, where the vault does not use IDs, with its name, held to `validateEntryName`, and the commit is a rename of that name, YAZ-2523 V3, "Two kinds of vault"; any other file: prefilled with its full name, `validateEntryName` + the extension re-append via `renamedPath`; the same text = no-op; no hotkey v1); and drag a row — a file, a folder, or the whole selection (YAZ-3251 D5) — onto a folder row, a file row (its folder, D7) or the root header → move there (same pipeline, through `requestMoves`: "A list of moves and the undo list" below; Cut ⌘X / Paste ⌘V, YAZ-1674, moves a multi-selection and folders through the same rename pipeline). Flow, in order: (1) the originating window FLUSHES its own autosave for the file, so the buffer travels with it; (2) it snapshots the vault index BEFORE renaming (afterwards the old name no longer resolves); (3) `file.rename` renames on disk, repairs the app state and broadcasts `file:renamed` (bridge table above) — for a title edit `file.retitle` stands in its place, writing `title:` first and answering with the path it built (YAZ-2420 D16); (4) every window's renderer — BEFORE remapping its tab — captures a DIRTY old-path buffer, RETIRES the old autosave controller (its unmount/close flushes become no-ops: the old path can never be resurrected) and stashes the buffer under the new path, where the freshly mounted editor applies it as an UNSAVED change (`lib/renameContinuity.ts`; since YAZ-2940 D3 every editor of the old path — each copy of a duplicated tab — is captured and retired, and the stash stays ONE buffer per new path: copies are in sync, so the last dirty capture wins; title/hash follow the active tab's existing effects); (5) the originating window drops, from each note that moved, the values of the folders it left (D20 — "Folder settings": Leaving a folder), then rewrites every referencing note (`links/renameLinks.ts`): the referencing set is the index records whose `links`/`embeds` resolve — through THE shared resolver (`resolverFor`) — to the old path; per file read → rewrite → write with `expectedMtime`, one CONFLICT re-read-retry, a second conflict skips the file. Rewrites preserve `|alias` and `#heading`/`#^block`, preserve link FORM (bare→new bare name, pathed→new root-relative, explicit extension stays), cover `![[embeds]]`, skip fenced/inline code (a length-preserving mirror of the index's `stripCode`), and touch frontmatter only as whole-value exact `[[…]]` strings via `setFrontmatterProperty` — at the top level, and by the same rule in each folder's block of `in` (D19), each rewritten where it stands (`setFrontmatterIn`). ONE key is walked DEEPER than whole-value (YAZ-864): `folder_settings`, the single app-owned key with app-defined link semantics (🔒 Q1 — "Folder settings: `.folder.md`"; since YAZ-2290 it lives in the folders' `.folder.md` files, which ride the rename as referencing files beside the notes — `UpdateLinksOptions.folders`, rewritten like notes, never resolved to), whose `views[].order` entries, outline LINES that are exactly a wikilink (YAZ-900, `mapOutlineLinks` — a link inside prose is not a leaf) and `columns.<name>.target` strings are links the index never extracted and a rename therefore used to leave dangling; they rewrite exactly as a top-level entry does (same `resolves`/`newTarget`, so the bare-vs-pathed and alias rules cannot drift), the whole key goes back through `setFrontmatterProperty` as the one door's own write shape, and the referencing-set probe learned the SAME leaves — a page whose only reference lives in there has no `links` entry to be found by, so probe and rewrite stay one construction. The key's own module owns both the key name and the list of link-bearing leaves (`folderSettings.ts` `mapFolderSettingsLinks` / `folderSettingsLinks`), read from the RAW value rather than the tolerant read, so a hand-written unusable shape is never normalised away by a rename; a stale entry that never resolved to the renamed page stays byte-identical, as it always did. Outcomes are PASSIVE (never a dialog): one summary notice "Updated links in N notes" (+ "; M skipped (unsaved changes)"), `ALREADY_EXISTS` and other failures land in the same link-notice; another window's dirty referencing editor falls back to the normal conflict bar — EXCEPT for a referencing note that the rename itself remaps (a folder rename moving an open dirty note), whose editor remounts, re-reads from disk and adopts the post-rewrite baseline, so the conflict never surfaces (GRO-2197 audit, deferred). Accepted residual race: a save already in flight over IPC when the rename lands can still recreate the old path — the systematic paths (debounce, unmount flush, close flush) are all covered by the retire step. ALIAS-form links are never rewritten (E2, GRO-2214): `[[CAC]]` reaching the moved file through its frontmatter `aliases` keeps resolving afterwards — the alias travels with the file — so the referencing-set probe resolves BY NAME ONLY (`resolverFor(records, root, { aliases: false, ids: false })`); a note referencing the moved file only by alias is never even read. ID-form links are never rewritten either (YAZ-2293 D5): `[[k3m9x2pq7abc]]` reaches the moved file through the `id` in that file's own frontmatter, which travels with it too, so the same probe resolves no ids (`ids: false`) — an id link is never counted, stays BYTE-IDENTICAL beside a name link that is rewritten, and a note referencing the moved file only by id is never even read. TITLE-form links travel the same way (YAZ-2420 D17): `[[UP-001 - Abdul]]` reaches a note through the `title:` in its own frontmatter, or a folder through the one in its `.folder.md`, so a rename or move never counts or rewrites it; a page with no `title:` is titled by its name, and a link spelling that is a name link, rewritten as ever — as is every link where the vault does not use IDs (`UpdateLinksOptions.ids` false, also given to `countLinkReferences` and `preRenameRecords`; YAZ-2523 V12): a `title:` line is an ordinary property there, every title is the file's name, and no link travels by one. The ONE rename a title does not travel through is a TITLE EDIT (D16 — `UpdateLinksOptions.title`, also given to `countLinkReferences`): a link that spelled the old title is counted and rewritten to the new one — or to the page's `id` when a link cannot spell the new title or another page answers to it (YAZ-2478), and by name, as below, only when the page has no id — for a note and for a folder alike, while a link that reaches ANOTHER folder by its title is left alone; links by name or by path follow the new file as in any rename, and id links stay as written. KNOWN GAP (GRO-2197 audit, deferred): the banner's N and the number of notes actually written can still disagree on a pure MOVE — N counts every note whose links RESOLVE to the old path, while the rewrite writes nothing for a bare link that stays bare, and in a pure move every bare link stays bare, so "update N links?" can be followed by "Updated links in 0 notes". Closing it needs N to become link-FORM aware, not just resolution aware. E1b bare-vs-pathed rules, LOCKED: a FOLDER rename rewrites only PATHED links/embeds to the notes inside it (to the new root-relative path) — bare-name links keep resolving (names unchanged) and stay BYTE-IDENTICAL; links to the FOLDER ITSELF (🔒 D10, YAZ-2290 — "Links to folders" below) follow the FILE rule — a bare `[[Projects]]` becomes the new name, a pathed one the new path, and a bare one stays untouched while the name still reaches the folder (a move), resolved over the PRE-rename folders (`UpdateLinksOptions.dirs`); a FILE move keeps a bare link bare only when the bare form still resolves to the moved file AFTERWARDS (checked through the resolver against a POST-move record set — the shallowest rule can hand the name to a duplicate), else it escalates to the pathed form (a kept bare form is never spliced, padding included). TOMBSTONE (YAZ-844): the base-embed half of this rule is gone — `resolveBasePath`, the PRE-rename TREE snapshot the rewrite used to take beside the index one, and the `tree` argument of `updateLinksAfterRename` / `countLinkReferences` all died with `![[X.base]]`. The retired engine `tree` argument stays gone: Markdown targets resolve through index records, while explicit text/PDF/image targets use the separate catalog; App may fetch `api.tree` only before the rename gate to pin that catalog. Refusals (all passive notices): existing target → `ALREADY_EXISTS`; missing target parent → `NOT_FOUND` (never a mkdir); dot-dirs and a vault ROOT of the calling window — any vault it shows, YAZ-2602 S47 — → `BAD_REQUEST` (root identity is a recents/vault question, out of E1b scope). A window with a vault AT (or under) the renamed folder follows it live, for every such vault it shows (S48): its tabs prefix-remap and its local vault list remaps without an identity write (main's store repair already moved `WindowEntry.root` and `roots`; a vault that moved keeps its slot and its scope). The sheet itself is one setting since YAZ-2420 D35: `confirmRename` ("Ask before renaming", on by default). Off, a rename or a title edit runs at once and the links still update; the sheets that warn a folder's values will be cleared are not governed by it.
- **External renames** (E1c, GRO-2242 — LOCKED ruling): a rename/move done OUTSIDE the app (Finder, terminal, sync tools) is detected and repaired too — CONFIRM-FIRST, never automatically, never a dialog (ahead of Obsidian, which does not repair external renames at all — verified). ONE hypothesis detector (`client/src/links/renameDetector.ts` `detectRenames`), TWO feeds: (a) COLD-START — after the first index snapshot the client reads `coldDiff(root)` (bridge table above) and joins `removed` × `added`; trusted only on `cacheStatus === 'hit'`; (b) WHILE-RUNNING — consecutive `useIndex` snapshots (`WikilinkIndexBridge.onSnapshot` — no new watchers, no polling), diffed into the same removed/added shape, with UNMATCHED removals and additions carried forward exactly ONE snapshot generation. That carry is load-bearing, not belt-and-braces (GRO-2197): the watcher settles each path on its own (100 ms; chokidar's `awaitWriteFinish` ~200 ms on the polling fallback), so an `add` can trail its `unlink`, and the index applies `unlink` synchronously but `add` behind an async `scanFile`, so the index genuinely passes through a ~100 ms window showing the removal WITHOUT the addition. The 300 ms refetch debounce usually straddles both — but when it does not, the pair splits across two generations, `detectRenames` never sees it, and the hypothesis was previously lost forever (measured: `externalRename.spec.ts` steps 1 and 3 failed ~50-100% of runs under CPU load, 0/9 idle). Carried entries are re-validated against the new snapshot first (a removal whose path came back was a save, not a rename; an addition that vanished again is dropped) and only the CURRENT generation's leftovers are carried on, so the memory is bounded to one generation. Guard rails, firm: markdown files only; join key = EXACT (size, mtime) equality (macOS rename/move preserves both); zero-byte files skip; only UNAMBIGUOUS 1:1 pairs — a signature carried by several removed or several added files skips entirely (no guessing); equal basenames (a pure move) still hypothesize — pathed links may need rewriting. Either feed lands in ONE passive app-level banner (`useExternalRenames` — the link-notice idiom with two actions, one hypothesis at a time, oldest first): "Looks like `X` became `Y` — update N links?" [Update] [Dismiss]. N is the rewrite engine's own referencing-set count (`countLinkReferences`, the dry-run twin of `updateLinksAfterRename`, over a PRE-rename snapshot synthesised by re-pathing the moved record back — `preRenameRecords`); N === 0 → no banner, nothing happens at all. Update → (1) `file.repairRename` (bridge table above — store/tabs/editors follow via the existing `file:renamed` downstream; a refused claim, e.g. the old path came back, lands as a passive notice), (2) the E1/E1b rewrite engine old→new over fresh index/tree snapshots re-pathed pre-rename, (3) the usual summary notice — always shown here (the user explicitly asked). Dismiss → the pair joins a SESSION-level dismissed set and is never re-offered (the next refetch re-detects the same diff; the set is what keeps it quiet); a handled (Updated) pair joins the same set. In-app renames echo through the watcher as identical unlink+add pairs, so every `file:renamed` push also feeds the suppression set (exact pair for files; prefix mapping for dirs, since a folder rename echoes as one pair per moved note) — own renames never banner. The DIR prefix mappings are cleared on a root switch (GRO-2197): they exist only to swallow the current vault's echoes, and left standing they sat in the per-hypothesis linear scan for the rest of the session, across vaults. (The dismissed PAIR set is session-level by ruling and deliberately survives a root switch — its keys are absolute paths.)
- **Backlinks** (Links D, GRO-2193 — decision D of GRO-2096, LOCKED): the reverse direction is RENDERER-LOCAL too. "Linked mentions (N)" is a collapsible block in the note's own scroll — and in a folder's page (YAZ-2290 D10) — computed per render from the index snapshot the window already has through the ONE resolver (so alias-form and id-form links count) — no reverse map in main, no new IPC, no index field, no new watcher. Context snippets are read on demand for the rows actually shown. Full rules: Editor rule 25.
- **Links to folders** (🔒 D10, YAZ-2290 — `client/src/links/folderLinks.ts`): a folder is a page, so it is linkable. `linkResolver(records, root, dirs, folders)` is THE path-level resolver every wikilink surface shares (`ResolveLink`: target → absolute path or null), built by `WikilinkIndexBridge` per snapshot: a NOTE first — id, path, title, name, a path of titles, alias, through `resolverFor` ("Link resolution") — and a FOLDER only when none answers, so no link that resolved before means anything new and a note or alias of the same name always wins. `folderResolver` tries the id of the folder's `.folder.md`, then its root-relative path, then its title (YAZ-2420 D17), then its bare name — duplicates of either to the SHALLOWEST, equal depth to the first in tree order, case-insensitive, `[[…]]` / `|alias` / `#heading` stripped. Which folders exist is the Files tree's to say (`vaultDirs`, off the one tree feed of the note's own vault — links never leave it, YAZ-2602 R1), so empty folders count and the vault ROOT is not linkable. A folder has no index record: what its link resolves to is the DIRECTORY path — a folder tab's identity — so a click opens the folder tab, ⌘-click a background one, and the backlinks pass compares it like any path ("Linked mentions" on a folder's page lists the notes and the folders that link to it; a folder's settings are a mention source, Editor rule 25). `[[` completion offers folders (`folderLinkCandidates`) after the note rows, each reading `<title> (folder)` — display text only, never typed or written. A folder whose `.folder.md` holds an id is inserted by that ID, under its title (YAZ-2420 D17) — its root-relative path when another folder takes the title — so a note of the same name is simply a second row. A folder with no id is inserted by that TITLE — or by root-relative path when the title belongs to something else — and gets no row when neither spelling reaches it. The picker never writes a `.folder.md`. A link to a folder READS as the folder's title in view cells and in the properties panel (`pageResolver`, over `FolderHost.resolveLink` in a view), and sorts and groups under that name. Renaming a folder rewrites the links to it (Rename, above). A link column's `target: "[[Folder]]"` narrows its picker to what that folder shows — the notes that live in it and its shortcuts (`belongsToBasenames`, 🔒 Q2 of YAZ-815): resolved like a click, so a note of that name wins and narrows nothing; when the target is no folder, or the folder holds none, the picker offers ALL notes (report-don't-block: it narrows when it can and never goes empty). Candidates are offered by title (YAZ-2420 D17) and written by `id` (YAZ-2293). Tests: `links/folderLinks.test.ts`, `links/renameLinks.test.ts`, `views/FolderView.page.test.tsx`.
- The in-app `#/abs/path.md` hash (Editor rule 17) is separate and unchanged.

**YAZ-1289 rename amendment (supersedes the tombstone's final `api.tree` sentence):** the removed base-embed tree argument stays dead, and semantic Markdown targets still resolve only through index records. For a text/PDF/image file rename, App reuses a ready catalog only when it proves that exact target; a directory rename always obtains one fresh lightweight `api.tree(root)` snapshot so newly arrived descendants cannot be missed. A required snapshot failure stops before confirmation or mutation, the accepted root/generation is checked after the await, and the same pre-rename catalog is pinned through confirmation into count/rewrite. Switching roots cancels an old request silently and clears any open rename sheet. Explicit-extension links resolve through that catalog, while the referencing and written files remain Markdown records only. Post-move catalog resolution decides whether a bare duplicate spelling can remain bare or must escalate to a root-relative path. View-only target files are never read or written by link repair.

## Two kinds of vault (YAZ-2523 — decisions V1-V13, LOCKED)

What the app may write into a folder it opens, and what it offers there. Read this before changing either: every rule in the other sections about ids, titles, built names, a folder's `.folder.md` at birth, shortcuts and per-folder values holds in a vault that uses IDs, and only there.

**The answer** (🔒 V1, V5, V10): a vault is one of two kinds by its OWN recorded answer, `<root>/.yaseendocs/ids.json` — `{ "enabled": true | false, "letters": "YAZ", "was": ["OLD"] }` (`IDS_FILE`, `idsAnswer`, `idLettersOf`, `shared/noteId.ts`; `letters` and `was` are the vault's ID letters, YAZ-2677 R9 — "Note ids": The letters — and every write of the file keeps each key it does not change, R10). Yes is an **ID vault**: everything this document describes. No, or NOT ANSWERED — the file missing, unreadable, not JSON, or its `enabled` not a boolean — is a **plain vault**: the app is a viewer and editor of the files as they are, and writes nothing the user did not ask for. There is no third kind. The file is ordinary vault config (bridge table, `vaultConfig`), so it syncs with the vault. 🔒 That `.yaseendocs/` EXISTS means nothing: a favorite, a review setting or the sync switch never turns IDs on, and neither does a note or a folder made in the app. TOMBSTONE (YAZ-2293's gate): the dotfolder's existence, or the first create from a window rooted there, used to start the id sweep; neither does now.

**ONE question, ONE source per process** (🔒 V5): "does this vault use IDs?" No feature works the answer out for itself — not from `.yaseendocs/`, not from a note that holds an `id`, not from a file's name. MAIN: `vaultIds(root).answer` (`vaultIndex/mint.ts`) reads the file off the disk each time it is asked — no cache and no watcher, so the command line shares it — and `givesIds(root)` (`vaultIndex/idSweep.ts`) is that answer `=== true` (TOMBSTONE: `idsOf`, which stood between the two, is gone); the fs handlers ask through `doorFor(e, req)` (`ipc/fs.ts`): a vault of the calling window holds the path (`rootsOfSender` → `rootOfPath`, the most specific one — YAZ-2602 S78: a window may show several vaults, of both kinds), and THAT vault said yes — the answer is then that vault's door (`mint.ts` `doorOf(root)`, "Note ids": The door), and else null. `vaultIds(root)` also reads the vault's letters. THE WINDOW: `IndexResponse.ids`, which `useIndex` → `WikilinkIndexBridge` put on the vault's own `WikilinkResolveSource` as `source.ids` (ONE source per vault of the window, in its scope — "Multi-window": Several vaults in one window) — false until the first index lands, and forgotten (`source.update(null)`) the moment the vault leaves its slot — and hand to the vault's scope through `onSnapshot`. Every surface reads `source.ids`, or an `ids` argument its caller read there (`reservedKeys(ids)`, `folderSettings(record, ids)`, `createNote(dir, title, ids, …)`, `UpdateLinksOptions.ids`). A gesture whose outcome depends on the kind — a create, a rename — refuses while no index has landed (`source.resolve === null`).

**What the index hands out** (🔒 V12 — `vaultIndex/live.ts`): the live record map holds what is in the files, whatever the answer; the kind is applied in `getIndex`, as each response is built. An ID vault: the records as scanned — each `id` read as an ID of THIS vault ("Note ids": Where a note gets it) — with `ids: true`, `letters`, the vault's ID letters (the current ones first, then each of `was`), and `unfinished: true` while the plan file of a backfill that stopped is in the vault (`planLeft` — "Note ids": Give old IDs numbers). A plain vault: each record through `plain` — NO `id`, and its `title` its file name (`scan.ts` `fileTitle`; a `.folder.md`'s is its folder's name), `id` and `title` still among its `properties` — and `ids: false`. While the answer is NOT YES — no answer, or a no — the response also carries `ask: { notes, folders, foreign, letters? }` (YAZ-2677 🔒 D2, S12: the box in Settings shows the counts for a vault that said no too; before, only a vault with no answer carried it), what a yes would write (`wouldWrite`): the notes with no id that can take one, `foreign` of them holding another tool's `id`, and the folders with no `.folder.md` or no id in the one they have; `letters` is the ID letters the vault's `ids.json` already holds, absent when it holds none (S9). So a change of answer needs no rescan and no `CACHE_VERSION` bump: `useIndex` refetches at once on `vaultConfig:changed` for `ids.json`, and the same notes go out as the other kind.

**The per-write gate** (🔒 V1, V4): the sweep asks `givesIds(root)` before EVERY write, not once per pass ("Note ids": The sweep), and `restoreFolderId` asks too — so nothing is written in a plain vault, and a no that lands while a pass is running stops it at the next file. The same gate stands before the clash fix (`clash.ts` `settleClash`, its `writes.gives`: no number taken, no link changed) and before EACH file of "Change letters" and of the backfill (`reletter.ts` `rewriteFiles`): a no stops the pass (`Pass.stopped`), the backfill's plan file stays, and the next run after a yes finishes it. A yes that `getIndex` meets on an index built before it starts the pass over what is indexed (`sweepIndexed`). A no removes nothing: ids, `title:` lines, built names and `.folder.md` files stay as they are (V13).

**The quiet yes** (🔒 V11): a vault that already uses IDs carries over with no question. At the index build, a vault with no answer is saved as yes — `ids.json` is the only file written, through `changeIds`, every key it already holds kept (YAZ-2677 R10) — exactly when some note holds an id AND a yes would write nothing at all (`ask.notes === 0 && ask.folders === 0`): one folder without its `.folder.md` is enough to leave the vault plain instead (S3). A save that fails leaves the vault unanswered, an `ids.json` that is not valid JSON is not written over, and an answer that arrived meanwhile stands.

**No box when a vault opens** (YAZ-2677 🔒 D1, S1 to S4): a vault with no answer, or with a no, opens as plain files. The app asks nothing and writes nothing, in a window with one vault or with several; IDs are a setting. TOMBSTONE (YAZ-2523 V2): `components/ConfirmIds.tsx`, a sheet App rendered whenever a vault's snapshot carried `ask` — **Give IDs** / **Not for this vault**, Esc closing it for that window only (`idsAsk`, `closeIdsAsk`, `idsAskClosed` in `useVaultScope.ts`). All of it is gone; its words moved to the box below, and `ask` now only feeds that box.

**The box** (YAZ-2677 🔒 D2, S5 to S13 — `settings/registry.tsx` `GiveIdsSheet`, on the one typed-confirm piece `TypedConfirmSheet` of `settings/IdLettersControl.tsx`, which "Change letters" and "Give them numbers" use too — "Note ids"): a click on **On** in Settings opens it, and NOTHING is written before it is confirmed. Its text is `idsAskMessage(ask, vault)` (`settings/idsAskMessage.ts`): what an ID is (`like BUS-12`), what a yes would write, counted from the snapshot's `ask` — `write an ID into N notes`, `add a hidden settings file to N folders`, always `name the file of each note you make or retitle`, and how many notes hold an ID from another tool, which the app replaces — and how to undo it (`To undo, turn it off. The IDs stay in the files and the app stops using them.`). With two or more vaults in the window the question NAMES its vault (S13, YAZ-2602 S40: "Give the notes in <vault> IDs?"; with one, "this vault"). A yes that would write nothing still opens it: it sets the letters (S10). Under the text is ONE text field, which holds the focus, and the line above it (`idsLettersAsk`): a vault with no saved letters CHOOSES them — `Type the ID letters for this vault: 2 to 5 letters, like BUS.` (S5) — and a vault that has them types exactly those, in any case — `Type this vault's ID letters, YAZ, to confirm.` (S9). The saved letters come with the index, as `ask.letters` (main reads them — `vaultIds`; letters that are not valid count as none); the renderer does not read `ids.json` (TOMBSTONE: `readLetters` in `useVaultScope.ts` did, at the click on On). A file that is not valid JSON holds none, and the save then refuses (`INVALID_CONFIG`, said in the notice). **Give IDs** and Enter do NOTHING until what is typed is valid (`ConfirmSheet`'s `confirmDisabled`; `isIdLetters`, `shared/noteId.ts`: 2 to 5 letters A to Z in any case, nothing trimmed — an empty field, one letter, six, a digit or a space is not valid, S6). Confirmed, the typed letters go out in capitals: `ids.set(root, true, letters)` (bridge table) saves `enabled: true` and `letters`, and this Mac gives the numbers at once (S7, R32). Cancel, Esc or a click outside closes the box with nothing written, and the switch stays Off (S8); the keys stay inside the sheet, so the dialog under it does not close. A device that opens the vault before the answer has synced is a plain vault until `ids.json` arrives, and then waits before it sweeps ("Note ids": Which Mac gives a number, S65).

**The switch** (🔒 V4, V13, YAZ-2677 D2 — `settings/registry.tsx` `IdsControl`): Settings › Files & Links › This vault › "Give this vault's notes IDs", present only with a vault open whose index has loaded (`SettingsCtx.ids`). It shows the snapshot's `ids`: a vault that said no and one that has not answered both read Off (the renderer cannot tell them apart, and need not). Only a CHANGE acts: a click on the side the row shows is nothing — so a click on Off in a vault with no answer writes nothing (before YAZ-2677 it saved the no, so that the box at the opening did not come back). On: the box above. Off where a note holds an id (`held`) asks first, on a `ConfirmSheet` whose keys stay inside it — `This vault's notes will show their file names, and links stored as IDs will not open, until you turn this back on. Nothing is removed.`, Cancel / **Turn off** (S11) — and anywhere else saves at once. The save is `ids.set` in MAIN (`useVaultScope.ts` `saveIds` only calls it; a refusal is said in the notice): the read and the write of `ids.json` are one step there (`changeIds`), so Off keeps `letters` and `was` (R12) and an `ids.json` that is not valid JSON is never written over. While the vault uses IDs three more rows stand under the switch — "Duplicate IDs" (`duplicates`), "ID letters" (`idLetters`) and, while the snapshot holds an old ID or says `unfinished`, "Old IDs" (`oldIds`): "Note ids".

**Create, rename and copy in a plain vault** (🔒 V3) are what Finder would do. MAIN: `createFile(req, ids)` writes the content it was given and nothing else — none is zero bytes — and answers no `id`; `createDir(req, ids)` makes the directory and no `.folder.md`; `copyEntry(from, toDir, ids)` is `fs.cp` under Finder's next free name for EVERY entry, a folder whole (`freeName(dir, name, kind)`: a folder's name is not split at a dot). A request shaped for an ID vault — a `createFile` `id`, a `createDir` `title` — and every `fs:retitle` is refused `BAD_REQUEST` `this vault does not use IDs`, nothing made or written: it comes from a window one answer behind. CLIENT: what is typed is the NAME on disk (`sidebar/createEntry.ts` `plainEntryName`: as typed, held to `validateEntryName`, a note given `.md` unless a Markdown suffix was typed). `createNote` writes the folder's template as it is — or, with a seed, the seed's keys as the note's own properties — and no `title` or `id`; "New" in a folder's view is `Untitled`, then `Untitled 2`, …; a note made from a link is `<typed>.md`, each segment of a pathed target a name on disk, and the `[[` picker's Create row leaves `[[typed text]]`. Every title surface — the page title, the sidebar's Rename, a table's Name cell — still reaches App's `requestRetitle`, which there builds the path and goes through the one door as a rename of the NAME: `file.rename`, the same confirm, and links rewritten by name (`UpdateLinksOptions.ids` false: a `title:` line names nothing, so no link travels by one).

**Not offered in a plain vault** (🔒 V5, V7, V12). Gated on `ids`: "Add note shortcut" (`MenuTargets.shortcutDir`), the ID rows of the link menu and its Copy ID (`wikilinkMenu.ts` `idOf`), per-folder properties (the panel's "Properties from" and its folder rows) and "Delete column…". The rest falls out of the index handing out no ids, with no gate of its own: no shortcut rows, nothing found by id in ⌘K, the `[[` picker and the link cells insert names, and no block of `in` is ever stale, so a move asks nothing and drops nothing. A click on an unresolved link shaped like an id says `This vault does not use IDs, so this link cannot be opened` and creates nothing. 🔒 The keys that stay the app's are `reservedKeys(false)`: `comments` and `reviews`. `id`, `title`, `also_in` and `in` are ordinary properties there — rows with editors in the panel (`in` a map, so the YAML chip), columns in a table. Favorites, review, GitHub sync, comments, backlinks and Copy path work in both kinds.

**A folder's page in a plain vault** (🔒 V6, V11): the same `FolderView`, asking once (`ids = source.ids`). Its rows carry the notes' OWN properties — no block of `in` is read — so a view with no saved order shows Name and every key the notes hold (`propertyKeys`), and a value written — a cell, a board drop, a "New" seed — is that one top-level key of that note (`writeProperties`); no folder id is asked for or made. The defaults (`folderSettings(undefined, false)`) are a Table alone and no column: no Board, no `status`. Opening writes nothing; the first SETTINGS change — a view, a column declared or hidden — creates `.folder.md` holding `folder_settings` and nothing else, no `id` and no `title`. The host has no `deleteColumn` (`FolderHost.deleteColumn?`), so neither menu offers "Delete column…": a column is hidden instead.

**The command line** (🔒 V10 — `cli.ts` `idVault`): "no" means no for agents too. For `id` and `links` the vault is the nearest folder at or above the page that has ANSWERED — a folder that only holds app settings is passed over — and only a yes counts. A no, or no answer anywhere above, refuses with exit 1 and nothing written: `id`, even for a page that holds one, with `<page>'s vault does not give its notes IDs (turn on "Give this vault's notes IDs" in the app's Settings)`; `links` with `<page>'s vault does not use IDs, so there are no ID links to list`. The comment verbs and `due` work in both kinds — `HELP` says so — and `vaults` (YAZ-2556) asks no vault anything: it reads the app's state file alone ("Multi-window": The vault list).

**NOT built** (🔒 V7, V8): REMOVING IDs from a vault that has them — Off stops future writes and removes nothing; a vault that ever needs it is done once, by an agent from written steps. And per-folder properties keyed by FOLDER NAME: in a plain vault a property is the note's own frontmatter, and a folder's own values are what an ID vault gives.

**Testing**: `desktop/src/main/vaultIndex/liveIds.test.ts` (the gate, the quiet yes, `ask`, the two hand-outs), `idSweep.test.ts`, `desktop/src/main/ipc/fs.test.ts` (`doorFor`, the refusals, `ids:set`), `desktop/src/main/fs/create.test.ts` / `copy.test.ts`, `desktop/src/cli/cli.test.ts`; in the client `App.test.tsx` (no box when a vault opens, the switch, a typed name), `components/ConfirmSheet.test.tsx` (`confirmDisabled`), `settings/SettingsDialog.test.tsx` (the box and its typed letters) / `idsAskMessage.test.ts` (its words), `views/useIndex.test.tsx`, `editor/wikilink/WikilinkIndexBridge.test.tsx`, `sidebar/Sidebar.test.tsx`, `sidebar/createEntry.test.ts`, `views/scaffold.test.ts`, `views/FolderView.test.tsx`, `views/folderSettings.test.ts`, `editor/FrontmatterPanel.test.tsx`, `links/reservedKeys.test.ts` / `renameLinks.test.ts` / `shortcuts.test.ts`. Hand steps: `docs/REGRESSION.md`, "Two kinds of vault"; the flow end to end is `desktop/e2e/ids.spec.ts`.

Files: `shared/noteId.ts` (`IDS_FILE`, `idsAnswer`, `isIdLetters`), `shared/types.ts` (`IndexResponse.ids`, `letters`, `ask`, `unfinished`), `desktop/src/main/vaultIndex/mint.ts` (`vaultIds`, `changeIds`, `doorOf`) + `idSweep.ts` (`givesIds`) + `live.ts` (`getIndex`, `plain`, `wouldWrite`, `sweepIndexed`, `saveIdsAnswer`) + `scan.ts` (`fileTitle`), `desktop/src/main/ipc/fs.ts` (`rootsOfSender`, `doorFor`), `desktop/src/main/fs/create.ts` + `copy.ts`, `desktop/src/cli/cli.ts` (`idVault`, `HELP`), `client/src/views/useIndex.ts`, `client/src/editor/wikilink/wikilinkPlugin.ts` + `WikilinkIndexBridge.tsx`, `client/src/vault/useVaultScope.ts` (`ids`: `saveIds` — per vault since YAZ-2602), `client/src/App.tsx` (`requestRetitle`), `client/src/components/ConfirmSheet.tsx`, `client/src/settings/registry.tsx` (`IdsControl`, `GiveIdsSheet`, `SettingsCtx.ids`) + `IdLettersControl.tsx` (`TypedConfirmSheet`) + `idsAskMessage.ts`, `client/src/sidebar/createEntry.ts` (`plainEntryName`), `client/src/views/scaffold.ts`, `client/src/links/reservedKeys.ts` + `renameLinks.ts`, `client/src/views/FolderView.tsx` + `folderSettings.ts` + `engine.ts` (`propertyKeys`).

## Note ids (YAZ-2293 — decisions D1-D8)

This whole section describes a vault that uses IDs ("Two kinds of vault"): in any other the app writes no id, and the index hands none out.

- **The id** (🔒 YAZ-2677 D3, `shared/noteId.ts`): every Markdown note carries a permanent identity in its frontmatter — `id: YAZ-12`, the key spelled `NOTE_ID_KEY`. It is given once and never derived from the file's name or place, so a rename or a move by ANYTHING — the app, Finder, a sync tool, an agent — keeps every `[[<id>]]` link pointing at the note. **Two shapes** (`isNoteId`). The NUMBER ID (R1, `isNumberId`): the vault's ID letters, a hyphen and a number — `^[A-Z]{2,5}-[1-9]\d*$`, no leading zero (`YAZ-012` and `YAZ-0` are no ID, S24), 15 digits at most (every such number is one JavaScript counts exactly). The NUMBER is the real ID: the next one of the vault, given by the door below. It is READ in any case and WRITTEN and indexed with capital letters (R2, `canonicalNoteId`): `[[yaz-12]]` opens `YAZ-12` (S17), and `id: yaz-12` written by hand is held as `YAZ-12` with the file NOT rewritten for the case alone (S18). The OLD ID (YAZ-2293 D2): exactly 12 characters of lowercase Crockford base32 (`0123456789abcdefghjkmnpqrstvwxyz` — no `i l o u`) with ALWAYS at least one digit. 🔒 An old ID is still read everywhere — links, `also_in`, a folder's values, search — and is NEVER written again and never written over (R3, the seat belt: `liveIds.test.ts`, "a vault that has only old IDs behaves as it did before number IDs"). It has no letters and no number, so it never counts for the next number (S20). **An ID of THIS vault** (R5, `vaultNoteId(value, letters)`): an old ID, or a number ID whose letters are the vault's — or letters the vault had BEFORE (`was`), which read as the same number with the current letters, because a number is used one time in a vault whatever the letters (R4). Any other `LETTERS-NUMBER` text is not an ID here: as a link it is a NAME (`[[GPT-4]]`, `[[BUS-12]]` — R6, S21, S22), and as a frontmatter `id` it is another tool's, as an `id` of any other shape is — never an id to the index, the resolver or any menu, and the app writes its own over it (R7, S23; YAZ-2420 D30, The sweep below): every note in a vault holds an id of that vault. The frontmatter `id` is the truth; the id at the end of a file name the app built (`<kebab-title>-<id>.md`, in LOWERCASE as the whole name is — `my-note-yaz-12.md`, R8, `shared/noteName.ts`) is a copy of it, written when the name is built, so every other tool sees it too (YAZ-2420 D1, D4). TOMBSTONE (YAZ-2677): `mintNoteId()`, a random 12-character id, and `noteIdFrom(draw)`, one built from any byte source, stood in `shared/noteId.ts`; nothing in `shared/` or the renderer makes an id now.
- **The letters** (R9 to R12, `idLettersOf`, `defaultIdLetters`; read off the disk by `mint.ts` `vaultIds(root)`): a vault's ID letters are `letters` in its `ids.json` (2 to 5 letters A to Z, read in any case), and `was` lists the letters it had before. A vault that said yes and holds no valid `letters` uses a DEFAULT — the first three letters A to Z of its folder's name in capitals, `DOC` when the name has fewer than two (R11) — and the door saves that default in the file when it gives the first number (`saveDefaultLetters`, through `changeIds`), every other key kept (R10).
