The letters reach the renderer as `IndexResponse.letters` (the current ones first, then each of `was`; only when `ids`), and from there the window's link source (`WikilinkResolveSource.letters`), the link resolver (`ResolverOptions.letters`) and the search candidates (`SearchCandidate.was`).
- **The door** (🔒 YAZ-2677 D4, R13 to R21 — `desktop/src/main/vaultIndex/mint.ts` `mintIds(root, count, floor?)`): THE ONE place that makes an id; plain Node, no Electron and no watcher, because the `yaseendocs` command uses it too. The next number is 1 plus the highest of (a) each number ID of this vault among its notes and folders and (b) `last` of each Mac's count file (R16) — so a number a deleted note had is never given again (S28, S29), a number written by hand is the new floor (S37), and a new vault starts at 1 (S15). **One count file for each Mac** (R13 to R15): `<root>/.yaseendocs/ids/<mac id>.json` — `{ "name", "since", "last", "made" }`: `name` the host name (for people; nothing reads it), `since` when the file was made (ISO time), `last` the highest number this Mac gave, `made` each number it gave in the last 30 days as RUNS `{ "from", "to", "at" }`, oldest first, one run on a line (a new note is a run of one; a sweep of many notes is ONE run, so the file stays small after a large sweep). Only the Mac that owns a file writes it, atomically (`atomicWrite`), so two Macs that sync a vault never change one file. `made` drops a run older than `MADE_DAYS` (30, R21) and keeps `MADE_MAX` (5,000) runs at most. The MAC ID is `{ "id": <12 random characters> }` in `mac.json` in the app's user-data folder — made one time with `createDurable` (an exclusive create, so a crash leaves no cut file), never the host name (`macId`; main hands the folder in with `initMint(app.getPath('userData'))`, the command finds the same one by `userDataDir`, so both use ONE count file: R20). **One request at a time for a vault** (R17): a queue per root. Each request lists the count folder and `stat`s each file (64 at most), reading again only one whose size or time changed; asks for the vault's highest number — from the live index's records in memory (`highestFrom`, registered by `live.ts`; the sweep hands in its own records as `floor`; with no index, the command, the vault is walked and scanned as `links` does); checks that its own count file did not change under it (the app and the command are two processes of one Mac) and starts again if it did; saves the default letters where the file holds none — a no found at that moment gives NO number and writes nothing more, and other letters saved meanwhile count the number again; writes its count file; and only THEN answers (R18) — a crash, or a create that then fails, leaves a gap and never a number given two times (S30, S31). All the ids of one call are saved with ONE write (R19). A count file that is missing or not valid JSON reads as empty, and this Mac's is written good again (S38, S39); another Mac's is never written. `null`, and nothing written, where the vault does not use IDs. Cost, measured by `mint.test.ts`: about 6 ms a number, almost all of it the one fsynced write. The count files are hidden (`.yaseendocs/`), so the index and the tree never hold them, and the config watcher reports only files DIRECTLY in `.yaseendocs/`, so a new number wakes no window (`vaultConfig.test.ts`). Every id the app writes comes from here: `createFile` / `createDir` and a copy (`fs/copy.ts` — one request for a whole copied folder, S34, S53) take an `IdDoor` (`doorOf(root)`) from `ipc/fs.ts`, the sweep and a title edit call `mintIds` / `nextId`, and the renderer asks through `mintNoteId` (bridge table). Two Macs CAN give one number before they sync: **Two notes with one ID** below settles that. The same module answers what that rule and the next one ask of the count files — `countsOf(root)` (each Mac's count by its Mac ID and which is this Mac's, in the door's turn and from what the door already holds: a `stat` for each count file, a read only for one that changed), `firstMac(files)` (R33) and `makersOf(files, number, now)` (R22, R23). A count file holding `last: 0` is read as a Mac that gave no number yet; the door never writes one. The app and the `yaseendocs` command are two processes of one Mac with no lock between them: two numbers taken in the same millisecond can be one number, and the two notes are then a COPY by R22 (one Mac holds the number in `made`) — the keeper rule gives one of them its next number, on one Mac, with no link changed.
- **Where a note gets it**: BORN with it — every creation goes through `createFile`, which sets it in the creating write (bridge table) — or, for a note that ARRIVED without one, given it by the sweep below; either way it is the door's next number. The index carries it as `IndexRecord.id` ("Property index"), and that field is what the whole renderer reads: no surface parses a file to learn an id. 🔒 `scan.ts` puts the id in the record as the FILE holds it, in capitals (R2); WHOSE id it is is said where the index is handed out (`live.ts` `getIndex`, which reads `ids.json` once a call, as it always did for the vault's kind — YAZ-2523 V5) and where it is swept: a number ID with letters of before goes out with the current letters, one with any other letters goes out as none (`owned`). The letters can change after a record was scanned and cached, so a record never holds a reading of them (`CACHE_VERSION` 8).
- **The sweep** (D3, D4, D13 — `desktop/src/main/vaultIndex/idSweep.ts` `sweepIds(root, records, among, knew, dirs, opts)`): a note the app did not create arrives with no id, or with another tool's, and a note copied OUTSIDE the app arrives carrying its original's (a copy made in the app is born with its own — `fs/copy.ts`, YAZ-2420 D21). The sweep runs in main on the live index (`live.ts`): after EACH watch-event scan (`add` / `change`), over that one record, and once after the cold-start reconcile, over every record — NOT awaited, so a vault of id-less notes never holds up its first index. Each note in its batch that has NO id is given one, and an `id` that is not an ID of this vault is none — another tool's, a number with a leading zero, a number ID with another vault's letters (YAZ-2677 R7, S23, S24): the app's is written over it and the old value is not kept (YAZ-2420 D30). An OLD id is an id like any other here: kept, never written over (R3). 🔒 **Every folder holds its id** (D13): each of `dirs` whose `.folder.md` the index does not hold is given one holding only its `id` — at the cold start every folder the index walk went into (`scan.ts` `walk`'s `dirs`: what the tree shows, so no dot-folder, no `node_modules`, nothing inside one, and never the vault root), on a watch `addDir` that one folder, and for a vault that says yes after its index was built, a fresh walk (`sweepIndexed`). An empty folder and one holding only images get it too. A `.folder.md` deleted while the app runs, from a folder that is still there, is created again holding the id it had (`restoreFolderId`, on the watch `unlink`). Of the indexed notes SHARING an id — a COPY; two Macs that each gave one number are a clash, settled by **Two notes with one ID** below — only the KEEPER keeps it — the note the index already knew to hold it (at cold start, per the persisted cache; on a live event, every other indexed note is known to hold what it holds and the scanned one what it held before the event), else the first in path order, which is the same answer on every device — and any other note in the batch is given a fresh one. So a copy gets its own id, and every link to the original stays the original's. A `.folder.md` given a fresh id in place of a shared one is a COPIED folder's, whose notes still hold their values (D19) under the original's id: `carryFolderValues(dir, from, to)` walks that folder itself (the index's `walk`, not the index) and, in every note under it at any depth that holds a block of `in` for `from` and none for `to`, names that block `to` (`moveFolderValues`). Each re-IDed folder carries its own; the original, its notes and a MOVED folder (same id) are never written; a note that will not parse is left, and one that changed under the write is read again, once; a second run writes nothing. The folder takes its new id LAST, after its notes hold their values under it (`giveId`'s `first`): a carry cut short by a quit leaves the folder still holding the original's id, so the next sweep finds it again, gives it the next number and carries what still holds the original's (the number of the pass that was cut is a gap). The copy is remembered while the app runs (`carried`): a long copy is still arriving when its folder is given its id, so the sweep carries each copied note that reaches that folder afterwards. The app's own folder copy calls `carryFolderValues` too, once the folder it made holds its fresh id (YAZ-2420 D21): its notes were written holding their values under the original's. The sweep's writes run one at a time (`inTurn`), so a copied note's own id and the values carried to it never lose a compare-and-set to each other. The sweep never removes a block. 🔒 **Only in a vault that said YES** — its `.yaseendocs/ids.json` holds `{ "enabled": true }` (`givesIds`, YAZ-2523 V1 — "Two kinds of vault"): the app never writes behind the user's back into a folder it has merely been pointed at (the standing rule of YAZ-797), and that `.yaseendocs/` exists means nothing. The sweep is started by every index event all the same and asks `givesIds(root)` before EACH write, so a no stops a pass that is running; a yes that arrives after the index was built is met by the next `getIndex`, whose `sweepIndexed(root)` (`live.ts`) gives ids to the notes already indexed and to the folders there. In any other vault the sweep touches no file, a note that arrived without an id stays without one, and it is linked by name; a folder there has no `.folder.md` until something changes it, and reads as the defaults. **The id is the vault's next NUMBER, from the door** (YAZ-2677 D4): one pass takes ALL its numbers with one write of the count file (R19) before it writes any note (R18), and its floor is the highest number among the records it was handed. Only what can take an id is counted — a note the index could read (no number for one whose YAML is invalid or that is over the size limit, pass after pass), and a `.folder.md` the index has not seen is read first, so a folder that arrives WITH its file costs none. A note that changes between the count and the write loses its number: a gap. The number is higher than every number in the vault, so it is never an id some indexed note holds (YAZ-2378). TOMBSTONE (YAZ-2293): the id was DERIVED — `noteIdFrom` over the sha256 of the note's place and bytes — so that two devices meeting one note before syncing made the same edit; with numbers they would not, and which Mac gives the number is YAZ-2677 D8's rule (**Which Mac gives a number**, below). **Compare-and-set**: `giveId(file, held, letters, fresh, first?)` re-reads the file, goes on only while its frontmatter `id` — read as an ID of this vault (`letters`, R5) — still IS what the index saw (none — another tool's reads as none, D30, R7 — or the shared one), asks `fresh` for the number only then, sets that one key through `setFrontmatterProperty` — every other byte kept — and writes with `expectedMtime`, so a note that changed under the sweep is left for its next index event. Left ALONE, silently: a properties block that does not parse and an oversize file. It never throws and is safe to run any number of times: its own write comes back as a watch `change`, rescans the note, and the second look needs nothing. A folder's settings file (`.folder.md`) sits in the same record map and is given an id like any note. The ONE file it creates is a missing `.folder.md` (D13): `giveId` reads it as empty and creates it exclusively (`createDurable`), holding only its id, so one that appears before the write stays as it is; a folder gone by then is passed over. A folder renamed or moved keeps its file and its id.
- **One sweep at a time, and one number for a file** (YAZ-2677, a finding on YAZ-2681): every index event starts a sweep, and a file that just arrived is often in two of them — the first index and its own `add`, an `add` and a `change`, a folder's `addDir`. `sweepIds` therefore runs ONE pass at a time for a vault (each waits for the one before it and then reads what the index holds for its paths NOW), an index event that arrives while a pass of the index waits its turn JOINS that pass — so a sync that brings many files is few passes, each with one write of the count file, and what a pass did is reported one time, to the event that started it; a pass the user asked for is never joined — and a pass reads the BYTES of each file it means to number before it asks the door (`needs`, 16 files at a time): a file that already holds an ID is not counted. All the numbers of a pass are still taken with one write (R19). A file a pass could not write is remembered with its mtime while the app runs (`refused`, 1,000 entries), so the next pass takes no number for it until it changes. Still a gap by design (S30): a file another writer changes between the count and the write. `sweepIds(root, records, among, knew, dirs, opts)` resolves to a `SweepResult` — `fixes`, `theirs`, `copies`, `later`, `kept` — and never throws.
- **Two notes with one ID** (🔒 YAZ-2677 D7, R22 to R30a — `desktop/src/main/vaultIndex/clash.ts`, called by the sweep for each ID that two or more notes ON DISK hold; two paths of one file are one note, by the inode). **Clash or copy** (R22): a CLASH when the count files of two or more Macs hold the number in `made`, in a run not older than 30 days (`makersOf`); any other pair is a COPY — a Finder duplicate, two notes with one old ID, a `made` that expired (S49). The count files are read only then, never for each index event. **A clash has ONE writer** (R23, R24): the note of the Mac that gave the number first keeps the ID (equal times: the Mac ID that is first in order, S50); each OTHER Mac that gave it fixes ITS OWN note, and a Mac that did not give the number writes nothing. **Its own note** (R25, `myNote`) is the one this Mac's index held with the ID before the other arrived (`knew`); it is said ONCE, at the first sight of the pair, and saved in the diary, because the index holds both notes from then on. A Mac that cannot tell — its index cache is lost — falls to R29: the first note in path order keeps the ID, the Mac of the newer time gives each other note the next number, no link is changed, and the notice says so (S48). **The fix** (R26, R28, `settleClash`), in this order: (1) the note is read — nothing is taken for one that cannot take its number now; (2) the next number from the door, SAVED IN THE DIARY before the vault changes; (3) each file the diary first saw naming the ID more than `LINK_GRACE_MS` (5 s) before the other note arrived has that ID changed to the new one (`rewriteIds`, a compare-and-set, tried once more on a conflict); (4) the note takes its ID — LAST, and a folder's notes carry their values to it first (`carryFolderValues`, R30a, S54); (5) a note whose file name is the one the app builds from its title and the old ID is renamed to the name of the new ID (`followName`) — the bridge runs the rename handler's downstream for it, so its tab, favorite and stored paths follow; a link written BY FILE NAME or by path to that note (`[[bar-yaz-101]]`) is NOT changed, because no window started this rename and the record names only links by ID for a clash (the app writes links by ID in such a vault, and a link by title still opens the note); (6) the diary marks the fix done, and ONE notice goes to each window of the vault (`windows.ts` `vaultNotice`, the `link:notice` push): `YAZ-101 was used on two Macs. "Bar" is now YAZ-102. 1 link updated. Not changed: "Inbox", "Log".` — the list is each indexed file that still names the old ID (5 names, then `and N more`). 🔒 SAFE TO RUN AGAIN AND TO STOP ANYWHERE: a fix that stops before step 4 leaves the note holding the old ID, so the next sweep finds the pair, finds the saved number and continues — it never takes a second number, and a link already changed names the old ID no more. 🔒 The number STAYS in the fixing Mac's `made`: taken out, the other Mac could read the pair as a copy for a moment (a count file can arrive before a note) and renumber the same note. So while both count files hold the number only that Mac writes for it, and a note that holds the ID later (a Finder copy of the keeper) is a copy that Mac renumbers at once. **A copy** (R30) keeps the keeper rule of YAZ-2293 D4, with one change: the note the index knew FIRST is saved in the diary at the first sight of the pair too, because a number that waits for the vault's first Mac (below) is given ten minutes later, when the index holds both. A copy is silent, as it always was. **While a clash stands** (S46 — the fixing Mac is off, or a write lost): the sweep reports which note keeps the ID (`SweepResult.kept`), and `getIndex` hands that ID out for the keeper only — the other note goes out as a note with no id yet — so `[[YAZ-101]]` opens the keeper on every Mac. A clash is settled only after the index has read every file its watcher already reported (`SweepOptions.indexed`), so the links that arrived in one sync with the second note are in the diary and in the notice's list.
- **The diary** (R21, R25, R27 — `desktop/src/main/vaultIndex/diary.ts`): one JSON file for each vault in THIS Mac's user-data folder, `id-diary/<sha256 of the vault path, 16 hex>.json`, never in the vault. `links`: for each ID this Mac made (in its `made`), each file where its index first saw a link, an embed, an `also_in` entry or a link leaf of a folder's settings name it, with the time. `clashes`: for each ID two notes held, the path of the note this Mac knew first, when the other arrived, the new number once taken, the links changed so far, and `done`. Every index event feeds it IN MEMORY (`see`; a note that names no number ID costs nothing); the file is written 2 s after the first change and once at quit (`flushDiaries`, in the quit sequence beside the index cache), atomically — never one write for each event. Limits: only IDs in this Mac's `made` (so 30 days), 20,000 link entries, a pair seen more than 30 days ago is dropped. A diary that is lost only means that no link is changed and each is listed.
- **Which Mac gives a number** (🔒 YAZ-2677 D8, R31 to R34): a number the SWEEP gives — to a note with no id, to a copy, to a folder's settings file — comes at once only on the vault's FIRST Mac: the one whose count file has the lowest `since`, and of two equal the Mac ID that is first in order (`firstMac`). Every other Mac leaves the file, notes when (`SweepOptions.waits`, held by the live index for each open vault), and gives the number `ID_WAIT_MS` (10 minutes) later if the file still needs one — two Macs must never write two numbers into one file (S60 to S62). A vault with NO count file has no first Mac: every Mac waits there, because a Mac that took "no count file" for "I am first" would number every note the moment a yes arrives by the sync ahead of the first Mac's count file (S65); the Mac that then gives the first number is the first. ONE timer for each open vault (`live.ts` `armWait`, R34), set for the file that waited longest and set again for the next; it sweeps only the files whose wait is over, is cleared when the index entry of the vault is evicted, and an entry with a file waiting is not evicted for idleness. A restart starts the wait again (S66). A number the USER asks for comes at once on that Mac (R32): a new note, a new folder, a copy made in the app, a title edit, "Give IDs" (`ids.set`), "Check for duplicates" (`ids.check`) and `yaseendocs id` — none passes `waits`. A clash fix never waits: the rule already names its one Mac. Known and accepted (S67): the first Mac is on with its sync stuck for more than 10 minutes.
- **The ID rewrite** (🔒 D5, D6, D7 — `shared/linkRewrite.ts` `rewriteIds(content, change, { own? })` → `{ content, changed }`): ONE function changes an ID to a new ID in a file's text, for a clash fix, a change of the vault's letters and the backfill of old IDs. `change` is a map or a function from an ID as the app writes it to its new ID. It changes `[[id]]`, `[[id|label]]`, `[[id#heading]]`, `![[id]]`, a link that is a property's whole value (in a list, in a folder's values, in the link leaves of a folder's settings), an `also_in` entry, a folder-value key (`in.<id>` moves with its values, never over a block the new ID has) and, with `own`, the file's own `id:` line. An ID is matched WHOLE (`YAZ-1` is not in `YAZ-12`) and in any case; code blocks and code spans are left; a file that names no changed ID keeps every byte; a second run changes nothing. The file holds the per-file half of the rename engine too (`maskCode`, `rewriteInner`, `rewriteBodyLinks`, `rewriteNoteLinks`, `WIKILINK_RE`), moved from `client/src/links/renameLinks.ts`, and `shared/folderSettingsLinks.ts` holds the link leaves of a folder's settings (`mapFolderSettingsLinks`, `mapOutlineLinks`), moved from `client/src/views/`: one link parser, never two.
- **Change letters** (🔒 YAZ-2677 D5, S79 to S87 — `desktop/src/main/vaultIndex/live.ts` `changeLetters`, `reletter.ts` `reletter`; Settings › This vault › "ID letters", `client/src/settings/IdLettersControl.tsx`, shown only while the vault uses IDs). The row shows the vault's letters and "Change letters"; the box counts the notes that change and takes the new letters in a text field — bad input, and the letters the vault already has, do nothing (S80, S85). TWO STEPS, in this order (S81): (1) `ids.json` takes `letters: NEW`, and the letters of before go to the front of `was` (`configWithLetters`; NEW leaves `was` when it was there — letters of before may come back, S85); (2) ONE PASS over every Markdown file of the vault as it is on disk, in path order: `rewriteIds(content, (id) => vaultNoteId(id, letters), { own: true })` — each `id:` line, link, `also_in` entry and folder-value key with letters of before takes the letters of now — and then the file's NAME, only where it is the name the app builds from the title and the ID with letters of before (`noteFileName`, the rule of R26). A number never changes; an old 12-character ID has no letters and is not touched (S87); `[[GPT-4]]` stays a name. 🔒 After step 1 every note opens whatever happens next, because the index reads an ID with letters from `was` as an ID of the vault (S82, S83): a change that stopped, or a file that arrived later by the sync, leaves notes that `IdsState.stale` counts, the row then says "N notes still have the old letters", and "Finish" runs the same change again with the letters of now. 🔒 Safe to run any number of times and to stop anywhere: each write is a compare-and-set against the bytes and mtime read (tried one more time when the file changed under it), a file that names no changed ID keeps each byte, and the content is written BEFORE the name — a run that stopped between the two is finished by the next, which finds the new ID under the old name. 🔒 The same change on two Macs writes the same bytes (S84): the pass takes no number and reads no clock. 🔒 The vault is asked before EACH file (`givesIds`): a no stops the pass, and "Finish" after a yes ends it. A vault with no `letters` in its `ids.json` shows its default (R11); a change there saves the chosen letters and keeps the default in `was`, so a note that carries the default follows.
- **Give old IDs numbers** (🔒 YAZ-2677 D6, S88 to S91 — `live.ts` `giveOldIdsNumbers`, `reletter.ts` `backfill`; Settings › This vault › "Old IDs", shown only while the vault uses IDs AND either its index snapshot holds a note or folder with an old 12-character ID, which the renderer counts itself — `useVaultScope.ts` `ids.old` — or the plan file below is still in the vault, an unfinished backfill — `IndexResponse.unfinished`, `ids.unfinished` — so a second run can finish it). The box says the count, tells the user to sync the vault and close the app on the other Macs first (S91), and takes the vault's own letters as the typed confirm. Each note and each folder's settings file with an old ID takes the vault's next number: oldest file first (`IndexRecord.ctime`, the creation time), then the path, starting after the highest number in use, ALL with one write of this Mac's count file (R19). 🔒 THE PLAN: the map from each old ID to its number ID is saved in the vault, `.yaseendocs/ids-backfill.json` (`BACKFILL_FILE`), BEFORE any note is written. A run that stopped is finished by the next with the SAME numbers — a note in the plan takes the plan's number, only a note that is not in it is given a new one (after each number of the plan) — on this Mac or another. The plan is deleted when a run ends with no file left and was not stopped. 🔒 The vault is asked before EACH file (`givesIds`): a no stops the run, the plan stays, and a run after a yes finishes with the same numbers. 🔒 THE ORDER: part A writes each old note's own `id:` line, oldest first, and its built file name; part B is the same pass as "Change letters" over every Markdown file with the plan as the map — each link, `also_in` entry and folder-value key. A link changes only after its note holds the new ID, so an old ID that remains after a stop still works: its note holds it and no link to it was changed (S90). Compare-and-set writes and the rename downstream as above. A file of part B that cannot be written (two tries) keeps its old links and the plan stays: the row stays too, also when no note holds an old ID any more, and says to run it again (TOMBSTONE: the row used to go then). Never run by the app on its own, and the code that reads old IDs stays: a file with an old ID can still arrive by the sync.
- **Links by id**: resolution tries the id first ("Link resolution"); the app writes `[[<id>]]` from every `[[` picker row and its Create row (Editor rule 24) and from the views' link editors ("Cell editing"); a rename never counts or rewrites one ("Links": Rename). Still written BY NAME: a link to a note that has no id, a hand-typed link, and a link to a FOLDER that has no id — the `[[` picker inserts a folder's id when it has one, else its title or path (YAZ-2290 D10, "Links": Links to folders). A hand-typed `[[Name]]` resolves by title before file name (YAZ-2420 D17, "Link resolution").
- **Search by number** (🔒 YAZ-2677 D9, S69 to S78 — `shared/noteId.ts` `holdsId`, `client/src/search/searchCandidates.ts` `searchRows`): the search box finds a note by its number. `12`, `YAZ-12`, `yaz-12`, `yaz12` and `yaz 12` all find `YAZ-12`, as the FIRST row, with the title matches for the same text after it; a bare number is the whole text of the box (`meeting 2024` is a title search) and finds that number in each vault of the window, each row showing its full ID; an ID matches whole (`12` is never `YAZ-1` or `YAZ-120`); letters the vault had before find the note too (`OLD-12`), and so does an old 12-character ID, a pasted `[[YAZ-12]]`, a file name or a whole path. The hyphen is optional in the search box ONLY: on disk an ID is always `YAZ-12`. The rule in full, its cost and the row are in "Repo layout", at `sidebar/` (the search).
- **What a link reads as** (D8 — the file stores the id, the app shows the title): in the editor, Editor rule 23; in the backlinks snippets, rule 25. In views the ONE answer is `linkText(link, resolve?)` (`client/src/views/expr/values.ts`): the hand-typed label, else the current title — `IndexRecord.title`, YAZ-2420 D14 — of the note the id names (a `#heading` rides along), else the target as written. `render(v, resolve?)`, and `chip` / `cellContent` / `GroupHeader` in `client/src/views/view/GroupHeader.tsx`, take that optional resolver, and WITH it the title is what is shown and what is ordered by: table, list, cards and board values and chips, group headers and board column headers, the summary values, the properties panel's link rows, a link column's sort, the order and label of groups, and the views' search. WITHOUT a resolver `render` is exactly the stored `[[…]]`, and that is what every write-back and persisted key passes — a cell commit, the group-drag swap, a group "+" seed, and the collapse key `groupKeyOf` (`v:[[<id>]]`) — so renaming a note never rewrites a property and never reopens a collapsed group. A formula's `list.join()` renders without one too. The hover preview (`ReadOnlyNote`, through `useReadOnlyNote(host, body, wikilinks?)`) receives the window's link source, because an id link has no readable text of its own.
- **Copy ID** (`client/src/editor/linkMenu.ts` `copyText(id, 'ID', onNotice)`, the link menu's one copy helper, YAZ-3910): exactly the note's id on the clipboard, said through the passive notice either way — `Copied ID`, or `Can't copy ID: <reason>` when the clipboard refuses. ONE surface (YAZ-2420 D31): right-click on a rendered id link in the editor (Editor rule 23; the one link menu, YAZ-3609 D23), where the id is the LINK's — the note it points at — and a link has no path to copy. A file's own menus — the sidebar row's, the tab's, a view row's — carry one copy item, **Copy path**, which copies the plain path and nothing else (D7): the id of a note the app named is in that path, and the id of a folder, or of a file the app did not name, is read from its `.folder.md` or its frontmatter.
- **Reserved**: `id` is one of `reservedKeys(true)` (`client/src/links/reservedKeys.ts`: the keys the app owns where the vault uses IDs) — a **Reserved** row with no editor in the properties panel ("The properties panel") whatever its value (a hand-written `id: 42` is the app's key too, which writes its own id over it — YAZ-2420 D30), and a column a view can hide but never delete ("Folder settings: `.folder.md`": Delete column). It is no column of a folder's table, because the rows hold the folder's values and not the note's own keys ("Folder settings": Values); `propertyKeys` (`client/src/views/engine.ts`) itself leaves no key out (YAZ-2523). In a vault that does not use IDs `id` is an ordinary property — an editor in the panel, a column in the table ("Two kinds of vault").
- **The command line** (`desktop/src/cli/cli.ts` — the `yaseendocs` door of "Comments", whose `--help` is the contract an agent reads): two verbs, so an agent can work in names while the files hold ids. 🔒 Both work only in a vault that gives its notes IDs (YAZ-2523 V10 — "Two kinds of vault": The command line): the vault is the nearest folder at or above the page that has ANSWERED in its `.yaseendocs/ids.json` (`idVault`), and only a yes counts. `yaseendocs id <page.md>` prints the page's id. A page that has one is only read — not a byte and not its mtime changes. A page with none — or with an `id` some other tool wrote, another vault's letters included (YAZ-2420 D30, YAZ-2677 R7) — is given one first, through the sweep's own `giveId` and the app's own door (`mint.ts`): the vault's next number, counted in this Mac's ONE count file, so the command gives the number the app would (R20, S40). The command holds no index, so the door walks and scans the vault for its highest number, as `links` below does; it finds this Mac's ID in the app's user-data folder (`userDataDir`). A number ID is printed as the app writes it, whatever its case in the file. Refused with exit 1, the reason on stderr and the bytes untouched: `<page>'s vault does not give its notes IDs (turn on "Give this vault's notes IDs" in the app's Settings)` — the vault said no, or nothing above the page has answered, and whether or not the page holds an `id`; `the properties block does not parse (invalid)`; and `<page> changed while it was being given an id — run this again`. `id <folder>/.folder.md` on a folder with no settings file yet creates it, as the sweep would, and prints its id; a folder that is not there is not found. `yaseendocs links <page.md> [--json]` lists every id ON a page once, number IDs and old IDs alike (S92; each read as an ID of this vault and printed as the app writes it, so `[[yaz-12]]` and a link with letters of before are `YAZ-12`, and `[[GPT-4]]` is a name) — the note ids among its links (the index's own `links` extraction, a folder's values included) first, then the note ids in its frontmatter `also_in` list — each with what that id names NOW, found by walking and scanning the vault exactly as the index does (`walk` + `scanAll`), in path order, so of two pages still sharing an id the one named is the sweep's first choice too. One line per id, `<id>  <title>  <where>` (the title since YAZ-2420 D14 — the path stays the real one): a note → its title and its vault-relative path; a folder (its id is carried by its `.folder.md`) → its title and the folder's path with a trailing `/`, followed by `  (also in)` when the page reaches it only through `also_in`; no page or folder → `<id>  (missing)`. A link written by name is not an id and is not listed; a page with none prints `no ids on <page>`. After them, apart — a blank line, then `in:` — the folders the page holds values for (the blocks of its `in`), one line each: `<id>  <title>  <folder path>/`, or the id alone when no folder has it. `--json` prints `{ links, in }`, 2-space indented: the same rows as `{ id, kind: 'note' | 'folder' | 'missing', title?, path? }`, and the folders as `{ id, title?, path? }`. `--help` says that a vault gives its notes IDs only when the Settings switch is on and that `id` and `links` are refused in one that does not, where a folder's values live, what a folder's id is, and that a page's title is its `title:` line, from which, with the id, the app builds the file name (`<kebab-title>-<id>.md`) — so a page is found from an id by searching the vault's file names for it, and a file the app did not name by its `id: <id>` line. A page whose vault does not use IDs is refused: `<page>'s vault does not use IDs, so there are no ID links to list`.
