**The door** (🔒 YAZ-1617 D1–D5): an agent leaves a comment through `yaseendocs` — the app's own Electron run as plain Node (`ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1`, VS Code's `code` pattern): a shell shim at `Contents/Resources/bin/yaseendocs` runs `app.asar/out/main/cli.js`, a second main entry that never imports `electron`. Never the app window, never the single-instance lock, no Node install, no checkout. It writes through the SAME `addComment` / `editComment` / `deleteComment`, guarded the SAME way as D8 on node fs (`transformOnDisk`: fresh read, `expectedMtime`, one retry on CONFLICT, a second conflict refuses). Eight verbs — four for comments, `comment`, `comments [--json]`, `edit`, `delete`; two for a page's id and the ids it points at, `id` and `links [--json]` (YAZ-2293 — "Note ids": The command line); `due [--json]`, when a page — or each page under a folder — is next due for review (YAZ-2322 — "Review": For agents); and `vaults [--json]`, the one verb that takes no page: the app's list of vaults, read from its state file and never written (YAZ-2556 🔒 D2 — "Multi-window": The vault list) — a comment is NAMED the way the app shows it, `#3` / `#3.1` (or bare `3`), or by its id, and a name that matches nothing is REFUSED with nothing written (🔒 YAZ-1627: the model forgives an unknown `reply_to` in a hand-written file; the command never creates one) — and `--help` IS the contract: the only documentation an agent reads, so its wording is UI copy. `comment` writes `by: agent` unless `--by` says otherwise (choosing the tool IS the declaration; D3 stands — the UI still writes no `by`); `edit` and `delete` REFUSE a comment with no `by` — a person's comment is the app's alone (D17 asks first there; a script cannot ask). Exit codes 0 done · 1 refused or failed · 2 usage. **The handshake** — TOMBSTONE (YAZ-2420 D8, D22, reversing 🔒 D2): the right-click item that put a page's path and the command's `--help` line on the clipboard is removed, and nothing replaces it. Everything that existed only for it went with it: `shared/agentInstructions.ts`, `client/src/lib/copyForAgent.ts`, main's `shell:agent-prompt` door (`desktop/src/main/ipc/agent.ts`) and their tests. A page is handed to an agent by its plain path ("Copy path", D7), and the command still ships where it always did — the shim when packaged, `node "<out/main>/cli.js"` in dev. Rejected and NOT to be added back: a PATH installer (🔒 D3 — on Apple Silicon `/usr/local/bin` means admin prompts for no gain), per-vault `AGENTS.md` (loads only when the agent STARTS inside the vault), writing into global agent files (imprinting config unasked), vault detection (the command works on the file), the `yaseendocs://comment` deep link (no receipt; a link anywhere could write).

Files: `shared/comments.ts` (the model, `COMMENTS_KEY`), `desktop/src/cli/cli.ts` + `index.ts` + `cli.test.ts` (the command), `desktop/build/bin/yaseendocs` (the shim, mode 755), `client/src/comments/CommentsSection.tsx` + `comments.css` (the block), `client/src/comments/markdown.ts` (`commentHtml` / `commentSummary`), `client/src/comments/comments.test.ts`, `client/src/views/writeProperty.ts` (`transformFile`'s `{ mtime, content }` return), `client/src/hooks/useAutosave.ts` (`absorbFrontmatterOnly`, unchanged — relied on), `client/src/editor/Editor.tsx` (the mount, between the Crepe host and "Linked mentions") and `client/src/views/FolderView.tsx` (a folder's stream, under its views), `client/src/editor/FrontmatterPanel.tsx` (the RESERVED entry), `desktop/src/main/vaultIndex/scan.ts` (the drop) + `cache.ts` (`CACHE_VERSION` 3), `client/src/app.css` (`--agent` / `--agent-soft`), `client/src/lib/relativeTime.ts`, `client/package.json` (`marked`, `dompurify`).

## Review (YAZ-2322 — decisions D1-D9 and C of its scoping, LOCKED)

Upkeep review: a note that has gone unchanged and unchecked long enough comes up in an Inbox, to be confirmed as still relevant or fixed. It is NOT a memory algorithm — there is no front and back, no grading of recall (🔒 D3, D5). The model is `shared/reviews.ts` and `shared/schedule.ts` (whose header docs are the spec), the app's state is `client/src/review/`; the decision record and its scenario tables are the comments on YAZ-2322. This section is the rules.

**Storage IS the note** (🔒 D1): ONE reserved frontmatter key, `reviews`, holding a flat list with one line per review — `- {at: 2026-10-04T14:02:11Z, rating: keep, text: 9f3a1c2e}`. `at` is ISO UTC at seconds precision, `rating` is `keep` (the one answer v1 writes, 🔒 D4), `text` is the fingerprint of the body the review was written into. It travels with the file, and sync conflicts only when the same note is reviewed on two devices between syncs. A vault-wide log and a sidecar were REJECTED. Like `comments`, every write carries what it does not understand (unknown keys on an entry, unknown entries), a `reviews` value that is not a list is the user's own and is never overwritten, and an emptied list deletes the key.

**The file stores what happened; the date is computed** (🔒 D2): nothing writes a due date anywhere. `dueAt` in `shared/schedule.ts` is the ONLY place one is computed, from the record's `mtime`, `reviews` and `text` and the vault's settings — so an edit made by anything, on any device, moves the date with no extra write, and a changed setting moves every note at once. The cost, accepted: the due date is not a property or a view column, and an agent reads it through `yaseendocs due`.

**The rule** (🔒, v1): a note never reviewed, or whose body changed since its last review, is due `baseDays` after the file last changed. Otherwise it is due after its last review by `baseDays × growth^n`, capped at `maxDays`, where n is the reviews in a row that saw the body as it is now. With the defaults: 30 days untouched, then 60, 120, 240, 365. "Due now" is anything due before local midnight tonight. Smarter signals are a Future issue (YAZ-2372); they change `dueAt` and no file.

**"Changed" is the body, by fingerprint** (🔒 C): `textFingerprint` is FNV-1a over the body with line endings normalised and outer whitespace trimmed, eight hex characters, the same in the renderer and the main process. A reviewed note whose body still matches its last review is unmoved by comments, properties or the log itself. A note with NO matching review has only the file's modified time for a clock, so any write to it restarts the base wait — the one place the modified time decides.

**Who is in review** (🔒 D6): with upkeep on (🔒 D7, below), every Markdown note, until turned off. `review: false` takes one out, `review: true` puts one in whatever the vault default; any other value is ignored. `setInReview` writes the flag only when it differs from the vault default and never touches the log. Never in review: a folder's `.folder.md` (it is not among the index's `records`), a file too large to read (no `text`), a note whose frontmatter does not parse (a review could not be written into it).

**The index carries it**: `IndexRecord.reviews?` (the log as `at` / `rating` / `text`, time order; absent when never reviewed) and `IndexRecord.text?` (the body fingerprint; absent when the file was not read). `scanFile` lifts `reviews` off `properties` exactly as it drops `comments`, so the key is never a property or a column. `reviews` is one of `reservedKeys(ids)`, in both kinds of vault; `review` is an ordinary true/false property, the user's to edit.

**Settings are the vault's** (🔒 D7): `<root>/.yaseendocs/review.json` — `{ algorithm: "upkeep", enabled: false, baseDays: 30, growth: 2, maxDays: 365, reviewByDefault: true }` — through the generic `vaultConfig` door, sanitised field by field (`sanitizeReviewSettings`), so every device computes the same dates. No file means the defaults; nothing is created until a setting is changed. A file that is not valid JSON (a hand edit, a file half synced) changes nothing: the window keeps the settings it has, an open review stays open, and a save is refused with a notice, never written over it. `algorithm` has one value: it is in the file so a second algorithm is a new value, not a new shape. App owns the one `useReviewSettings`; the Settings dialog's Review section edits it.

**Upkeep is off until a vault turns it on** (🔒 D7): `enabled` is false with no file, with no `enabled` in it, and with one that is not true or false. ONE gate: `isInReview` answers false for every note, so the queue is empty, nothing is due, and `yaseendocs due` says so. Off, the app shows none of it — no Inbox row, no "Review this folder", no "Turn review on / off" (`useReview`'s `inReview` is null for every path), no Reviews section (App hands the editor no settings), and the Settings dialog's Review section is the one switch, "Enable upkeep review" (its other rows are `available` only while it is on). An open review closes when upkeep turns off. Nothing is written either way: a note's `reviews` and `review` stay as they are, `reviews` stays reserved, and the index carries the log and the fingerprint whatever the setting, so turning upkeep back on finds every note where it was.

**The Inbox and a session** (🔒 D8, D9): `useReview` (ONE PER VAULT of the window since YAZ-2602, in the vault's scope — `vault/useVaultScope.ts`) gives the due count — the Inbox row above the lens tabs, there while upkeep is on, one row per vault that has it on (R5) — and one session per WINDOW: each vault can hold a session, and App's `startReview` closes every other vault's before it starts one (S41), so a review of vault B runs with B's settings and B's notes whichever vault the tab in front is in (S42). A session takes its queue ONCE at start, most overdue first, for the vault or for one folder and its subfolders ("Review this folder"). It REPLACES the main pane and is not a tab: tabs, their history and the right panel are untouched underneath. The page shown is the real editor. A note is checked against the live index only when its turn comes (gone, turned off or no longer due, it is passed over) and never while it is showing, because editing the page it shows is what makes it no longer due. "Still relevant" (⌘⇧⏎) appends one review through `transformFile`; Skip (⌘⇧S) writes nothing and sends the note to the end; Undo removes the review just written. Leaving: Esc, the bar's ✕, the Inbox row again, or ⌘W close the review and nothing else (⌘W never closes the tab hidden under it); going to a tab — a sidebar click, ⌃Tab — ends it and shows that tab; a link clicked in the note opens in a background tab and the review stays. One editor per note: a note already open in a tab shows through that tab's own layer, and one open in the side panel is reviewed there.

**Seeing it** (with upkeep on): the Reviews section follows "Linked mentions" on a note's page — the next check, then one row per review with a delete, and "Reset review history". A note's row and tab menus turn its review off or on.

**For agents**: `yaseendocs due <page.md>` prints the day a page is next due; given a folder it lists the pages due now under it, each by its day, its title and its path (the title since YAZ-2420 D14); `--json` for the raw shape. It runs the app's own scanner and `shared/schedule.ts`, so it answers what the app shows.

Files: `shared/reviews.ts`, `shared/schedule.ts`, `client/src/review/` (`useReview`, `useReviewSettings`, the bars, the Reviews section), `desktop/src/main/vaultIndex/scan.ts`, `desktop/src/cli/cli.ts`. Tests: `client/src/review/*.test.*`, `desktop/src/main/vaultIndex/scan.test.ts`, `desktop/src/cli/cli.test.ts`.

## Text formatting (YAZ-3047 round 2 — decisions D10-D17 on YAZ-3048, LOCKED; YAZ-3066, YAZ-3067, YAZ-3068)

**The file is the vault's** (🔒 D10): `<root>/.yaseendocs/text-formatting.json`, through the generic `vaultConfig` door (the pattern of `review.json`, no IPC of its own), so GitHub sync carries it to the other Macs. Its shape: `{ "version": 1, "text": { "size": 17 }, "h2": { "size": 21, "underline": true } }` — the version, then ONLY the levels and fields the reader changed (`textFormattingFile`). `text.size` is whole px from 12 to 24 (`TEXT_SIZE_MIN`, `TEXT_SIZE_MAX`; 16 when absent, `TEXT_DEFAULT_SIZE`). `h1`–`h6` are `HeadingStyle` `{ size?, bold?, underline?, highlight? }`: `size` whole px from 12 to 48, `bold` and `underline` booleans, `highlight` ∈ yellow/green/blue/pink. `sanitizeTextFormatting` (`shared/textFormatting.ts`) ignores `version` and unknown keys, and a bad level, or a bad Text line, falls back ALONE: the others stay. No file means the app's look, `{}`; nothing is created until a change. A file that is not valid JSON shows the app's look, and a save is refused with the notice "Can't save the text formatting: text-formatting.json is not valid JSON", never written over it. A change from another window or another Mac arrives as `vaultConfig:changed` and is read again. Two Macs that change the file offline get a rebase conflict, which sync reports as "attention", as for any file. The Welcome window has no text formatting. The Markdown never changes.

**The hook** (`client/src/settings/useTextFormatting.ts`): one for each vault, in the vault's scope (`useVaultScope` → `textFormatting: { formatting, save }`). `save` shows the change at once, then writes; a write that fails falls back to what the file holds. `formatting` keeps its identity until the formatting changes.

**Each page layer carries its vault's look** (🔒 D12, D17): App puts `textVars(formatting)` (`client/src/settings/headingStyles.ts`) as the `style` of each layer that shows a note — the tab layer, the review layer, the side panel layer and `QuickLook` (the search preview) — from `scopeOf(path)`, so two vaults in one window look different. `--text-size` is there only when the Text size is set; `--hN-size` (px), `--hN-weight` (400 when bold is off), `--hN-decoration` (underline) and `--hN-bg` (the `==highlight==` mark colour) only for a changed field. Nothing sits on `.app`. `app.css` reads `--crepe-base-font-size: var(--text-size, 16px)` on `.editor-instance .milkdown`, so paragraphs, list text, bullet label rows, code blocks, tables and inline code follow the Text size, and the default stays pixel-identical. Each `h1`–`h6` rule reads its variables with the em of 1.0.14 as its fallback, so a heading with no size of its own follows the Text size (round(scale × Text) in Settings, `HEADING_SCALE`, `defaultHeadingSize`); a size the reader set stays in px. A folder page, its board hover card and its outline are inside the folder's layer and inherit its vault's look. The page title, comments, the table of contents and the heading level tag keep their fixed sizes; headings in comments and in "What's new" do not change. Each heading keeps its full width; the wash is painted on the `.heading-text` spans (`client/src/editor/outline/headingText.ts`), so it hugs the words (YAZ-3049 D7). A change costs one style update on the layers of that vault; no editor renders again (one cached style object per formatting object).

**Settings › Appearance › Text formatting** (🔒 D14, D15, D16; `client/src/settings/TextFormattingControl.tsx`, `registry.tsx`): the group's hint is "How text looks in every note of this vault."; one BARE row (`bare: true` — no label on screen and so no gap; the label "Text formatting" stays for search and as the row's `aria-label`), `data-setting="textFormatting"`, `available` only when App hands `SettingsCtx.textFormatting` over (a window with a vault). With two or more vaults a "Vault" dropdown (the `Select` control) sits above the lines: the window's vaults by name, in the window's order (a vault with no name shows its folder name); it starts on the active tab's vault each time Settings opens, and falls back to the first vault when the chosen one leaves the window. The group has no "Vault: name" line: the dropdown replaces it. A "Text" line above Heading 1: "−", the size, "+", 12 to 24 px in steps of 1; "Reset" only when it is not 16, and a step back to 16 removes `text` as Reset does. No bold, underline or highlight for all text. The six heading lines as in 1.0.15; a level with no size shows `defaultHeadingSize(level, textSize)` and its first "−" or "+" starts from that number. A change writes only the chosen vault's file. Not in scope: a guard that keeps a lower level smaller than a higher one, and one change for all vaults at once.

**The default line** (YAZ-3208, 🔒 D8–D11 and cases S90–S100 on the working log YAZ-3165; rule 41): the file's optional `line` key, `{ "darkness"?: 5–100, "thickness"?: 1–24, "pattern"?: "dotted" | "dashed" }`, holds the vault's default line — only the fields that differ from the app's 50%, 3px, solid (solid is no `pattern` field). The line's values, ranges and app defaults are `shared/line.ts`, which `sanitizeTextFormatting` uses: a bad `line` (a field out of range, an unknown field or pattern, not an object) falls back ALONE and the other keys stay (`isLineDefaults`, S95). `textVars` adds `--line-default-darkness` (`70%`), `--line-default-thickness` (`4px`) and `--line-default-pattern` (`dashed`) for the set fields only (`lineVars`), so a change shows at once in every open note of that vault and in no other (S91), and a change from another window or Mac arrives as `vaultConfig:changed` like any other (S98). The Settings row "Line" sits below Heading 6 (`LineDefaultsLine`, D10): "Line" with a preview of the default line (S99), a darkness `Stepper` in steps of 5% (5–100; `Stepper` has a `unit`, and a value off the grid steps onto it), a thickness `Stepper` in steps of 1px (1–24), the style buttons Solid, Dotted, Dashed, and "Reset" while the key exists (S96, S97); its controls share one box over the size, B/U and dots columns, so the heading lines keep their columns. `withLineDefaults` drops a field stepped back to the app default and the key when no field is left.

**The 1.0.15 styles move once** (🔒 D11): 1.0.15 kept the heading styles app-wide in `yaseendocs.json` `settings.headingStyles`. The store's loader keeps a VALID map of that key (`isHeadingStyles`; any bad level or field is `{}`), and `store.takeLegacyHeadingStyles()` hands it out once, then `{}`; the state never holds it, so the next write of `yaseendocs.json` drops the key. At start, before `manager.restore`, `moveLegacyHeadingStyles` (`desktop/src/main/textFormattingMove.ts`) writes `{ version: 1, ...map }` into each vault of each window the state holds where `text-formatting.json` is absent; it never writes over a file (a malformed one too), writes nothing for `{}`, skips a root that is not a folder (so a drive that is not connected gets no new folder), and logs a vault that fails while the others continue. It does not hold up a window: a window that read no file yet hears the write as `vaultConfig:changed`. A vault opened later starts with the app's look. A downgrade to 1.0.15 ignores the vault file and has no app-wide value.

## The sidebar lenses (YAZ-847, YAZ-1766, YAZ-2619; the Search tab, YAZ-2638, YAZ-2662)

Three readings of the window's vault — or vaults: with two or more in the window each lens reads all of them (YAZ-2602, Several vaults below) — switched by the tabs at the top of the sidebar: **Files**, the folder tree on disk — the only hierarchy there is — **Focus**, the focus lists of the window's vaults (YAZ-2619; kept in the vault since YAZ-2702), and **♥ Favorites**. All three are the same `Tree` component, the same `.tree__row` family and the same context menu — and a row of Focus and of Favorites has one item more, "Show in sidebar", first (YAZ-2638 🔒 D3, below). The tabs row holds a FOURTH tab, **Search**, second in the row (YAZ-2638 🔒 D2). It is a tab and no lens: its body is the search, and it is never stored (The Search tab, below).

**The chrome stack** (🔒 D4/D5, YAZ-847, as amended by YAZ-2638 🔒 D2): above the lens row sits the Inbox row while the vault has upkeep on ("Review") — ONE ROW PER VAULT of the window that has upkeep on, in vault order (YAZ-2602 R5, S41): a single row reads "Inbox", two or more read "Inbox · <vault>", each with its own vault's count (`aria-label` "Inbox · <vault>, N due"), and a click opens the review of THAT vault or closes it when it is the one open — one review runs per window at a time. The Inbox row stays above the tabs on each tab, the Search tab too (YAZ-2638 S25). ROW 1 is the tablist (`client/src/sidebar/SidebarTabs.tsx`; its pure rules are `client/src/sidebar/tabRow.ts`) — **Files · Search · Focus · ♥ Favorites · Sessions · Recents** by default (Search is second since YAZ-2638 🔒 D2; every tab but Files is a glyph — a `SearchIcon` since YAZ-2638 D2, an `EyeIcon` since YAZ-2619 D4, a `HeartIcon` since YAZ-1766 D1, a `StackIcon` since YAZ-3147 D4 and a `ClockIcon` since YAZ-3235 D4 — each with its word only in `title` + `aria-label`, and Files stays a word at every width, YAZ-3273 D6; the ACTIVE glyph tab is in the accent, the heart filled too — `.sidebar__lens--glyph.sidebar__lens--active`, S18). It is drawn in the reader's order, `settings.sidebarTabs.order`, without the tabs in `sidebarTabs.hidden` (YAZ-3273 D8; `SIDEBAR_TABS` is only the default order; `SidebarTab` = `SidebarLens | 'search'`; `SIDEBAR_LENSES` is still the three lenses, the values that are stored). After the tabs comes the **⋯** button ("More tabs", D2), then Sort and the expand/collapse-all button, pinned at the right end by `margin-left: auto` (D7). Focus Mode's eye BUTTON ("Exit focus mode", YAZ-1605) is removed (YAZ-2619 D4, R14).

**The fit of row 1** (YAZ-3273 D1 to D3, D10; S1 to S8, S24, S30) is MEASURED: a `ResizeObserver` on the row and on each of its buttons. The tabs that do not fit leave the row from its right end, in the row's order, into ⋯, so the row never spills over the editor, never wraps and never scrolls; at `SIDEBAR_MIN_W` = 180 px the row on Files is Files, ⋯, Sort and fold (S3). `overflow-x: clip` on `.sidebar__lenses` is a guard only. The state is the COUNT that fits, so a width change that keeps the count draws nothing (S30). The fit counts only the buttons that show on the tab (Sort on Files, Focus, Favorites and Search (YAZ-3511 D3); fold when there is something to fold), so a tab switch can change it (S5). ⋯ shows only when a tab has no room, a tab is hidden, or Sort or fold is off the bar on a tab that shows it (D2, D9). It wears the accent and the accent underline while the tab that shows is inside it (D3), and the tabs on the bar do not move for it. With ⋯ off (`hiddenButtons` has `more`, D10) it never shows, the row keeps no room for it, and the open tab takes the last place on the bar when it is hidden or has no room.

**The row's menu** (YAZ-3273 D4, YAZ-3279; S9 to S16) is a `ContextMenu`. A click on ⋯ opens it below ⋯ (a second click closes it); a right-click on a tab or on blank space in the row opens it at the pointer; Shift+F10 or the context-menu key on a tab or on ⋯ opens it below that button with the focus on its first item. Its rows: "Hide <tab>" first when a tab was right-clicked (off on Files, hint "Files stays"; none for a tab that is hidden already), then the tabs with no room, a line, the hidden tabs (hint "hidden"; the open tab's hint is "open", which wins), then "Sort…" (the sort menu, at ⋯) and the fold button's label when those buttons are off the bar, then "Edit tab row…" — the one row every menu has. Empty groups do not show, and there are no group names. Each tab row and each button row has its glyph, Files a folder (`rowGlyph`, `TabRowPanel.tsx`, the same map the panel draws). **The Tab row panel** (`client/src/sidebar/TabRowPanel.tsx`, D4, D5, D9, D10; S17 to S27) opens from "Edit tab row…" where the menu was, pulled back inside the window, with the right-clicked tab's row lit. It is a popover of its own (`role="dialog"`), not `ContextMenu`: "Tabs · drag to reorder" (a row per tab: a grip, a box with `role="checkbox"`, the glyph, the name; Files' box is off, "always shown"), a line, "Buttons at the right" (Sort, Collapse all, More tabs (⋯), each with a box), a line, "Reset tab row" (the default order, every tab and button shown). A row drags by pointer events, never native HTML drag: it lifts after 3 px and follows the pointer clamped to the list, the other rows slide apart by `transform` (160 ms), and on release it glides into its gap (140 ms) and the order is written once; a press during the glide writes that drop first (YAZ-3301). A press on a box never drags; `Escape` during a drag puts the row back and writes nothing; with reduce motion nothing animates. The tabs on the bar never drag (S27). The panel closes on `Escape`, a press outside and a window blur (S26); closing it mid-drag ends the drag, and closing it mid-glide writes that drop at once. When the menu or the panel closes, the focus goes back to the button that opened it, else to the tab that shows (`ACTIVE_TAB_SELECTOR`), when the focus was in it or on the page body. Every change is ONE write of `settings.sidebarTabs`, and a change that changes nothing writes nothing (`sameTabRow`).

ROW 2 is the search bar of YAZ-801, and it is on the Search tab ONLY (YAZ-2638 🔒 D2). This overturns 🔒 YAZ-797, where search was never a tab and the bar was ALWAYS visible, on every lens, loading / error / empty vault included. The expand/collapse-all button is gone on the Search tab (YAZ-2638 S17). The tabs carry `role="tab"` + `aria-selected` and nothing else — no `aria-controls`, no `tabpanel` — because the one body below is every tab's.

**The lens is App's, and it is WINDOW IDENTITY** (🔒 D4, amended by YAZ-1628): one value, `WindowEntry.sidebarLens`, beside per-window `sidebarCollapsed`, so two windows on one vault browse on different lenses. It lives in App rather than in the Sidebar because the Sidebar is mounted on ONE vault of the window — `key={sidebarKey.current}`, the vault that was first when it mounted, so a vault that joins, leaves behind it or moves does not remount the panel (YAZ-2602; YAZ-2631 R12) — and only while it is open. `changeLens` writes a LENS through `window.setIdentity` (anything but the three lenses → `BAD_REQUEST`) and then mirrors locally; another window's switch never reaches this one. The Search tab it mirrors and does NOT write (YAZ-2638 🔒 D2, S15): App's state is a `SidebarTab`, the stored value stays the last lens, and that lens is where Esc goes back to and where a window that starts again opens. A new, first or deep-link window starts on `DEFAULT_SIDEBAR_LENS` (Files, YAZ-1846), a duplicate inherits and then diverges, and a root CHANGE lands on Files (🔒 D2, YAZ-1846). On load, a window entry with no valid lens of its own takes the file's retired global `sidebarLens` when that is valid, else the default.

**The Search tab** (YAZ-2638 🔒 D2, cases S1–S25 on the issue; it overturns "Search across the lenses", 🔒 D5 of YAZ-847, where a typed query replaced the ACTIVE tab's body and the bar stood on every lens): search is a tab of its own, the second in the row. The bar is on that tab alone. Its body is the search: with no text one line of help and the keys of the search below it (YAZ-2662 🔒 D10), with text the search tree — in two groups when a match is a pinned item or is inside one (YAZ-2662 🔒 D2, The search from the keyboard, below). A typed query never replaces the body of Files, Focus or Favorites. The tabs row stays visible and clickable, and a switch to a different tab keeps the text, the folds and the highlight. ⌘K and a click on the tab show it, with the caret in the bar and the text selected — also when the tab already shows. A plain show of the sidebar on the Search tab does not take the caret. Esc in a page, while the tab shows, puts the caret in the bar. Esc in the bar and the `esc` keycap go back to the lens the window last showed, the text stays, and the caret goes into the open page (YAZ-2662 🔒 D9, which overturns "after Esc in the bar the focus is given up"). While a different tab shows, the search does no work; on return the text, the results, the folds and the highlight are back. The tab is never stored. "Add to focus" on a search row stays on the Search tab (this overturns YAZ-2619 🔒 D3 for the Search tab), and the row moves to the top group at once (YAZ-2662 S27). Everything else about the bar is the search contract under the `sidebar/` entry in "Repo layout".

**The search from the keyboard** (YAZ-2662 🔒 D1–D11, cases S1–S64 on the issue, S19 and S19A in its "S19 changed" record, S65–S67 and the key-repeat rules in its "Cases S65 to S67" record; it overturns S23 of YAZ-2620, "Enter on a folder opens the folder's page", and the YAZ-2638 rule "after Esc in the bar the focus is given up"). WHY: the search is the first door to each page — ⌘K, and ⌘T —, Yasin pins his important folders, and he wants to reach them, look inside them and look at a note with no mouse and no extra tab. The words: a MATCH is a row that the typed text found; the HIGHLIGHT is the one row that the keyboard is on; a PINNED ITEM is a file or a folder that is in the focus list or in the favorites; the LIST KEYS are Space, `←` and `→`. **Two groups** (🔒 D2–D4). The matches that are a pinned item or are inside one show FIRST, under the label "Favorites and focus". A line and the label "Everything else" come next, then the other matches. Each row shows one time. The top rows of the top group are the pinned items: the focus items first, in the order of the focus list, then the favorites, in the order of the Favorites tab. An item that is in both lists shows one time, at its place in the focus list. A pinned item inside a different pinned folder shows inside that folder. A pinned item with no match, and none inside, is not drawn. With no pinned match there is no label and no line, and the tab looks as it did before. The ranking puts each pinned match before each other match, so the limit of 50 never cuts a pinned match while another match shows, and the highlight starts on the best pinned match. **Enter** (🔒 D1, D8). Enter on a file opens it, as before: the first Enter previews, and Enter on the page that is open puts the caret in it. Enter on a FOLDER shows the folder in the Files tab: the folders above it are open, the folder is open, its row flashes for 3 seconds and has the keyboard focus. No tab opens, the page on show does not change, and the text stays in the Search tab. ⇧⏎ does that for a file too. ⌘⏎ opens a background tab, of a folder's page too, and ⌘ is read first. A click on a folder still folds it, and a double-click opens nothing (YAZ-3377 D1); its menu's **Open folder page** opens its page. "Show in sidebar" in a row's menu moves no keyboard focus: only ⏎ and ⇧⏎ do. **The list keys work after ↑ or ↓** (🔒 D7). Before `↑` or `↓`, Space types a space, and `←` and `→` move the caret. After `↑` or `↓`, the three keys act on the highlight. A change of the text gives them back to the text. A list key with nothing to do stays a text key. **Space, → and ← on a folder** (🔒 D6). Space opens the folder in the search tree and shows each row that it holds, a match or not; a row that is no match is dim. `↑` and `↓` then stop on each row inside it. Space again puts the folder back as the search drew it. `→` does what the first Space does. `←` closes an open folder. A change of the text puts each folder back. **Space on a file: the preview panel** (🔒 D5). Space shows the file in a panel over the page area. It shows a note, read only, a text file, an image and a PDF; nothing in it can be edited, and it writes nothing. No tab opens and the workspace does not change. The caret stays in the search bar: `↑` and `↓` move the highlight, and the panel follows 120 ms after the last move. Space again closes it, and so do the first Esc, a change of the text, ⏎, ⌘⏎ and ⇧⏎, a different sidebar tab, a click or a right-click on a row of the search tree, the ✕ of the panel, the tab board and a review. On a folder no panel is drawn, and it shows again on the next file. A click in the panel puts the keyboard focus on it; Esc there closes the panel and puts the caret back in the search bar. **Esc** (🔒 D9). With the panel on show, the first Esc closes the panel only. With none, Esc goes back to the tab that the window last showed, the text stays, and the caret goes into the open page; with no page open no caret moves. A click on the `esc` keycap is the Esc key. **The empty tab** (🔒 D10). The empty Search tab keeps its line and lists the keys below it: `↑` `↓` Move, `↵` Open, `⌘↵` Open in a background tab, `⇧↵` Show in Files, `space` Preview a file or open a folder, after ↑ or ↓, `→` `←` Open or close a folder, after ↑ or ↓, `esc` Back to the page. With text typed the keys do not show. **The arrows on a tree** (🔒 D11 — decided in the build, because D1 puts the keyboard focus on a row of Files and a sidebar tree had no arrow keys: only Tab moved between its rows). With the keyboard focus on a row of Files, Focus or Favorites, `↓` and `↑` move the focus to the next row on show and to the row before, and stop at both ends. `→` opens a closed folder row and `←` closes an open one. They change no selection and open no page, and they do nothing while a rename box or a create box has the focus. A row of the search tree has no arrows: its keys are the search bar's. **A held key acts one time.** A held Enter in the search bar is one Enter. A held Enter on a row of a sidebar tree does nothing. A held Space on the highlight acts one time; Space as a text key still repeats. NOT INCLUDED: Ctrl+N and Ctrl+P; a wrap of `↑` and `↓` (locked, YAZ-803); ⌘1 to ⌘9 for the matches; Tab between the groups; a change to the note-shortcut picker; a change to the main process, the IPC, the stored focus list or the stored favorites; a new dependency. The code names, `pinnedRoots`, `full`, `PREVIEW_FOLLOW_MS` and the rest, are in the search contract under the `sidebar/` entry in "Repo layout". Files: `client/src/sidebar/{Sidebar,Tree}.tsx` + `revealRow.ts` + `hooks/useSidebarSearch.ts`, `client/src/search/{QuickLook.tsx,quickLook.css,searchCandidates.ts,searchTree.ts,useSearchResults.ts}`, `client/src/editor/useReadOnlyNote.ts` (moved out of the folder views' old hover card, removed by YAZ-3743), `client/src/lib/{treeState,focusHandoff}.ts`, `client/src/App.tsx`, `client/src/app.css`; tests in `sidebar/Sidebar.test.tsx` ("Enter and Shift+Enter show a row in Files; the arrows walk a sidebar tree (YAZ-2662 D1, D8, D11)", "the matches of the pinned items show first (YAZ-2662 D2, D3, D4)", "Space, → and ← on a folder of the search tree (YAZ-2662 D6, D7)" with "Space on a file: the preview panel (YAZ-2662 D5)" inside it, and the `YAZ-2662` tests of "the Search tab (YAZ-2638 D2)" and of "several vaults in one window (YAZ-2602)"), `search/QuickLook.test.tsx` + `QuickLook.crepe.test.tsx`, `search/{searchTree,searchCandidates,useSearchResults}.test.ts(x)`, `search/searchCandidates.perf.test.ts`, `lib/{treeState,focusHandoff}.test.ts`, `sidebar/revealRow.test.ts`, `App.test.tsx` (the `YAZ-2662` tests); end to end in `desktop/e2e/search.spec.ts` (step 9) and `desktop/e2e/lenses.spec.ts`, each written and not run.

**"Show in sidebar" on a row** (YAZ-2638 🔒 D1 and 🔒 D3 — the D3 of the "D3 changed" record on the issue, which replaces the first D3 — cases S26–S38): a right-click on a row that is not the Files tree's own shows "Show in sidebar" as the FIRST item of the menu. That is a row of the Search tab, of the Focus tab and of the Favorites tab: a file and a folder, a top row and a row inside a folder, and a vault row of the search tree (S26, S34). A row of the Files tab never has it: that row is in the sidebar's tree already. Blank space of any tab never has it (S28, S38). A right-click inside a selection of two or more rows does not show it: the item names one row (S35). The label is the label of a document tab's item. A click shows the Files tab, opens each parent folder and a closed vault row, scrolls to the row and flashes it for 3 seconds (`tree__row--revealed`, `SIDEBAR_REVEAL_MS`); a folder row opens itself too (S29, S31, S36). It opens no tab, does not change the active document, selects no row, and changes neither the focus list nor the favorites (S30, S36). If the row is gone the notice says `Can't show "<name>" in Files — it is no longer there` (S32, S37). From the Search tab the text stays (S33). It moves NO keyboard focus: the keyboard's two ways to the same reveal — Enter on a folder of the search and ⇧⏎ on a row — put the focus on the row too (YAZ-2662 🔒 D1, D8, S12: the request's `focus`). WHY first: the row is the reason for the right-click, and the item writes nothing to disk, which is the rule of the Open/View group. WHY on Focus and Favorites: a favorite or a focus item can be deep in the tree, and from those tabs there was no way to see where it is. RULES IT AMENDS: YAZ-2050 🔒 D1 (the menu of a search row was the SAME as the menu of its row in Files) and the same-menu rule of YAZ-1766 and YAZ-2619 (a row of Favorites and a row of Focus carried the same menu as the row in Files). Each is now that menu plus this one item. Refused: the item lower in the menu, or in the "Open in ▸" flyout (it is harder to find there). HOW: `MenuTargets.showPath` — its OWN field, set in `openMenu` when `lens !== 'files'` and the right-click is outside a plural selection — the `showInSidebar` leaf that leads `OPEN_GROUP` in `menuSections.ts`, and `MenuHandlers.onShowInSidebar`, which is `onRevealInFiles` (App's `revealInFiles`: `changeLens('files')` and the reveal request the tab menu uses). Files: `client/src/sidebar/{Sidebar,menuSections}.ts(x)` + `hooks/{useSidebarSearch,rowGestures}.ts`, `client/src/App.tsx`, `client/src/lib/focusHandoff.ts`, `shared/types.ts` (`SidebarTab`, `SIDEBAR_TABS`), `client/src/app.css`; tests in `Sidebar.test.tsx` ("the Search tab (YAZ-2638 D2)", `"Show in sidebar" on a row of Search, Focus and Favorites (YAZ-2638 D1, D3)`, "lens tabs"), `menuSections.test.ts` (`"Show in sidebar" item (YAZ-2638 D1, D3)`), `App.test.tsx` ("S15 (YAZ-2638)", "S16 (YAZ-2638)"); end to end in `desktop/e2e/search.spec.ts` (steps 1 and 5 to 8) and `desktop/e2e/lenses.spec.ts`, each written and not run.

**Several vaults** (YAZ-2602 🔒 D3–D5, R2, R5, R9, R11, cases S10–S28 as amended by A1–A7 and A9, and by YAZ-2631 🔒 D1 and D4–D6, which overturn D5, S16, S24, S26 and the "does not drag" of S14 — the window's half is "Multi-window": Several vaults in one window): with ONE vault the sidebar is exactly as it was — no vault row, the tree at the top (S11). THE VAULT ROWS (🔒 D3): with two or more each vault is ONE top row of the Files tab, in the window's order (the order added, or the order a drag gave) — `useVaultTree`'s `forest`, a `dir` node per vault whose children are that vault's tree and whose path is the vault's root (trailing slash off), named by the vault's display name, else its folder name (S12); a vault whose tree has not landed has no row yet. `vaultRows` (path → name) tells `Tree` which rows they are: `.tree__row--vault`, the label in the header's weight, and NO page — a double click and Enter do not open one as a tab, they fold it. Rejected: always showing the row (a window with one vault pays nothing), and one panel per vault with its own header. THEY START OPEN (R9): a vault row is open unless the user closed it, and a closed one stays closed for the SESSION only — App's `closedVaults`, in neither `expanded` nor the store, and App's because the Sidebar unmounts while hidden. A tab switch does not open a closed vault row; a gesture that SHOWS a row does (`openTo`: a reveal, a create, a paste). "COLLAPSE ALL" AND THE VAULT ROWS (YAZ-2631 🔒 D6, cases S56–S62): on the Files tab with two or more vaults the button closes each folder AND each vault row, and "Expand all" opens them all — one button, one rule (`foldVaults`: the folders through the one `setAll` dispatch, the vault rows through App's `closedVaults`). It reads "Collapse all" while any folder or any vault row is open, so one vault row opened again is enough (S58), and it shows on Files also when no vault holds a folder (S59). A vault row is still in no `dirs` list and is never stored as an open folder (S62), and its closed state stays for the session and the window alone (R9). On the Focus tab and the Favorites tab the button acts on that tab's folders alone and leaves the vault rows of Files as they were (S60), and with one vault it works as it did (S61). Rejected: "Collapse all" closes the vault rows and "Expand all" opens folders only (one button with two rules). "Show in sidebar" opens the row's vault and its folders and flashes the row, asked of the tree of the vault that holds it (S17). THE VAULT ROW'S MENU (S13 as amended by A2): [Paste · Copy path] · [New note ▸ · New drawing ▸ · New folder ▸ (YAZ-3085)] · [Open in ▸ — VS Code, Reveal in Finder] · [Remove from this window]; each create and the paste land in that vault's root, by that vault's kind. A vault row is not opened, cut, copied, renamed, deleted, favorited, reviewed, given a shortcut — and has NO focus item (🔒 A2: you add its folders or files; an item for a vault root would have no row in a window with one vault). A selection may hold rows of two vaults (S18), and one that holds a vault row offers no plural item, no Cut and no Copy (A3). BLANK SPACE: with one vault it is the vault's root, as before, and its "Open in ▸" group ends with "Add vault to this window ▸"; with two or more it is no one vault's — its menu is "Add vault to this window ▸" ALONE (S10), and `⌘V` with no selection pastes nothing and says `Select a vault or a folder first`. THE HEADER (S14, S15): the trigger names the vaults or the workspace ("Multi-window": Open beside), and with two or more vaults it is no drop target — a file dropped on a vault row moves to THAT vault's root, when the file is in that vault (R11: a drag to a different vault is refused, with the notice that names cut and paste). THE VAULT ROWS REORDER (YAZ-2631 🔒 D5, cases S45, S50–S52): a vault row drags over the top half or the bottom half of a different vault row, the 2px accent line shows on that edge, and the drop hands App the vaults in the new order (`onReorderVaults` → `reorderVaults` — "Multi-window": Reorder the vaults) — `Tree.reorder` on the Files tree, which it has only with two or more vaults. A file dropped on a vault row still moves to that vault's root and shows the fill of a drop folder, never the line (S50); a vault row dropped on a row below a vault row changes nothing (S51); the vault rows of the search tree do not reorder (S52). Known and accepted: on an OPEN vault row the line of an "after" drop shows under the row itself, above that vault's files, and the row still lands after that vault. THE FOCUS TAB ACROSS VAULTS (A1–A7, amending D4, and as amended by YAZ-2702 🔒 Decisions 1 and 3, which overturn A5): each vault of the window has its OWN focus list, kept in the vault, and the tab shows them as ONE flat list — `focusList` in `useVaultTree.ts` is `favoriteOrder(roots, focusByRoot, focusOrder)`, the Favorites tab's rule: `focusOrder` ("App state") says which vault has each place, each vault fills its places in the order of its own list, and an item with no place goes after the placed ones, in vault order (A1, A4; YAZ-2631 D3); `focusNodes` resolves it over the forest. "Add to focus" / "Remove from focus" work on a row of any vault and on a selection across vaults (A7): each path goes to the list of the vault that holds it, so a selection across two vaults is one write for each vault (YAZ-2702 S2). With two or more vaults each TOP row of the tab, file or folder, shows the name of the vault that holds it (`.tree__vault` — THE VAULT NAME, below); with one vault no row shows it. A vault that leaves the window takes its ROWS off the tab and keeps its list — nothing is written — and its rows are there again when it comes back (YAZ-2702 S8, S9); main repairs a rename and a delete in the vault's file; nothing is pruned here, so an item whose tree has not landed, or whose file is not on this Mac, has no row and stays in the list (S13), and the tab shows "Loading…" and not its empty text until EVERY vault's tree is in (`loaded`). "New note" on the tab hops to Files when its folder is a vault's root: Focus never holds a vault row. FAVORITES ACROSS VAULTS (YAZ-2631 🔒 D1, rules R1–R5, R13–R18, R23 and R25, cases S1–S20, overturning YAZ-2602 D5, S24 and S26): each vault KEEPS its own `.yaseendocs/favorites.json`, so the favorites still travel with the vault through sync. With two or more vaults the tab is ONE flat list across the vaults of the window — no vault row (S2) — and each top row shows its vault's name (THE VAULT NAME, below). THE ORDER is `favoritePaths` = `favoriteOrder(roots, favoritesByRoot, storedOrder)`: the stored order across vaults, `AppState.favoritesOrder` ("App state"), says which VAULT has each place, and each vault fills its places in the order of its own file, so a synced file still wins inside its vault (R2, S8); a favorite with no place goes after the placed ones, in vault order and then in its file's order (R13 — so with no stored order the list is in vault order, S3, and a new favorite is not always the last row, S6); with one vault it is that vault's file order, whatever the store holds (S1). The rows are `favoriteRoots(forest, favoritePaths)`, the Focus tab's rule: a favorite whose file is not on this machine draws no row and stays in its vault's file (S9), and a favorite inside a favorited folder shows as a top row and inside its parent (S16). A DRAG moves a favorite to any place of the list, between the rows of any vault (S4 — Drag in the tree, below), and is `saveFavoriteOrder(next)`: each vault's file gets its own part of the new order, only when that part changed (R3, S5), and then, where the window has two or more vaults, the store gets the order across vaults once (`storage.setFavoritesOrder(read, next)`, R4 — `read` is the vaults whose list this window has read, so a vault whose `favorites.get` has not answered keeps its places, R25) — each write is whole alone, so a crash between them leaves a valid list. A file that refuses the write (malformed → `INVALID_CONFIG`) puts THAT vault's list back with the notice `Can't save favorites: …`, while the store keeps the new order across vaults, which stays valid because each vault fills its places from its own file (S15, R16). The cache holds the new order at once (R15), and a drag in another window that shows these vaults lands here through `storage.subscribe` (S12). "Add to favorites" writes to the file of the vault that holds the row — the path goes to the end of that file — a selection across two vaults writes one file per vault, and the notice counts every row (S17; YAZ-2602 S25); "Remove from favorites" takes the row and the others keep their order (S7), and takes the removed paths out of the store's order where that order holds one, so the same favorite added again goes last (R23); "Add to favorites" does not write the store (R13). A vault that leaves the window takes its rows, and the store keeps their places for when it comes back (S14). A vault row closed on the Files tab hides none of that vault's favorites (R18), "Expand all" and "Collapse all" act on the favorited folders (S18), and "New note" on a top file row hops to Files as on Focus, since neither tab holds a vault row (R17). With no favorite that exists in any vault the tab shows its empty text (S20). A `favorites:changed` for a vault of the window re-reads that vault's list (S27). Rejected: the order in the window identity (a new window with the same vaults loses it); a flat list with no stored order (a drag works inside one vault only). The Favorites tab has no focus of its own (A6, YAZ-2619). THE VAULT NAME (YAZ-2631 🔒 D4, cases S41–S44): with two or more vaults each top row of the Focus tab and of the Favorites tab, file or folder, shows the name of the vault that holds it — `.tree__vault`: 10px, the muted colour at 60%, at the right edge of the row, 40% of the row at most with an ellipsis, so the row's own name has the rest. A vault row of Files shows none, a deeper row shows none, and with one vault no row shows one. WHY on Favorites too: without it two files with one name look the same in a flat list. Rejected: the name only on hover; a second line below the row's name. SEARCH ACROSS VAULTS (R2, 🔒 A9 amending S38): the bar covers every vault of the window — one index feed per vault, ONE ranking over the matches of all of them (`useSearchResults(vaults, query, pinned)`) — and the tree that is cut is the forest: each match stands under its vault's row, which is a PARENT row like any folder, dim, never a match, open over its matches whatever its fold on the Files tab, and with the Files vault-row menu plus "Show in sidebar" first (YAZ-2638 S26). A match of a pinned item stands in the search's TOP GROUP instead, under its pinned item — a top row that names its vault, as on the Favorites tab, the focus items of every vault before the favorites — and "Everything else" keeps its vault rows; a vault whose matches are all pinned has no row there (YAZ-2662 S26). A vault row is never the highlight, so no list key acts on it (YAZ-2662 S55), and Enter on a folder of a vault whose row is closed on Files opens the vault row first (YAZ-2662 S9). `SEARCH_CAP` (50) counts the matches of all the vaults together; inside one rank the first vault's rows lead, and the pinned matches of every vault go before each other match and are cut last (YAZ-2662 🔒 D4). The flat row that named its vault in muted text is gone with the flat list (YAZ-2620). PER VAULT IN THE ROW RULES: a row's shortcut rows, review state, IDs (`shortcutDir`, the Rename input's mode), delete count and link rewrite all read the vault that holds the row (`vaultOf` / `rootOf`), and "Open in ▸ New window" opens that vault alone. Files: `client/src/sidebar/{Sidebar,Tree,VaultSwitcher,menuSections,vaultMenuSections}.ts(x)` + `hooks/{useVaultTree,rowGestures,useSidebarSearch}.ts`, `client/src/lib/treeState.ts` (`favoriteOrder`), `client/src/lib/storage.ts` (`getFavoritesOrder`, `setFavoritesOrder`), `shared/types.ts` (`mergeFavoritesOrder`, `MAX_FAVORITES_ORDER`), `client/src/search/useSearchResults.ts`, `client/src/app.css` (`.tree__row--vault`, `.tree__vault`); tests in `Sidebar.test.tsx` ("several vaults in one window"), `menuSections.test.ts` ("the vault items"), `treeState.test.ts` (`favoriteOrder`), `storage.test.ts` (`storage.getFavoritesOrder / setFavoritesOrder`), `store.test.ts` (`favoritesOrder`), `ipc/state.test.ts` (`state:set-favorites-order`), `search/useSearchResults.test.tsx` ("over several vaults"); end to end steps 1 to 5 and 7 of `desktop/e2e/multiVault.spec.ts` and the whole of `desktop/e2e/sidebarOrder.spec.ts`, each written and not run.

**Plain DOM, no virtualization** (🔒 D6): every row of an expanded directory is mounted. `TableView`'s windowing is deliberately not taken here — a tree's mounted set is bounded by what the USER opened.

**The Focus tab** (YAZ-2619, 🔒 D1–D5, cases S1–S40, rules R1–R20 on the issue; it REPLACES the Focus Mode of YAZ-1605 / YAZ-1628 and the Favorites tab's own focus of YAZ-1766 D5 — nothing narrows a lens now, and the Files tab always shows the full vault, S40. WHERE THE LIST LIVES is YAZ-2702's, 🔒 Decisions 1, 3 and 4, cases S1–S17 on YAZ-2703: the list is the VAULT's, kept in the vault. That OVERTURNS YAZ-1628 D1 and YAZ-2619 D1 (the list is the window's), YAZ-2619 S25 (two windows on one vault each keep their own), S27 (a root change clears it), R13 with S31 (the renderer prunes an item the tree does not hold) and the line "Not included: a list shared between windows or machines", and YAZ-2602 A5 (a vault that leaves takes its items). Nothing changed in how the tab LOOKS): the second lens, the eye — the third tab, since YAZ-2638 D2 put Search second — shows a list the user builds. THE LIST (YAZ-2702 🔒 Decision 1) is ONE list for each VAULT, kept IN THE VAULT — `<vault>/.yaseendocs/focus.<mac id>.json`, one file for each Mac, the newest file being the list (Decision 2; the `focus.get/set/onChanged` bridge row has the file's rules R1–R13): vault-relative paths on disk, absolute paths on the bridge, files AND folders, in the order added or the order a drag gave (YAZ-2631 D3), `MAX_FOCUS` (500) at most FOR EACH VAULT (S5). WHY in the vault: it is the only place that makes focus the same on each Mac, and a window is forgotten — closed beside another window, not brought back by a launch, changed to a different vault — where a vault is not. So two windows on one vault show the same list and a change in one shows in the other at once (S7); a new window and a duplicate (⌘⇧N) show the vault's list (S10); the list stays after a quit, a closed window, and a change to a different vault and back (S8); a sync that brings a newer file changes the tab at once, with no restart (S12). The window holds NO focus list: `WindowEntry.focusList` / `WindowIdentity.focusList` are gone, with `storage.getFocusList` / `setFocusList`, and nothing was migrated (Decision 4 — the first launch of the new build shows an empty tab, S16; "App state": `windows`). IN THE RENDERER the list is `focusByRoot` in `client/src/sidebar/hooks/useVaultTree.ts`, held by the hook that holds `favoritesByRoot` (`useVaultLists(kind)` — one code path for the two lists a vault keeps): ONE read for each vault of the window when it joins (`api.focus.get`), ONE more on each `focus:changed` for a vault of the window — an own write's echo, another window's write, or a file that a sync brought — and none for a different vault; a vault that leaves the window drops its entry, so its rows leave the tab, and its file is not written (S9). ONE writer of a vault's list (`save`): optimistic, then `api.focus.set`; a write that main refuses puts that vault's list back and shows "Can't save focus: <reason>" in the `error` kind (S14). The panel writes nothing back on its own — no effect mirrors the list anywhere. THE FLAT LIST the tab draws is `focusList = favoriteOrder(roots, focusByRoot, focusOrder)` (`client/src/lib/treeState.ts`), with `focusOrder` the store's order across vaults (🔒 Decision 3 — "App state": `focusOrder`); with one vault it is that vault's list. Every reader works off this flat list: the rows, the count line, the menu's `focusIsOn`, the search's pinned items and the drag. THE MENU ITEM (D3) is one state-aware rule, the favorite toggle's: the `focus` leaf in `menuSections.ts` CLOSES the Open group (R6 — on a single file row it is that group's one item) on every file or dir row in every lens and on a search row, never blank space (R7); its OWN targets `MenuTargets.focusPaths` (the row, or the ordered 2+ selection holding it; a shortcut row gives the note's real path, R8) and `focusIsOn` (true only when EVERY target is in the list, read ONCE when the menu opens — a mixed selection reads "Add" and the add puts in only the missing ones, R9, S4); the label is "Add to focus" / "Remove from focus" and counts a plural ("Add 3 to focus"). `toggleFocus(paths, isOn)` in `useVaultTree.ts` — the favorite toggle's code, `toggleIn` — sends each path to the list of the vault that holds it, so a selection across two vaults is one write for each vault (YAZ-2702 S1, S2): it removes every path, or appends the ones not yet listed in the order given and keeps the first `MAX_FOCUS` of that vault (R2, S5), and it writes a vault's list only when the list changed. A remove also takes its paths out of `focusOrder`, where that order holds one (S3). When the list of a vault that holds a target has NOT been read yet in this window, the toggle writes nothing and shows "Focus is still loading. Try again." in the `error` kind (S6 — a write would replace the list on disk; the rule of YAZ-2631 R26). A folder just added is opened with the synthetic-child `expandTo`, a file opens nothing (R4); the notice is "Added to focus" / "Added N to focus" / "Removed from focus" / "Removed N from focus" in the plain `info` kind (R3, R15 — never the `favorite` kind, which draws a heart), or, when the add goes past the limit, "Focus limit reached: 500 items" in the `error` kind (R16, S12). THE TAB CHANGE: an ADD shows the Focus tab (D3 — `onToggleFocus` in `Sidebar.tsx` calls `onLensChange('focus')`, also when the limit cut the add to nothing, and not again when the tab is already Focus, R17 — and NOT from the Search tab, which stays: YAZ-2638 🔒 D2, S20, overturns D3 for a search row); a remove and "Clear" keep the tab (R5); the lens change clears the row selection, as every lens change does (R12). SEARCH KEEPS ITS TEXT (S11, as amended by YAZ-2638 🔒 D2): the toggle is not a `viaTree` item, so an add from a search row changes the list and the Search tab stays, with its text and its results, to add more results (YAZ-2638 S20 — before, the add changed the active tab under the results). Esc goes back to the lens the window last showed, and the text stays (before, Esc cleared the query). Search is a tab of its own and covers the full vault (S23). The focus items and the favorites are the search's PINNED ITEMS: their matches show first there, the focus items before the favorites, and an add or a remove on a search row moves the row between the search's two groups at once (YAZ-2662 🔒 D2, D3, S27 — The search from the keyboard, above). THE ROWS (D2): `favoriteRoots(tree, focusList)` — over the forest, where the window shows two or more vaults (YAZ-2602 A1) — the heart tab's rule: one node per stored path via `findNode`, the list's order, nesting KEPT (an item inside a focused folder draws as a top row AND inside its parent, S7–S9) — into the same `Tree`, the same `expanded` set and the same menu, plus "Show in sidebar" FIRST on each row (YAZ-2638 🔒 D3, S34 — "Show in sidebar" on a row, above; it amends the same-menu rule here). DRAG (YAZ-2631 🔒 D3, cases S26–S28 and S39, overturning S37 for a TOP row — Drag in the tree, below): a top row, file or folder, drags to a new place in the list — between the rows of any vault, where the window shows two or more — and moves nothing on disk; the writer is `reorderFocus`, by the rule of `saveFavoriteOrder` and through the same helper (`saveOrder`): each vault's file gets its own part of the new order, only when that part changed, and `focusOrder` gets the order across the vaults, only where the window has two or more, for the vaults whose list this window has read (YAZ-2702 S11) — so a drag inside one vault writes that vault's file alone, the order inside a vault travels with the vault, and the new order survives a tab change and a restart (S27). A file INSIDE a focused folder drags into a folder and moves on disk, as on Files (the tab's `move` is `fileMove`); an item that shows on both levels does each (S39). Above the rows sits THE COUNT LINE (D4, `.sidebar__focus-bar`): "N in focus" on the left — N is the number of top rows on screen, `focusNodes.length` (R11) — and "Clear" on the right (`.sidebar__focus-clear` → `clearFocus`: one click empties the list of EACH vault of the window that has items, one write for each such vault, and takes those vaults' places out of `focusOrder` — S17; YAZ-2702 S4: the change goes to each window and each Mac); the line is absent with an empty list, and the Search tab has none (S19, S20). An empty list shows "Nothing in focus. Right-click a file or folder → Add to focus." (S15), and the tab shows the tree error and "Loading…" as the other two do (R20). The expand/collapse-all button acts on the folders this tab shows (`bodyDirs` = `focusDirs`, `allDirs(focusNodes)`, R10) and is gone when it shows none (S21). NO PRUNE (YAZ-2702 S13, which overturns R13 and S31): an item the tree does not hold draws no row (`favoriteRoots`) and STAYS in the list — its file may simply not have synced to this Mac yet, and a prune here would take it out of the list on every Mac (Favorites' D14). The count line counts the rows, so it can be lower than the list; a tab whose items all have no row shows the empty message. The LIST is repaired in main: an in-app rename or delete moves or drops the entry in the vault's file (`focus.ts`, R10), and a write drops each entry whose path is not on disk (R7). THE CREATE RULE (S35, S36, R18, R19 — `startCreate` in `hooks/rowGestures.ts`, ONE rule for the two list tabs): "New note" / "New folder" on a folder the tab shows mounts the input inside that folder, on the tab; a target dir the tab does not hold, or the vault root on a tab with no rows, hops to Files first; the vault root on a tab that HAS rows mounts the input at the top of the tab — the new note opens as a tab, and its row does not stay, since it is not in the list. "Show in sidebar" goes to Files from any tab and never changes the list (S34 — the old "a reveal outside the focus exits it" went with the narrowing): a document tab's item and, since YAZ-2638 🔒 D3, the first item of each row's menu on this tab. Not included: a keyboard shortcut for the tab, a keyboard gesture to reorder the list, a focus item on blank space, a merge of two focus lists that two Macs changed while offline (the newest list is the list), and a migration of the lists the windows held before YAZ-2702. Focus across several vaults in one window was not included here and is built since YAZ-2602 (A1–A7: ONE flat list on the tab, over the own list of each vault of the window — Several vaults, above). Files: `shared/types.ts` (`MAX_FOCUS`, `SidebarLens`, `FocusConfig`, `AppState.focusOrder`), `shared/ipc.ts` (`focus.*`, `state.setFocusOrder`), `desktop/src/main/focus.ts` + `ipc/{focus,fs,state}.ts`, `desktop/src/main/store.ts` (`focusOrder`), `client/src/lib/storage.ts` (`getFocusOrder`, `setFocusOrder`), `client/src/lib/treeState.ts` (`favoriteRoots`, `favoriteOrder`, `findNode`), `client/src/sidebar/{Sidebar,menuSections}.ts(x)` + `hooks/{useVaultTree,rowGestures}.ts`, `client/src/app.css`; tests in `Sidebar.test.tsx` (`focus tab (YAZ-2619)`, and the Focus cases of `several vaults in one window (YAZ-2602)`), `menuSections.test.ts`, `treeState.test.ts`, `storage.test.ts`, `store.test.ts`, `ipc/state.test.ts`, `focus.test.ts`, `ipc/focus.test.ts` — and `windows.test.ts`, `ipc/window.test.ts`, which hold that a window has no focus list; end to end in `desktop/e2e/focus.spec.ts` (rewritten for YAZ-2702 without being run).

**The Favorites tab** (YAZ-1766, 🔒 D1–D10 on the issue; D11–D15 in 6A–6C): the third lens, the heart — the fourth tab, since YAZ-2638 D2 put Search second — shows the vault's pinned files and folders — of every vault of the window, as ONE flat list, when it shows two or more (YAZ-2631 D1 — Several vaults, above; everything below is ONE vault's list). THE LIST is `<root>/.yaseendocs/favorites.json` (D11 — it moved out of `FolderState` in 6A, D15: a clean break, no migration) — VAULT-RELATIVE POSIX paths on disk, absolute over the bridge (`favorites.get/set/onChanged`), so it TRAVELS WITH THE VAULT and GitHub sync carries it between machines; shared by every window on the vault (a second window's — or another machine's — write arrives through `favorites:changed` and a re-read), in the user's order: add appends, drag-to-reorder rewrites. The Sidebar has ONE writer of a vault's file, `saveFavorites(vault, next)`: optimistic, then `favorites.set`; a refusal (a malformed file → `INVALID_CONFIG`, D12) reverts that vault's list and toasts an error. A drag reaches it through `saveFavoriteOrder`, which writes a vault's file only when that vault's own order changed (YAZ-2631 R3). THE MENU ITEM (D3) is one state-aware rule, `toggleFavorite`, LEADING the "Open in ▸" group (… Rename · ─ · Add to favorites · Add note shortcut (a folder row, YAZ-2290) · Open in ▸ · ─ · Delete) on every file or dir row in every lens, never blank space; its OWN targets `MenuTargets.favoritePaths` (the row, or the ordered 2+ selection holding it) and `favoriteIsOn` (true only when EVERY target is pinned — a mixed selection reads "Add" and pins the missing ones); the label counts a plural ("Add 3 to favorites"), and the toast (`'favorite'` kind, the same heart) says "Added / Removed N to/from favorites". THE ROWS: `favoriteRoots(tree, list)` in `treeState.ts` — one node per stored path via `findNode` (file OR dir), STORED order, nesting and redundancy KEPT (a file pinned inside a pinned folder draws at the root AND inside it; the Focus tab draws its own list with this same function, YAZ-2619 D2); a path the tree no longer holds yields no row and NOTHING ELSE — there is no renderer prune (D14): a note that has not synced to this machine yet simply does not show until it arrives, in-app rename/delete repair the file in main (D13), and main heals dead entries on the user's next write. A pinned folder unfolds through the SAME `expanded` set as Files (D7) — open here, open there. DRAG (D4, as amended by YAZ-2631 🔒 D3 — Drag in the tree, below): top rows carry `Tree.reorder` (depth 0 only) — ALWAYS on, since the tab has no focus list of its own (YAZ-2619 S39: the tab's own focus of YAZ-1766 D5, which made reorder inert while it stood, is removed): a 2px accent line on the hovered row's edge (`.tree__row--drop-before/after`), drop rewrites the list and moves nothing on disk. Below the top rows the tab's `move` is `fileMove`: a file inside a favorited folder drags into a folder and moves on disk, as on Files, and a folder there does not drag. THE SUBSET RULE (D10, 3B1): the tab shows a subset of the vault, so a gesture that needs a row it lacks goes to Files — "Show in sidebar" hops the lens and reveals there (`App.showInSidebar`, a document tab's item; since YAZ-2638 🔒 D3 each row of this tab has the item too, FIRST in its menu — `App.revealInFiles`, "Show in sidebar" on a row, above — so a row's menu here is the menu of its row in Files plus this one item, and a click never changes the list), and "New note" / "New folder" from a row whose target dir is not on the tab hops before the inline input mounts (`startCreate`) — ONE create rule with the Focus tab, so on an EMPTY ♥ tab "New note" on the blank space hops to Files too (YAZ-2619 R19; before, the input had no place to show). Search is a tab of its own (YAZ-2638 🔒 D2): this tab has no search bar, and a typed query never replaces its body. Not in v1: reordering nested rows, a shortcut. Files: `desktop/src/main/favorites.ts` (the file, the repair) + `desktop/src/main/ipc/favorites.ts` (the bridge half, the per-root subscription and broadcast), `desktop/src/main/ipc/fs.ts` (the repair calls), `client/src/api.ts` (`api.favorites`), `client/src/lib/treeState.ts` (`findNode`, `favoriteRoots`), `client/src/sidebar/{Sidebar,Tree,menuSections}.ts(x)`, `client/src/views/view/icons.tsx` (`HeartIcon`), `client/src/components/NoticeIcon.tsx`, `client/src/lib/notice.ts`, `shared/types.ts` (`MAX_FAVORITES`, `FavoritesConfig`); tests `favorites.test.ts`, `ipc/favorites.test.ts`, `ipc/fs.test.ts`, `treeState.test.ts`, `menuSections.test.ts`, `Sidebar.test.tsx` (`favorites (YAZ-1766)`), `store.test.ts`, `ipc/window.test.ts`, `windows.test.ts`.

**The Sessions tab** (YAZ-3147 🔒 D4, D6, cases S12–S15 and S28–S37 on the working log YAZ-3149 — the data is "App state": `sessions`, the restore is "Multi-window": Sessions): the fifth tab, right of Favorites, a stack glyph (`StackIcon`) named "Sessions" in `title` and `aria-label`. A STORED lens, like Focus and Favorites: `SidebarLens` has `'sessions'`, so the tab stays selected after `⌘R` and a restart (S35), and main's lens check names it. It is not a reading of a vault: it shows the app's saved sessions, so it has no file tree, no expand-all button, no drag, and its blank space has no menu. Rejected: a section in the vault switcher under Workspaces. The body is `client/src/sidebar/SessionList.tsx`. It reads `storage.getSessions()` through `useSyncExternalStore`; the cache answers the same array until the sessions change — a broadcast for anything else keeps the held array, as the two orders do — so the list renders again only then, and each row is memo, so a fold, a menu or the name field of one row does not render the others. ON TOP the Focus tab's line (`.sidebar__focus-bar`): "N sessions" ("1 session", "No sessions") and **Save open tabs**; with no session one help line follows, `Save your open tabs as a session. Restore them later in one click.` (S37). THE ROWS, last used first, main's order (no drag): a plain list, not a `tree` (the sidebar's arrow keys walk file rows only; Tab reaches each row). A session row is a `.tree__row` button with `aria-expanded`, a chevron, the name and the count on the right ("1 tab", "4 tabs", "0 tabs" — a session with no tab stays, S31). A click folds or unfolds it. Two clicks ON THE NAME, at most `RENAME_CLICK_GAP_MS` (300 ms) apart — tighter than the Mac's double-click time, so quick clicks to fold and unfold do not rename (Yaseen, guided test) — open the name field (`TextField`, `normalize={cleanVaultName}`, `maxLength={MAX_VAULT_NAME}`, the name selected): `⏎` saves through `window.renameSession`, `Esc` keeps the name, a blank name is refused and the old name shows again, a name past 80 characters is cut (S12–S15); a session row is no file, so the double-click clashes with nothing. Right-click: **Restore session**, **Update with open tabs**, **Rename** (the same field, S14), then **Delete session** in a group of its own (`danger`), which asks with the app's sheet — `Delete "<name>"?` / `Your files and open tabs do not change.`, Delete / Cancel — and then calls `window.removeSession` (S32). Unfolded, a TAB ROW shows the tab's display name, else its page's name (`pageLabel`, as the tab strip names it), and the name of its vault on the right (`.tree__vault`); a click opens the page as a click on a tree row does — `openCurrent`, the preview tab — and the session does not change (S33); its one menu item, **Remove from session**, sends the tabs that stay to `window.setSessionTabs` (a copy by its place in the list), and the file and the open tabs do not change (S30). Every change is main's, so the other windows show it at once (S36). Proof: `client/src/sidebar/SessionList.test.tsx`, `client/src/sidebar/Sidebar.test.tsx` ("lens tabs": the Sessions tab), `desktop/src/main/ipc/window.test.ts` (the lens check).

**The Recents tab** (YAZ-3235 🔒 D3–D7, cases S13–S22 on the working log YAZ-3236 — the data is "App state": `folders[root].edits`): the sixth tab, right of Sessions, a clock glyph (`ClockIcon`) named "Recents" in `title` and `aria-label`. A STORED lens, like Sessions: `SidebarLens` has `'recents'`, so the tab stays selected after `⌘R` and a restart, an older build reads it as unknown and opens Files, and main's lens check names it (S13). It is not a reading of a vault tree: it lists the files that the app saved last, so it has no expand-all button, no drag, and its blank space has no menu (S20). Rejected: the disk time (`mtime`) of each file — a pull gives each file that it writes the time of the pull, so the edits of the other Mac jump to the top (D1); the `liveTimes` flag of YAZ-3227 (D2, dropped: the save log is live already, each logged save is a broadcast of the app state). The body is `client/src/sidebar/RecentList.tsx` (memo), over the pure `client/src/sidebar/recents.ts`. **The list** (`recentFiles(trees, roots, edits)`, D3, S14, S22): the save logs of the window's vaults, `storage.getEdits(root)` for each, as ONE list. A logged file draws a row only while the tree of its vault has it as a FILE that the app opens (`kind !== null`): the set of those files is read once per tree (a `WeakMap` by `TreeResponse`, so a new tree is read again). Thus a folder, a file the app cannot open and a file that went outside the app draw no row; a vault with no tree yet adds nothing, and a vault the window does not show adds nothing. A file that two nested vaults logged is one row, at its newest save. Newest save first, then by path; `MAX_RECENTS` (200) at most, and at the limit the line `Showing the 200 newest files.` follows (S21). With no row: `Files you edit show here.` (S22), or `Loading…` while a vault of the window has no tree yet. **The snapshot:** the logs are read through `useSyncExternalStore(storage.subscribe, read)`, and `read` answers the SAME array until a log's content really changes — each app-state broadcast is a new copy of all the state, and `storage.getEdits` gives a new `{}` on each read for a vault with no folder entry, so a compare by identity would loop. Thus a tab click, a fold or a save in another vault's field draws nothing here. **The days** (`recentDays(files, now)`, D5, S15): one heading per local day (key `toDateString()`): `Today`, `Yesterday`, then `toLocaleDateString` with weekday, month and day ("Mon, Oct 20"), and the year only when it is not this year. A timer to the next local midnight, and a focus of the window (a timer can fire late after the Mac sleeps), draw the headings again: "Today" becomes "Yesterday" with no save and no click (S16); the timer goes with the list. A heading is a `.tree__row.recents__day` button with `aria-expanded` and a chevron: a click folds that day and a second click opens it; all days are open at mount, and the folds are not stored (S17). **A row** (D6, S18): a `.tree__row` button, indented under its day, with the page name (`pageLabel`, as a Files row names it) and the time of the save on the right (`timeOf`, `toLocaleTimeString` hour and minute, "3:42 PM", in `.tree__count`); `title` is the full path; the open file lights (`tree__row--active`). Rows are buttons in a plain list, not a `tree`: the sidebar's arrow keys walk file rows only. A click opens the file as a Files row does — `openCurrent`, the preview tab; a ⌘-click a background tab; a double-click keeps the tab (S19). A right-click opens the ONE-ROW file menu, "Show in sidebar" first, as a row of the new tab page does: the Sidebar's `recentMenu` calls `openMenuAt({ type: 'file', path }, x, y, true)` through a ref, so the memo list does not draw again on each selection (D7, S20). "Show in sidebar" shows the Files tab, unfolds to the file and lights it; its label comes from `menuSections.ts`, so the rename to "Show in files" (YAZ-3245) reaches this menu with no work here. Not included: a hover preview on a row, keyboard arrows inside the list, drag, a sort control, a "Clear" control. Proof: `client/src/sidebar/recents.test.ts`, `client/src/sidebar/RecentList.test.tsx`, `client/src/sidebar/Sidebar.test.tsx` ("lens tabs": the Recents tab; "a row menu asked for a path": a Recents row), `desktop/src/main/ipc/window.test.ts` (the lens check), `desktop/e2e/recents.spec.ts`.

**Drag in the tree: one rule for the three tabs** (YAZ-2631 🔒 D3, rules R8, R9, R20 and R24, cases S26–S40; it overturns YAZ-2619 S37 for a top row, and the "nested rows do not drag" of YAZ-1766 D4): a TOP row drags to REORDER, and a FILE inside a folder drags to MOVE on disk. Both lift only `LIFT_PX` (10 px) from the press (YAZ-3467 D1, D2). Since YAZ-3467 D2 the reorder is mouse events, not the HTML5 drag: the row's `dragstart` is stopped and arms it; after the lift a pill of the row's name (`dragPill`, `.tree__reorder-pill`) follows the pointer and the row stays in its place (D3); each held `mousemove` takes the row under the pointer (`.tree__row[data-reorder]`, a top row of a list that reorders) and its half for the line, and anything else takes no line; the release drops; Esc, the window's `blur` and a move with no button end it and save nothing. WHY: one rule is easy to learn, and it is the smallest code. Rejected: the rule for Focus alone, with a special case for Favorites; three drop zones on a folder row (a harder gesture). WHICH TREES REORDER: the ones that get `Tree`'s optional `reorder` (`TreeReorder`) — the Favorites tree and the Focus tree always, the Files tree only with two or more vaults, where its top rows are the vault rows. The Files tree of ONE vault gets none, so its top rows stay in name order and a file drag there moves on disk (S38); the search tree gets none and an inert `move` (`INERT_MOVE`), so no row there reorders and none moves on disk (S37). The gesture lives on depth 0 alone (`rowReorder`): the top level is the only one handed `reorder`, so a drag's line draws no level below again. A top row, FILE or FOLDER, dragged over the top half or the bottom half of a different top row puts a 2px accent line on that edge (`.tree__row--drop-before/after`, `edgeOf`) and never the fill of a drop folder (S40); the drop moves the row there — a top file over a top folder too, with nothing moved on disk (S29). BELOW THE TOP ROWS: a file drags as on Files — into a folder row, through the rename flow, with the links updated and nothing overwritten (S30), and refused between two vaults with `To move between vaults, use cut and paste` (S31) — since YAZ-3251 a folder drags too, as a file does (it overturns S32), a file dropped on a top FILE row changes nothing (S33), and a reorder drag shows no line on a deeper row, where a drop changes nothing (S34). A row dropped on itself changes nothing, and a drag that ends outside the list clears the line (S35); a shortcut row never drags (S36). ONE REORDER STATE (R8 — `useTreeDrag` in `hooks/rowGestures.ts`): the dragged top row, and the hovered row with its edge, for the tab that is shown; the Sidebar hands it the one list that tab reorders and its writer (`orderRef` / `saveOrder`) — every favorite of the window and `saveFavoriteOrder`, every focus item of the window and `reorderFocus` (the two are one helper, `saveOrder`, since YAZ-2702), or the vault roots and `onReorderVaults`. A drop that changes no order writes nothing — no vault file, no store order, no window identity, no saved workspace (R20: the guard is in `reorderGesture.drop`, `rowGestures.ts`, so it holds on each tab). A drop does nothing when the dragged row is not in the list of the tab that is shown (R24, in `reorderGesture.drop` too): a reorder that started on a different tab or tree, and is still in flight, clears and writes nothing — so no path of a favorite can land in the vault roots or in the focus list. A reorder hover changes one small state (the line's row and edge), only when that row or edge changes, and nothing else; a move hover changes no state at all (YAZ-3251 D2). Not included: a keyboard gesture to reorder, a drag of a file between two vaults (cut and paste does that). Files: `client/src/sidebar/Tree.tsx` (`TreeReorder`, `rowReorder`, `rowDrag`), `hooks/rowGestures.ts` (`useTreeDrag`), `Sidebar.tsx` (`orderRef`, `saveOrder`); tests in `Sidebar.test.tsx` (the YAZ-2631 cases under `focus tab (YAZ-2619)`, `favorites (YAZ-1766)` and "several vaults in one window"); end to end `desktop/e2e/sidebarOrder.spec.ts`, written and not run.

## Packaging (F1 — GRO-2175)

`npm run desktop:build` = electron-vite build + `electron-builder --mac` with the config in `desktop/package.json` `"build"`: appId `com.yasinarshad.yaseendocs`, productName `Yaseen Docs`, targets `dmg` + `dir` for arm64 ONLY, `identity: null` (ad-hoc signature — no Developer-ID, no notarization, locked), category productivity, icon `desktop/build/icon.icns` (placeholder). Output: `desktop/dist-app/mac-arm64/Yaseen Docs.app` + `desktop/dist-app/Yaseen Docs-0.1.0-arm64.dmg` (`${productName}-${version}-arm64.dmg` — the version is the ROOT package.json's, injected via `-c.extraMetadata.version`). `tools/packDesktop.mjs --mac` then recompresses electron-builder's zlib dmg to LZMA (ULMO, macOS 10.15+; −32 MB) in place, mounting the new image and verifying its app's seal before it replaces the old one, and deletes the stale `.blockmap` (nothing reads it — no auto-updater) (`tools/lib/dmg.mjs`, YAZ-2181). Its test, `tools/dmg.test.mjs`, drives the real `hdiutil` and `codesign` only when `YASEEN_DOCS_DMG_TEST=1`: `npm test` skips it, since every `desktop:build` already runs that path and checks the new image's seal.
