Before the ad-hoc signature, the `afterPack` hook (`desktop/build/adhocSign.cjs`) deletes Chromium's non-English `locale.pak` folders from the framework (Windows: all but `locales/en-US.pak` + `en-GB.pak`), −47.6 MB installed; the app-level `Contents/Resources/*.lproj` markers stay, so Open/Save panels keep the OS language, while on a non-English macOS sorting and dates follow en-US (🔒 YAZ-2131 D1, YAZ-2182). The bundle's Info.plist claims: `protocols` registers the `yaseendocs` scheme, and since YAZ-3028 D7 Draw's `yaseendraw`, with LaunchServices (so OS-level link opens route to the app), and `fileAssociations` lists `.md`/`.markdown` with role Editor, rank **Alternate** — Yaseen Docs appears in Finder's Open With but never steals the default handler. `.excalidraw` ("Excalidraw Drawing") and `.drawio` ("draw.io Diagram") are Editor, rank **Owner** (YAZ-3028 D7): a double-click opens Docs. With Draw also installed, macOS picks the default. Packaged files are `out/**` only, and `app.asar` carries NO `node_modules`: every dependency is bundled into `out/main` — electron-vite 5 externalizes `desktop/package.json`'s `dependencies` by default, so chokidar is a devDependency and main/preload set `externalizeDeps: false`; `tools/mainBundle.test.mjs` fails if the bundle requires anything but Node built-ins and electron (YAZ-2185). The renderer is esbuild-minified with `sourcemap: 'hidden'` maps (no `sourceMappingURL`), and `renderSourcemapsAside()` moves every `.map` to the gitignored `desktop/.maps/<version>/` as the bundle is written, so none ships and a minified stack can still be symbolicated locally; main, preload and the cli stay unminified (YAZ-2183). No auto-update, no Intel/universal, no Windows/Linux (locked — Future issues).


**Size and integrity gate (YAZ-2131 1B).** `npm run perf:budget` measures the build against `tools/perf/budget.json` and exits 1 when a row crosses its ceiling or an integrity check fails. Rows: packaged `appBytes`, `frameworksBytes`, `asarBytes`, `dmgBytes`, `chromiumLocaleCount`/`chromiumLocaleBytes`, `lprojCount` (exactly 55: the app-level markers that keep Open/Save panels in the OS language), `asarNodeModulesFiles`; build `rendererEagerJsBytes`/`rendererEagerCssBytes` (the entry's static-import closure + its stylesheet), `rendererTotalBytes`, `rendererMapBytes`, `mainBundleBytes`. Integrity: `out/main/{index,cli}.js`, `out/preload/index.js`, `out/renderer/index.html` exist (and are in the asar); every `./x.js|css` a renderer chunk names is shipped (a lazy Mermaid or CodeMirror chunk that went missing would only fail on first use); KaTeX and the drawing fonts are present; Info.plist carries `yaseendocs` and `yaseendraw`, `.md` as Editor/Alternate, and `.excalidraw` and `.drawio` as Editor/Owner (`plistFails`); the bundle is ad-hoc sealed and `codesign --verify --deep --strict` passes; `Resources/bin/yaseendocs` is executable. `drawingAssetBytes` (`out/renderer/excalidraw-assets`) is reported on its own row and never gated: the drawing component is out of scope. **The ratchet:** a change that shrinks a row lowers its ceiling in `budget.json` in the same PR; raising a ceiling needs Yasin's OK in the PR description. `tools/perf/baseline.json` is the frozen v0.9.27 @ 63aeeea measurement every before/after quotes, and is never edited. Since YAZ-3028 D5 the gate also requires the draw.io webapp under `out/drawio` (its editor, our overlay and fonts sheet, draw.io's licence, `app.min.js`, `stencils.min.js`, `viewer-static.min.js`, and a non-empty `img/` and `math4/`) and reports its bytes as `drawioBytes`, never gated on its own (`asarBytes` holds it).
## Editor rules (client)

1. **Frontmatter**: on load, `splitFrontmatter(content)` → `{ frontmatter, body }`; only `body` goes into Crepe. On save, write `frontmatter + getMarkdownForSave(crepe)`. Frontmatter is re-prepended byte-identically (Crepe would otherwise turn `---` YAML into `***` + paragraph + setext heading underline).
2. **Crepe construction**: always via `createCrepe()` — features come ONLY from `src/editor/featureConfig.ts` (`ENABLED_FEATURES` / `DISABLED_FEATURES`, every `CrepeFeature` classified; ImageBlock, TopBar, AI off; Placeholder off since YAZ-3695 (12: no "Please enter…" on empty lines); `featureConfig.test.ts` asserts the running editor loads exactly the allowlist); the `Crepe` class itself is `src/editor/crepe.ts` (YAZ-2184) — Crepe rebuilt from its own `CrepeBuilder` and per-feature entry points with ONLY the enabled features bundled, because the package root imports every feature (KaTeX with Latex) and one VALUE import from it puts them all back in the main chunk; production code imports only types from `@milkdown/crepe`, `crepe.test.ts` guards that and holds the class to the package's own `Crepe` (same loaded features, schema, plugins, rendered DOM), and `main.tsx` imports Crepe's common theme file by file without `latex`/`placeholder`/`top-bar`/`ai`/`diff` CSS, list_item content `block+` (extended from GFM task item schema), `markdownUpdated` listener wired. The allowlist says which features load; **`featureConfigs` configures one of them**. Its ONE entry is `[CrepeFeature.BlockEdit]`: `listGroup.orderedList = null` removes Crepe's stock Ordered List row (YAZ-1329), while optional `buildMenu` appends Drawing (YAZ-877); neither changes the feature SET. **The Drawing slash item** (`src/editor/drawingMenu.ts`, second build unit of the Excalidraw embed YAZ-852): Crepe builds its stock groups and then hands the `GroupBuilder` to `buildMenu`, so Drawing is APPENDED to the existing `advanced` group (Image / Code / Table / Math) of Crepe's OWN menu — never a parallel slash plugin, so filtering, keyboard navigation and hiding all come for free. HOST-SUPPLIED CREATOR: the row exists only when `createCrepe({ drawing })` provides `create()` (Editor wires `() => createDrawing(root)` plus the window's passive `onNotice`) — absent → NO Drawing row is added, while Ordered List remains absent in both cases. `onRun` matches the stock items' mechanism as far as it can: `clearTextInCurrentBlockCommand` first (the same opening move every stock item makes — it clears the block the `/query` was typed into), then, where a stock item would call a schema command, a `tr.insertText` of the embed — because a drawing embed is PLAIN MARKDOWN TEXT (rule 23's `![[…]]`, no schema change, no serializer change, round-trip byte-identical outside the one inserted line). Crepe's `onRun` is synchronous and the write is not, so the view is re-read after the await and the text goes at the LIVE selection; a failed create inserts nothing and goes to the passive notice, never a dialog. The file itself: `createDrawing()` (`src/drawings/`) writes a valid EMPTY Excalidraw scene (`{ type: 'excalidraw', version: 2, source: 'yaseen-docs', elements: [], appState: {}, files: {} }`, pretty-printed + trailing newline) to `assets/drawings/Drawing YYYY-MM-DD HH.mm.ss.excalidraw` through `writeAsset` with `create: true` — the drawings home is made by `writeAsset`'s own `mkdir -p`, never scaffolded, and NEVER OVERWRITES: a same-second collision comes back `ALREADY_EXISTS` and the bounded loop retries ` 2`, ` 3`, … (any other failure propagates to the notice). It returns the BASENAME, which is all the embed needs — `readAsset`'s shortest-path rule finds it anywhere under the root. End-to-end in `desktop/e2e/drawing.spec.ts` step 1 (the spec the preview YAZ-878 extended in steps 2-4, rule 27, and the modal YAZ-879 extended in step 5, rule 28).
3. **Save post-processing**: `postProcessMarkdown()` un-escapes `\[\[` → `[[` (wikilinks/embeds) and restores the visible same-line numeric bullet spelling armored by rule 8. It is ONE walk through `mapOutsideFences` (rule 8's 🔒 one-walk rule, YAZ-2660 D2): each line outside fenced code gets `restoreWikilinks` (`\[\[` → `[[`, and rule 31's `\=` → `=` inside a `[[…]]`) and then rule 8's `restoreItemLine`; a line inside a fence keeps its bytes. 🔒 The wikilink rule also skips a code span on its line (D3): remark escapes nothing inside code, so a backslash there is the user's own text — `` `\[\[page]]` `` saves as written, and a link beside it on the same line is still restored. A line with no backslash does no work. Not covered: a code span that runs over two or more lines. After the walk the text ends in a single `\n` (rule 6). Contract tests: `listItemRoundTrip.test.ts` and `roundtrip.test.ts` ("the text rules never read code" / "… never change code"). Before the walk, remark's `text` handler is ours (YAZ-3727 B5, `textStringify.ts`, set in `remarkStringifyOptionsCtx`): Milkdown's wrote text that ends in whitespace (and has no `*`, `_`, `\`) RAW, so a line that is only `1. `, `# `, `> `, `- `, `+ `, `1) ` or `--- ` reloaded as a list, a heading, a quote or a line. Ours escapes the text before the trailing whitespace (`state.safe`) and writes the whitespace raw, never `&#x20;`; text with nothing to escape keeps Milkdown's bytes. Test: `textStringify.test.ts`.
4. **Replacing content in a live instance** (external change / Reload): `setMarkdown(crepe, md)` → `replaceAll(md, true)` from `@milkdown/kit/utils`, keeping focus and caret. TAB SWITCHES never remount (GRO-2234): every VISITED tab keeps its editor mounted in its own layer, inactive layers hidden via `visibility: hidden` plus `content-visibility: hidden` (YAZ-2195: a hidden layer skips style, layout and paint, so switches, resizes and theme changes stop scaling with the number of mounted tabs; the right panel's editor layers do the same) — never `display: none`, which would reset the scroller's scrollTop — so scroll position, caret, undo history and the unsaved buffer all survive a switch. Opening a DIFFERENT file in the same tab still remounts the Crepe host (`key={path}`): the old file's editor unmounts (→ autosave flush) and the previous file stays on screen until the next one has loaded.
5. **Outline folding** (GRO-2011): `createOutlineFolding()` (`src/editor/outline/`) is registered in `createCrepe()`. Parent `list_item`s (those owning a nested `bullet_list`/`ordered_list`, or since YAZ-3696 D11 a `table` — a bullet with only a table gets the arrow too) — and since YAZ-1709 any `list_item` holding an `image` in its own blocks, leaf or not — get a widget `<button class="outline-toggle" aria-expanded>` at the start of their content (one stroked SVG chevron sized by `--fold-chevron-size`, default 14px, rotated −90° via CSS when collapsed — GRO-2093; the 18px box is unchanged so strip/gate geometry holds); collapsing adds `data-outline-folded="true"` to EVERY nested list and EVERY table of the item (`findFoldedChildren`, `listNodes.ts`; CSS `display:none` under `.editor-instance .milkdown`, so it outranks Crepe's `.milkdown .milkdown-table-block { display: block }` — the heading fold's `data-heading-folded` rule is prefixed the same way, so a folded heading hides tables and code blocks, YAZ-3696 B1; `foldCss.test.ts` holds both weights) — mixed markers at one indent (`* a` then `- b`) are unified on load (rule 8, GRO-2112); should sibling lists still arise (e.g. bullet + ordered), all of them fold (GRO-2031). An image bullet's fold additionally stamps every image in the item's OWN blocks (nested lists excluded) with `data-outline-folded-image="true"` — a node decoration on the `image` node, so the image node view (rule 30) knows nothing about folding — and `imageView.css` turns that `.image-view` into a one-line chip (a fixed text-height thumbnail, `object-fit: cover`, NO label — a pasted image's alt is its file name, and images are named by typing beside them on the bullet; no handles); the plugin's `handleClickOn` on the chip's THUMBNAIL (not the wrapper) unfolds its bullet — the chevron's toggle, from the chip. Every image of a foldable item, folded or not, also carries `data-outline-foldable-image="true"`, which is what shows the node view's corner `button.image-view__fold` on an expanded image; the plugin's `handleDOMEvents.mousedown` folds the bullet from that button (taken on mousedown so PM never turns the press into a node selection). Fold-all and the guide-line click read the same `entries`, so image bullets take part like any parent. Toggles are metadata-only transactions (`tr.docChanged === false`) — the listener never fires `markdownUpdated`, `getMarkdownForSave()` is unchanged, and the file's mtime is untouched. Fold keys = FNV-1a hash of the item's first-block text (an image counts as its alt text, width stripped, src as the fallback — `itemLabelText`, YAZ-1709) + occurrence index (`outlineFoldKeys.ts`), persisted via `storage.getFolds/setFolds`. Fold transactions carry one of: a position (toggle), `fold-all` / `unfold-all`, `{ set, collapsed }` (guide-line click: direct parents on collapse, their full parent-item subtree on expansion), `undo-fold`; the multi-item ones remember the previous collapsed set so ⌘Z reverts them as one step.
6. **Accepted lossy normalisation** (standard remark-stringify behaviour; content preserved, formatting normalised): `-`/`+` bullets → `*` (alternating `-` for adjacent sibling lists), tabs → 2-space indent, structural `1)` ↔ `1.` ordered markers swap/renumber (but rule 8's same-line numeric bullet text keeps its visible delimiter), setext → ATX headings, two-space hard breaks → `\`, trailing whitespace stripped, `___` → `***`, indented code → fenced, tables re-padded, lazy blockquote continuation gets `> `, `_`/`*`/`[`/`=`/`&` escaped in text where ambiguous, bare URLs/emails → `<autolink>`, file always ends with a single `\n`. First save of an untouched file WILL rewrite the file in this normalised form.
7. **Outliner keymap** (GRO-2012, `src/editor/outline/listCommands.ts`, registered in `createCrepe()` with keymap priority 100): Tab = indent (inside one list the line goes into the item above's sublist of either kind, else a new sublist in the kind of the nearest sibling's sublist, above first, else bullets, YAZ-3727 D10; a first sibling moves into the last item of a list right above, also of the other kind, YAZ-3727 D3; otherwise no-op — never inserts spaces), Shift-Tab = outdent (level 1 → paragraph; following siblings nest under the lifted item), Enter keeps the line's node, so its fold, zoom and format stay (YAZ-3695 D1, D2, D8): at the start of an item an empty plain item goes above (on the zoomed item's own line: a new first child); at the end or in the middle of a parent item the text after the caret is its new FIRST child, in its own format (after the subtree when the parent is folded and not zoomed); on a top-level heading the start puts an empty plain line above and the middle of a FOLDED one puts a same-level heading after the hidden section. Enter on an empty item = outdent / leave the list. Backspace at the start of an item, a top-level heading or a top-level paragraph and Delete at the end of a line JOIN two VISIBLE lines by one rule (`joinLines`, YAZ-3695 D4-D7, YAZ-3780, see Keyboard); ⌘Z gives back the text and the folds a join opened (YAZ-3781); Milkdown's `LiftFirstListItem` keeps Backspace only and `DowngradeHeading` has no key (D3, `createCrepe.ts`). After any document change a caret inside a folded line opens the folds that hide it, and ⌘Z closes them again (`outline/foldReveal.ts`, YAZ-3695 11, YAZ-3781). Multi-item selection + Tab/Shift-Tab moves all selected items — the items whose text the selection covers; a line a ⇧↑/⇧↓ selection only touches at zero width stays put, and the selection stays (YAZ-3003, `onCoveredLines` in `lineSelection.ts`).
8. **List-item round trip** (`src/editor/listItemRoundTrip.ts`): an empty bullet/ordered item is written as a bare marker (`*` / `1.`), never `* <br />` — `<br />` opens a CommonMark HTML block that swallows the item's nested children on reload. Parsing gives an item whose nested list starts on a later line (`* ` + children, Obsidian's empty parent) an empty leading paragraph. A table on a later line gets one too (`*` + an indented table). The app's own Table slash row (`slashMenu.ts`, YAZ-3696): in an empty bullet the table becomes the item's first child, on the marker line (`* | … |`, YAZ-3805); in a bullet with text it goes below the text, inside the item (D12). **Same-line numeric bullet text** (YAZ-1329): a numeric delimiter immediately after a bullet marker (`* 6) text` / `* 6. text`, any bullet spelling or indent) is temporarily escaped before CommonMark parses it, so it remains the bullet's paragraph text rather than becoming a nested ordered list; save removes that boundary escape and preserves the visible digits/delimiter. Real ordered Markdown on its own line remains structural. Fenced code, decimals, prose and non-immediate numeric text are untouched. Before parsing, `normalizeEmptyItems()` also rewrites legacy `* <br />` lines to bare markers and an empty task `* [ ] ` / `* [x]` to `* [ ] <br />` (remark alone reads `[ ]` as text and would write `* \[ ]`); on save `restoreItemLine()` writes it back as `* [ ]` — `<br />` never reaches the disk. **Mixed markers** (GRO-2112): the same pass runs `unifySiblingMarkers()` — `-`, `*` and `+` are one bullet: bullets at one indent parse as ONE list (the first sibling's marker wins on load; a blank line starts a new list, as in Obsidian). CommonMark would otherwise start a new list on every marker change. Line rules live in the function's docblock. Disk is untouched by loading; the first save writes `*` throughout (rule 6) as before. **Empty nested item** (YAZ-1357): the same pass runs `separateEmptyNestedItems()` LAST — a text item followed on the very next line by a DEEPER bare marker gets one blank line between them, because CommonMark forbids an empty item from interrupting a paragraph (without it `* a` + `  *` reads back as the text `a *`, and the outline seed's `-` spelling as a setext heading the bullets-only schema drops whole, which is what tripped the YAZ-974 guard). The blank line is what Milkdown writes back, so the file converges on it; fenced code is untouched. **List depth from indentation** (YAZ-3727 D1, rule 8 of the file's header): the same pass runs `alignNestedIndent()` after the two empty-item rewrites and BEFORE `unifySiblingMarkers()`, which reads the indent. CommonMark nests a line only at its parent's text column, and that column moves with the marker (`9. ` is 3 wide, `10. ` is 4): an AI's 3-space children of 10 and up fell out of the list, and the next save wrote the flat shape. Now a list line indented past the marker of an open item is that item's child, however wide the indent (tabs, 3 spaces under `10.`, 6 spaces under `*`), and moves to the parent's text column; a line at or left of a marker closes that item. A text line moves with the deepest item whose text column it reaches; after a blank line it takes the list line's rule (YAZ-3855: past an item's marker it moves to that item's text column, and the next lines at its indent, a table's rows, go with it); a lazy line (no blank line above) stays as written. After a blank line, a line 4 or more columns past its item's text column is indented code, list marker or not: it moves with its item and opens no level. A numbered child that does not start at 1, right under its parent's text, gets a blank line first (CommonMark lets only `1.` interrupt a paragraph; Milkdown writes the same blank line back); an empty parent gets none, because a blank line would end it. A heading, a quote, a thematic break or a fence left of an item's text closes that item, as in CommonMark, so a line below it is never moved into the closed item (where 4 spaces read as code). Markdown the app writes passes through byte-identical. Known limit: a fence inside a moved item keeps its indent (the walk skips fences); and a list inside a quote (`> 10. …`) is read the CommonMark way, since the rule reads lines that start with a marker, not with `>` (YAZ-3852 nit 3). Files that an earlier save already flattened are not repaired (YAZ-3727 S2). **Paste runs the same rules** (YAZ-3727 S1, `clipboardPaste.ts`): a plain-text paste (no HTML) and **Paste as → Markdown** parse `normalizeEmptyItems(text)`, so a pasted list nests as the same file would open; a plain-text paste takes this parser only when the text has a list line, and any other text keeps Milkdown's own text paste. 🔒 **ONE WALK FOR EVERY TEXT RULE** (YAZ-2660 D2): EVERY text rule of the editor, on load (`normalizeEmptyItems()`: the same-line escape, the two empty-item rewrites, `alignNestedIndent()`, `unifySiblingMarkers()`, `separateEmptyNestedItems()`) and on save (`postProcessMarkdown()`, rule 3), reads the text through the ONE walk `mapOutsideFences(markdown, (line, next) => …)` — a rule that reads the text by itself reads code as Markdown, and changes the user's code. A new text rule MUST use the same walk. **What the walk knows**: the fence character (`` ` `` or `~`), the fence length, and that a closing fence has no text after it — so a line of 3 backticks inside a fence of 4, a backtick line inside a `~~~` fence, and a line such as `` ```js `` inside a fence do not end the code; a fence in a bullet is found at any indent, and a fence that never closes runs to the end of the text. The callback gets the line below as `next`, for a rule that looks ahead (`separateEmptyNestedItems()`), and a rule adds a line by returning the line plus `\n`. **Two known limits**: indented code (4 spaces, no fence) is not seen as code — one rare shape still gets a blank line there, a text bullet and a deeper bare marker (a guess at indented code can read a nested list as code, which is worse in an outline note; the editor writes each code block as a fence at the first save, rule 6) — and a code span that runs over two or more lines (rule 3). Contract tests: `listItemRoundTrip.test.ts` (the rules as pure functions) and `roundtrip.test.ts` (real editors; one note with every trigger inside code keeps each code line).

9. **Depth bullet glyphs** (GRO-2013, `src/editor/outline/bullets.css`): CSS only — Crepe's bullet svg is hidden and `.label.bullet::after` draws ● / ○ / ■ by nesting depth of `.milkdown-list-item-block` (repeating every three levels; ordered levels count), `--list-indent: 2.15em`, marker colour 78% of the text colour, all from Crepe theme tokens. A number (`.label.ordered`) takes the same `--list-marker-color`, not Crepe's grey outline, so bullet threading's accent reaches it too (YAZ-3727 D7, test `outline/numberColour.test.ts`). Heading-first items (`* # Part 1`) offset the label row by the heading's margin and size it to the heading's line box (`--list-label-offset/height`, shared with the fold chevron). **Done tasks read as done** (YAZ-1514, 🔒 D1–D4): the same file strikes and dims (`--list-done-color`, 55% of the text colour) the FIRST line (a textblock — a first-child code block or table is left alone) of any `li.list-item` whose label carries Milkdown's own `checked` class — so `Mod-Enter`, the ☑ click and a `[x]` written by Obsidian all look identical; nested children keep their own state, a second paragraph in the item stays normal, and `~~` is NEVER written to the file. Markdown untouched.
10. **Typography** (GRO-2009, `src/app.css`): Obsidian defaults — system font stack, 16px / 1.5 body, heading scale 1.802 / 1.602 / 1.424 / 1.266 / 1.125 / 1em at weight 600 (h1 700), line-height 1.3 — set through Crepe's `--crepe-font-*` / `--crepe-base-font-size` custom properties on `.editor-instance .milkdown`.

11. **Underline** (GRO-2028, `src/editor/marks/underline.ts`): ProseMirror mark `underline` (`<u>` in the DOM). On disk it is obsidian-underline's inline HTML `<u>text</u>`: a `$remark` plugin wraps each mdast `html("<u>")` … `html("</u>")` pair (nearest match, any depth, inside any inline parent such as `**…**`) into an `underline` mdast node after parsing, and registers the remark-stringify handler that writes it back as `<u>` + children + `</u>` — so `a <u>b</u> c` round-trips byte-identically. Unmatched tags and every other inline HTML keep going through Milkdown's `html` atom node unchanged. Not a Crepe feature (allowlist untouched); the selection toolbar's U button runs the same command (YAZ-3806 T8).

12. **Zoom into a bullet** (GRO-2029, `src/editor/outline/zoom.ts` + `zoom.css`): view state ONLY, like folding — the plugin holds the zoomed `list_item` position (mapped through every transaction; cleared if the item is deleted), and decorations hide every block off the path root → zoomed item (`outline-zoom-hidden`), strip the ancestors' glyph/chevron/first block (`outline-zoom-ancestor`, a folded ancestor renders expanded without touching fold state) and render a breadcrumb widget (`File name › Ancestor › … › Item`, labels = first-block text truncated at 40 chars; crumbs zoom to that ancestor, the file crumb zooms out fully). Triggers: click the bullet glyph (`.label-wrapper`; task checkboxes keep toggling), `Mod-.`, `Mod-Shift-.` (see Keyboard). Zooming dispatches a metadata-only transaction: never `markdownUpdated`, disk untouched, fold state unaffected. Not persisted — switching files remounts the editor and clears it, and an external file change (watcher → `replaceAll`) replaces the doc and clears it too. allowlist untouched. ⚡ AMENDED by YAZ-3647 D2: the browser history below is gone. Every user-driven zoom change calls `createCrepe({ zoom: { onZoom } })` with the zoom key (null = zoomed out); the page's tab keeps it (`Tab.zoom`) and the window's Back list gets a step. Back and Forward set the tab's level, and the editor follows its `zoomKey` prop (`zoomPageTo` → `zoomToKey`, which tells no one). A page that starts drilled in tells its tab quietly (`quiet`: no step), and the zoomed bullet's key, which is its text, goes to the tab quietly `KEY_SETTLE_MS` after typing stops. ⌘- and ⇧-click on a dot call `onOpen` instead (YAZ-3646 D10), as does the bullet menu's "Open in new tab" (`openBulletRow`), which a right-click on the dot opens too (`bulletDotTarget`, D8), and so do ⌘- and ⇧-click on a crumb (YAZ-3647 E2: `onOpen(null, …)` from the title crumb). Signatures: `onZoom(zoom, quiet, label, from?)` — `from`, on a quiet key report only, is the key it replaces: the one the page last reported or was set to (YAZ-3662 F6b); the Editor sends it on as `ZoomFrom { path, key }`, and App's `zoomTab(id, zoom, quiet, from)` dispatches `zoom { from }`. A report still waiting goes at once, with the key before the change and its `from`, when the level changes (a zoom, ⌘Z, `zoomToKey`) and when the plugin view goes (another page in the tab, a close, a rebuild); a report of the same key is not sent; `onOpen(zoom | null, background, label)`, `label` the bullet's crumb text (`zoomLabelAt`, `getZoomLabel`). A press with any button but the left on a task's box, and a ⌃-press on macOS (YAZ-3694 F7b), is stopped at document capture (`isTaskBox`, `pointerdown`; YAZ-3694 F7): Crepe's list item ticks the task on `pointerdown` for every button, and a right-click must not tick it. That right-click opens the bullet's menu, as on a dot (`bulletDotTarget`, YAZ-3727 D20); "Open in new tab" shows no ⇧-click hint there either (D20). Only the dot's own `.label-wrapper` opens a tab: a ⇧-click on the text still extends the selection (E5). Only main tabs give `onZoom` / `onOpen`. A rebuild from outside (`applyExternalMarkdown` → 'rebuilt') zooms the page back to the key it was at, before the settle timer can tell the tab null (E1); a key that is gone stays zoomed out. The tab's key always matches what the page shows (YAZ-3676 F3): after a reload, and after `zoomPageTo` for a key that is no longer found, the editor tells the tab the real key (or null) quietly, when it differs. A rename that carries a dirty buffer (`takeRenameBuffer` → `setMarkdown`) zooms back to the tab's key, as E1 does, so a zoom that is still valid stays. **History** (GRO-2091, replaced by YAZ-3647 D2): every zoom change (glyph, crumb, `Mod-.`, `Mod-Shift-.`, zoom-out included) pushes one in-memory entry `history.state = { mdappZoom: { file, key } }` with the URL untouched (2-arg `pushState`; `key` = fold-key scheme over ALL list items, `null` = zoomed out), and `popstate` restores that level without pushing — so Back / Forward walk zoom levels. Entries of another file are ignored (left behind by a file switch → a Back press can be silent), an unresolvable key zooms out, the original page entry (no zoom state) = zoomed out. ⚡ AMENDED by YAZ-2951 (D1, S7, S21, S22): a copied page STARTS drilled in — "Duplicate tab", ⌘⇧N and "Move to new window" give the copy its source's zoom key as `createCrepe({ zoom: { startKey } })`; the plugin's FIRST `init` resolves it against the parsed doc (`itemPosForZoomKey`; not found → zoomed out, S7), as plain plugin state: no transaction, no history entry (S21), no ⌘Z level (S22). A rebuilt state (`setMarkdown` → `replaceAll(md, true)`) starts zoomed out, as before. The host then moves the caret into that bullet with `caretIntoZoom` (`moveCaretIntoZoom(crepe)`, after `crepe.create()`, before the caret grab), never from the plugin view, which ProseMirror builds inside the `EditorView` constructor. `getZoomKey(state)` / `getZoomKeyOf(crepe)` read the drilled-in bullet's key for the page view (`lib/pageView.ts`). Persisted since YAZ-3646 D14, with each tab only (`StoredTab.zoom`).

13. **List guide lines** (GRO-2030, `src/editor/outline/guideLines.ts` + `.css`): every nested list (`li.list-item > .children > .content-dom > ul/ol`) gets a CSS `::before` strip — 10px wide, absolutely positioned (`-1 * (--list-indent / 2 + 10px)`) so its centred 1px line runs under the parent's glyph centre; zero layout shift, folded lists take their line with them, colours from `currentColor` (14%, hover 35%). Pseudo boxes hit-test as the list element, so a pointer left of the list's border box = the strip: the plugin's `handleDOMEvents` turns mousedown into `toggleOutlineFoldChildren(listPos)` (GRO-2107/YAZ-1317: any direct parent expanded collapses the direct parents; when all are collapsed, the click unfolds every parent item in their full subtree; the line's owner and leaves remain untouched; an all-leaf line is a swallowed no-op; markdown/mtime untouched, caret unmoved) and mousemove into the `outline-guide-hover` highlight (element `:hover` would light up while editing text inside).

### Clipboard input and paste modes (YAZ-1394)

Normal Paste keeps Milkdown’s supported rich HTML preference, document typography, existing fake-bullet outline conversion, and Markdown interpretation when only plain text is available. `editor/clipboardPaste.ts`, registered after `outlinePaste`, converts external root-level `p / br… / p` separators into one empty paragraph per standalone break. A break-containing paragraph otherwise acquires an extra visual line. This preserves intentional blank spacing rather than deleting it; inline breaks, nested blocks, explicit empty paragraphs, and unmarked internal `data-pm-slice` HTML are untouched. Our marked copy-out separators are restored to empty paragraphs first, including within internal slices and nested lists, preserving attributes and slice metadata. The upstream Google Docs wrapper cleanup runs first. This rule is based on a reproduced clipboard shape; it is not a promise to normalize arbitrary source HTML.

Native Edit and right-click menus expose **Paste as → Plain text / Markdown**; Plain text uses **⌘⇧V**. Main captures text once per gesture and sends `ClipboardPasteRequest` to that window. Plain text inserts characters literally, preserves spaces and line breaks (CRLF/CR become LF), and does not parse Markdown. Markdown explicitly parses that text with the existing schema, even when the clipboard also has HTML; open slice boundaries let inline content remain in its surrounding sentence. Both modes apply existing paste rules (including table repair and the bullets-only lock of a folder's outline), replace the active selection in one undoable transaction, and leave empty clipboard text as a no-op. In code, text remains literal.

**Normal pasted numbering (YAZ-1429, YAZ-3727 D6):** a plain run — labels exactly `n.`, `n+1.`, … from the list's start, the numbers the app draws — stays a real numbered list: in plain text each item's source position must start with its expected label (`plainRun`), and in HTML a plain decimal `<ol>` (no `reversed`, no item `value`, `type` `1` or none, no inline `list-style-type` other than `decimal` on the list or an item) is left for ProseMirror to parse, its `start` kept. Google Docs and Word set letters and roman numerals with that CSS, so such a list keeps its labels as text (`a.`, `I.`; YAZ-3855). Every other external numbered list becomes ordinary text with visible labels (`3)`, `09.`, gaps, repeats, `a.`, `i.`), so Enter cannot continue or renumber them. The folder outline cannot hold a numbered list (`holdsNumbers`: its `list_item` takes no `ordered_list`), so there every label stays text, as before D6. `editor/clipboardNumbers.ts` converts the other HTML ordered-list markers before DOM parsing, honoring numeric start, reverse order and explicit item values while retaining rich inline content, nested blocks and empty parent labels. Foreign `data-pm-slice` context is removed so it cannot recreate automatic numbering. Plain-text-only paste uses the existing remark AST and each item's source position to preserve original labels/punctuation, repeated numbers and task markers; code nodes remain literal. Mixed fake-bullet outlines use the same conversion, paste constraints and undo boundary. Saved ordered Markdown, Number children and explicit Paste as Markdown remain unchanged. Newly copied app HTML carries `data-yaseendocs-clipboard` alongside ProseMirror's slice metadata so intentional internal lists round-trip. This identifier exists only in clipboard HTML, never in note files. A text-only copy has no source identity and follows normal external-paste rules; explicit Markdown is the deliberate override. Existing notes are not migrated. Source-specific CSS counters are outside this normalization contract.

Each Crepe view subscribes through `menu.onPasteAs`, claims only its own focused surface, and unsubscribes on destroy. CodeMirror and ordinary inputs use the private validated native `insertText` fallback, retaining their own caret and edit handling. Read-only Crepe views cannot be changed by either path. No clipboard writes, mode flags, async clipboard reads, new dependency, or changed save serializer are involved in paste handling. `clipboardPaste.test.ts`, native menu, preload bridge, and window IPC tests cover these boundaries; native input undo and the actual source-app clipboard still require a pointed manual check when validating a release.

### Clipboard output (YAZ-938, YAZ-1389, YAZ-1411, YAZ-1443)

Normal Copy/Cut provides readable `text/plain` and rich `text/html` (YAZ-1443). `editor/clipboardPlainText.ts` reads the selected ProseMirror structure rather than Markdown source. Paragraph boundaries contribute one newline and each explicit empty paragraph contributes one additional blank line; repeated/leading/trailing selected empty rows, inline breaks, code whitespace and literal punctuation remain intact. Headings/marks/links copy their visible text without Markdown syntax; links retain their target in HTML and explicit Markdown. A `[[link]]` copies as the note shows it (YAZ-3744 S8, `copyLinkTextCtx` → `linksAsShown(…, withId)`): its page's name, an ID link as its title with the ID as the app writes it (`nameAndId`: "AR v2 plan (YAS-466)", the "Copy name and ID" text), a missing note as its ID; embeds and code stay as written. The app's own HTML keeps the raw `[[…]]`, so a paste into a note keeps the link. Lists retain readable labels, nesting and task state, and table cells use tabs. A single text block selected inside open list wrappers copies its selected words without inventing a bullet; selections spanning parent and nested children keep their hierarchy. No global whitespace collapse or note migration is involved.

Edit and right-click menus expose **Copy as → Plain text / Markdown**, then a line and **Without folded lines** (YAZ-3653). Plain text and Markdown write text only, removing rich formats so destinations cannot select HTML instead. Without folded lines writes the two formats normal Copy writes (`text/plain` and `text/html`, `menu:copy-text` with its optional HTML; text plus HTML is bounded together) from the selection minus what folds hide: a folded bullet's children, a folded heading's section, the lines outside a zoom. With the selection inside one line it copies the bullet under the note menu's pointer, else the bullet at the caret; a toast says how many folded lines it left out. Plain text matches normal Copy’s readable text. Markdown uses the existing source serializer, including intentional syntax and empty-paragraph markers. Each Crepe subscribes through `menu.onCopyAs`, claims only its focused selection (including read-only selections), and unsubscribes on destroy. Focused CodeMirror uses its public editor-state selection API, preserving all nonempty ranges and line breaks as literal code in both explicit modes. Preload falls back to selected input/textarea or focused DOM text; password fields and empty selections leave the clipboard unchanged. Main validates the registered live sender, main frame, renderer URL, current target and bounded string before the private `clipboard.writeText` / `clipboard.write` call. No arbitrary clipboard writer is exposed through the renderer API.

A note's right-click menu (YAZ-3653, `editor/noteMenu.tsx`) is drawn by the app's `ContextMenu` instead of the native one; on a line's text (not code, not a table cell) the bullet menu's rows for that line follow the spelling rows, each group its own (YAZ-3727 D15, rule 26): Open in new tab, the Turn into strip (`MenuStrip` in `menuSections.ts`, drawn by `ContextMenu` with the block menu's markup and CSS), the children rows; a row does nothing once the note changed under the open menu, and shows no hint (D17: "⇧-click" names a click on the dot, and widened the menu); a link keeps its own menu (the one link menu, YAZ-3609 D23). An image in the note shows its own two rows there instead (YAZ-3727 D22, `imageMenuSections`): **Copy image** (`copy-image`, with the point right-clicked in page px) and **Reveal in Finder** (`reveal-image`, with the `<img>`'s `src`; inert unless it is an `app://vault/` image). A fold chevron's right-click is the line's menu, as on its text (D23). A right-click beside a bullet's text (the gap after its checkbox) counts as on its line (D22, `textLineTarget`). Its rows reach main through `menu.edit(action, arg?)` → `menu:edit`, all but one: with words selected in a note that can change, a last group holds **Add link…** (YAZ-3609 D17), which stays in the renderer — `markdownLink.ts` `addLinkOn(view)` opens Crepe's link box on the selection once the menu has closed. The preload refuses it outside a user gesture (`navigator.userActivation`); main checks the same live sender, main frame, renderer URL and current target, then runs `webContents.cut/copy/paste()`, sends `menu:copy-as` / `menu:paste-as` to that window as the native menu does, adds one word (no spaces, 64 characters at most) to the spellchecker's dictionary, copies the image at the point (`copyImageAt`, the point times the window's zoom factor: Chromium's point is in the window's px), or reveals the file of an `app://vault/` image of at most 8,192 characters (`revealVaultImage`, as the native image menu does). Any other action is refused.

For rich HTML (YAZ-1411), the existing clipboard-only DOM serializer reuses paragraph rendering/attributes and marks, sets paragraph margins to zero, and exports each empty paragraph as a standalone BR carrying `data-mdapp-empty-paragraph`. Actual Google Docs testing showed that it drops `p > br` empty paragraphs but preserves a standalone BR as an empty paragraph; our paste adapter restores the marked BR before ProseMirror parsing. The app clipboard identity and ProseMirror slice metadata remain intact for intentional internal lists. No placeholder spaces or invisible characters are introduced. Default HTML, the live editor and the save serializer are unchanged by the plain-text fix. Destination apps can apply their own formatting; real-app review remains useful. Clipboard copy/paste integration tests and native menu, preload and private IPC tests cover these contracts.

## Keyboard (client)

All bindings are `$shortcut` keymaps registered in `createCrepe()` with priority 100 (Crepe's own keymaps are 50), so they run first and fall through (`return false`) when they do not apply. `Mod` = ⌘ on macOS, Ctrl elsewhere (ProseMirror decides by `navigator.platform`). App-level window & tab shortcuts (⌘⇧N / ⌘⇧O / ⌘W / ⌘⇧W New Files Window / ⌃Tab / ⌃⇧Tab) live in the application menu — see "Menus & shortcuts". The LAST rows of the table are the sidebar's, and they are no keymap: React key handlers on the search bar (`useSidebarSearch`'s `searchKeyDown`) and on a tree (`Tree`), where ⌘ is `metaKey` (YAZ-2662; "The sidebar lenses": The search from the keyboard).

|---|---|---|---|
| `Tab` / `Mod-]` | caret/selection in list items | indent (sink) the item(s) whose text the selection covers — a line touched only at zero width (a ⇧↑/⇧↓ edge) never moves; the selection stays; no-op on a first sibling — never inserts spaces. Inside one list the items join the item above's sublist of either kind and take its kind; with none, the new sublist takes the kind of the nearest sibling's sublist (above first, then below), else bullets (YAZ-3727 D10). When the first item's list sits right after another list (a numbered list under a bullet, or the reverse), the covered items move into that list's last item; they join its child list and take its kind, or keep their own kind when it has none; the items after them stay a list of their own; one ⌘Z | GRO-2012, YAZ-3003, YAZ-3727 D3, D4, D10 `listCommands.ts` |

| `Tab` / `Shift-Tab` | a text selection over two or more lines that are not all list items | nothing — never types spaces into the text, never moves focus | YAZ-3003 `listCommands.ts` |

The upper line may be in the note, a bullet or a quote (YAZ-3783). A code block or a table above, or the top of a zoom: nothing. A rule (`hr`) above is selected; the next press removes it (YAZ-3784). Top of the note: an empty line goes and the next line moves up with its format and fold (YAZ-3798); an item lifts to a paragraph, a heading becomes a paragraph, a paragraph declines (native). | `Shift-ArrowUp` / `Shift-ArrowDown` | any text selection | **Whole-line selection (YAZ-1734, D1–D7; `lineSelection.ts`, one file, registered before the outliner keymap).** A "line" is the textblock — a paragraph, a heading, a list item's own text — never the visual row (D1). Only the HEAD moves. On a block edge it moves to the same edge of the previous / next VISIBLE textblock, so `⌘←` `⇧↓` and `⌘→` `⇧↑` select exactly one whole line and each repeat adds exactly one more; mid-line it first moves to its own line's near edge (`⇧↓` the end, `⇧↑` the start); an empty block: `⇧↓` takes the start edge, `⇧↑` the end (D2). A press never crosses the anchor and always reaches it, so `⇧↑` undoes exactly one `⇧↓`; collapsed on the anchor, the next press flips past it (D5). Hidden lines — inside a folded bullet's subtree, inside a folded heading section, or outside the zoom (`isHiddenTextblock` asks the three plugins' STATE: `collapsedItemsHiding`, `collapsedHeadingsHiding`, `getZoomedItemPos`; never the DOM) — are skipped, so the range may span hidden text. Hidden text is NEVER deleted: `⌫`, `Delete`, typing and `Enter` over such a range (`deleteVisible`, `visibleTypeOver`, `enterVisible`) remove only the visible pieces by explicit construction (the last block and every whole visible block between go as nodes together with the wrappers they were the only child of; the first block keeps its head and gains the last block's tail — selected from its start it goes as a node and the last keeps its tail), and `Enter` then re-presses itself on the view so the ordinary Enter splits at the caret it left (the keymap hands every handler of one key the same pre-delete state, so merely declining is not enough). `⌘X` stays the ordinary cut on purpose: it MOVES the whole range, hidden kids included, and paste restores them (D6, D7). A `list_item` left without its own paragraph never survives a transaction: `liftHeadlessItems` (`appendTransaction`, every doc change, whatever path) lifts its kids one level up, subtrees intact — a deleted parent's kids move up, folded or not (D3); to delete a folded parent WITH its kids, unfold it first. No visible neighbour (document edge, zoom edge) is a consumed no-op. Falls through to the native pixel-column move only for a node selection or a leaf block (`hr`) in the gap; an image is an inline atom inside a paragraph (ImageBlock off), so an image line is a line. Pinned neighbours (`lineSelection.scenarios.test.ts`): a fenced code block is a line (the head lands at the start of its text); above a table the head never enters it — `prosemirror-tables` normalises the cross-cell selection back to the paragraph above, selected whole; the zoomed item's own text is the visible line above its children; in a folder's outline (bullets-only) a deleted parent row leaves an empty bullet keeping its kids, because that schema cannot drop the row. A selection with no hidden line inside falls through to the ordinary path untouched. The zero-width touch on the line after (⇧↓) or before (⇧↑) stays — ⌫ needs it — but Tab, Shift-Tab, `Mod-]` / `Mod-[` and `Mod-Enter` ignore it (`coveredLines`, YAZ-3003). | YAZ-1734, YAZ-3003 `lineSelection.ts` |

One walk (`eachVisibleTextblock`) decides what is hidden for formatting and `Mod-Enter` alike, from the plugins' STATE in O(1) per block: a fold hides only its item's nested lists (the item's own other blocks stay visible), a folded ancestor of the zoomed bullet hides nothing (the zoom shows it expanded), a folded section's blocks are skipped by their start, and the zoom is one range. The line keys (`isHiddenTextblock`) follow the same zoom rule. The toggle decides add or remove from the visible lines only, and the toolbar lights Bold, Italic, Strikethrough, code and the swatches only for a mark on a visible line (`visibleRangeHasMark`, checked inside each block; the Link button keeps Milkdown's whole-range answer). 14. **Multi-block drag** (GRO-2019, `src/editor/multiBlockDrag.ts`, registered in `createCrepe()`): dragging the block handle while a multi-block selection contains the grabbed block moves the WHOLE selection. A document-capture mousedown expands the selection to whole sibling blocks (`expandedBlockRange`: deepest level containing both ends — sibling `list_item`s inside a nested list, not the outer list) and suppresses Crepe's single-block selection replacement; a capture dragstart hands ProseMirror a fully CLOSED slice (an open slice would splice into the target paragraph) via `dataTransfer` + `view.dragging`; after the drop an `appendTransaction` (on `uiEvent: 'drop'`) deletes the merged empty shell the move-deletion leaves at the origin, walking up wrappers it was the only child of. Drop X-position controls nesting depth (ProseMirror `dropPoint`). A grab OUTSIDE the selection never arms the plugin — Crepe's single-block drag is untouched. Folded parents drag with their hidden children.
15. **Block handle gate** (GRO-2081, `src/editor/blockHandleGate.ts`): while the pointer is inside a guide-line strip band, a fold chevron's box or the band of a section line (rule 18a), `.milkdown-block-handle` gets `mdapp-handle-muted` (pointer-events none + invisible) so those clicks land; muting pauses during drags. Band geometry is imported from `guideLines.ts`, and a section line's from `sectionIndent.ts` (`sectionLineAt`) — one source of truth each. Crepe's `blockHandle.shouldShow` config is typed upstream but never consumed; do not reach for it.
16. **Hotkey reference** (GRO-2067; the Settings › Hotkeys page since YAZ-1679, `src/settings/hotkeysSection.tsx` — a `standalone` section of the dialog, a reference page under the nav divider rather than one of the settings pages — which retired the keyboard button beside the settings cog): every key of the app is one row of `shared/keys/` (`ALL_KEYS`, YAZ-3564 K1), and the page has ONE CARD PER KEY (YAZ-3564, after K7): one BOX per row whose key it is now, titled by its tab (an App action's box by the tabs it works in now: "Every tab", or "Notes · Folder views · Drawings"), a changeable key a BUTTON, a built-in one muted text. A shared key's drawing, diagram or code box is a dropdown where an App command and that tab's action meet (`settings.hotkeysAside`, `<App row id>@<drawing|diagram|code>` → true when the tab keeps its own; an old entry by the row id alone means all three until the store rewrites it), and a pick asks "⌘D in drawings: Show in sidebar? Drawing › Duplicate will have no key in drawings." [Take it] first. A tab's box whose pick went to the App action says "Duplicate has no key here now."; a row an App key always takes says "No key here now: ⌘K is App › Search the vault.", with a link to that key's card when it is another (code's two-step ⌘K keys: ⌘K's card has a box for code's pick). The shared keys a pick settles come first, then the other shared keys, App keys, and the tabs' own; then "Actions with no key". A row whose key changes moves to its new card, and takes the keyboard and the eye there. Then **the clicks and drags** (YAZ-3936, C4 of YAZ-3879, hotkey first like the keys): "Clicks and drags", then ONE CARD PER GESTURE ("Click", "⌘-click", "⇧-click", "⌥-click", "⌘⇧-click", "Drag", "/", "Right-click", "Double-click"), then "Clicks with no gesture". The changeable rows are `GESTURE_ROWS` (`shared/keys/gestures.ts`): two places, "Links in a note" and "Bullet dots", each with Open in this tab / Open in a new tab / Open in a background tab (defaults: Links ⌘-click / none / ⌘⇧-click; Bullet dots Click = zoom in / ⇧-click / ⌘-click). A gesture is modifiers + a click (`'CmdOrCtrl+Shift+Click'`); a change is a `settings.hotkeys` entry by row id (`'links.thisTab': 'Click'`, null = "No gesture", a default is never stored; the store's `isHotkeyEntry` checks it). Its box is a click recorder (`GestureBox`): click it, then hold the keys and click it again; the gesture goes to the same pop-up as a key ("Change the gesture for Links in a note › Open in a new tab?" No gesture → ⌥-click [Save]); a gesture of another action of the SAME place moves ("⌘⇧-click is Links in a note › Open in a background tab now. It will lose its gesture." [Move it here]) — two places never clash; ⌫ or "No gesture" asks to remove it; Esc and a click outside cancel; ⌃-click is refused (the Mac's right-click). Reset and "Reset all hotkeys" cover the clicks too. The other clicks are built in, `MOUSE_TIPS` (`src/settings/hotkeys.ts`, `{ gesture, place, label }`), in the same boxes: bullet lines, fold arrows, the 6 dots, `/`, the sidebar's ⌘-click (background tab, I3) and ⇧-click (multi-selection), tables and boards, the right-click tips, the vault right-click tip (YAZ-1798, with Set display name since YAZ-1974 and Set shortcut since YAZ-2555 D2) and a tab's double-click. A click row's search text is its action, its gesture, its hint and its place ("links in a note"). The recorder asks `clashesOf` over the same rows (K3), so a built-in key, a Mac standard key and a fixed menu key read as taken (`MENU_FIXED_KEYS`, `shared/hotkeyBindings.ts`, YAZ-3419: export, share, Paste as plain text ⌘⇧V, the zoom keys with the hidden ⌘=, the hidden tab twins; `menu.test.ts` walks the real menu and fails on a fixed key not listed there, `menuKeysTaken.test.ts` checks each is taken, and the store refuses each one too). A keymap change anywhere goes with a change to its place's rows in `shared/keys/`. **"Used by macOS"** is `shared/macosHotkeys.ts` (the Mac's own keys as it ships them) with this Mac's System Settings choices laid over it by main (`desktop/src/main/systemHotkeys.ts`: `plutil -convert json` of `~/Library/Preferences/com.apple.symbolichotkeys.plist`, async, kept until its mtime moves; `enabled: false` removes a row, `value.parameters [ascii, keyCode, modifiers]` rebinds it and the row says "(you set it on this Mac)"; any failure is the table as shipped; off macOS no rows), fetched once per open through `state.systemHotkeys` when the page or a search shows. **Search** (D5): each key is its own `bare` row, so the dialog's search filters the page down to single rows — a row's text is its label, its key (a changed key's text is the key it has NOW: the dialog rebuilds the candidates when `settings.hotkeys` or the Mac's keys change, never on a keystroke), its hint and "keyboard shortcuts". The page has its own search bar at the top ("Search hotkeys…", `KeySearch`): it filters this page alone, the nav's box staying the whole dialog's, and Esc clears it before Esc closes. Both boxes match by WORDS when no text matches (`searchSettings`: every query word starts a word of the row, then the same with one slip forgiven in a word of four letters or more — "file winodw" finds New Files window first). "Press keys to search", beside it, records ONE key, puts it in that box and answers in one line ("⌘⇧K is free. You can use it." / "⌘D: App › Show in sidebar; Drawing › Duplicate; …", every action on the key, K10 / "⌘⇧Q: macOS uses it for Log out. You can't use it."). **A change has two steps** (D6): the key button records ("Press new keys…", a window CAPTURE listener that swallows every key, Esc and the dialog's own included; main drops the menu's keys meanwhile), and the pressed key only opens a pop-up (the `ConfirmSheet`, `contained`, so its Esc never closes Settings) that shows the key NOW → the NEW key in two key caps — "Change the key for Search the vault?" ⌘K → ⌘⇧K [Save], with "⌘⇧W is New Files window now. It will lose its key." [Move it here], ⌫ "Remove the key from Close window?" ⌥⌘W → No key [Remove]; a Mac-standard key leaving its command adds "⌘W is the Mac standard for Close tab. Most Mac apps use it." and the button is a red "Change anyway" / "Move anyway" (the keyboard starts on Cancel; otherwise on the button); a built-in or macOS key, or one with neither ⌘ nor ⌃, is a red line and the row keeps recording; its own key again just stops. Only those buttons write `settings.hotkeys`, through the dialog's `onChange`. **Reset** (D7): a changed key is in the accent colour with a Reset link that asks in the same pop-up ("Reset Search the vault?" ⌘⇧K → ⌘K [Reset], naming the command that holds ⌘K now and loses it); "Reset all hotkeys", the last row and there only with a change, asks in the `ConfirmSheet` ("Reset N changed hotkeys?" with each change, "Reset N hotkeys"). The keys of the sidebar's SEARCH BAR are not on this page, which keeps the one Search the vault row: the empty Search tab lists them itself, where they are used (`SEARCH_KEYS` in `sidebar/Sidebar.tsx`, YAZ-2662 🔒 D10).
17. **URL** (GRO-2069, `src/lib/urlHash.ts`): the open file is mirrored as `#/abs/path.md` via `history.replaceState` (never pushState); on boot a hash file wins, then the window's own file, else the window opens blank (YAZ-3487 D7) — `bootTabs` falls back to the folder's `lastFile` only when Settings › Open on is "Its last note" and the window was not opened empty on purpose (D15); a hash file may live OUTSIDE the current root (the sidebar's stale-file validation skips out-of-root paths). No file → no hash. The shareable `yaseendocs://` link is separate — see "Links".

18. **Bullet threading** (GRO-2094, `src/editor/outline/bulletThreading.ts` + `.css`): view-only decorations derived from the anchor on every update (`threadAnchor`: `selection.$from`, or CMD+F's active match while you step, see the end of this rule) — `outline-thread-node` on each list_item on the root → caret path (glyph takes the app accent `--accent` via `--list-marker-color` on its `.label-wrapper`; Crepe's frame `--crepe-color-primary` is #333 and would read as black), and inside each NESTED list on the path `outline-thread-seg` on items 0…pathIndex plus `outline-thread-stop` on the path child (segment cut at its glyph centre, elbow into the bullet). Top-level lists have no guide line and get no segments (Logseq-identical). 2px `--accent` `li::before` at the guide-line x with `pointer-events: none` (a pseudo hit-tests as its element; guide-line click-to-fold needs the UL as target). No state, no persistence, never `markdownUpdated`. Drawn only under `.app[data-threading='on']` — the dialog's Bullet threading › "Show" row (default On, `settings.bulletThreading` in the app state); the dialog's Bullet threading › "Line width" (1/2/3px) and "Line colour" (picker + Default = accent) rows feed `--thread-width` / `--thread-color` (GRO-2109). Caret semantics: the path is that of `selection.$from` — a NodeSelection on an item threads to its parent, a multi-item range threads the first item. While CMD+F shows a match after a query or a step, the path is that of the active match (YAZ-3166, `threadAnchor`); a caret move, an edit, or a click or a key in the note that moves nothing (YAZ-3200) gives it back to the caret. Tests: `editor/outline/bulletThreading.test.ts` ("the active match"), `editor/find/findInPage.test.ts` ("the thread anchor").

18a. **Section indent** (YAZ-2709, decisions D1–D15 are comments on its working log YAZ-2711; `src/editor/outline/sectionIndent.ts` + `.css`, `src/editor/usePageSwitch.ts`, the host effects in `Editor.tsx`; registered in `createCrepe()` right after rule 18's plugin, and numbered 18a so that no later rule changes its number): in a note that uses headings the text stands below its heading, one step in for each section that holds it, and thin vertical lines show the sections; the lines on the way to the caret take rule 18's colour. The heading-shaped twin of rules 13 and 18. **VIEW STATE ONLY**, like folding (rule 5) and line numbers (rule 34): `showSectionIndent(crepe, on)` sends the page's switch in a metadata-only transaction with `addToHistory: false` — never `markdownUpdated`, never the autosave, never undo — and the file on disk never changes. **THE MARKS**: ONE node decoration on each TOP-LEVEL block that is inside a section — `data-sd` (1–6), how many sections hold the block, so how many steps it stands in, and, on the way to the caret, `data-sp` (1–6), how many of its lines, counted from the left, are on the caret's path. Only a direct child of the doc counts: a heading inside a list or a quote makes no section, and a bullet moves in with the list that is its top-level block. A page that is off carries neither mark, so no CSS rule but one (the query container, below) reads the switch. 🔒 **STEPS COUNT BY NESTING, NOT BY HEADING NUMBER** (D3, `sectionDepths`): a stack of the open heading levels — a heading closes every open level at or below its own, stands at the depth that is left, and opens its own. So the first headings of a note stand at the edge whatever their number (a note that starts at H2 has its H2s at the edge), an H3 right under an H1 is one step in, not two, and a heading stands with the text of the section that holds it. **SIX LEVELS** (D9): each of H1–H6 makes a section. Folds stay H1–H3 (rule 29), so an H4–H6 gets an indent and a line but no fold arrow. 🔒 **THE PATH STOPS AT THE CARET'S BLOCK** (D6, rule 18's rule): line k is purple from the block after the k-th heading above the caret, outermost first, down to the top-level block of `selection.$from` — or of CMD+F's active match while you step (YAZ-3166, rule 18) — and no block after that one has a purple line. **NO MARKS WHILE A BULLET IS ZOOMED** (rule 12): the `decorations` prop answers `DecorationSet.empty` while `getZoomedItemPos(state)` is set — asked there and not in `apply`, because a zoom in or out is a metadata-only transaction of its own — and the indent is back on the way out. 🔒 **THE SET IS HAND-BUILT, AND MEASURED** (D1): `build` makes the decorations in ONE pass over the doc's children and hands them, in document order, to ProseMirror's OWN `DecorationSet` constructor (`(local, children)`, which the types of `prosemirror-view` hide as internal). The set is REBUILT — on a document change, on a caret move to another top-level block, on the switch — and never mapped; a caret move inside one block returns the SAME state object (YAZ-2189), and every page that is off shares the one `OFF` state and builds nothing. The reason is a number: `DecorationSet.create` and `set.map` validate each root-level node decoration with a linear scan of the doc's children — 23.6 ms for each key at 2,500 blocks, more than the whole typing budget of 20 ms (YAZ-2236) — against 0.19 ms for the one pass. The VIEW has the same trap on its own side: on every document change it asks the set, for each child of the doc, what reaches INSIDE that child (`forChild`), and ProseMirror answers with a scan of every root-level decoration — 16.5 ms for each key at 2,557 blocks, measured in the running app, where a key cost 23.4 ms with the feature on. So the set is `SectionSet`, a subclass whose `forChild` returns `DecorationSet.empty` at once, which is true because nothing of this set is ever inside a block; after it a key costs 7.2 ms with the feature on and 6.6 ms with it off. `sectionIndent.test.ts` ("the hand-built set") pins the set to what `DecorationSet.create` builds from the same decorations, so an upgrade of `prosemirror-view` that changes the constructor fails a test. Do not swap either for the public API, and do not put an inline or a widget decoration in this set. **THE DRAWING** (`sectionIndent.css`, CSS only): the indent is a transparent `border-left` on the block, `--sd` steps wide, and the lines are a `border-image` gradient INSIDE that border, line k centred one third into step k, sliced to the block's first `--sd` steps. NO pseudo-element — line numbers take `::after` and the table's `::before` (rule 34), and the `overflow` of a table or a code block clips a pseudo-element, which it does not do to the block's own border image — and NO sibling selector: a `~` rule for the path cost 25 ms for each caret move at 2,500 blocks, and a generated rule for each section 77 ms for each structure change. ONE rule for every kind of block (D8): a paragraph, a list, a table, a code block, a quote, a rule and an image all move in; a table and a code block become narrower, and a table still scrolls sideways. The block's box still starts at the column's edge, so what hangs off its padding box moves in with the text and needs no rule — the fold chevron (rule 29), a quote's bar, the line numbers — and the drag handle of a paragraph, a heading, a table or a code block stays at the left edge (D10). `border-image-outset` carries the lines over the block's own margin (a heading's top margin; 4px above and below a code block, a table and a quote). The custom properties of one block (`--sd`, `--section-line`, `--l1`…`--l6`, `--w1`…`--w6`) are registered with `@property` as NOT inherited, so a change of the path restyles the top-level blocks and never their content: a list of a thousand bullets is one block. The grey is OPAQUE (14% of the text colour mixed into `--bg`), so two outsets that overlap do not add up to a darker dash. The empty paragraph Crepe keeps after a last list, table or code block keeps its indent — the first key must not move it — and shows no grey line; the path still reaches it. **THE STEP**: the setting below, or 18px when the note column is 480px or less (D11; a container query on `.milkdown`, the page's parent, which does not zoom, so 480px is the width on screen; `.editor-host[data-section-indent]` makes it the container). **THE PURPLE** (D7): drawn only under `.app[data-threading='on']`, in `--thread-color` and `--thread-width` — rule 18's three rows are the path's too, one look for both, and with Bullet threading off no section line is purple. **THE PAGE SWITCH** (D2): "Section indent" in the page cog (rule 34), one for each note, off by default; there is no setting, hotkey or menu item for it and no default for all notes. `CrepeHost` puts `data-section-indent` on `.editor-host` and tells the plugin when the switch turns on, when a recreated editor is ready, and again after each outside change that lands (`diskLandings`), because `setMarkdown` can rebuild the editor state, which starts off. **ITS STORE** (D2, YAZ-2731): the app state, with the note — `folders[root].sectionIndents[path]`, a boolean ("App state": `folders[root]`), the record YAZ-2700 keeps for a note's table of contents source (`tocSources`, rule 35) on the same terms. `usePageSwitch(root, path, storage.getSectionIndent, storage.setSectionIndent)` reads it when the editor mounts and writes each click through `storage.setSectionIndent` → `state.setSectionIndent`; callers see only `[on, toggle]`. The cog's "Table of contents" uses the same hook with `storage.getTocSwitch` / `storage.setTocSwitch` (YAZ-2950). So the switch is there after a restart, follows a rename or a move of the note, and goes when the note is deleted. 🔒 On AND off are stored — off writes `false` and never removes the entry — so that a default for all notes can come later with no repair of the data; a note with no entry is off. No web storage is used ("App state": "Renderer web storage is not used at all"). ⚠️ Like the table of contents source, the switch is read at MOUNT and not followed after it: an editor that opens the page later — a second tab, the right panel, a second window, the app after a restart — starts with the stored switch, and two editors that are open on one page at the same time each keep what they show until they mount again. **THE TWO LOOK SETTINGS** (D4, D5 — Settings › Editor › Section indent, app-wide, "App state" › `settings`): "Step width" is `sectionStep`, 24 / 30 / 36 px, default 30, which App puts on `.app` as the plain number `--section-step-setting` (`border-image-slice` takes numbers); "Grey lines" is `sectionLines`, "Always show" (`always`, the default) or "Only near the mouse" (`hover`), on `.app` as `data-section-lines` — under `hover` the grey lines show only while the pointer is over the note, and the purple path does not ask the pointer. Another window's change lands live, like every setting. 🔒 **A CLICK ON A LINE FOLDS THE SECTIONS BESIDE IT** (D12, the habit of rule 13): a left press within 5px of a line's centre — the 10px band of a guide line; `sectionLineAt` measures from the block's own border, so the setting, the narrow step and the document zoom all agree with what is drawn — takes the DIRECT child headings of the heading that owns the line (`sectionLineFoldTargets`), and of those only what a chevron folds (H1–H3 with something under them, rule 29). If one of them is open it folds them all; if not, it opens them all (`setHeadingFoldSet`, heading folding's own metadata-only transaction). The press is swallowed BEFORE the fold, so the caret does not move and no text is selected — also when nothing beside the line folds. Over the band the page carries `section-line-hover` (the pointer cursor), and the block handle mutes (rule 15): a bullet's handle floats on the innermost line of its list and would take the press. Known limits, accepted (YAZ-2735, YAZ-2736): the fold arrow of an H1–H3 inside a section covers part of the band of the nearest line on that heading's first text line — 3 of 10 px at a step of 30px, 7 at 24px, all 10 at 18px, none at 36px; when the caret's block is a code block, a table or a quote and a heading or another of the three follows, the next block's 1px grey lies on the path's wider line for 4px; and at a pixel ratio of 1 a 1px or 3px line has its edges on half pixels. Tests: `editor/outline/sectionIndent.test.ts` (depths, the path and CMD+F's active match, the hand-built set, the click, the empty last paragraph, zoom), `editor/blockHandleGate.test.ts` ("a section line"), `editor/Editor.test.tsx` ("section indent is the page's own switch"), `editor/PageSettings.test.tsx`, `App.test.tsx` ("App section indent settings"), `settings/SettingsDialog.test.tsx`, `settings/searchSettings.test.ts`, and for the store `lib/storage.test.ts` ("the section indent switch"), `desktop/src/main/store.test.ts` ("sectionIndents", "setSectionIndent", the rename, the delete and the folder rename), `desktop/src/main/ipc/state.test.ts` ("state:set-section-indent"), `desktop/src/preload/surface.test.ts`. End-to-end: `desktop/e2e/sectionIndent.spec.ts` — the switch from the page cog, the depths and the 30px steps, three purple lines to a caret in an H3 section, a click on the H1's line that folds and opens the H2 sections with the caret in place, the same bytes on disk after a quit, and the switch in the state file and on again after a restart, with off saved as `false` (written for YAZ-2709 and YAZ-2731, not run). Typing speed: `npm run perf -- typing`, rows `prose5k` and `prose5kIndent` (`tools/perf/README.md`; written, not run).

19. **Base files** — TOMBSTONE (GRO-2125, deleted in YAZ-844): `.base` is no longer a file the app opens. `BaseHost` (the main-pane host with its view/raw-YAML modes, its own autosave baseline and the "opening a base and doing nothing never writes" invariant) is gone, `Editor` has no `.base` branch: it dispatches supported files to their Markdown/text/PDF/image capability owners, while a `.base` on disk remains unsupported: invisible to the index, not openable in-app, not creatable — it lists in the tree with `kind: null` (YAZ-1577 D4) and clicking it hands it to the OS. What survives is the ENGINE, the views, `ViewsPane` and the schema types (`viewSchema.ts`'s `parseViews` / `serializeViews` / `updateViews`), all of them a folder's internals now: the views live in the folder's `.folder.md`, under `folder_settings`, and render on the folder's page, where the behaviour lives on ("Folders are the pages"). The 1B normalisation note travels with them — `yaml`'s `indentSeq` is document-global, so a views block mixing sequence-indent styles is re-indented to one style on its first REAL save. What the `.base` file's byte-identical round trip becomes here is narrower and stated honestly: every other frontmatter key of `.folder.md` survives, because `writeFolderSettings` goes through the one-key writer — but the settings block itself is rebuilt from the parsed value, so comments and hand-formatting INSIDE `folder_settings` do not survive an edit to it.

20. **Base embeds** — TOMBSTONE (GRO-2145, deleted in YAZ-844): `![[X.base]]` / `![[X.base#View]]` no longer renders anything. The whole `src/editor/baseEmbed/` folder — the `$prose` decoration plugin, the slot store, the `BaseEmbed` widget and `resolveBase`'s shortest-path resolution over `api.tree` — is gone, and with it the read-only embed chrome's only production caller — `ViewsPane`'s `readOnly` and `initialView` props outlived it by one unit and were amputated in YAZ-846 (see "View chrome"). An `![[X.base]]` left in a note is now just an ordinary embed whose target does not exist: the text stays byte-identical, nothing renders under it. A folder's page is where views are read now, and it is not embeddable anywhere else — one folder, one page, always its own notes ("Folders are the pages").

21. **`base` code blocks** — TOMBSTONE (GRO-2146, deleted in YAZ-844): a fenced block with `language === 'base'` is a plain CodeMirror code block again. `src/editor/baseCodeBlock/` — the `$view` replacement for `code_block`, its slot store, the `BaseCodeBlock` widget and the raw-YAML toggle — is gone, `createCrepe` no longer takes `baseCodeBlocks`, and every language now delegates to Crepe's stock block. The text on disk was always the exact code-block text, so nothing about any existing note changed except that the block stops rendering as a view. Views live in a folder's settings now, edited through the toolbar rather than through YAML by hand (rule 19's tombstone, "Folders are the pages").

22. **Typed-page scaffolds & the new-entity flow** — TOMBSTONE (Bible B GRO-2202, deleted in YAZ-836): the registry scaffold, `page_type`, per-type templates, the starter `All <pluralName>.base`, `createType` / `NewTypeDialog` and the sidebar's "New ▸ <type>" submenu are all gone; a new note is born in its FOLDER from that folder's `.template.md` and the caller's seed, and nothing else ("Folders are the pages": Births — `createNote`), and the still-valid vault-wide property declarations moved to `.yaseendocs/properties.json` ("Properties"). The number is kept because rules 23-26 and the `// rule N` citations in the code index into this list; `ensureFolder` is the one helper of `src/views/scaffold.ts` that outlived the type half.

23. **Wikilinks in the editor** (Links A, GRO-2190, `src/editor/wikilink/`): `[[target]]` renders Obsidian-live-preview style via DECORATIONS only (`wikilinkPlugin.ts`, registered in `createCrepe()` — never a Crepe feature, the allowlist is untouched; never a schema/serializer change, so the text round-trips byte-identically — `roundtrip.test.ts` pins alias / heading / `#^block` / adjacent / inside-bold / unicode-and-spaces / unclosed-`[[` forms). Caret OUTSIDE the match: the `[[` `]]` brackets (plus `target|` before an alias and each `#`) get `wikilink__syntax` (CSS `display: none`); visible text carries `wikilink` (accent colour; a resolved link is a pill with its file's icon, YAZ-3609 D13); `[[t|alias]]` shows only the alias; `[[t#h]]` shows `t > h` (each post-`#` segment gets `wikilink__sub`, whose `::before` draws the separator). An ID link (YAZ-2293 — the target is a note's `id` and the source resolves it) hides the id as well and shows the note's CURRENT TITLE — `IndexRecord.title`: its frontmatter `title`, or with none its file name without the extension (YAZ-2420 D14) — in its place: the ONE widget decoration here (`idLinkTitle` gives the title; the widget is keyed by it and wears the classes the id text would have worn), where every other decoration only hides or styles characters the document holds. The title is read off the index at each build, so a rename — by anything — changes what the link shows and not one byte of the document. `[[<id>#h]]` shows `Title > h`; a hand-typed `[[<id>|label]]` shows its label, never the title; an id NO note has, in a vault with IDs, shows "Missing note · <id>" in a widget in the title's place, dimmed (`missingId`, YAZ-3905 S10; elsewhere it is the raw id, dimmed exactly like an unresolved name); an unresolved `[[LETTERS-NUMBER]]` with the letters of another vault of the window shows its vault after it, " (<vault>)" or " (another vault)" when two share them, in a `vaultSpan` widget, dimmed (`otherVaultId`, the window's `VaultsOfLetters`, S23); and before the index has loaded an id shows raw and undimmed. A link that resolves shows its page's NAME (`pageTrim`, YAZ-3778 D2, D3): the folders of a pathed `[[folder/name]]` and an extension the sidebar hides (`fileLabel`: `.md`, a drawing's, a diagram's) are `wikilink__syntax` too, but a drawing's or a diagram's extension is the pill's last piece with `name-ending`, which app.css shows only with File icons Off, as the sidebar's (YAZ-3924); a dead link keeps its whole text (S12). An ID link's title widget is drawn at the link's END, before the caret there, when nothing follows the id, and where the id was before a heading part (`[[<id>#h]]`): a click past it reads as the link's end (YAZ-3916). Every shown part, title and vault widget has spellcheck off (S13). Each hidden range carries `syntax: true` in its decoration spec and the title widget `title`, which ⌘F reads (`pillLinks`): a match in a pill's hidden text marks the whole pill once, and each match in its title is one (YAZ-3744 S9, `editor/find/findInPage.ts`). `linkDisplayText(inner, titleOf?)` is that one mapping, shared with the backlinks snippets (rule 25). Resolved vs unresolved comes from the ONE resolver (`resolverFor`, see "Link resolution" — and, for a target no note answers, the FOLDER of that name: `linkResolver`, YAZ-2290 D10, "Links": Links to folders; such a link is resolved, opens the folder's tab on click and is never created): an unresolvable target dims via `wikilink--unresolved`; an empty target (`[[#h]]`) is a same-file link, never dimmed. A match whose DISPLAY would be empty (`[[Note|]]`, `[[|]]`, `[[#]]`) gets NO decorations at all and stays raw and editable (GRO-2197): hiding every part of it would erase the text from the page and leave no `.wikilink` span for the click handler either. EVERY LINK IS ONE UNIT (YAZ-3744 D1 for ID links, replacing YAZ-2293's "caret inside an ID link shows the raw `[[<id>]]`"; YAZ-3935, point 3 of YAZ-3879, for every link, replacing the old caret-adjacency reveal of name links): a link that shows as a pill (`isLinkUnit`: its display is not empty) opens — its decorations drop, raw editable syntax — only with the selection STRICTLY inside it, which "Edit link" alone puts there (`OPEN_ID_LINK`); a caret next to it keeps the pill (`opens`, no index lookup). Its sibling `idLinkCaret.ts` keeps the caret off its hidden text, which is why `display: none` hiding is arrow-safe: a caret that lands inside a closed link (after a selection change, never on an edit or a composition) steps to the other edge from one edge only after ← or → (with ⇧ or ⌥; G2 of YAZ-3966), else to the nearer edge; Backspace right after it and Delete right before it (⌥ and ⌃H / ⌃D too) remove the whole link (⌘Z puts it back). A double-click on a word next to a link (C2) is cut at the links on each side of the word clicked, so it never runs into a pill's text, hidden or shown. A link with nothing to show (`[[Note|]]`) stays raw text and is no unit. A plain-text copy and the crumb, tab tooltip, Back list and TOC labels read links through `linksAsShown` (YAZ-3744 D6, S8). Excluded: `![[…]]` embeds (they stay plain text — the base-embed widget that used to claim some of them died in YAZ-844, rule 20's tombstone) and code (`code_block` nodes and inline-`code` marks — mirrors the index's `stripCode`). Resolution reaches the plugin through a per-window `WikilinkResolveSource` (`createCrepe({ wikilinks })`): App owns one stable source and `WikilinkIndexBridge` feeds it from `useIndex`; an index update swaps the resolve function and pokes each subscribed editor with a META transaction — decorations recompute live, the editor never remounts, the doc never changes, `markdownUpdated` never fires. Interaction (Links C, GRO-2192, `wikilinkClick.ts` + `createFromLink.ts`, wired as `createCrepe({ wikilinkNav })` — App threads this window's tabs API + its notice setter through `Editor`): THE CLICK MODEL (YAZ-3935 and YAZ-3936, C1–C4 of YAZ-3879, reversing GRO-2192 / YAZ-3609 D11's "a plain click opens a link" in an editable note): a click on a link in an editable note works as on text. On a collapsed `.wikilink` span a plain click acts on MOUSEDOWN with the default prevented (so no raw-text flash): the caret goes to the pill's nearer edge, the pointer's x against the middle of the link's shown pieces on that line; a double-click selects exactly the link; a triple-click and a ⇧ / ⌥ click stay the browser's. A Markdown link that is a pill (a path in a vault of the window) is one unit by the same rules (YAZ-4021, demo round 4, replacing point 3's "Markdown links keep their real text"): `markdownPillsAround` (`markdownLink.ts`) gives each pill's range from its decorations, `idLinkCaret.ts` keeps the caret out of it and removes it whole, its mousedown puts a click on its nearer edge and a double-click over all of it, and `handleTextInput` keeps a letter typed at its end out of the link mark. Any other Markdown link takes the native caret in its words.
