Only a gesture of Settings › Hotkeys › "Links in a note" opens (`shared/keys/gestures.ts`, `gestureAction`, read at the click from `settings.hotkeys` through `nav.hotkeys`): by default (browser style, G6 of YAZ-3966) "Open in this tab" has no gesture (`nav.openCurrent`, App's `openLink(path, 'thisTab')`: the workspace's `navigate` since YAZ-2648 D3 — the target takes the tab the link was clicked in, an already-open path goes to its tab, and Back returns to the note with the link, D10), ⌘-click → "Open in a background tab" (`openBackground` — appended, never activated, focus untouched; already-open → no-op), ⌘⇧-click → "Open in a new tab" (`nav.openNewTab`, App's `openKept`); "the old way" is Links › Open in this tab on Click. A read-only note keeps "a click opens" (a plain click → this tab, `linkClickAction`); a preview has no click plugin. Clicks on REVEALED raw text never navigate (a revealed match has no decoration span — that IS editing). The pointer is the text cursor on a link of an editable note and the hand only while a bound open gesture's modifiers are held: `data-link-hand` on the editor's root, set by a window keydown / keyup / blur listener that acts on a modifier's own key alone (`trackLinkHand`); a read-only note shows the hand. The hover card says how to open it, in one quiet line from the bound gesture ("⌘-click to open", `linkOpenHint`; "Click to open" in a read-only note). An UNRESOLVED link CREATES its page first (`createFromLink`) — only on an open gesture, never on a plain click (point 5 of YAZ-3879) — then opens by the same gesture — except an unresolved ID link (YAZ-2293), which is NEVER created: an id names a note that existed, so a page called `<id>.md` would be a different note wearing its name, and the click says `That note no longer exists` through the passive link-notice — `This vault does not use IDs, so this link cannot be opened` where it does not (YAZ-2523) — and does nothing else. What an ID link IS, is asked of the vault (`vaultNoteId(page, source.letters)`, YAZ-2677 R5): an old ID, or a number ID with the vault's letters, now or before (`[[YAZ-99]]`, S25); any other `LETTERS-NUMBER` text — `[[GPT-4]]`, `[[BUS-12]]` from another vault — is a NAME and is created like any name (R6, S21, S22), and a vault that does not use IDs has no letters, so `[[COVID-19]]` is a name there (a RESOLVING id link opens from its title widget, which carries `.wikilink`; the hit-test reads a widget as the position before it, `linkPosAtDOM`, so it finds its own link like any segment). For every other unresolved link: `|alias`/`#…` stripped (`linkPageName` — the ONE strip with the decorations); `[[#h]]` (empty target, same-file) is a no-op — the heading jump is GRO-2239; a bare target creates under the "Default location for new notes" setting (C2-, GRO-2240): `current` (default, YAZ-1643) → the SOURCE page's folder — the page the link was clicked or typed in, so a right-panel editor creates beside ITSELF, and a folder's outline as a note in that folder would (its `.folder.md` stands in as the source), never beside the main tab (a source outside the vault → the root), `root` → the vault root, `folder` → `<root>/<newNoteFolder>` — App resolves it (`newNoteBase`) behind a stable ref-backed `newNoteFolderFor(sourcePath)` getter threaded through `Editor` into `wikilinkNav` as `createFolder` (each editor binds its OWN path) and read at CLICK time, so settings changes land live without remounting any editor; a pathed `[[Sub/Page]]` (or `[[/Page]]`) is an EXPLICIT AIM: always root-relative whatever the setting (Obsidian's behavior), with missing parents — the base FOLDER of the setting included — created level by level (scaffold's `ensureFolder`); what was typed is the new note's TITLE (YAZ-2420 D20) — for a pathed target its last segment, the earlier ones being the TITLES of its folders (D6), each a folder that is already there, by title and then by directory name, before it is one to make (YAZ-2478) — and the file is the name `createNote` builds from it; two notes of one title are two files, so the disk refuses no second one, and a click on a dead link whose note is still being made does nothing (YAZ-2478); an invalid segment of the setting's base folder (`validateEntryName`) and create failures surface via the passive link-notice — never a dialog. Two more notices, both GRO-2197: a click landing in the PRE-INDEX window (no resolver yet, so every link still renders resolved and creating anything could shadow an existing note) is still swallowed, but now SAYS so instead of doing nothing at all; and a background open that CREATES a page names it in a notice, because a background tab is by definition not shown and the gesture otherwise looks like nothing happened. The watcher-driven index refetch then flips unresolved→resolved styling everywhere on its own (the live restyle above). **Right-click on a rendered link** (YAZ-2293, YAZ-3609 D23, `wikilinkMenu.ts`, registered with the click plugin on the same source and nav — so only when `wikilinkNav` is given): the one link menu (`linkMenu.ts`, "Links": One link menu) in rule 26's `.ctx-menu.ctx-menu--editor` popup. An id link hides its id, so this menu is where the id can be SEEN and copied: its id as one disabled top line, `ID: <id>` (YAZ-3747: the title is the pill's, so the line no longer repeats it; a name link, a folder link and a Markdown link have no top line), and **Copy ID** — the one place it is offered, and only where the vault uses IDs (`source.ids`, YAZ-2523) (YAZ-2420 D31; "Note ids": Copy ID). An id no note has reads (Missing note) (its id) (S10); any id before the index loads has no name row; the id and Copy ID are still offered. The right-button MOUSEDOWN — and a Ctrl-click's left-button one, macOS's other right-click — is swallowed on a rendered link for the click handler's own reason: left to its default the caret lands in the match, the reveal rule drops the rendered span, and `contextmenu` arrives on raw text. The popup closes on a row click, an outside mousedown, a scroll, Escape, window blur and any doc change, one at a time. A name link and a view-only link get the same menu with no ID rows; revealed raw text and plain text keep the native menu — nothing is prevented or drawn for them.

24. **The `[[` link picker** (Links B, GRO-2191, `src/editor/wikilink/wikilinkPicker.ts` + `.css`): typing `[[` in any non-code textblock opens a suggestion popup over every markdown note in the vault — and, since YAZ-2290 D10, every folder, its rows after the notes', reading `<title> (folder)` and inserted by id — by title or path when it has none ("Links": Links to folders) —; typing filters, ↑/↓ navigate (wraparound), Enter or click INSERTS PLAIN TEXT — `[[<id>]]` when the note has an `id` (YAZ-2293, **By id** below), else `[[name]]` — (replacing `[[fragment` up to the caret — never a schema/doc-structure change; the rule-23 decorations restyle it on their next pass, raw while the caret still touches it), Esc dismisses leaving the typed text — and that same `[[` stays closed while typing continues (a fresh `[[` reopens). Candidates come from the index through the shared matcher (`links/completion.ts` — the ONE `[[…]]` matcher with EditableCell's link editors). Matching is case-insensitive over the candidate NAME with the typed fragment trimmed at its ENDS (internal spaces are letters to the three text tiers and splits between words to the two word tiers), RANKED exact → prefix → substring → word match → joined match (YAZ-3748 D2) and stable within each tier, capped at 8 AFTER ranking (GRO-2197 — so `[[cac` puts the note actually named `CAC` first instead of whatever the path order happened to reach first). Ranking means the full candidate list is scanned every keystroke, which the per-candidate lowercase precomputed at construction pays for; the 5,000-record smoke in `completion.perf.test.ts` (the `perf` project) is the budget guard: `linkCandidates(records)` lists each note under its TITLE (YAZ-2420 D17 — the basename of a note that has no `title:`) — duplicate titles follow the resolver's shallowest-depth rule, so the bare title belongs to the shallowest match and every other duplicate shows as `folder/title` and inserts its root-relative `folder/basename`, the path no title joins. **Aliases** (E2, GRO-2214): a note with frontmatter `aliases` also gets ONE row per alias — typed as the alias, shown as `CAC — Customer Acquisition Cost` (the note half is that note's own unambiguous name, so duplicate aliases are folder-disambiguated by construction) and INSERTING the piped `[[Customer Acquisition Cost|CAC]]`, which targets the note and displays the alias. The piped form is exact whoever else claims the alias, so an alias row is unambiguous exactly like a folder-disambiguated duplicate; a row matches on its own name only (never on the note half of its label). Two alias rows are skipped outright (GRO-2197): one whose alias IS the note's own chosen name (it would read `CAC — CAC` and insert the pointless `[[CAC|CAC]]`), and one whose alias contains `[` or `]` (its piped insert would re-parse as the inner link and point somewhere else entirely). **By id** (YAZ-2293, 🔒): a note that has an `id` is offered under exactly the same rows — typed and read by its title, its `folder/title`, or `Alias — Note` — but EVERY one of them inserts the plain `[[<id>]]`: no name, no pipe, so the link survives any rename or move, and rule 23 shows the note's current title in its place. The names above are then only what a row is TYPED and READ as; a note with no id keeps inserting them. A non-empty fragment that no matched row is NAMED (trimmed, any case) offers ONE "Create" row, below the matches (YAZ-3748 B1; before, only when nothing matched — the word tiers made that rarer): it creates the page right there AND links it by the id it is born with (YAZ-2293), in a fixed order (🔒 YAZ-2677 S35): the NUMBER first, then the link, then the note. At the pick the picker replaces `[[fragment` with the name link `[[typed text]]`, the caret after it — the brackets are closed at once, so what the user types during the wait lands after the link and no character is lost (S36) — and asks the door for the vault's next ID (`api.mintNoteId(nav.root)`, bridge table). The plugin state follows the place of the typed page name through every edit made meanwhile (`PickerState.waiting`, each place mapped per transaction). When the number comes, `[[<id>]]` takes the place of the typed page name where it now stands (a `#heading` typed after it rides along) — only while that text still reads as it was typed: a name the user changed or deleted during the wait is theirs and stays — and the same id goes to `createFromLink`, which passes it to `createNote` and so to `createFile({ path, content, id })`, the typed text being the note's title (YAZ-2420 D20). No number (the door fails): nothing is made, the link stays the typed name, and the failure is said. `null` from the door (the vault stopped using IDs after the pick): the page is made the plain way (YAZ-1357, 🔒 D3 revised — Yasin's ruling that a picked Create shows up in the sidebar at once: `createFromLink` under `nav.createFolder()`, the same placement as create-on-click — beside the page being typed in (YAZ-1643), no navigation, a passive `Created "…"` notice). When NO page is born with that id — a create failure, said through the same notice — the id in the document goes back to the typed page name, found by its text wherever typing has since pushed it. Without a nav there is no vault to create in, so the row only inserts `[[typed text]]` as-is. Where the vault does not use IDs (`source.ids` false, YAZ-2523 V3 — "Two kinds of vault") the door is not asked: the row inserts `[[typed text]]` and the page is made the plain way, as `<typed text>.md`. A hand-typed dangling link is still created on click (rule 23's Links C interaction); typing `|` is alias entry: the suggestions close and typing continues as plain text. Anatomy: a `$prose` plugin owns the state (session recomputed per transaction from doc + selection; candidate updates poke a meta transaction — same live-update pattern as rule 23) and the row DOM (`role="listbox"`/`option`, mousedown-preventDefault, theme tokens); `SlashProvider` (`@milkdown/kit/plugin/slash`) positions the popup at the caret and toggles `data-show` (its one-char `trigger` cannot express `[[`, so it runs a custom `shouldShow` over the plugin state; closing hides directly — the provider skips meta-only transactions). Keys ride `wikilinkPickerKeymap` (`$shortcut`, priority 100 — see "Keyboard"): every command declines (`return false`) while the picker is closed, so ↑/↓/Enter/Esc are NEVER swallowed then; the Enter tie with the outliner's priority-100 Enter breaks by addition order — `createCrepe()` MUST `use` this keymap before `outlinerKeymap` (`wikilinkPicker.test.ts` pins both directions). Per-window plumbing mirrors rule 23: `createCrepe({ wikilinkCandidates })`, App owns one `WikilinkCandidateSource`, `WikilinkIndexBridge` feeds it `linkCandidates(records)` per ready snapshot. No new GLOBAL hotkeys — the Hotkeys page (rule 16) is untouched.

25. **Backlinks — "Linked mentions"** (Links D, GRO-2193, `src/links/backlinks.ts` + `BacklinksSection.tsx` + `backlinks.css`; decision D of GRO-2096 and the GRO-2193 placement thread, both LOCKED). **Storage**: none — the referencing set is computed CLIENT-SIDE in ONE pass over the Markdown index snapshot the window already holds (`backlinksFor`), through THE shared semantic resolver (`resolverFor`, see "Link resolution"). View-only files never enter that snapshot or resolver and therefore never receive or contribute backlinks. No reverse map in the main process, no new IPC, no new `IndexRecord` field, and no watcher of its own: auto-refresh rides the existing 300 ms-debounced index refetch. A mention is a Markdown record's `links` **or** `embeds` entry resolving to the open Markdown path — an `![[embed]]` mentions its target exactly like a `[[link]]` — with the open note itself excluded, ONE entry per referencing note however many mentions it holds, path-sorted. A FOLDER's page mentions what its settings record links by the rename engine's rule (`referenceTargets`, never a second reading of `folder_settings`): its own link properties (`owner: "[[Alice]]"` in `.folder.md`), a view's `order` entry, a link column's `target`; and any link in a line of its outlines, prose included, as a note's body does (`folderMentionSnippets`). The folder is ONE entry — its `.folder.md` record, sorted by that file's path — and never lists itself. Alias-awareness is free (E2, GRO-2214): a note linking `[[CAC]]` IS a linked mention of the page whose frontmatter aliases it. So is id-awareness (YAZ-2293): a note linking `[[<id>]]` IS a linked mention of the note that id names. Results are memoized per (records array identity, path) in a WeakMap (`resolverFor`'s idiom), so one snapshot costs one pass per open path however many Markdown tab layers are mounted. **Placement**: a collapsible block near the BOTTOM of a Markdown note, INSIDE the editor's scroller — `.editor-host` holds `.page-title` (block ZERO, ⚡ YAZ-888), `.frontmatter-panel` (block ONE, ⚡ YAZ-883), `.editor-mount` (where the Crepe instance lands), the comment stream ("Comments", 🔒 D4), then the section, then "Reviews" (YAZ-2322) — so it scrolls WITH the note, Obsidian's in-document mode. No right panel, no sidebar section; one per Markdown tab. A FOLDER's page carries the same section as its last block, listing the notes and the folders that link to the folder (YAZ-2290 D10, `FolderView`); text/PDF/image dispatch before these hosts and mount none of it. **Header**: "Linked mentions (N)" with the view-group chevron (rotated −90° while collapsed), no hairline above it (YAZ-1680), COLLAPSED by default, N always visible — and N === 0 renders NOTHING at all (quiet over complete: Obsidian's in-document mode keeps an empty block, we do not). **Snippets, on demand**: an entry only mounts while the section is EXPANDED and reads its Markdown file from that mount (`fs:read`) — collapsed costs zero reads, and the index stores no positions. A snippet is the mention's own LINE — one snippet per line however many mentions it holds (GRO-2197) — whitespace-trimmed and windowed to ~120 chars around the FIRST mention with `…` on the clipped sides, at most 5 lines per note. The line reads exactly as the editor renders it: every wikilink on it is shown as its DISPLAY text through the shared `linkDisplayText` (`[[Note|CAC]]` → `CAC`, `[[Note#H]]` → `Note > H`, an id link → its note's current title through `idLinkTitle` and an id no note has → the raw id, exactly as rule 23 draws them (YAZ-2293), embeds and the empty-display forms of rule 23 stay raw), never the raw `[[…]]` source, and EVERY mention of the open note on that line is highlighted (`<mark class="backlinks__match">` per range, so a line mentioning it twice is one row with two marks; a mention pushed outside the window by the ~120-char clip drops, the centred one never does). Code is skipped through the rename engine's length-preserving `maskCode` (the index's `stripCode` mirror), and frontmatter lines scan like any other — the index reads links there too, though only as whole-value exact `[[…]]` strings, so a frontmatter line CAN highlight a mention the index did not count (GRO-2197 audit, deferred). A skeleton bar shows while a read is in flight; a FAILED read leaves the entry standing WITHOUT snippets — never a dialog, never a notice. A FOLDER entry reads nothing: its snippets are the bullets of its outlines that hold the link (`folderMentionSnippets` — the same `mentionSnippets`, over the outline text the index already holds), and none when it links only by `order` or `target`. **Live**: a fresh snapshot recomputes N (and drops the whole section when the last mention goes); an EXPANDED entry re-reads its snippets only when its own record's `mtime` moved — changed files only, so unrelated vault activity costs no reads. **Clicks**: plain → the CURRENT tab (the section's `openCurrent` prop, fed `navigate` like a wiki link's), ⌘ → a BACKGROUND tab (`openBackground`) — the same model as wiki-link clicks (rule 23); a sidebar row's plain click is no longer the same (YAZ-2648 D1: it goes to the preview tab); entry title and snippet rows behave identically (title = the page's title, YAZ-2420 D14, tooltip = the full path; a folder entry is titled by the folder's title and opens the folder's page). **Collapse state** is per-component and in-memory: since every visited Markdown tab keeps its editor layer mounted (rule 4) it is effectively per tab for the session, and it is never persisted — an open backlinks block is not part of a note's identity. **Feed**: the per-window `WikilinkResolveSource` carries the semantic resolver AND the Markdown snapshot it was built from (`update(resolve, records)`, fed by `WikilinkIndexBridge` — one semantic snapshot feed for decorations, the Markdown picker rows and backlinks alike), while the view-only catalog remains a separate navigation-only source; the section subscribes only to the semantic source, so index updates never re-render App or remount an editor.

26. **Block handle menu + numbered lists** (YAZ-726/728/729/793/1329, YAZ-3727, `src/editor/blockHandleMenu.ts`, `outline/numberChildren.ts`, `outline/numberChildrenRow.ts`, registered in `createCrepe()`): right-click on the 6-dot handle opens a `.ctx-menu.ctx-menu--editor` popup mounted in the editor's own parent (no overlay; closes on outside mousedown, Escape, scroll, window blur and any doc change). Rows are DATA from a `RowProvider` called at open time with the probe target (`blockHandleTarget.handleTargetPos`, shared with multi-block drag) — the plugin never knows what a row does. An item is a row (`MenuRow`: a label, `disabled`, a `run`) or, since YAZ-3164 (🔒 D3 as amended in the guided test, rule 41), a PICKER: a NUMBER FIELD (`MenuNumberField`, `kind: 'number'`: a label, a unit `%` or `px`, the current value or `null`, presets, the current default, a range, an error text and a `run(value | null)`) or a CHOICE (`MenuChoiceField`, `kind: 'choice'`: a label, the current value or `null`, choices — each a value, a label and an optional sample class — the current default and a `run(value | null)`). Each picker is ONE row (`.block-menu-picker`): the name on the left, a value button on the right (`50% ▾`, `Solid ▾`; `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls` its panel); one divider separates the rows from the pickers. The menu opens with every picker closed and takes NO focus (S80). A click on a value — or Enter / Space on a focused one — opens that picker's panel and closes any other (S81); a second click closes it (S82). A number panel is the document zoom menu's, on its own classes (`.document-zoom__custom`, `.document-zoom__divider`, `.document-zoom__presets`, `.document-zoom__error`): the box (focused, text selected), a divider, the presets; a choice panel lists the choices in `.document-zoom__presets`, each with its sample. Each list starts with "Default (<the current default>)" (`fallback`), which runs `null`; a picker whose value is `null` reads that on its value button (YAZ-3208 D11). The current one is `aria-pressed` with a ✓. Enter applies a whole number in range, the unit optional; a preset or a choice applies; each then closes the WHOLE menu (S83). A bad number shows the error (`role="alert"`), sets `aria-invalid` and keeps the menu open, and typing clears it; the current value runs nothing (no document change, no undo step); the box's Escape closes and stops there. Enter on a box the user has not typed in since the menu opened closes with no run (YAZ-3222): the box starts with the current default for a field that follows it, and that text is no pick; a typed value is a pick, the default's too (D9). Tab pressed in the editor while a menu with pickers shows goes to the first value button (Shift-Tab to the last), before the outliner's Tab (S84); inside the menu Tab is the browser's. Every other close is the rows' (a draft is dropped), and a close with the focus in the menu puts it back in the editor. The added CSS (`app.css`, scoped under `.ctx-menu--editor` so Crepe's `.milkdown button` reset does not win) is the row, the value button, the panel's padding, the samples' gap, and the zoom menu's 12px for its classes inside the editor. A menu of rows only takes no focus and no Tab, so the id link's menu (rule 23, `wikilinkMenu.ts`, which shares `renderMenu`) is unchanged. The line's kind first (YAZ-3727 D13, D14, `outline/turnIntoRows.ts`): ONE strip (`MenuStrip`, `.ctx-menu__strip`) of four icon buttons drawn as the selection toolbar's (32px boxes, 24px glyphs, outline colour, the toolbar's hover; the lit one in a soft accent box in the accent colour, `--accent-soft` / `--accent`, D16: the toolbar's dark-on-grey was too faint) — Bullet list, Numbered list, Checklist, then Text last (D18: the most used first, Text the least used; the toolbar keeps its own order); icons only, each named by its tooltip and `aria-label`, `aria-pressed` when lit. They run the toolbar's own commands (`toggleListKind`, `turnLinesIntoText`, rule 42b) for the LINE the handle or dot points at — a list item's first block, or a paragraph or heading; never a code block, a table cell, or a table, rule or image the handle points at, also in a bullet. Which lines: highlighted text (more than zero width) that covers the line → the highlighted lines; else on an item line → the WHOLE list it is in, one level (`listLines`: its siblings; their children keep their kind), except the zoomed bullet's own line (its siblings are hidden); else that line. Lit = every one of those lines is that kind; a lit button takes them out of their list, as on the toolbar; one undo step. So a paragraph or a heading has a menu too. A note that cannot change has no strip and no children rows. "Open in new tab" has no glyph (YAZ-3727 D19), so no row of the menu is pushed right to line up after one. Its line between groups spaces as the app menus' (4px above and below, `.ctx-menu--editor > .document-zoom__divider`, D21). A right-click on a line's TEXT shows the same rows (D15): Open in new tab, the strip and the children rows come from this menu's own list (`blockMenuItems(view, target)`, the pickers left out; the target is `textLineTarget`, a bullet's first line standing for its bullet) into the note's own menu (below). There a highlight is read on the selection from before the right press, since the press may select the word under the pointer. On a line that folds (a bullet with children, or a heading of level 1-3 with a block in its section), the children group ends with **Collapse all** and **Expand all** (YAZ-3727 D23, `outline/foldAllRows.ts`): `setAllDocumentFolds` from `outline/foldAllHotkeys.ts`, every bullet and heading at once, one ⌘Z, the note keys' hints (⌘⇧U, ⌘⇧I) — the dot's, the text's and the fold chevron's menu alike, as a code tab's fold arrows offer them (YAZ-3478). Then, after a line: "Number children" ↔ "Bullet children" flips EVERY direct child list of the hovered `list_item` between `bullet_list` and `ordered_list` in one transaction (one undo step); it REPLACES the child list's marker type, never stacks a bullet and number on one row; grandchildren untouched; absent when the item has no direct child list (D13; before, a disabled row) and when the block is not in a list item (YAZ-3696 B3). The menu does not open with no rows (a code block). Next row, on a line of a numbered list only: "Bullets with written numbers" (YAZ-3727 D12, `writeNumbersAsText`, `writtenNumbersRow`) turns that list into a bullet list and writes each line's shown number at the start of its text as `n) ` (`3. apples` → `* 3) apples`); sublists untouched; one transaction, one undo step. That row is the ONE list command that writes paragraph text, and only on the user's click; every other list command NEVER reads or writes it — hand-typed same-line `* 1) Setup` is literal text under rule 8. **This is the only editor COMMAND that numbers children**: `createCrepe()` removes `Mod-Alt-7` `orderedListKeymap` and configures BlockEdit without the slash-menu Ordered List row. Typing a marker (YAZ-3727 D8, D9, `listMarkerTyping.ts`) replaces upstream's `wrapInOrderedListInputRule` and `wrapInBulletListInputRule`: a typed SPACE after `n.` (1 to 9 digits, as CommonMark reads a marker) or `*` / `-` / `+` that is the whole text before the caret, on a line in no list item and not code, goes in as text, then the line is wrapped in a list as its own undo step (`closeHistory`) — a number starts at `n` and joins a numbered list right above when `childCount + order === n`, a bullet joins a bullet list right above. ⌘Z, or Backspace right after the conversion (`undoListMarker`, priority 200), runs history `undo`: the line is plain `1. ` again. Its "just converted" flag survives the appended `listMarkers` transaction and the list node view's same-caret restore one frame later; any other document change or caret move clears it. It is a `handleTextInput` prop, not an input rule, so Enter never converts (Milkdown runs input rules on Enter). Inside a list item the marker stays text (E1), and so does a marker typed right below a plain line (same parent) that starts with a written label of its kind — `2. `, `2) ` for a number, `* `, `- `, `+ ` for a bullet (YAZ-3727 D11). Explicit ordered Markdown still loads/persists because it is the command's disk format and valid imported/pasted content. Each item's marker (`listType`, `label`) follows its list: `outline/listMarkers.ts` replaces Milkdown's `syncListOrderPlugin` and, after every document change, visits only the lists the change touched (YAZ-3727 D2); a change whose every step writes inside one textblock, before and after the step (typing), visits none (YAZ-3855). Right-button mousedown/mouseup on the handle are stopped at document capture so Crepe's NodeSelection + focus never fire for a right-click.

27. **Drawing previews in the page** (YAZ-878, third build unit of the Excalidraw embed YAZ-852, `src/editor/drawing/drawingPreview.ts` + `.css`, registered in `createCrepe()` only when `opts.drawingPreview` supplies the vault root): an `![[Sketch.excalidraw]]` embed RENDERS AS THE SCENE. **DECORATIONS ONLY** (🔒 the same rule as 23): the embed stays plain markdown TEXT — no schema node, no serializer, no node view — so round trip is byte-identical (`roundtrip.test.ts` plus a guard in the plugin's own test). ProseMirror has no replace-a-range-with-a-widget decoration, so the mechanism is the honest pair the codebase already uses: a `Decoration.inline` over the whole match carrying `drawing-embed__syntax` (CSS `display: none`, `wikilink__syntax`'s exact mechanism) plus a `Decoration.widget` at the match START (`side: -1`, `contenteditable="false"`, `key` = target + state so PM reuses the DOM node and a settled preview never flickers). **REVEAL** is rule 23's, with boundaries **EXCLUSIVE** instead of inclusive: a selection strictly INSIDE the match drops both decorations (raw, editable syntax), while the caret sitting immediately before or after it keeps the preview — because YAZ-877's insert leaves the caret exactly there and an inclusive rule would hide the preview the insert exists to show. Boundary behaviour stays sane either way: an arrow key off an edge steps inside and reveals, and Backspace at the right edge eats the final `]`, un-matching the embed and leaving what a plain-text delete leaves. **ONLY `.excalidraw` TARGETS** (`isDrawingTarget`, case-insensitive suffix): every other embed (`![[img.png]]`), every link, and anything inside a code block or an inline-`code` run is untouched. The target goes to `readAsset` **RAW** — path or bare basename — because that is where the resolution rule lives (YAZ-876); the renderer never joins paths. **STATES**: *loading* is a quiet empty frame (no spinner — nothing to jitter); *ready* is the SVG inside that same frame (`max-width: 100%`, `max-height: 24em`, `cursor: pointer` only when a click handler exists) — one shared frame so the wait never jumps into the render AND an empty drawing, which exports to a near-nothing SVG, is still a visible clickable line; *broken* — missing file, unreadable bytes, not a scene, a render that threw — is a small INERT chip (“Broken drawing”) and the embed text **stays visible and editable**, because a drawing whose file is gone must remain a line the user can fix by hand. Nothing is ever repaired or rewritten. **THE DEPENDENCY** (`@excalidraw/excalidraw`, PINNED 0.18.1, the one addition of this unit; since YAZ-868 the yaseendraw fork build, vendored as five tarballs in `client/vendor/` and PINNED to fork commit `1caba0b6` — YAZ-3177, Enter keeps the line format, and YAZ-3175, a double click selects the word and a triple click the line in styled text; it was `57727ef6`, then `10fa3958` (YAZ-3028 D3), and `9e63bdf2` before that): loaded ONLY through a dynamic `import()` on the first preview render (`drawings/renderScene.ts`; since YAZ-3028 the import and its two global pins live in `drawings/engine.ts`, which the preview and the canvas share), so the editor's main chunk never carries it and a note with no drawing embed loads none of it. 🔒 **OFFLINE**: the renderer must NEVER reach a CDN, and Excalidraw falls back to esm.sh whenever `window.EXCALIDRAW_ASSET_PATH` fails — so that path is set to the app's OWN copy of the package's asset folder (`app://yaseen/excalidraw-assets/`) BEFORE the module is imported. The copy is made at build time by `excalidrawAssets()` in `desktop/electron.vite.config.ts` (from node_modules into `out/renderer/`, and served from node_modules by a dev-server middleware) — never committed, and carried into the packaged app by electron-builder's existing `out/**`. Fonts are fetched at all only for scenes containing TEXT; a text-free scene asks for nothing. **REFRESH**: scenes are cached per target for the life of ONE editor mount; a `DrawingFeed` poke (`drawings/drawingFeed.ts` — the `WikilinkResolveSource` subscribe/poke idiom with no state, threaded as `drawingPreview.feed`) drops that target's entry and rebuilds the decorations, which re-read and re-render it. Since YAZ-879 `CrepeHost` creates exactly ONE feed per editor mount and gives it to both the preview plugin and the modal, so the modal's close after a save (YAZ-3528) redraws every preview of that target in place — no remount, no reload, no document change. Without a feed previews still render, they just never refresh short of a remount. **CLICK**: a rendered preview calls `drawingPreview.onOpenDrawing(target)` and swallows the mousedown so the caret never lands in the match; Editor threads it to the modal (rule 28), and a mount that supplies neither wire keeps inert previews. CSS note: every rule in `drawingPreview.css` is scoped under `.milkdown`, because Crepe's own reset carries `.milkdown * { margin: 0; padding: 0 }` at equal specificity and loads later — an unscoped class silently loses all spacing. End-to-end in `desktop/e2e/drawing.spec.ts` steps 2-4 (previews render and the raw text is not duplicated; a drawn scene WITH TEXT renders with its font inlined from a `data:` URL and **zero** http(s) requests leave the app; a corrupted sidecar reopens as the broken chip with the note still byte-identical).

28. **The drawing modal** (YAZ-879, fourth build unit of the Excalidraw embed YAZ-852, `src/drawings/DrawingModal.tsx` + `drawingModal.css` + `ExcalidrawSurface.tsx` + `saveDrawing.ts`): clicking a rendered preview opens the scene FULL SIZE, edits it, and the modal AUTOSAVES the sidecar (YAZ-3528): there is no Save button. 🔒 **A MODAL, NEVER AN INLINE NODE VIEW**: the embed is plain text under decorations (rule 27), so there is no node to host an editor in, and a drawing canvas inside the text column would fight the caret for every key it owns. It is React BESIDE the editor — the `PageTitle` precedent: `CrepeHost` holds `openDrawing: string | null`, the preview's `drawingPreview.onOpenDrawing` sets it, the modal is keyed by target and unmounted (never hidden) on close. 🔒 **ONE ENGINE SEAM** (shared with the drawing TAB since YAZ-3028, rule 36): `ExcalidrawSurface` is the ONLY component that mounts `<Excalidraw>`, the only place a scene is serialized, and the only place "changed" is defined; the chrome — overlay, save label, autosave, failed-save strip, error line — imports nothing but that component and its types, so YAZ-868's swap to yaseendraw rewrites one file. The boundary is pinned as SOURCE in `DrawingModal.test.tsx` (a runtime assertion would pass with a second hidden import). Everything is LAZY: the module through `renderScene.ts`'s one `loadExcalidraw()`, the stylesheet through the surface's own dynamic CSS import — the entry chunk gains only the chrome's own few KB, and a note with no drawing loads neither. ⚡ Every prop handed to the engine is STABLE (memoized `initialData`, ref-backed `onChange`, module-level `UIOptions`): `<Excalidraw>` is memoized and calls `onChange` whenever it renders, so a prop rebuilt per render is an infinite loop (React #185, caught in e2e). The modal keeps the latest snapshot in a REF and only the save STATUS in state, so a drag costs at most one render in the chrome (Saved → Unsaved), never one per pointer move. **LOAD / SAVE**: `openDrawing` (`drawingScene.ts`) reads through `api.readAsset` with the embed's RAW target and keeps the resolved ABSOLUTE path and the read `mtime` — and, for a LEAN scene a drawing tab saved (YAZ-3028), fills each referenced image the scene does not carry from `<vault>/assets/` through `drawing.load` at that path (only then: a sidecar that carries its images never pays the read; an id found nowhere stays the engine's placeholder; the preview of rule 27 reads the same way); the save goes to `api.writeAsset` at that explicit path (writes are never fuzzy, 🔒 YAZ-876) with that mtime as `expectedMtime`. **AUTOSAVE** (YAZ-3528 D1, the tab's rule 36 seen in the modal): `Autosave<number>` (`lib/autosave.ts`) is created on the surface's FIRST snapshot, the clean baseline, and fed only the cheap version after it; `standalone()` runs once per save, inside the write, 500 ms after the last change — never once per change. Each save is guarded by the mtime the last read or write returned. The title bar shows `SaveIndicator` where the Save button was (D2: Saved / Unsaved / Saving… / Save failed; none for a read-only drawing). The quit handshake (`window.onFlush`) saves a pending change, and an unmount for any other reason flushes, then disposes. **THE FIRST SAVE WINS** (YAZ-3028 edge case; YAZ-3044 A4 amends YAZ-879's "the canvas wins"): every save writes ONCE. A `CONFLICT` — the same drawing saved from a tab since the modal last read or wrote it — is a `SaveConflict` (`saveDrawing.ts`), blocks the autosave, and raises the tab's `ConflictBar` under the title bar ("File changed on disk." Reload / Keep mine): Reload reads the disk's scene into a fresh, clean canvas (the remounted surface's first snapshot is the new baseline, nothing is written); Keep mine is `Autosave.adopt` — this canvas over the disk mtime the CONFLICT reported, and the autosave goes on. Two scenes are never merged. **SHAPE ON DISK**: the library's own `serializeAsJSON(…, 'local')` — so element cleanup and the `files` filter (an image paste survives) are its rules; the modal saves the snapshot's `standalone()`, the scene with its images inside it (rule 36's tab saves the lean `serialize()`) — with two of ours: `source` stays `yaseen-docs` (pinned as `window.EXCALIDRAW_EXPORT_SOURCE` before the import, beside the font path) and a trailing newline, so a file YAZ-877 created and this saved back differ only in what was drawn. The `DrawingFeed` (rule 27) is poked ONCE, on close, when any save landed — never after each save behind the scrim. ⚡ **KEYS ARE THE OVERLAY'S, NEVER `window`'s** — the YAZ-888 lesson `ConfirmRename` learned and paid for in e2e: React flushes mount effects INSIDE the dispatch of the event that opened the component, so a `window` listener hears the very click or keystroke that opened it, and this modal is opened by a CLICK. The overlay takes focus on mount so Esc lands before the canvas exists. **LEAVING** (YAZ-3528 D3) is one gesture with three triggers (Esc, click-away, ✕): save what is pending NOW, then close — no question. Only a save that fails, or one a conflict blocks, raises an INLINE strip under the title bar ("Changes are not saved. Discard them?" / Cancel / Discard), never a second sheet stacked over this one; Discard disposes the autosave first, so nothing more is written (the unmount flush included), and Esc while the strip is up answers the strip. **A DRAWING OPENED AND NOT TOUCHED IS NEVER WRITTEN** — the first snapshot the surface emits (at mount, from the loaded scene, before the engine volunteers one) is the baseline, and the surface's version is the comparison: the sum of element versions, each the version at which that element's content last moved (`contentVersion.ts`, YAZ-3210), because the engine bumps `version` on writes that change nothing (a text editor left with no edit), and such a bump must not write the file. **FAILURES ARE INLINE, NEVER A DIALOG**: a sidecar that is missing, unreadable or not a scene opens as the error state (message + close, nothing to write — reachable only by a race, since rule 27's broken chip is inert), and a failed write leaves the modal open with its error line and the canvas untouched. **THEME** is App's already-resolved appearance read back off `<html data-theme>` (`lib/theme.ts` `appliedTheme`), once, at open: the setting lives in App and threading a prop down to one transient modal is plumbing the feature has not earned. Known gap for the polish pass: a theme change while the modal is open does not follow. End-to-end in `desktop/e2e/drawing.spec.ts` step 5 (a preview click opens the modal on a real canvas with the label at Saved and no Save button; the rectangle tool is picked on the engine's own toolbar and DRAWN with real mouse drags; the autosave writes it into the sidecar while the modal is open — still `yaseen-docs`, still pretty-printed with a trailing newline — a second rectangle drawn just before ✕ is on disk once the modal is gone (the close saves it when the timer has not; unit test S4 pins the close's own save), the in-page preview redraws from the feed's poke, and reopening the saved drawing writes nothing and Esc-closes, with the note byte-identical throughout). The 21 approved scenarios (S1–S21) are on the YAZ-3528 working log, YAZ-3538, and `DrawingModal.test.tsx` names each one it pins.

29. **Heading folding** (YAZ-1140, `src/editor/outline/headingFolding.ts` + `.css`, keymap `headingHotkeys.ts`): the heading-shaped twin of rule 5, registered in `createCrepe()` right after the bullet plugin. Foldable = an H1–H3 outside every list whose SECTION — its following sibling blocks up to the next heading of the same or a shallower level, or the end of the parent (blockquotes are walked; lists are skipped whole: the bullet chevron owns that gutter) — is non-empty. Each gets a widget `<button class="heading-toggle" aria-expanded>` at the start of the h element's inline content — INSIDE the h element, so it inherits the heading font-size and one `height: 1.3em` rule centres the chevron on the first line at every level — and collapsing adds `data-heading-folded="true"` to every section block (CSS `display:none`; an inner collapsed heading's widget sits inside a hidden block, so nesting compounds for free). Toggles are metadata-only transactions stamped `'heading-fold'` (`viewActions.ts`): never `markdownUpdated`, disk and mtime untouched. Fold keys = `h:` + the rule-5 scheme (`getOutlineFoldKey`) — a third key space beside fold and zoom keys — persisted in the SAME `folders[root].folds` bucket: `Editor.tsx` splits by prefix on load and writes the union of both plugins' latest reports, so neither kind can wipe the other's keys and rename/delete remapping rides the existing store path unchanged. ⌘↑/⌘↓ fold/unfold the innermost section at the caret (declining inside lists — rule 7's bullet handler owns those; ⌘⇧U/⌘⇧I stay bullets-only in v1); ⌘Z joins the view-action protocol, which YAZ-1140 made SYMMETRIC: every view-action plugin (fold, zoom, heading fold) drops its pending panic-undo when any OTHER kind fires, so ⌘Z reverts the single latest view action and a second ⌘Z can never resurrect an older one. CMD+F reveals matches hidden by collapsed sections silently and re-collapses them on its own `revealedHeadings` books (`findInPage.ts`); the block handle mutes over the chevron (rule 15); the bullets-only outline editor computes zero entries and stays inert. End-to-end: `desktop/e2e/headingFold.spec.ts` — chevron → section hidden → `h:` key in `yaseendocs.json` → quit → relaunch → restored, with a bullet fold coexisting in the same bucket.

30. **Inline `<br>` ↔ hardbreak** (YAZ-1452, `src/editor/inlineBreaks.ts`, registered in `createCrepe()` right after underline): a `<br>` (any spelling, any case) is the hardbreak node, not an `html` atom — inside table cells it is the only line break GFM has, and Milkdown's `remarkPreserveEmptyLinePlugin` used to delete every one of them on parse (data loss on the next autosave). 🔒 **ORDER IS THE MECHANISM**: our `$remark` plugin runs BEFORE Milkdown's, which is removed and re-registered AFTER ours — never dropped, because `shouldPreserveEmptyLine` resolves its id to keep writing `<br />` for empty paragraphs. **LOAD**: a `<br>` becomes `break`; in a prose paragraph a `<br>` with nothing after it is dropped (CommonMark has no trailing hard break; remark would write a stray `\`), which is also what keeps the lone `<br />` blank-line marker round-tripping. 🔒 **A `<br>` BESIDE A LINE ENDING IS ONE BREAK** (YAZ-2659 D1): Milkdown has already made the line ending inside a paragraph a break of its own (a soft break, `isInline`), so a `<br>` at the end of a line, or on a line of its own, takes the soft break before it and the soft break after it — `a<br>` + `b` on the next line is ONE paragraph with ONE hardbreak, in prose, in a bullet and in a quote, and `a<br><br>` + `b` has two. Two breaks in a row would save as `\` + a blank line, which ends the paragraph, and the next save would write `\\`. Files that an earlier build already split are not repaired (D4). **SAVE**: a hardbreak inside `tableCell` is written as `<br>` (remark's default writes a space there); elsewhere remark's default `\` + newline — so `a<br>b` in prose, and `a<br>` + `b` on the next line, normalise to the backslash form (rule 6), and a second save writes the same text. **CELLS SERIALISE THEMSELVES**: `table_cell` / `table_header` `toMarkdown` feed the cell's inline content directly instead of going through the paragraph runner, because that runner always drops a paragraph's LAST hardbreak (a trailing `<br>` in a cell decayed one per save) and wrote `<br />` for an empty cell; several paragraphs in one cell are joined by a break, an empty cell is written empty. **ENTER AND SHIFT-ENTER IN A CELL** are our shortcut (priority 90 — above Milkdown's 50, below the wikilink picker's and outliner's 100 so an open `[[` picker still takes Enter): both always insert a hardbreak, a new line in the cell as in Google Docs (🔒 YAZ-1462). Milkdown's own Shift-Enter refuses to run inside tables, and its "second Shift-Enter after a break makes a new paragraph" rule split the table. Mod-Enter is still Milkdown's `exitTable`. Contract test: `inlineBreaks.test.ts` (19 cases, one row copied verbatim from the reporting doc; and the cases B1–B12 of YAZ-2659, each saved, opened again and saved again). A single line break inside a paragraph (Markdown's soft break; Milkdown's `hardbreak` with `isInline: true`, drawn as `<span data-type="hardbreak" data-is-inline="true"> </span>`) SHOWS as a line break, as in Obsidian (YAZ-3727 6C, `src/editor/softBreaks.css`, loaded by `Editor.tsx` and `OutlineEditor.tsx`): CSS only — the span's space takes no width (`font-size: 0`) and its `::after` is a newline (`'\A'`, `white-space: pre`); the document and the file keep the soft break byte for byte, and a hard break (`<br>`) is untouched.

31. **Highlight** (YAZ-1480, `src/editor/marks/highlight.ts` + the shared `marks/htmlPairs.ts`): ProseMirror mark `highlight` with ONE optional attribute `color`. **On disk**: `color: null` (yellow) is Obsidian's `==text==` — a vendored micromark tokenizer (gfm-strikethrough's attention run with `=`, exactly two: a lone `=` is text, `===` cancels, `\==` escapes) plus stringify `unsafe` rules: any `=` touching another `=` is written `\=` (`a == b` → `a \=\= b`, reads back as the same text; a lone `=` never; URLs never; an odd run escapes one short, `a === b` → `a \=\== b`, still stable). `postProcessMarkdown()` restores `=` inside `[[…]]` so a wikilink target keeps its bytes (outside code only, rule 3). `==` on its own line under a paragraph is still a setext heading. Two tight runs on one line pair up (`x==5 and y==6` on disk highlights `5 and y`, as in Obsidian); the typing rule is stricter than the parser (no `=` inside, no word character before), so the same string TYPED stays text and saves escaped. `green`/`blue`/`pink` have no Markdown syntax and store inline HTML `<mark class="highlight-<name>">text</mark>` — rule 11's `<u>` mechanism through the shared pair walk. A bare `<mark>` is read as yellow and written back as `==…==` (rule 6 normalisation); any other `<mark class/style>` is not this mark and passes through as inline HTML, bytes untouched — on PASTE every `<mark>` becomes the mark (unknown class → yellow): a pasted `<mark>` is a highlight. 🔒 A highlight nested inside a highlight ENDS the outer one (Milkdown's `ParserState` keeps one mark set) — lossy on the first save, stable after; a highlight inside a DIFFERENT mark is unaffected. **Toolbar** (`buildToolbar` in createCrepe.ts): four swatches (yellow, green, blue, pink), dots filled with the wash token, added into Crepe's own `formatting` group after Strikethrough — `getGroup('formatting')` THROWS if Crepe ever renames that group; `headingToolbar.test.ts` pins it. 🔒 D5, Bold's toggle rule: a dot is LIT when ANY selected text carries its colour (at a caret: the marks it would type with); pressing a lit dot removes exactly that colour, an unlit one applies it over any other colour; edge whitespace stays outside the mark; where marks cannot apply (code) the command declines and the key falls through. A lit dot is painted as a pressed button (`--crepe-color-selected`). `setHighlightCommand(color)` is the one command behind the swatches, `Mod-Shift-h` (yellow; a `$useKeymap`, so Crepe's `keymapRef` labels the yellow dot and its `aria-keyshortcuts` from it) and the `==x==` typing rule (yellow). Copy-out emits `<mark>`. **Styling**: translucent washes `--mark-bg` + `--mark-bg-<name>` in `:root` (one value per colour, both themes), text colour inherited, selector `.milkdown .ProseMirror mark` so every Crepe surface paints it. Not a Crepe feature (allowlist untouched).

**YAZ-1289 editor-link amendment to rules 23–25:** the editor still mounts these plugins only for Markdown source notes. Rule 23 consults the separate view-only source only when the raw target has a recognized explicit text/PDF/image extension; missing/loading/removed targets and heading/block suffixes remain unresolved and never run create-on-click, while `|display` is presentation only. Rule 24 composes explicit-extension catalog candidates with the Markdown candidates before the same matcher/ranker; recognized view-only target spellings suppress unroutable semantic rows, but semantic aliases whose display text matches remain. `WikilinkResolveSource.resolve` and `.records` stay the original Markdown feed by identity, so rule 25 and every other semantic consumer remain Markdown-only.

30. **Images, first-class** (YAZ-1656 — decisions D1–D8 and the demo learnings are comments on that issue; `src/editor/image/`): `![alt](src)` RENDERS from the vault, a pasted or dropped image is SAVED to the vault, and the picture can be resized, opened full-size and copied. 🔒 **THE ONE NODE VIEW** (`imageView.ts`, registered in `createCrepe()` only when `opts.image` supplies the vault root + the note's absolute path): rules 23/27 forbid node views for wikilinks and drawing embeds because those are plain TEXT with no node to view; the commonmark `image` node ALREADY EXISTS, so a node view here changes no schema and no serializer and `![alt|300](src "t")` stays byte-identical (`roundtrip.test.ts`). The rule it establishes: a node view is allowed only on a node the schema already has and never touches the serializer — with TWO exceptions: rule 41's line (YAZ-3164 D2) — the `hr` node keeps its name but gains four attributes and its own `toMarkdown`, because Markdown has no carrier for a line's style the way the alt text carries an image's width — and rule 41a's table (YAZ-3758), whose `table` node and cells gain attributes and whose `toMarkdown` writes a comment after the table, for the same reason. **SRC** (`imageSrc.ts`): anything with a scheme passes through untouched (`https:`, `data:`; a foreign `app://fs/…` simply 404s); a leading `/` is root-relative; everything else becomes `app://vault/<encoded root>/<ref, each segment decoded ONCE then encoded>?from=<note's root-relative dir>` — decode-once because a markdown src is already percent-encoded (Obsidian writes `%20`), so `case%20a.png` reaches main as `case a.png`, never `case%2520a.png`. Main (`vaultProtocol.ts`) resolves note-relative → root-relative → shortest-path basename, images only. **STATES**: loading is quiet; broken (missing, foreign, escaped, non-image) is a small INERT chip "Broken image: <src as written>" with the markdown still editable — nothing is repaired or rewritten. **WIDTH** is Obsidian's `![alt|400](src)` — alt is already preserved byte-for-byte, so no serializer work — parsed for display (`parseAlt`; `a|b` is not a width) and written back by the resize. On the `<img>` the width is the `--image-width` custom property (`width: var(--image-width, auto)` in `imageView.css`; no property when the alt carries none — the stylesheet's `auto` fallback), NEVER `style.width` — an inline width beats every stylesheet rule, and a stylesheet state must be able to override it without `!important`. **FOLDED CHIP** (YAZ-1709): a bullet holding an image folds like a parent (rule 5); the fold plugin's `data-outline-folded-image` node decoration turns the view into a one-line chip — one fixed text-height box for every image (1.75em wide × (line box − 4px) tall, so it follows the line-spacing setting; `object-fit: cover`; short enough not to grow the row), no label, handles hidden — and a click on the thumbnail unfolds the bullet. An expanded image inside a foldable item shows a corner fold button (`.image-view__fold`, top-left, on hover/selection; absent while broken — the broken chip has no button) rendered dumb by the node view and driven by the fold plugin. The node view itself knows nothing about folding: it sets the width property and renders the button, the stylesheet reads the decorations. **RESIZE**: eight handles (four corners, four edge midpoints), every one WIDTH-ONLY so the aspect ratio can never break (only a width is stored): west handles grow leftward, north/south map through the aspect ratio, a corner follows the axis that moved more; clamp `MIN_WIDTH` 40 px … the editor column; the width is live on the `<img>` during the drag and ONE `setNodeMarkup` on mouseup writes `alt|<w>` (⌘Z is one step); Escape mid-drag cancels (capture-phase, so the editor's Escape→sidebar hand-off never hears it), `window` blur ends the gesture where it stands, a plain click commits nothing, read-only editors have no gesture. `update()` patches width/alt/title in place and rebuilds the `<img>` only on a src change; `ignoreMutation` answers false to PM's `selection` pseudo-mutation. **LIGHTBOX** (`ImageModal.tsx`, rule 28's shape): double-click → a full-window overlay of the FULL-resolution file (`95vw/95vh`, `object-fit: contain`, alt as caption); Esc / backdrop / ✕ close; keys are the overlay's (YAZ-888); focus returns to what had it. It is a GALLERY of every image on the page in document order (folded ones included — they are still in the doc): the node view walks the document at double-click time and hands over `{ images, index }` (no registry of node views, so the list is always current and stateless), the modal owns only the cursor; ← / → and the bottom bar's arrows page, an "n / m" counter sits between them, NO wrap-around (← at the first and → at the last are no-ops, the edge arrow disabled), and a single image shows no bar at all — the old lightbox exactly. **PASTE / DROP** (`insertImage.ts`, wired in `clipboardPaste.ts` through the `imageOptionsCtx` slice, D6): image BYTES on the clipboard or in a drop beat whatever HTML rode along — a "Copy Image" from another app carries the PNG and an `<img src>` only that app can read, and the old behaviour kept the private src and lost the bytes (the reported bug). The file is written FULL-RESOLUTION, never re-encoded, to `assets/images/<note, whitespace → '-'>-<yyyyMMdd-HHmmss>.<ext from mime>` with `create: true` — never overwritten, a same-second collision retries `-2`, `-3`… — the sibling of `assets/drawings/` and root-relative so moving a note never breaks the link; the inserted node is `![<name>|400](assets/images/…)`, the `|400` (`PASTED_IMAGE_WIDTH`) only when the bitmap is wider than 400 px, so a screenshot lands at a manageable size and a 16 px icon is not blown up. Never in code (a fenced block is a CodeMirror node view that owns its own paste anyway); a drop over code or outside the document is REFUSED rather than passed on, because the next handler is Milkdown's upload plugin, which would inline the file as base64; a selected image becomes a caret AFTER itself before the insert (paste adds, never replaces); the first image file wins when several are dropped; any failure is the host's passive notice and nothing is inserted. HTML with a foreign `<img src>` and NO bytes is left alone (renders the broken chip; foreign URLs are never fetched, nothing is silently deleted). **WHERE IT IS NOT**: a folder's outline editor (its bullets-only lock has no `image` node — wiring options there would write the file and then filter the insert away) and the hover preview card (no vault root in reach) get no `image` options and keep Crepe's stock `<img>`, both commented where they mount. **DEFERRED** (YAZ-1673): `![[img.png]]` embeds (zero in the vault, paste never produces them, would need a second decoration renderer) and a per-vault attachment-folder setting (free later: links are root-relative). End-to-end: `desktop/e2e/imagePaste.spec.ts` and `imageRender.spec.ts` (fixture PNGs encoded at test time by `imageFixtures.ts`).

32. **Code blocks wrap and follow Appearance** (YAZ-2270, decisions D1–D4 are comments on that issue; `src/editor/codeTheme.ts`, wired in `createCrepe()`'s `featureConfigs[CodeMirror]`): every fenced block is Crepe's stock CodeMirror editor with two app settings. **WRAP**: `EditorView.lineWrapping` — a long line wraps at the column edge and breaks mid-word only when it has no space; never a CSS `white-space` override, which bypasses CodeMirror's line measuring. Display only: the markdown is untouched. A diagram wider than the column wraps too (accepted). The `overflow-x: auto` on `.milkdown-code-block` stays as the guard for tables and the rare unbreakable element. **COLOURS**: the app's own theme replaces Crepe's One Dark (built for a dark block, ~2:1 on the light one). Every colour is an `app.css` variable — the `--code-*` syntax tokens plus `--fg`, `--fg-muted`, `--accent`, `--bg-hover` — defined under `:root` and `[data-theme='dark']`, so Appearance re-colours code live with no remount (the `crepeTheme.ts` mechanism). ONE look for every language: no per-language styling (D2, dropped — untagged fences mix code, diagrams and prose). `crepe.ts` no longer defaults a theme, so `@codemirror/theme-one-dark` is not bundled. `codeBlock.test.ts` pins wrapping, the theme, and that every `--code-*` is defined for both appearances and used.

33. **Marks on line breaks** (YAZ-2280, decisions D1–D3 are comments on that issue; `src/editor/breakMarks.ts`, registered in `createCrepe()` in place of Milkdown's `hardbreakClearMarkPlugin`, which is removed): a SOFT break is a newline inside a paragraph (`hardbreak` with `isInline`, shown as a space); a HARD break is `\` + newline. 🔒 **ONE RULE**, enforced by one `appendTransaction` on the span a transaction changed: a soft break keeps a mark only while the text on BOTH sides carries that same mark; a hard break never carries one. So a mark added across soft-wrapped lines runs through them as one span (`==two⏎three==`, `**two⏎three**`, `<mark class="highlight-green">two⏎three</mark>`) and the lines keep flowing, and a mark never starts or ends on a newline — Markdown cannot open or close one there, and the mark would be lost on reload with its markers left as text. The rule runs on every document change, not only when a mark is added: un-marking or deleting the text beside a marked break unmarks that break too. Adding a mark never changes a break's kind (the bug this replaced: Milkdown rebuilt each break with default attrs, turning soft into hard). Unchanged: hard breaks split a mark per line (`==a==\⏎==b==`), Shift-Enter inserts an unmarked hard break, and a file that already holds a multi-line mark saves byte-identical. Tests: `breakMarks.test.ts`.

34. **Line numbers and the page settings menu** (YAZ-2643, decisions D1–D9 and cases S1–S82 are comments on that issue; YAZ-3076 D3–D5 and cases S40–S51 on YAZ-3083; `src/editor/PageSettings.tsx`, `src/editor/lineNumbers/`, the host effects in `Editor.tsx`, `DocumentChips` in `src/documents/useDocumentHost.tsx`): each Markdown note, Excalidraw drawing and draw.io diagram has a cog as the FIRST chip of its status row — on a note: cog, zoom pill, the "Read only" chip (only while it is on), sync chip, save chip; on a board: cog, the "Read only" chip, sync chip, save chip (rule 40); a folder page, a text file, a PDF and an image have none. Its first row is "Read only", stored IN the file (YAZ-3076 D1, rule 40); a board's menu has only that row and no counts — each Markdown-only row, and the counts, show only when the host hands their handler (`readText` for the counts), the rule "Table of contents" already had. No hotkey and no menu-bar item for "Read only" (YAZ-3076 D5), and no row in the settings dialog. A click opens a small menu under the cog (`role="group"`, on the zoom menu's own CSS rules): the switch "Read only" (rule 40), then the switch "Line numbers", then, since YAZ-2709, the switch "Section indent" under it (rule 18a) (each `aria-pressed`, with a check mark while it is on, and the menu stays open), then the two switches and the one control of YAZ-2700 — "Heading levels", "Table of contents" and "TOC made from:", rule 35 — then a divider, and two grey lines, "N words" and "N characters". A second click on the cog, a press outside (a `pointerdown` in the capture phase), the window losing focus (a press inside the draw.io frame reaches no event of the app's document — YAZ-3121), or Esc closes it; Esc stops at the menu and puts the focus on the cog. 🔒 **NO SWITCH IS STORED** but "Section indent" (rule 18a) and "Table of contents" (rule 35, YAZ-2950), which are remembered for their page, and "Read only", which the file itself holds (rule 40): each other switch is React state of `CrepeHost`, beside the document zoom. Each mounted editor has its own, a tab switch keeps it, and a closed tab, a rename (a new editor) or a restart starts with the numbers off. The one other thing the menu stores is the choice "TOC made from:" (rule 35). No hotkey, no menu-bar item, no setting for the line numbers. **THE COUNTS** (D5): the menu reads `getPlainText(crepe)` ONE time, when it opens. The text it read IS its open state, so the counts cannot change while the menu shows, and nothing is counted while it is closed. The text is the note body only — not the title, the properties, the comments, the linked mentions or the reviews — with one line break between two blocks and none at the end: the empty paragraph Crepe keeps under a last bullet, heading, code block or table counts as nothing (S18). A word is a run of characters with no white space in it; both numbers use the locale's separators. 🔒 **WHAT A NUMBER IS** (D2): the line of the file ON DISK where the block starts. Line 1 is the first line of the file, so the frontmatter lines count, and a file the editor did not write (an AI's `-` bullets and blank lines) shows the lines of its own bytes. A paragraph, a heading, a code block (its opening fence), a rule and a table (its header row) each show the line where they START; a bullet shows the number of its first block; no line inside a code block gets a number in the lane, because the block's own gutter counts them (D8, below). 🔒 **THE RANGE** (D7): a block that is two or more lines of the file shows where it ENDS too, `8–10`, so that a line inside it can be found. A paragraph ends on its last line (soft-wrapped lines, in a bullet and in a quote too, and never its nested bullets), a fenced code block on its closing fence (one that is never closed: on the last line of the block), an indented code block on its last code line, a table on its last row, a setext heading on its underline, a raw HTML block on its last line, a styled line (rule 41) on its comment's last line. A block of one line shows ONE number. 🔒 **A STYLED LINE'S COMMENT IS NO BLOCK** (YAZ-3204): the editor joins `***` and the `<!-- line: … -->` right after it in the same container into ONE `hr`, so `blockLines` skips an HTML block that `parseLineComment` (`line/lineComment.ts`, which has no editor imports, so the worker bundle stays the parser only) reads as the line comment when it comes right after a thematic break with no new list item, list or quote between them — read from its `htmlFlowData` lines joined by a line break, the text remark gives the editor, so a quote's `> ` on a continuation line is not in it (YAZ-3206); the line's entry starts on the `***` line and ends on the comment (`3–5`, D7's range, as a setext heading ends on its underline). Any other HTML block is a block, as before. `blockLines` returns `ends` beside `lines`, in the same order and of the same length — the end of the block's token, and for the empty paragraph of a bare marker or of an empty quote the start — the worker posts it, and the host maps both through `toFileLine`. The plugin puts the start in `data-line` (an integer, as before) and the end in a SECOND attribute, `data-line-end`, only when the end is the greater: never one merged string, so CSS alone decides how a range looks. **WHEN IT IS BUILT**: only when the page and the disk agree — the switch turns on, a save settles, an outside change lands (a reload, a frontmatter-only absorb, "Reload" or "Keep mine") — never on a keystroke, and never while the save state is `unsaved` or `saving`. `useAutosave().diskParts()` gives the frontmatter block and the body as they are on disk, and the counter `diskLandings` says an outside change landed, because `disk` does not follow this editor's own saves. `fileLines(frontmatter, body)` runs on the main thread: it gives the text the editor parses (`normalizeEmptyItems`, rule 8) and the map from a line of that text to a line of the file — it adds the frontmatter's lines and takes out the blank lines the load added; a lone CR is a line ending, as it is in the parse. An answer that comes back after a newer request, after the numbers went off, or for an editor that is gone is dropped. **THE WORKER** (D1): `blockLines(text)` reads the block structure from `micromark` events with the GFM extension — no syntax tree — and returns the start line and the kind of each leaf block. It runs ONLY in `lineNumbers.worker.ts`, its own renderer chunk, never on the main thread: `tools/lineNumbersWorker.test.mjs` fails when any other source module imports it as a value. ONE worker per window, started by the first request (`requestBlockLines`); a window that never shows line numbers never loads it. The worker imports `workerDocument.ts` FIRST: micromark's browser build decodes a character reference through a DOM element it makes at module load, a worker has no `document`, and the stand-in decodes nothing — a reference never makes block structure. A worker that fails (`onerror`, `onmessageerror`) rejects every request that waits on it, is terminated and is dropped, so the next request starts a new one; the host shows the passive notice "Line numbers could not load." and does not retry (S65). 🔒 **THE PAIRING AND ITS TWO STOPS** (`build` in `lineNumbers.ts`): the plugin pairs the page's leaf blocks with the file's, in order, and compares their kinds, because no number is better than a wrong one (the file has two kinds of code block, `c` fenced and `i` indented, and both pair with the page's `code_block`). D7 and D8 change neither stop. At the first pair whose kinds disagree — a footnote definition is such a block — the numbers stop, and the blocks before it keep theirs (S45). When every pair agreed and one side still has blocks — the file has an entry left, or the page has a block left that is not an empty paragraph — the page shows NO number at all (S64). The empty paragraph Crepe keeps at the end of the page is not such a block, and it has no number (S44). Neither stop shows an error. **VIEW STATE ONLY**, like folding (rule 5): `showLineNumbers(crepe, blocks | null)` sends the lines in a metadata-only transaction with `addToHistory: false` — never `markdownUpdated`, never the autosave, never undo — and each numbered block gets ONE node decoration: `data-line`, and on the same decoration `data-line-end` and `data-line-code` where they apply. Between two sends the set only moves through the position mapping, so typing builds nothing, and with the numbers off the plugin holds `DecorationSet.empty`. A new block, and a block that Enter split or Backspace joined, has no number until the next save settles (accepted: a node decoration does not survive a change of its node's bounds). 🔒 **A CODE BLOCK'S OWN NUMBERS** (D8, `lineNumbers/codeLines.ts`): while the numbers show, the gutter INSIDE a code block counts in lines of the file — a fenced block whose opening fence is line 27 reads 28, 29, … — so the page has ONE number system; with the switch off, and for a block that has no number, it reads 1, 2, 3 as before. A fenced block's first code line is the line under its fence; an indented block has no fence, so its first code line is the block's own start line. The plugin puts that line in a third attribute, `data-line-code`, ONLY when the page's block holds as many code lines as the file has inside the block: an empty block and a fence that is never closed do not, and keep 1, 2, 3. `createCrepe` adds `codeLines` to the CodeMirror extensions of every code block: ONE shared `Compartment`, empty, and a `ViewPlugin` with a constructor only. `syncCodeLines(cm)` reads `data-line-code` on the CodeMirror's block and reconfigures the compartment to `lineNumbers({ formatNumber })`, or back to empty; Crepe's own `lineNumbers()` sets no formatter, so the two configs merge with no conflict, and the changed config makes CodeMirror draw the gutter again. It dispatches ONLY when the line changed. `showLineNumbers` runs it, after its ProseMirror dispatch, for each code block that has a CodeMirror (`EditorView.findFromDOM`). Crepe makes a block's CodeMirror only when the block comes near the window, and drops it 5 s after the block left, so a NEW CodeMirror runs it for itself, one microtask after it is made. The transaction carries effects only. Crepe's `forwardUpdate` forwards a change of the text or of the selection and nothing else, so nothing reaches ProseMirror, `markdownUpdated` or the autosave, and the focus and the caret stay where they are. The staleness is that of the outer numbers: the lines are set at a build and never on a keystroke, a code block typed while the numbers are on reads 1, 2, 3 until the save settles, and inside a numbered block CodeMirror counts on from the block's first line. With the switch off nothing of this runs on a keystroke, and no CodeMirror transaction is dispatched unless the switch is or was on. **THE LOOK** (D4, `app.css`): pure CSS, no layout in JavaScript. While `.editor-host[data-line-numbers]` is set, `.ProseMirror` is a query container and a numbered block's `::after` draws `attr(data-line)` to the left of the column: a block's right edge is the column's right edge at every bullet depth, and `100cqw` is the column's width, so one rule puts every number in ONE column. A block with `data-line-end` draws its range on the SAME pseudo-element, on one line: `content: attr(data-line) '–' attr(data-line-end)` (a table on its `::before`). 🔒 **THE LANE** (D9, the new S51): the 48px margin left of the column belongs to the drag handle (on hover its box is 49px to 17px left of the column) and to the fold arrows (the last 18px), so a number in that margin was covered by the handle and a range did not fit. The numbers have a lane of their own, left of the margin, and the scroller makes it: `.editor-host[data-line-numbers] { padding-left: 64px; }`. It is the scroller's OWN padding — nothing else sets its left padding — so the title row, the body, the comments, the linked mentions and the reviews slide right together and stay one aligned column. So the page SLIDES RIGHT while the numbers show (64px in a window narrower than the column, half of that in a wide one, where the column is centred), text can wrap again, and the page slides back when they go off. A number ends 52px left of the column, 3px clear of the handle's box: the drag handle and the fold arrows are at their usual places, and neither covers a number. `--line-box: 1lh` puts the number on the block's first line. The number is inside the zoomed body, so its size and its gap are divided by `--document-zoom` (`calc(11px / var(--document-zoom, 1))`, `calc(100cqw + 52px / var(--document-zoom, 1))`): it is 11px on screen at every zoom, 52px left of the column, and it stays in the lane (S53). A rule and a code block give up their clip (`overflow: visible`) while the numbers show; a table keeps its clip, stays `position: static`, and draws its number as `::before`. The number is grey and monospace, with `user-select: none` and `pointer-events: none`. The lane is 60px: about 9 characters of the 11px code font (0.6em each, not measured in the app), `1207–1210`. In a window narrower than the column the left part of a range of two 5-digit lines can be cut off (accepted, S57). **NOT INCLUDED**: line numbers in the text, PDF and image viewers and on a folder page; "Go to line"; a raw text view; a live count chip; any change in the main process. Tests: `lineNumbers/lineNumbers.test.ts` (real editors: the hand-counted note shapes as loaded and after a save, the ranges, the first code line of each code block, the two stops, folding, zoom, undo), `lineNumbers/codeLines.test.ts` (real editors and the real CodeMirror of each code block: its own gutter on, off, built again, in an indented block, in a CodeMirror made after the build, and never a document change), `lineNumbers/blockLines.test.ts` (`blockLines` with its ends, `fileLines`), `lineNumbers/requestBlockLines.test.ts` (the one worker and its failure), `lineNumbers/lineNumbersCss.test.ts` (the CSS contract), `PageSettings.test.tsx`, `Editor.test.tsx` ("the page settings cog", "line numbers follow the file on disk"), `createCrepe.test.ts` (`getPlainText`), `hooks/useAutosave.test.tsx` (`diskParts`), `tools/lineNumbersWorker.test.mjs` (the worker bundle with no DOM). End to end: `desktop/e2e/lineNumbers.spec.ts`, written and not run.

35. **Table of contents** (YAZ-2700, decisions D1–D15 with their cases are comments on YAZ-2701; YAZ-3051 takes the rows down to `H5`, decisions D3 and D8 with their cases are comments on YAZ-3048; `src/editor/toc/tocPlugin.ts` the engine, `toc/tocChannel.ts` the channel, `toc/TableOfContents.tsx` + `toc/toc.css` what is drawn; and, delivered in the same work, `outline/headingLevelTag.ts` + `.css`, `buildToolbar` in `createCrepe.ts`, and the scrollbar blocks of `app.css`): a note shows its structure at its right edge, and one click goes to a part of it. Notes only: a folder page, a text file, a PDF and an image have none. **THE ROWS** (D1, D6, D14): the engine publishes a list of rows `{ level: 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5, text }` through the ONE `TocChannel` that `CrepeHost` makes for each editor mount and hands to `createCrepe` (`opts.toc`) and to the component; the component never reads the document and is never told what a row is. `scanNote(doc, source)` decides. Auto (`source: null`): the `H1`–`H5` outside lists (`DEEPEST_TOC_LEVEL`, 5, in `tocChannel.ts` — NOT rule 29's `DEEPEST_FOLDABLE_LEVEL`, which stays 3; rule 29's helpers; a blockquote is walked; a heading with nothing under it is listed; an empty one reads "Untitled heading") when the note has two or more of them (`ENOUGH_ROWS`), else its bullets — each labelled item of each list that is a direct child of the document, bulleted or numbered, three levels deep, the level its depth and the text its label (`itemLabelText`, so a bullet whose first block is a heading reads that heading; a bullet with no label is no row and its children still are; a list inside a blockquote does not count) — else what the headings gave. `headings`: each `H1`–`H5` of the note, the ones inside bullets at each depth too, and no bullet. `bullets`: the bullets, however many headings the note has. A chosen source never falls back to the other one. `H6` is never a row. Bullets stay at three levels. `H4` and `H5` rows do not fold (rule 29 is unchanged): a jump to one opens each fold above it, the same as for an `H3`. 🔒 **THE TYPING BUDGET** (YAZ-2236): the plugin has no state field and no decorations. It scans ONE time at view creation and then `SCAN_DELAY_MS` (150 ms) after the last document change: a keystroke only starts the timer again, a caret move scans nothing, a change of source scans at once, and a jump scans first. The channel tells its subscribers only when the list of (level, text) changes or the `hidden` flag changes; `hidden` is true while a bullet zoom is active (rule 12). The positions of the last scan stay in the engine, only to find a row's element for the scroll spy, and one is trusted only while its node is an `h1`–`h5` or the element of a list item. **VIEW STATE ONLY**, like folding (rule 5): the jump dispatches unfolds (metadata-only) and a selection — never `markdownUpdated`, never the autosave. Its ease and its flash are Web Animations on the editor's own elements: no attribute, class or style is written. **WHAT IS DRAWN** (D3, D4): `<nav class="toc" aria-label="Table of contents">`, a sibling of `.editor-host` in `section.editor`, after the find bar — chrome, so the document zoom does not reach it — on `z-index: 1`, BELOW `.status-chips` (2), whose menus open over its corner. It draws nothing while the page shows none (mode `off`), with fewer than two rows, and while `hidden`. `shownRows` keeps `MAX_ROWS` (200) at most: all levels, else it drops level 5, then 4, then 3, then 2 until 200 or fewer are left, else the first 200 of level 1. TWO LOOKS: NAMES (`data-names`) — a column of names 200px wide until the reader drags its edge (toc.css `--toc-width`; THE WIDTH OF THE NAMES, below), left of the note's scrollbar, over room the scroller makes with `padding-right`; the note's find bar moves left by the same width — and LINES — a rail of small lines, one for each row (18 / 12 / 7px long for level 1 / 2 / 3, and 7px for levels 4 and 5; 10px apart, down to 4px when there are many, then the rail clips and follows the current line), and a card with the names (`.toc__card`, 440px tall at most) on top of the text. 🔒 `namesShow(mode, noteWidth, columnMax)` selects: `auto` shows the names when `noteWidth - 200 >= columnMax` (`COLUMN_MAX`: 1040 at Narrow, 1440 at Medium, never at Full), so the names never make the text narrower; `pinned` shows them when `noteWidth >= 700` (`NAMES_FLOOR`). `noteWidth` is the width of `section.editor`, from a ResizeObserver — never a scroll or a keystroke, and never a CSS container query (a container traps the full-window drawing and image dialogs). ONE scrollbar, the note's: the lists show none and fade at an edge that has more. **THE WIDTH OF THE NAMES** (YAZ-2752, decisions D1–D5 with their cases are comments on YAZ-2754): ONE app-wide width, `settings.tableOfContentsWidth` ("App state": `settings`), a whole number of px from `TOC_MIN_W` (160) to `TOC_MAX_W` (480), `TOC_DEFAULT_W` (200) by default. 🔒 `namesShow` does NOT read it: it counts with `TOC_WIDTH` (= the default), so a drag never changes which notes show names. `namesRoom(mode, noteWidth, columnMax)` is the widest the column may be in ONE note: `pinned` leaves the text `TEXT_FLOOR` (500px, what it has at `NAMES_FLOOR`), `auto` gives the empty margin and no more — `noteWidth - gutter - columnMax`, where `gutter` is the width of the note's own scrollbar (11px: a scrollbar is not margin), and never less than the `TOC_WIDTH` that `namesShow` gave the names — so a column wider than 200px never makes the text narrower; both stop at `TOC_MAX_W`. The column shows `min(saved width, room)`, and the saved width stays when the room is smaller.
