The component writes that number to `--toc-width` on `section.editor` while the names show (the column, the scroller's `padding-right` and the find bar all read it there) and removes it after. THE EDGE: `.toc__resize`, the first child of the names, `aria-hidden`, a 6px strip over the list's hairline that shows `--accent-soft` under the mouse and during a drag (`data-active`) — the sidebar's idiom. 🔒 A drag is the sidebar's (YAZ-2239): each move writes `--toc-width` straight to the section, with NO React state and so no render; the release writes the setting ONE time, and only when the width changed. An editor that goes away during a drag ends it and saves nothing. Mouse only (D5): no double-click, no keys, and a far drag stops at a limit — it never pins or unpins. **THE CARD** (D3): the mouse on the rail opens it and it closes 200 ms after the mouse left the rail and the card; a click on the rail opens or closes it (a click in the first 300 ms after it opened does not close it); a scroll of the note never opens it (YAZ-2886, which took back the wheel's card of D3): only the rail's lines change, so a reader who scrolls is never covered. The wheel over the table of contents moves ONE thing: a list longer than its box, which stops at its ends (`overscroll-behavior: contain`), else the note. **WHERE THE READER IS** (D5): on the scroller's `scroll` (passive, one read for each animation frame, nothing written) `current(indices, scroller)` answers the last shown row whose top is at or above the scroller's top + 40px; with none, the first; at the very bottom of a note that scrolls, the last one in view; a row inside a fold is skipped. The lines above the current one are `data-read`, the current one is `data-current` and 5px longer; the current name is `aria-current="true"`, a marker slides to it, and a list longer than its box moves in step with the note. After a jump the row that was clicked stays current until the reader's own wheel, press or key in the note. **THE HIERARCHY OF THE NAMES** (YAZ-2762, decisions D1–D10 are comments on its working log YAZ-2764; the cases are comments on YAZ-2774, YAZ-2775 and YAZ-2776): in the list of names — the column and the card, which the ONE component `Names` draws; the rail does not change (D4) — a level reads from its indent (12px for each level), its tone and its lines, never from a size. THE TONES (D1): level 1 is `--fg` at weight 500, level 2 is `color-mix(in srgb, var(--fg) 55%, var(--fg-muted))`, levels 3, 4 and 5 are `--fg-muted` (YAZ-3051 D8); the current name stays `--accent` and the name under the mouse `--fg`. The tones are always on: no setting changes them. THE LEVEL LINES (D2, D7): each `.toc__name` draws the lines that pass it as BACKGROUNDS of the row, so a line adds no element and no script — a 1px line at 12px on each row of level 2 or deeper, one more at 24px on level 3 and deeper, at 36px on levels 4 and 5, and at 48px on level 5 (YAZ-3051 D8: a level 4 name stands at 48px, a level 5 name at 60px), and on each level 2 row the LEVEL PIECE, 9px by 1px, from the line at 12px toward the name, at the middle of the row; a row of level 3 or deeper has none. Their colour is `--toc-rest`. A row draws its lines with or without a parent above it (the rule of indent guides). 🔒 `.toc__name:hover` sets `background-color`, never the `background` shorthand: the shorthand would take the lines away below the mouse. THE PATH (D3): `pathLines(rows, at)` gives each shown row `''` or `'1'` to `'4'` — the level whose line is on the way from the current row up to its parents — with a `t` after it on a row that the path ARRIVES at, a name one level in from that line (`'1t'` to `'4t'`); a row more than one level in from its parent (an `H4` right under an `H2`) is passed by the parent's line and gets no `t`; `Names` writes it as `data-path`, and a row that is not on the path has no attribute. The line of a parent passes each row below the parent, down to its child on the path, so it also passes the rows of the earlier siblings; the path stops at the current row (the rule of bullet threading, rule 18); a level 1 row has no path, and neither has a row with no parent above it. toc.css draws the path over the grey lines in `--toc-path`: `[data-path^='1']` is the line at 12px, `[data-path^='2']` the line at 24px, `^='3'` at 36px, `^='4'` at 48px, and on `[data-path='1t']` the first line stops at the middle of the row and the level piece has the colour of the path; `'2t'` to `'4t'` have no rule of their own, because a name of level 3 or deeper has no level piece. The level piece is ONE layer of the row (`--toc-piece`), below the four layers of the path and above the four grey lines: the line of a path that only passes a level 2 name crosses the grey piece of that row whole. The `1t` rule stands after the level 2 rule, which has the same weight. `pathLines` runs in a `useMemo`, when the current row or the list changes — on 200 rows at most — and never on a scroll inside one section. The path does not fade from row to row. WHEN THE LINES SHOW (D5): `--toc-rest` and `--toc-path` are registered colours (`@property`, `transparent` by default), and `.toc__names` eases them in 160 ms. ONE app-wide setting, `settings.tocLines` ("App state": `settings`), gives them their colours, `--border` and `--accent`; App writes it as `data-toc-lines` on `.app` — a CSS gate, so no editor renders for it. `always`: at all times. `hover` (the default): while `.toc__names:hover` or `.toc__names:focus-within` — the LIST, not the column, so the mouse on "Unpin" or on the drag edge does not show them. `off`: never, and toc.css has no rule for it. The grey lines and the path follow the setting together. The old hairline at the left edge of the list (`border-left`), with its marker, shows with each choice (D9). 🔒 THE PATH FOLLOWS THE WHEEL (D8): with `hover`, a turn of the wheel over the note sets `data-reading` on the `nav`, and ONE timer removes it `WHEEL_LINGER_MS` (1500 ms) after the last turn. It uses the `wheel` event, never `scroll`, so typing at the bottom of the window, a jump, a key and a drag of the scrollbar set nothing; a sideways turn (`deltaY` 0) and a pinch (`ctrlKey`) set nothing. A wheel over the table of contents that moves the NOTE (`onWheelOverToc`: beside the list — "Unpin", the padding of the column, the drag edge —, on a list that fits) sets it by the same rule; a wheel that scrolls the list itself does not. `.app[data-toc-lines='hover'] .toc[data-reading] .toc__names` sets `--toc-path` and no more: the path shows, and the grey lines wait for the mouse. The component writes the attribute on the element (`toggleAttribute`), so a turn of the wheel renders nothing. The cleanup of the effect clears the timer and the attribute. With "Reduce Motion" the lines do not fade: `.toc__names` is in toc.css's list of `transition: none`. **THE JUMP** (D7): scan again; open each folded heading section and each folded bullet that hides the row, and the row's own fold (under `headings`, also the bullet that a heading is the label of); put the caret at the start of the row's text and focus the note; glide there in 420 ms, the same for a near row and a far one (a row more than 3 windows away starts 3 windows from it; the reader's wheel, press or key stops the glide at once); land the row 24px below the top of the scroller, by the engine's own arithmetic; flash it one time (1.3 s, the accent at 34%; a bullet with its children). What the jump unfolded eases in — opacity and a 6px rise, 320 ms, 60 blocks at most, the first 8 each 18 ms after the one above — and never a height: the glide measures its target one time. From the card, the card closes. With "Reduce Motion" on there is no glide, no flash and no ease, the list of names does not glide either, and toc.css stops each of its transitions. **THE KEYBOARD** (D8): `⌘J` is a window capture listener, one for each table of contents and with no coordinator (the find bar's idiom): the editor whose `section.editor` holds the focus claims it; with the focus in no editor, the first visible one in document order; a hidden editor and a note that shows no table of contents never claim. It puts the keyboard on the current name (in lines mode it opens the card first, and the card stays while the keyboard is in it); `↑` `↓` `Home` `End` move, `⏎` jumps, `Esc` or a second `⌘J` gives the caret back to the note. The list has one tab stop. Settings › Hotkeys lists the key (`settings/hotkeys.ts`). **THE SETTINGS** (D2, D14, D15; YAZ-3558 D1–D3): app-wide, `settings.tocOnByDefault` (Settings' "Table of contents default", On / Off, with the hint "Off: a page can still turn it on in its cog.") and `settings.tableOfContents` ("Pin default", On = `pinned` / Off = `auto`; "App state": `settings`) — "Pin", in the card when the setting is `auto` and the note is 700px wide or more, writes `pinned`; "Unpin", at the top of the column of names when the setting is `pinned` and `auto` would give lines here, writes `auto`. The third row of the same group, "Level lines", writes `settings.tocLines` (THE HIERARCHY OF THE NAMES, above). For one page, in the cog (rule 34): the switch "Table of contents" — in the cog at all times, also with "Table of contents default" Off; a note with no choice follows that default, live (`usePageSwitch`'s `fallback`); the note's own choice wins over it (YAZ-3558 D1); and since YAZ-2950 STORED for the note: `folders[root].tocSwitches` through `state.setTocSwitch` ("App state": `folders[root]`), read when the editor mounts with `usePageSwitch`, so a new tab, a duplicated tab, a new window (`⌘⇧N`) and the app after a restart start with it, while two editors open on one note at the same time each keep what they show until they mount again (D2); a change of the default never writes the stored value — and the control "TOC made from:" with Auto / Headings / Bullets and a small "i" that opens its explanation beside the menu; it shows only while this page shows a table of contents, and it IS stored: `folders[root].tocSources` through `state.setTocSource` ("App state": `folders[root]`). `CrepeHost` puts the saved source in the channel BEFORE the editor exists, so a note saved as Bullets never shows its Auto list first. **THE HEADING LEVEL TAG** (D12): ONE node decoration, `data-heading-caret`, on the heading that holds the caret (`H1`–`H6`, in a bullet too; a selection across blocks is in no one heading). The tag itself — "H2", after the text — is a CSS `::after`: on that heading, on the heading under the mouse, and on each heading while the cog's switch "Heading levels" is on (`data-heading-levels` on the scroller; not stored). It shows at once, with no fade; it is never text, never selected, never saved; and it does not show while the line numbers are on, because they draw in the same `::after` (accepted). A caret move inside one heading, or outside headings, keeps the same plugin state. **THE SELECTION TOOLBAR** (D13): the strip reads H1, H2, H3, T, then Bold, Italic, Strikethrough and the four highlight dots, then code and link; the tab order is the same. `buildToolbar` adds the Heading group last — `addGroup` can do nothing else — and moves it to the front of the array that `builder.build()` returns; that array is the builder's own in the Crepe this app installs (7.22.1), and `headingToolbar.test.ts` reads the strip of a real editor, so a Crepe that returns a copy fails the test. **THE SCROLLBARS** (D11, `app.css`): `:root` and `[data-theme='dark']` each tell the system their theme (`color-scheme`) and name a thumb (`--scrollbar-thumb`: black at 40%, white at 20%); one `scrollbar-color: var(--scrollbar-thumb) transparent` on `:root` gives each scroller that thumb and no track, and `* { scrollbar-width: thin }` makes each one thin. A scroller that hides its bar does it with a class (`scrollbar-width: none`), never with `::-webkit-scrollbar`. The two blocks stand BELOW the two palette blocks: the palette tests take the first `:root` and the first `[data-theme='dark']`. **NOT INCLUDED**: a sticky heading or a bar at the top of the note (D9); `H6` as a row; a fold for `H4` or `H5` (YAZ-3051); a search box in the card; a sync of "TOC made from:" between computers; any write to a note. End to end: `desktop/e2e/tableOfContents.spec.ts` (the names in a wide window, the lines and the card in a narrow one, a scroll of the note that opens no card (YAZ-2886), a click and `⌘J` that land a row 24px below the top with the caret in it, "Pin" and "Unpin", a note of bullets, "TOC made from:" after a reopen and a restart, the two page switches; and step 5c for YAZ-2762: the tones, the level lines with the mouse and with the keyboard in the list, the path after a turn of the wheel, and the three choices of "Level lines"), written and not run.

36. **The drawing tab** (YAZ-3028 D2, ported from Draw's 🔒 YAZ-1810 / YAZ-2073 D16; `src/drawings/DrawingEditor.tsx` + `drawingEditor.css`, `src/documents/`): a `.excalidraw` opens full-pane in a tab. `Editor` dispatches `kind === 'drawing'` to `DrawingEditor`, loaded with `React.lazy` so a window with no drawing tab loads neither its chrome nor the engine. **THE DOCUMENT IS READ BEFORE THE ENGINE MOUNTS** (`DocumentShell`): `drawing.load` answers, `parseSceneText` checks the outline, and a missing, empty or corrupt file is ONE readable line ("This Excalidraw drawing can't be opened…"), never a blank pane and never an engine that could autosave over it. **ONE CANVAS**: the same `ExcalidrawSurface` as rule 28, with `autoFocus` (only the visible layer can take it) and Draw's engine options: fit-on-open (`openViewport`: every live element, `scale-down`, never past 100%), the `full` toolbar (`applyToolbarMode`, `getFormFactor` never `tablet`), and the canvas prefs. **AUTOSAVE** (`useDocumentHost`, generic `Autosave<number>`): the surface's cheap version (element versions counted only when content moved, rule 28, + the board's own appState edits) is the content key; the scene is serialised ONCE, when the 500 ms timer fires; the first snapshot is the restore-then-compare baseline, so an untouched drawing is never written. The save is `drawing.save` under the read `mtime`; `unpersistedFiles` ships only the images `assets/` lacks, and the persisted set only grows. ⌘S (caught on the host in the capture phase, never `window`) flushes now; the close/quit handshake, the pre-rename flush and the unmount flush write a pending edit; a delete or a rename RETIRES the host first (`registerRenameContinuity`, `capture` answers null: the tab at the new path reads the file back). **EXTERNAL CHANGES**: a watcher `change` whose mtime is our own save's is the echo; otherwise a CLEAN tab reloads (`replaceScene`, whose computed version is the new baseline, so a reload is never written back) and a DIRTY one shows the conflict bar ("File changed on disk." — Reload / Keep mine), as does a `CONFLICT` from the save door. The same drawing open in a tab and in the modal is this rule seen from both sides: the canvas that saves first wins, and the second shows the conflict bar — the modal too, with the same two words (YAZ-3044 A4: before, the modal refreshed the guard and wrote again in silence). **CHIPS**: the page cog (one row, "Read only" — rule 34), the "Read only" chip while it is on (rule 40), then the note's own `SyncIndicator` and `SaveIndicator`, in the engine's top-right row (`renderTopRightUI`), fed by a store so a save's status moves never re-render the host; the switch and the chip's box travel through the same store, because `renderTopRight` is one memoized function for the host's life. **READ ONLY** (YAZ-3076 D2, rule 40): the engine's own view mode (`viewModeEnabled: true`, and NO prop on an editable drawing, so the engine's own ⌥R toggle stays — YAZ-3120) — pan, zoom, Export Image, Export Drawing and Present work; the tools, the canvas panel's inserts and its slide reorder and rename (a handle with `insertElements`, `addFiles` and the elements of `updateScene` shut, `readOnlyHandle`) and Canvas Background do nothing; a version that moves anyway is never fed to the autosave, and the canvas is reloaded from disk at "Allow edits". The modal of rule 28 opens a read-only drawing in view mode too, with no save label and no autosave. **THEME** follows the app live (`useAppliedTheme`). **CANVAS PREFS** (Draw's 🔒 YAZ-1775 D9): `SettingsState.canvas` (`CanvasPrefs`, `shared/canvasPrefs.ts`; strict `isCanvasPrefs` at IPC, lenient `sanitizeCanvasPrefs` on load) is seeded at mount and kept in step both ways — engine changes reported 300 ms debounced, only when a value moved; a settings change pushed as changed keys only. **BOARD COMMANDS** (`documents/boardCommand.ts`): Export Image… (the engine's own dialog), Export Drawing… (`dialog.saveDrawing` with the canvas's `standalone` scene — the vault file is not touched) and Canvas Background reach the VISIBLE board through a non-bubbling `yaseendocs:board-command` event on its `.editor--drawing` section; the menu items that send them are File › Export Image…, Export Excalidraw Drawing… and View › Canvas Background (YAZ-3037; see "Menus & shortcuts"). The engine's own menu button is hidden in a tab (`.editor--drawing .excalidraw .main-menu-trigger`), never in the modal. **THE CANVAS PANEL** (YAZ-3038, ported from Draw's 🔒 YAZ-1775 D4 / D5 / D8 / D10, YAZ-1818 / 1819 / 1820): the TAB's only — `DrawingEditor` always passes `onCanvasPanelChange`, which is what turns it on, and the note embed's modal never does (rule 28 keeps the engine's menu and no library). The rail (`renderTopLeftUI`, `LauncherRail.tsx`: the hamburger that opens the panel on its last tab, and the Writing / Frames toggles, which write `SettingsState.canvas`), the docked panel (`CanvasSidebar.tsx`: Images = `image-studio/` — Iconify and Pixabay search through `media.search` / `media.preview` / `media.import`, the shapes, favorites and recent; Components = `components-library/`; Present = `drawings/presentation/`, whose player is a sibling of the engine so closing the panel never ends a presentation), and ⌘F → Images / ⌘C → Components, bound on the surface's own element in the capture phase and stepping aside on a selection, an edit, a dialog or a gesture in flight. Its tab and dock choice are `SettingsState.canvasPanel`. A note shown in the right panel keeps ⌘F for its own find bar (D12). Pinned in `DrawingEditor.test.tsx`, `documents/useDocumentHost.test.tsx`, `ExcalidrawSurface`'s engine-class pins in `engineSelectors.test.ts`, and end-to-end in `desktop/e2e/boards.spec.ts`.

37. **The diagram tab** (YAZ-3028 D2 / D5, ported from Draw's 🔒 YAZ-1802 D3–D16; `src/diagrams/` + `desktop/src/main/drawio/assets.ts` + `desktop/drawio-overlay/`): a `.drawio` opens in a tab on the bundled draw.io, offline. **THE WEBAPP SHIPS INSIDE THE APP** (D5, approved with the raised size ceilings): `tools/packDrawio.mjs` verifies the pinned `draw.war` (v31.5.2, exact size and sha256 — any other archive is refused), unpacks it pruned (`tools/lib/drawioPack.mjs`'s deny list: the servlet, source maps, the PWA worker, cloud pages and SDKs, unminified sources, other UI languages) into the gitignored `desktop/.cache/drawio/<tag>`, and lays the overlay over it every run (`PreConfig.js` / `PostConfig.js` hooks, the picture page `yaseen-render.html`, draw.io's Apache-2.0 licence, five Excalidraw font families as `yaseen-fonts/`); `drawioAssets()` in the vite config copies it to `out/drawio` (replaced whole), and electron-builder's `out/**` carries it. **ITS OWN ORIGIN** (🔒 D4): main serves it as `app://drawio/…` (`serveDrawio`: the pack cache in dev with `no-store`, `out/drawio` in a build; a path that leaves the folder is a 404 that never touches the disk), and EVERY answer carries `DRAWIO_CSP` — the network closed (`connect-src`, `img-src`, `font-src`, `frame-src` admit only that origin plus inline `data:` / `blob:`), so the iframe can reach neither the internet nor `window.yaseenDocs`. **THE EMBED PROTOCOL** (`drawioProtocol.ts`, JSON strings, only from THAT iframe's window and origin): our PostConfig says `yaseenReady` → the host answers draw.io's `configure` (plain uncompressed XML, page view and grid off, Excalidraw's look: 2 px lines, rounded corners, Assistant, the open-colour palette, the Excalidraw tool letters R O T A D L W P, and draw.io's bindings cleared on every chord the app menu owns — Docs' ⌘T ⌘W ⌘O ⌘⇧N ⌘⇧W ⌘⇧M among them) → `init` → the host `load`s the XML read through `diagram.load` BEFORE the iframe mounted (a refused file is the error pane, and draw.io can never autosave over it) → draw.io's `load` answer is the clean baseline → each `autosave` / `save` bumps a counter that `useDocumentHost` (rule 36's host: 500 ms, echo, reload, conflict bar, flush, retire) saves through `diagram.save`. The chips sit in a slim strip above the frame (another origin's toolbar cannot hold them): the page cog, the "Read only" chip while it is on, sync, save (rule 34, rule 40). **READ ONLY** (YAZ-3076 D2): our PostConfig's `yaseenReadOnly` message, sent after `init` (ahead of the `load`) and on every change, cancels a label being typed (never applies it — `stopEditing(true)`, called ONLY while `graph.isEditing()`, and with the cell editor's `focusContainer` shadowed by a no-op for the call: draw.io's `stopEditing` ends by focusing its container, which would pull the keyboard out of the host and close the cog's menu, YAZ-3119 and YAZ-3123), clears the selection, calls `graph.setEnabled(!value)` and turns off the toolbar's Undo and Redo; the wheel and the panning handler ask no `isEnabled()`, so pan and zoom still work (finding on YAZ-3114). The host reads the switch off the XML `diagram.load` answered, never off draw.io's (draw.io drops attributes it does not know), feeds no `autosave` to the autosave while it is on, writes the switch into any save that was queued before "on" landed (YAZ-3116 A3), and reloads the disk through the board's own `reload` at "Allow edits" if draw.io reported a change meanwhile. The app's theme follows live (`darkMode` / `lightMode`), and so does `SettingsState.diagramDarkColors` (`adapt` | `keep`, 🔒 D16; its Settings row is YAZ-3037's) through our `yaseenAdaptiveColors` message. ⌘B inside the frame is draw.io's own Bold: Toggle sidebar is the menu's ⌘⇧B (YAZ-3564 D10), so no key comes back from the frame. **PANELS START CLOSED** (YAZ-3420 D1): our PostConfig makes `mxSettings.getFormatWidth` 0 (like `getSidebarWidth`, YAZ-1802 D12a), makes `restoreVisibleWindows` and `showLayersDialog` no-ops, and clears `lastWindowWidth` before each `windowResized`, so draw.io opens no panel by itself — not from its saved state, not for a multi-layer diagram, not on a wider frame; the toolbar and the View menu still open them. **A RELOAD KEEPS THE VIEW** (YAZ-3420 D2): the board's `reload` sends `load` with `yaseenKeepView: true` (the first load sends `false`); our PostConfig records the page id, its place, the scale and `saveScrollState()` as that message arrives and, in place of the `fitInitialView` that ends draw.io's embed load, selects that page (by id, then by place) and puts the scale and the scroll back — inside the load, so no `autosave` follows. The fits draw.io runs INSIDE `setFileData` (a page shown for the first time) stay its own. **PICTURES** (🔒 D9, `renderDiagram.ts`): ONE hidden off-screen iframe on the same origin (`yaseen-render.html`, draw.io's own read-only viewer) draws every diagram picture — Export Image… (`dialog.saveImage`, PNG or SVG by the picked name; the menu item is YAZ-3037's) and the tree's hover preview (YAZ-3035). Pinned in `DrawioEditor.test.tsx`, `drawioProtocol.test.ts`, `renderDiagram.test.ts`, `desktop/src/main/drawio/assets.test.ts`, `tools/packDrawio.test.mjs` (with the real pack when it is unpacked), `tools/drawioOverlay.test.mjs`, `tools/yaseenRender.test.mjs`, and end-to-end in `desktop/e2e/boards.spec.ts` steps 3 and 6.

38. **Board rows in the Files tree** (YAZ-3028 D11 / D12; `src/sidebar/Tree.tsx`, `HoverPreviewHost.tsx`, `previewPlacement.ts`, `BoardPreview.tsx`, `NotePreview.tsx`, `BoardInfo.tsx`, `boardPreviewCache.ts`; main `src/main/drawings/`): a `.excalidraw` or `.drawio` row is a NORMAL row — not `tree__row--external`, a click opens it in the preview tab, a double click keeps it, ⌘-click opens it in the background — labelled with its FULL file name (Docs' rule for every non-Markdown kind, so `Flow.md` and `Flow.excalidraw` never read alike), and each row carries its kind as `data-kind` and its icon as `data-icon` (YAZ-3440 D4, which took the place of the diagram row's `.diagram-mark`). A NOTE (YAZ-3075 D1, D2; `NotePreview.tsx`), under a header that names it by its title as its tree row does (`pageName`), shows the top of its body below the frontmatter through the Space panel's own `ReadOnlyNote` (`editor/ReadOnlyNote.tsx`): read with `api.readFile` on each open — no cache, no board head, no watch subscription, and no redraw on a save while it shows —, cut to its first 4,000 characters (`NOTE_PREVIEW_CHARS`) at the last line end before them, in the vault's text formatting (App's `textVarsFor`) and with its wikilinks; the box is the board's place and width, 70% of the window tall, its last 64 px faded; "Empty page" for an empty body, "Preview unavailable" for a note that cannot be read; `focusOpenDocument` skips it (`.board-preview`); its lazy chunk starts to load when the note's dwell starts, and once loaded the host renders it without suspending (React holds a suspended reveal up to 300 ms — YAZ-3087 A1). A BOARD shows a picture of the whole board. Its key is `root, path, mtime, theme, diagramDarkColors`, the mtime read from `fs:board-head` when the panel opens (the tree is not read again on a save, rule 36); pictures stay in memory, 32 at most, least recently seen out first. A drawing is drawn by the engine (`exportToBlob`, `BOARD_PREVIEW_BOUNDS` 1200 × 800) from `drawing.load` with `imageMaxPx`, so each image comes back preview-sized from main's thumbnail cache; a diagram by draw.io's viewer (`renderDiagram`). 39. **Version history, the merge notice and Settings › Storage** (YAZ-3039, ported from Draw's 🔒 YAZ-1897 D4 and YAZ-1801; `src/history/`, `src/settings/storageSection.tsx`, `src/hooks/useVaultStorage.ts`): a drawing or diagram row's right-click has "Version history" just above "Info" (Info's gate). App owns ONE `VersionHistory` dialog (lazy), opened for the board's own vault: a list of versions and the chosen one AS A PICTURE — a drawing as "Changes since this version" (the board now, added / changed / removed shapes marked) or "As it was", a diagram as it was only — and "Restore this version" (confirm first; the current one stays in history). A sync pass that merged shows ONE notice (`history/mergeNotice.ts`) that stays until acted on, with "See changes" (Version history on the first merged drawing, starting on "your version before the merge"). Settings › Storage is a reference page of the ACTIVE tab's vault, measured only while it is open (page open, a pass finishing, a shrink): the git history on a fixed 10 GB bar with GitHub's 1 GB and 5 GB lines, "Needs attention" (files of 50 MiB or more; red at 95 MiB, the sync guard's line) and "Move pictures out" (skipping this window's unsaved drawings).

40. **The read-only switch** (YAZ-3076, decisions D1–D5 and cases S1–S51 on YAZ-3083; `shared/readOnly.ts`, `desktop/src/main/fs/boardReadOnly.ts`, `src/editor/ReadOnlyChip.tsx`, the hosts in `Editor.tsx`, `useDocumentHost.tsx`, `DrawingEditor.tsx`, `DrawioEditor.tsx`): each note, drawing and diagram can be "Read only" for the HUMAN in this app; an agent or any other tool still writes the file. 🔒 **STORED IN THE FILE** (D1), so it moves with the file — a rename by any tool keeps it and GitHub sync carries it: a note `readonly: true` in its frontmatter (a reserved key, "The properties panel"); a drawing `"readonly": true` inside its top-level `yaseendraw` block (which the save door carries forward like every extra key; "on" puts the block first and dates a dateless one by its file's mtime, so the head read trusts it); a diagram `yaseendraw-readonly="1"` at the END of its root `<mxfile>` tag (the dates stay first; a bare `<mxGraphModel>` is first wrapped in `<mxfile><diagram id="page-1" name="Page-1">` as draw.io saves it). No entry means editable — no migration. Only `true` / `"1"` counts; "on" writes the correct value over any other; "off" REMOVES the key or the attribute (and a frontmatter block, or a `yaseendraw` block, left empty by it), never `false`. On then off gives back the same bytes for a note and a diagram; a drawing is parsed and written again by the door (`serializeBoard`), so on then off keeps every other key of the block and of the scene, and a dateless block keeps the dates "on" gave it (YAZ-3116 A5). The same value again writes nothing. **THE TWO WRITE PATHS**, one read and one write each: a note saves its pending typing first (`flushRenamedPath`), then `transformFile(path, c => setNoteReadOnly(c, on))`, and adopts the bytes that landed (`absorbFrontmatterOnly` → `setDisk`), so the watcher's echo carries its own mtime and is skipped; a board runs `Autosave.writeBeside` — flush, then `board:set-read-only` (`{ root, path, on, expectedMtime }` → `{ path, mtime, size }`, kind by extension, bounded read, `CONFLICT` with the disk mtime on a stale guard, `IO_ERROR` on a file the board doors would not open, `atomicWrite`) in the autosave's in-flight slot, then the new mtime — so the echo never reloads the scene. A `CONFLICT` reloads the board and shows "The file changed on disk. Try again."; any other refusal is one notice, "Read only could not change: …". **THE READ** is the parse that already runs: `isNoteReadOnly(disk)` memoised on `disk` (an outside change, another window or tab, an agent: each lands through `disk`), the drawing's one scene parse (`DrawingScene.readOnly`, present only when on), the loaded XML of a diagram; a board's reload answers the switch again. **WHAT IT BLOCKS** (D2): the note body (`crepe.setReadonly(true)`, said only while on — typing, paste, drop, cut, undo, the task boxes, code blocks and tables all ask `view.editable`), its block handle (hidden: `.editor-host[data-read-only]`), the link menu's Edit and Remove ("Copy link" stays), the page title (no field; one open is put down unchanged), the properties panel (no editor, no menu, no Add, the raw YAML `readOnly` with no Save; a draft is kept), the drawing canvas (rule 36), the drawing modal (rule 28 opens it in view mode) the diagram canvas (rule 37), and the note's cells in every folder view (YAZ-3076 D6: no editor, no checkbox toggle, no card move, no title edit; the host refuses the write, and a muted lock follows its name — "Cell editing" under View modules). The `readonly` key is no AUTO-shown property (`propertyKeys`: no "Readonly" row on every card once one note is locked, YAZ-3130 nit); a view that orders it, or a folder that declares it, shows it, and the properties menu still offers it; `comments` and `reviews` never reach the views (the index drops them). 🔒 **EVERYTHING ELSE STAYS NORMAL** (D8, "the document is completely normal except the ability to edit"; YAZ-3125): a read-only body takes no focus and ProseMirror runs no keymap in a non-editable view, so `readOnlyKeys.ts` (registered in `createCrepe`) answers the view-action chords while the view is not editable — ⌘⇧U / ⌘⇧I, ⌘↑ / ⌘↓ at the clicked spot, ⌘. / ⌘⇧., the view-action ⌘Z — from `document`, only for the visible note the reader is in; a read-only NOTE EDITOR (a tab or the right panel, never a preview: `CreateCrepeOptions.readOnlyKeys`) takes the focus itself (`tabindex="-1"` while it is not editable, YAZ-3127), so its keys stay the note's, and the focus COMES BACK to it: ProseMirror's `view.focus()` focuses no non-editable view, so while the view is not editable the plugin's `focusReadOnlyBody` stands in for it (focus the body, put the DOM caret at the editor's selection, then ProseMirror's own `focus` draws it) — every return (`focusEditor`, Find's close, the table of contents' Esc and jump, the title's ↓) lands in the note (YAZ-3130) — the window chords (⌘⇧C, the file clipboard) leave it alone (`lib/readOnlyCaret.ts` `readOnlyNoteHoldsKeys`: a target in a read-only body, or `<body>` with the reader's selection in a VISIBLE one); 🔒 **A PAGE HOLDS THE KEYS** (YAZ-3140): the window's file clipboard (⌘C / ⌘X / ⌘V) and the sidebar's arrows "from nowhere" also yield when the focus is on `<body>` and either end of the DOM selection (a caret counts) is anywhere in a VISIBLE note page (`[data-page="note"]`, the `.editor-host` of a note tab or the right panel: title, properties, body, comments, backlinks, reviews; `pageHoldsKeys`) — so a click or a drag on a read-only title (which takes no focus) leaves ⌘C the native text copy, ⌘X / ⌘V nothing and ↓ in the page, and `readOnlyKeys` answers ⌘⇧U / ⌘⇧I / ⌘A from anywhere in its own visible page (the body takes the focus first; ⌘A selects the note's text); 🔒 **THE LAST CLICK DECIDES** (YAZ-3145, option 1): a page (and a read-only body with the focus on `<body>`, and `requestZoom`'s caret holder) holds the keys only while the reader's last `pointerdown` or last focus move (`focusin`) landed in it — one capture-phase pair of listeners per window in `readOnlyCaret.ts` (`claimPage`), no work on render; a press or a focus move outside every page (blank sidebar space, the tab strip, a row, the title bar) ends the claim, so after a click in a note and then on blank sidebar space ⌘V pastes the copied file, ⌘C copies the selected row's file and ↓ reaches a row, exactly as on `main`; routes with no click claim the page they focus (`focusEditor` — first launch, a tab open, Esc from the table of contents — and `focusReadOnlyBody`); a wikilink open focuses the note's sidebar row, as on `main`, so the row holds the keys; a focused control (a sidebar row) keeps its keys, and a real "nowhere" (no claimed selection in a page) is the sidebar's as before, and ⌘A selects only the note's text; through the editor's OWN keymaps with `view.dispatch` guarded so a document change is dropped (⌘Z never undoes an edit made before the lock); and `requestZoom` lets the VISIBLE read-only editor that holds the caret claim ⌘+ / ⌘− / ⌘0 when the focus is on `<body>` (a tab switch leaves the DOM selection in the hidden tab, YAZ-3128). ⌘B in a read-only body does nothing (in a normal note body it is Bold); Toggle sidebar is the menu's ⌘⇧B and works here too. The mouse paths (chevrons, a bullet's glyph, the breadcrumbs, links, a drag selection), ⌘J, ⌘F, copy, line numbers and scroll work unchanged. NOT blocked: comments, reviews, the sidebar's rename / move / delete, link rewrites, the ID sweep, GitHub sync merges, "Move pictures out", share links, any outside write — an agent's edit reloads a never-dirty editor with no conflict bar. **THE CHIP AND THE BOX** (D4, D4a option 1): while on, a "Read only" chip with a lock (`LockIcon`), tooltip "Click to allow edits", shows in the status row (rule 34), whatever else the row holds (S49). A click opens a small box under it — "Allow edits?", "Allow edits" (focused, so Enter allows) and "Cancel"; Esc cancels and puts the focus on the chip, a press outside cancels (a `pointerdown` in the capture phase: a read-only drawing's canvas cancels its `pointerdown` to pan, so no `mousedown` follows — YAZ-3116 A1), the window losing focus cancels (a press inside the draw.io frame reaches no event of the app's document), a second click on the chip closes it. Only "Allow edits" turns the switch off. The cog's row while on closes the menu and opens the same box (one box, the host's `askingUnlock`, per tab); while off it turns read only on at once and the menu stays open — turning on never asks (D5: no hotkey, no menu-bar item, no settings row). Tests: `desktop/src/main/fs/readOnly.test.ts`, `boardReadOnly.test.ts`, `lib/autosave.test.ts` (`writeBeside`), `documents/useDocumentHost.test.tsx`, `editor/Editor.test.tsx`, `PageSettings.test.tsx`, `ReadOnlyChip.test.tsx`, `PageTitle.test.tsx`, `FrontmatterPanel.test.tsx`, `markdownLink.test.ts`, `DrawingEditor.test.tsx`, `DrawingModal.test.tsx`, `ExcalidrawSurface.test.tsx`, `DrawioEditor.test.tsx`, `tools/drawioOverlay.test.mjs`, `links/reservedKeys.test.ts`, `views/deleteColumn.test.ts`; end to end `desktop/e2e/readOnly.spec.ts`.

41. **The line's darkness, thickness, style and length** (YAZ-3164, decisions D1–D11 and cases S1–S100 are comments on the working log YAZ-3165, with D3 amended and D4 / D6's defaults changed in the guided test; YAZ-3198 the style, YAZ-3199 the condensed menu, YAZ-3204 and YAZ-3206 the line numbers, YAZ-3208 the vault's default line; `src/editor/line/`): the `---` line has a darkness, a thickness and a length. 🔒 **ON DISK** (D1, `lineStyle.ts`, registered in `createCrepe()` right after highlight): the `hr` node (`hrSchema.extendSchema`, rule 30's one exception) has four attributes, each `null` while the line FOLLOWS the vault's default (YAZ-3208 D9) — `darkness` (% of the text colour, whole numbers 5–100, app default 50), `thickness` (whole px 1–24, app default 3), `pattern` (`solid`, `dotted` or `dashed`, app default solid; YAZ-3198, 🔒 D7 — not `style`, which is the DOM attribute of the custom properties) and `width` (% of the row, whole numbers 10–100, default 100). A plain line is `***`, the bytes of before (rule 6). A styled line is `***`, then the HTML comment `<!-- line: darkness 80%, thickness 6px, style dashed, length 40% -->` as the NEXT block — at the top level after a blank line, in a quote after `>`, in a tight bullet on the next line, indented, before the children. Only the set parts are written — a part that follows the vault's default (`null`) has none — always in the order darkness, thickness, style, length (S2, S3, S71). 🔒 D9 (YAZ-3208): a set value is written as it is, ALSO when it equals the default — `darkness 50%`, `style solid` — and a hand-written one is read as written, so a line set on purpose never moves with the vault's default (S93, S100); only the menu's "Default" item stores `null`, and a line with every part at Default is plain `***` (S94); a line that follows the default has no style part (S70); a comment that would hold none is not written (S94). A comment, never `<hr …>`: an HTML block of `<hr>` ends only at a blank line, so the `  * child` line under it in a tight bullet would go INTO it; a comment ends at `-->`, and Obsidian and GitHub hide it and show a plain line (S16); an older build of this app keeps it as text (S15). **LOAD**: `lineStyleRemark` walks every container — the root, lists, list items, blockquotes — and joins a `thematicBreak` with its next sibling when that sibling is our comment: a bare `html` node, or the paragraph that Milkdown's `remarkHtmlTransformer` (part of the preset, it runs first) wraps a block `html` in. The style goes to `data.lineStyle`, read by `parseMarkdown`, and the comment leaves the tree. OUR COMMENT is the exact form: one to four of `darkness <n>%`, `thickness <n>px`, `style dotted|dashed|solid`, `length <n>%`, in that order, each once, joined by commas, whole numbers with no leading zero, darkness 5–100, thickness 1–24, length 10–99 (100 is the full line, which the length handle stores as `null` and never writes, so a hand-written `length 100%` is not ours). Any other comment — other words, an extra word, another order, a value out of range, another style word (`style wavy`, S72), a block between it and the line, a comment BEFORE a line — stays an `html` node, bytes untouched (S5–S7). A hand-written value equal to the default (`darkness 50%`, `style solid`) is ours and stays as written (D9, S93; this replaces S4). Code is never a `thematicBreak` or an `html` node, so `***` and the comment in code are text (S14); `Text` over `---` is still a heading (S13); a first `***` is never frontmatter (S11, rule 1 reads only `---`). **SAVE**: `toMarkdown` adds the `thematicBreak`, then an `html` node with the comment when one is needed; a second save gives the same bytes (S17). `toDOM` writes the set parts as the custom properties `--line-darkness`, `--line-thickness` and `--line-width` in `style`, and a pattern as `data-line-pattern` (no attribute on a plain line), and `parseDOM` reads them back, each checked against its range, so a line copied inside the app pastes with its style (S26, S77); Copy as Markdown carries the comment, Copy as plain text is still `───`. 🔒 **THE VIEW** (D2, `lineView.ts` + `line.css`, registered in `createCrepe()` on EVERY editor, beside the image view): `<div class="line-view" contenteditable="false"><hr><span class="line-view__end"></span></div>`, rule 30's shape. The wrapper is the block and as wide as the row; it carries the set parts as `--line-darkness`, `--line-thickness`, `--line-width` and `data-line-pattern` (none on a plain line), NEVER `style.width` (rule 30's reason), and `update()` patches them in place, only when the attributes changed (a new line-number decoration is an update too), and never puts back `--line-width` while a drag holds it live; `destroy()` ends a running drag. The look is CSS only: `width: var(--line-width, 100%)`, `margin-inline: 0` (a short line starts at the left edge), `height: calc(12px + var(--line-thick))` — `--line-thick` is `var(--line-thickness, var(--line-default-thickness, 3px))` — on Crepe's border-box `hr` with `padding: 6px 0` and a content-box background — so the colour is exactly the thickness, and a thick line makes its row taller by the thickness only (D6) — and `background-color: color-mix(in srgb, var(--crepe-color-on-background) var(--line-darkness, var(--line-default-darkness, 50%)), transparent)`, a share of the text colour, so dark mode follows (D4, S20, S21). A line with no value of its own takes the vault's default line (`--line-default-*` from `textVars`, YAZ-3208 D8), else the app's; a line with no pattern of its own takes the vault's default pattern through a style query, `@container style(--line-default-pattern: dashed|dotted)` on `.line-view:not([data-line-pattern])` (the `hr`'s container is the wrapper, which inherits the property), CSS only — checked in Electron's Chromium 150 (S90–S92, S100). 🔒 The default line is darkness 50% and 3px thick (Yaseen, after the build — it was 10% and 1px, about the look of before): every plain line of every note draws so, while its bytes stay `***`, and 10% and 1px are ordinary values, written when picked. The line's colour is ONE custom property on the `hr`, `--line-color`; a solid line paints it as `background-color`, and a dotted or dashed one (`[data-line-pattern]`) as a background image on the content box (`background-origin: content-box`, `repeat-x`), so the dots and dashes take the darkness colour, dark mode follows, and a short line ends at its length (S75, S76): dashed is `linear-gradient(to right, var(--line-color) 60%, transparent 60%)` in tiles of 5 × thickness — a dash of 3×, a gap of 2× (S73) — and dotted a `radial-gradient(circle closest-side, …)` in tiles of 2 × thickness — a round dot as wide as the thickness and a gap as wide (S74). Line numbers (rule 34) sit on the WRAPPER (`.line-view[data-line]`, `top: 50%`), at the middle of the line, a thick one too (S22). `selectNode` adds `is-selected` only while `view.editable`: Crepe's selected tint over the row, and the round end handle at `left: var(--line-width, 100%)`; a read-only editor shows the style with no tint and no handle (S30, S38). **THE LENGTH HANDLE** (D5), rule 30's gesture: the length is LIVE on `--line-width` (a share of the wrapper's on-screen width, so a document zoom changes nothing, S28), clamped 10–100 (S33); ONE `setNodeMarkup` on mouseup writes it with the line selected again in the same transaction (one ⌘Z, S31, S37), 100 as `null` (S32); Escape mid-drag (capture phase) puts the start length back and writes nothing (S34); the window losing focus ends it where it stands (S35); a click with no move writes nothing (S36). `stopEvent` claims the handle's events; `ignoreMutation` answers false only to the `selection` pseudo-mutation. Each write — a drag, a pick — closes the history first, so it is always its own undo step. 🔒 **THE MENU** (D3 as amended, D4, D6, D7, `lineRows.ts`; rule 26's pickers): `createCrepe()` composes the block handle menu's provider as `numberChildrenRow` + `lineRows`. `lineRows` returns nothing unless `view.editable` (S51) and the handle points at a line: the probe's node is an `hr`, or a `list_item` whose FIRST child is an `hr` (Crepe's handle stands for the bullet when its first block is hovered). A line that is a LATER block of a bullet gets the pickers from its OWN 6-dot handle (Crepe gives that block a handle of its own); the bullet's own handle shows none (S41, S42; coordinator decision on YAZ-3165). On a line the menu is "Number children" (disabled unless the bullet has a child list), then three closed picker rows: "Line darkness" (`%`, presets 10, 50, 100, error "Use a whole number from 5–100%."), "Line thickness" (`px`, presets 1, 3, 6, error "Use a whole number from 1–24px.") and "Line style" (Solid, Dotted, Dashed, each with a 36 × 3px `line-sample` drawn by the line's own images, `line.css`) (S40, S44–S46, S78, S80–S84; S80 replaces S43, the focused darkness box on open). Each list starts with "Default (<the vault's current default>)" — `Default (50%)`, `Default (Solid)` — read from the line's own computed `--line-default-*` with the app default as the fallback; while a part follows the default its closed row reads that (`Default (50%) ▾`) and "Default" has the ✓ (YAZ-3208 D11). Each pick is ONE `setNodeMarkup` on that attribute, the history closed first (one ⌘Z, S50, S78), written as picked, also when it equals the default (D9, S93); only "Default" stores `null`, so its part leaves the comment and a line at Default in every part gives plain `***` (S94); the menu's close puts the focus back; the current value changes nothing (S47); a close changes nothing (S48). Line numbers (rule 34) number a styled line from its `***` line to its comment's last line, and the comment is no block of their own (YAZ-3204). Tests: `line/lineStyle.test.ts` (S1–S14, S17, S26's parse, S70–S72, S77), `line/lineCss.test.ts` (S73, S74 and the D8 fallbacks' CSS), `settings/headingStyles.test.ts`, `settings/textFormatting.test.ts`, `settings/useTextFormatting.test.tsx` and `settings/SettingsDialog.test.tsx` (S90–S99), `line/lineView.test.ts` (S20's properties, S23–S25, S27, S30–S38), `lineNumbers/lineNumbersCss.test.ts` (S22's rule), `lineNumbers/styledLine.test.ts` and `lineNumbers/blockLines.test.ts` (S22's numbers, YAZ-3204), `line/lineRows.test.ts` (S40–S42, S44–S51, S78, S80–S82), `blockHandleMenu.test.ts` (the pickers, S80–S84); end to end `desktop/e2e/lineStyle.spec.ts`.

41a. **The table's settings in the file** (YAZ-3758, part 1 of YAZ-3696; decisions D1, D3, D7, D8 and S3 and the table "The table comment (D1)" are in the "Decision and scenario record, final" comment on the working log YAZ-3697; `src/editor/table/`): a table keeps its column widths, cell fills, cell text colours and table settings in ONE HTML comment right after it. 🔒 **ON DISK** (`tableComment.ts` reads and writes it; `tableStyle.ts`, registered in `createCrepe()` right after `lineStyle`): a plain table is the GFM table, the bytes of before, with NO comment (R5). A table with settings is the table, then `<!-- table: widths 140 240 auto, fill A1:C1 blue B3 green, color B2:B5 red, align B2:C3 center, border 2px 40%, header plain, stripes, height compact, nowrap, freeze 2 rows 1 col -->` as the NEXT block — at the top level after a blank line, in a tight bullet on the next line, indented. Only the set parts are written, always in that order: `widths` (px per column, `auto` for none; one per column), `fill` and `color` (each a colour name — `red`, `orange`, `yellow`, `green`, `teal`, `blue`, `purple`, `pink`, `grey`, `brown` — or a custom `#rrggbb`, YAZ-3817: the reader takes any case, the save writes lowercase; anything else is a value it does not know), `align` (a cell's own alignment, `left`, `center` or `right`, YAZ-3819: it wins over its column's), `border <px>px <darkness>%` (whole px 0–10, darkness 0–100% of the outline colour), `header plain` (shaded is the default), `stripes`, `height compact|tall` (normal is the default), `nowrap`, `freeze <n> row(s) <n> col(s)`. A column's alignment is NO part: it is the GFM `:-` row (the cells' GFM `alignment`), so GitHub and Obsidian show it too; "Align all columns" (YAZ-3767) sets it on every column and clears every cell's own `align` in the same step (YAZ-3819). An `align` part names cells, never a column: an old `align center` (no cells) is a value the reader does not know. Cells are A1 addresses: columns are letters (A…Z, AA…), rows are numbers, row 1 is the header row. Each colour lists its cells before it, cells of one colour merged into rectangles (`A1:C1`), each colour once, in reading order. **LOAD**: `tableStyleRemark` walks every container and joins a `table` with its next sibling when that sibling is our comment — a bare `html` node, or the paragraph `remarkHtmlTransformer` wraps it in — with the walk rule 41 uses for `***` (`joinComment.ts`, shared). The reader is tolerant: an unknown part, or a known part with a value it does not know, is ignored and the known parts are kept (and the save drops the ignored ones). The reader takes wider values than the menu offers (a border of 0–10px and 0–100%, against the menu's 1–6px and 5–100%): a hand edit is allowed, and it saves as written (YAZ-3773). A comment with NO known part is not ours: it stays an `html` node, bytes untouched, and the table loads plain (no data loss). A comment that is not right after a table — before it, or with a block between — is a normal comment. Widths go to every cell's `colwidth` (prosemirror-tables); extra widths are dropped, missing ones are `auto`; cells out of the table are dropped. **THE NODES**: `table` gains `border` (`null` or `{ px, darkness }`), `header` (`shaded` | `plain`), `stripes`, `height` (`compact` | `normal` | `tall`), `wrap`, `freezeRows`, `freezeCols`; each cell (`withCellStyle` in `inlineBreaks.ts`'s `cellSchemas`, the same extension as the cell serialiser, since `extendSchema` always derives from the original) gains `fill` and `color`, `null` by default, a name or `#rrggbb`, and `align` (`null` by default; YAZ-3819); one check (`cellColor` in `tableComment.ts`) holds every value on load, on save, in `parseDOM` and on copy. Every value is checked on save: one the comment does not know is not written. **SAVE**: `toMarkdown` writes the table, then an `html` node with the comment when any part is set; a second save gives the same bytes. **THE PAGE**: cells carry `data-fill` / `data-color` (the value itself) through their own `toDOM`; a custom value also writes `--table-fill-custom` / `--table-text-custom` in the cell's `style`, after GFM's own style; a cell's own `align` writes `data-align` and is the `text-align` in GFM's style in place of its column's, so it wins on the page and in a copy to Docs, and then the column's goes in `data-column-align`, which `parseDOM` reads back as the cell's `alignment`, so a copy and paste in the app never turns a cell's own alignment into its column's. The table block (`@milkdown/components` table-block) is a node view that builds its own DOM, so `tableStylePlugin` puts the table's settings on `div.milkdown-table-block` as a node decoration: `data-table-header`, `data-table-stripes`, `data-table-height`, `data-table-nowrap`, and `--table-border-width` / `--table-border-darkness` in `style`. It depends on the attributes only, so it never redraws a table on its own (B4), and a transaction that changes the document rebuilds only the tables it changed (`changedTables`: the tables in each step's changed range, and the node of each attribute-only `AttrStep`, whose step map is empty); a table's own decoration is the one that starts at the table, not a neighbour's that only touches it. `table.css` draws them in light and dark: each name has its own fill wash and text shade, light and dark (`--table-fill-<name>`, `--table-text-<name>`; in light, yellow, green, blue and pink are the highlight washes `--mark-bg*`, YAZ-1480); text colours are darker shades in light and lighter in dark; a custom fill draws at `--table-fill-wash` (35%, `color-mix`; `FILL_WASH` in `colours.ts` is the same value for a copy, and `tableColoursCss.test.ts` holds each name's light and dark shades, swatch and rules), so text stays readable, and a custom text colour as picked; the header row is shaded by default; stripes on every second body row; a fill wins over the header shade and the stripes. **SETTINGS MENU** (YAZ-3767, D6 / D7, `tableRows.ts`, a `RowProvider` after `lineRows` in `createCrepe()`): a right-click on any point of a table's six dots (the handle's probe lands in the first cell below the table's top edge, so the target's nearest `table` ancestor counts, YAZ-3795) shows Border thickness (1–6px), Border darkness (5–100%), Header row (Shaded / Plain), Align all columns (Left / Center / Right: every cell's GFM `alignment`, "Default" is no alignment `---`), Fit columns to the page (a row: clears every `colwidth`, disabled with no width), Stripes (Off / On), Row height (Compact / Normal / Tall) and Wrap text (On / Off). Each picker shows the current value; a value that IS the default (it saves no part) reads "Default (…)" with ✓, and the list does not hold it a second time (`defaultOnce`, YAZ-3791; "Align all columns" keeps Left, since `:-` is not `---`); while any cell has its own `align`, "Align all columns" reads "Mixed", a value no item has, so no item has ✓ and every pick runs and clears them; each pick is one transaction with the history closed (one undo step); a border back at 1px 20% is `null` (no part). A read-only note shows no rows. **CELL TOOLBAR** (YAZ-3768, D8, `cellToolbar.ts`, after `tableColumnResize`): our own strip over a CellSelection of two or more cells (Crepe's toolbar hides on a non-TextSelection by design), placed by `TooltipProvider` (20 ms, 10px, above) in Crepe's toolbar look (`.cell-toolbar` in `table.css`). Left to right, with dividers: "Fill" + three fixed quick swatches (yellow, green, blue) + ▾; "Text" + three quick "A" swatches (red, blue, green) + ▾ (YAZ-3817, demo round 2). Each ▾ opens a palette: "No fill" / "Default colour", the ten named colours in a 5 × 2 grid, then "Custom colour…", which opens the system colour picker (a hidden `<input type="color">`, `pickCustomColour` in `colours.ts`; its `change` sets the cells, its live `input` events do nothing). The pick goes to the cells selected when the picker opened: `customColourPick` (registered after `cellToolbar`) keeps their corner cells, mapped through each transaction, and the pick does nothing when one is gone or the view is destroyed (⌘W); the callback is a no-op after each `change`. The picker opens on the cells' custom colour when they share one, else on `#000000`, so the same colour picked for other cells is a change and applies. One palette is open at a time; it closes on a pick, on Escape, on a second ▾ click, on a mousedown in the editor and when the toolbar hides. Then Bold, Italic, Strikethrough; Align left / center / right; Clear cells — each with a plain-words `title` and `aria-label`. Each acts on every selected cell in one transaction with the history closed (one undo step) and keeps the cells selected: Fill / Text set `fill` / `color` (a custom pick, lowercase `#rrggbb`); a mark turns on in all cells when any cell's text lacks it, else off in all (as Sheets); Align sets the selected cells' own `align` only (YAZ-3819; the GFM `:-` row stays), and `null` in a cell whose column alignment is the picked value (none counts as left; `setCellsAlign` in `cells.ts`), so the cell follows its column again; Clear cells is `deleteCellSelection` (text goes, attributes stay). Hidden on a caret or one cell, in a read-only note, with no focus, and while a mouse drag selects (shown on mouseup). **ONE TABLE MENU** (YAZ-3769 D5, YAZ-3820, `tableMenu.ts`, in `noteMenu.tsx` after the paste rows): a right-click in a cell of an editable note, and a click or right-click on a row or column handle, open the SAME note menu with the same Table part, in five groups — Insert row above / below, Insert column left / right, Duplicate row; Delete row, Delete column, Clear cells; Align ▸ (Left, Center, Right: the cells' own `align`, as the toolbar's Align), Fill ▸ and Text colour ▸ (the cell toolbar's palette: "No fill" / "Default colour", the ten names with a swatch, "Custom colour…" by the same hidden picker input, `pickCustomColour`); Sort A to Z / Z to A (by the target's left column; the header row stays first, empty cells last, equal cells keep their order; whole rows move, so cells keep their attributes; the same cells stay selected); Freeze up to this row, Freeze up to this column, Unfreeze rows, Unfreeze columns. The labels count the target (YAZ-3801). A row acts on the CellSelection in the clicked table, else on the clicked cell (the command runs on a state with that cell selected; the note keeps its selection), in one transaction with the history closed. The header row has no row above it and is never deleted or duplicated; the last body row and the last column are not deleted. A new row takes each column's alignment. **ROW AND COLUMN HANDLES** (YAZ-3762 D9, YAZ-3801, YAZ-3820, in the vendored table block): the block has no menu of its own. A click or right-click on a handle selects (it keeps a selection of whole columns, or rows without the header row, that holds the hovered one; Shift grows it to the hovered one; else the hovered column or row), then sends `milkdown-table-handle-menu` from the handle (it bubbles; `detail` `{ x, y, pos }`, `pos` a cell of the column in row 1 or of the row in column A), and `NoteMenu` opens the note menu there as on a right-click in that cell. The header row's handle opens no menu; a read-only note selects nothing and opens none. A right-click on a handle never reaches the note's own right-click. **MOUSE SELECT** (B2): a drag across cells makes a CellSelection (`tableEditing`); a click puts the caret; Delete / Backspace clear the text and keep the attributes. **COLUMN RESIZE** (D2, `tableColumnResize.ts`): `prosemirror-tables`' `columnResizing` as installed, just before `tableEditing` so a grip drag selects no cells; the drag writes `colwidth` once on mouseup (one undo step), at least 60px; the travel is in layout px under document zoom (R2); the table block draws the `<colgroup>`. **PASTE** (D4 / S2, `tablePaste.ts`, from `clipboardPaste.ts` before Milkdown's clipboard): in a table, a copied `<table>` (this app, Sheets) or tab-separated text fills from the caret cell (or the top-left selected cell), right and down, in ONE `replaceWith`, and grows the table; one value fills each selected cell; HTML cells bring `fill` / `color` / `align`. **COPY TO DOCS** (YAZ-3802, `clipboardCopyOut.ts`): a copied table carries inline styles, since Google Docs and Sheets read only these — the lines, the bold header, and each cell's colours in the light theme: a named fill as its wash over white, a custom fill as its wash (`FILL_WASH`) over white, a text colour as its light shade, a custom one as picked (YAZ-3817); a paste into this app reads `data-fill` / `data-color` and ignores the styles. Outside a table, tab-separated text of 2 lines or more with the same number of tabs on each makes a table (the first line is the header row). In both, a line that starts with a tab is indented code and the text stays text; several lines without tabs keep the cell paste of YAZ-1452 / YAZ-1462. One paste is one undo step. **FILL DOWN** (S4, `tableFill.ts`, `fillSeries.ts`): a square in the bottom-right corner of the selected cells (or the caret's cell), in the app's accent (`--accent`, as the dashed line of the range); a drag down or right fills the cells passed with the series (a step of two or more numbers, times, dates, weekday or month names, text ending in a number; one date, weekday or month name, or text ending in a number continues by 1 (a day for a date, YAZ-3789); else a copy, so one number or one time is copied), each column or row alone, in one transaction; it stops at the table's edge and never adds rows or columns; no ⌘D; a read-only note has no square; a note closed mid-drag drops the drag's listeners. **FREEZE** (S3, `tableFreeze.ts`): "Freeze up to this row" sets `freezeRows` to the clicked row's number (row 1 is the header), the column item `freezeCols`; no "Freeze header row". The counts stay inside the table: an appended transaction clamps them after a transaction that shrinks it (same undo step), and the load clamps a file's counts. Decorations from the attributes only: `table-frozen-row` on each frozen row, `table-frozen-col` + `--table-frozen-left: var(--table-frozen-x-<n>)` on each cell of a frozen column, and `data-table-frozen` on the table block. A failure, a Cancel or the quit (`cancelHelperInstall` in the quit sequence's `stopHelpers`) deletes the `.partial-` folder; a `.partial-` folder a killed app left goes at the next start; the folders of older pinned versions go after a download that worked. **WHERE A HELPER IS** (`resolveTypescriptServer`, `resolvePyright`): the downloaded copy of the pinned version, then (a dev build, unless `YASEEN_DOCS_LSP_DOWNLOAD_ONLY=1`) the `node_modules` copy, else none. **ONE SOURCE FOR EACH FEATURE** — Monaco's own TS/JS definition and reference providers are off (`monaco.ts`: `setModeConfiguration({ definitions: false, references: false })`); the providers of `languageClient.ts` (`typescript`, `javascript`, `python`) are the only ones: they ask the project's helper (`api.lsp`), and on `null` ask Monaco's TS worker (`getDefinitionAtPosition` / `getReferencesAtPosition`) and keep the places in the tab's own file. Hover stays Monaco's for TS/JS; for Python the helper answers it. The tab's own file maps to the tab's own model (a jump inside it stays in the tab); another file gets a read-only `file://` PREVIEW model, read with `readFile`, so the peek box can show it — at most 200 (oldest first out, never one the current answer needs), all disposed with the last code tab; a reference whose file cannot be read has no row. Monaco's TS diagnostics run on visible models only (`onlyVisible`), so preview models cost no worker time. **THE JUMP** (`codeOpener.ts`, `monaco.editor.registerEditorOpener`): a `file://` target opens through the tab's `onOpenFile` — the note link's door (`navigate`: this tab with history, or the tab that already shows the file) — and the place rides beside it: the code tab that mounts on the file takes it (10 s at most), a tab already on the file shows it at once (`setPosition` + `revealPositionInCenter`). The peek box's own editor opens through the code tab focused last. Only a `text` kind file opens; any other target (`.pyi`) does nothing. **THE PROJECT'S OWN PYTHON NEVER RUNS** (YAZ-3480; `desktop/src/main/lsp/python.ts`): pyright runs the interpreter it is given, so it gets no `pythonPath`; the venv's `site-packages` folders, found on disk, are its `analysis.extraPaths` (pyright reads their simple `.pth` lines itself). Its `PATH` has no folder inside the project, no relative or empty entry (the working folder is the project), and on macOS no `/usr/bin`; on Windows `NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath=1` (not tested there). A Python outside the project may still run.

42b. **The selection toolbar's lists and T** (YAZ-3806 T1–T4; decisions and the scenario table on the working log YAZ-3807; `src/editor/listButtons.ts`, `buildToolbar` in `createCrepe.ts`): the strip is `H1 H2 H3 T │ ☐ • 1. │ B I U S ● ● ● ● │ <> 🔗` by default, put in the user's order by `arrangeToolbar` (`toolbarPrefs.ts`; a group with no shown button is dropped with its divider). A LINE is a visible textblock the selection covers (`coveredLines` + `eachVisibleTextblock`): an item line (an item's first block) has the item's kind — checklist (`checked` is a boolean), numbered (an `ordered_list`), bullet — and any other line in the page or a quote is text (a paragraph) or neither; an item's later block is neither (in a list, no marker), and a click first splits it into an item of its own (the zoomed bullet's own later blocks are text: the page inside the zoom). A list button lights when EVERY line is its kind; T lights only when every line is a paragraph outside a list. Not lit, a click makes each line its own item of the kind (a line outside a list is wrapped, a heading becoming `* ## x`; an item changes kind, its list split around it for bullet ↔ numbered, and a numbered part after the split keeps its numbers; a list beside one of the same type joins it; a checklist line keeps its tick). Lit, a click takes each line out of every list level — `prosemirror-schema-list`'s two lifts, repeated — so its children and the siblings after it stay a list below it; its heading stays a heading. T (and `Mod-Alt-0`, and the slash menu's Text row, which `slashMenu.ts` points at it: `turnIntoTextCommand` is replaced under its own key) does the same lift, then makes the line a paragraph. A line in a table cell is no line here, so T does not light in a cell (it never changed one). `Mod-Alt-8` runs the Bullet button (`wrapInBulletListCommand` replaced). Inside a zoom a line lifts only down to the zoomed bullet (it becomes a block of it, like `blockEscapingLift`'s limit), and the zoomed bullet's own line keeps its list. Hidden lines keep their kind. Every change is a lift, wrap, split, join or markup change in ONE transaction (one ⌘Z), so folds, the zoom and the selection ride the mapping; the lines go last to first, so no line's position maps through the steps before it, and lines side by side change as one run (a wrap round the run and a split per line, or a markup per item and a split each side): about one step per line. A markup change of the zoomed bullet (a list button, ⌘Enter) keeps the zoom: `zoom.ts` maps the start of its content when its start maps as deleted. In Settings the last button that shows cannot be unticked, and Crepe's own buttons show Crepe's icons, copied from a toolbar's items once one has built (`toolbarButtons.ts`). The Numbered button is a click; typing `n. ` at the start of a PLAIN line also makes a numbered line, and inside a list item it stays text (YAZ-3727 D8, D9, rule 26); `Mod-Alt-7` and a slash row stay off.

43. **The daily note** (YAZ-3607 D1–D19, scenarios and edge cases in the Locked comment on the working log YAZ-3608; `shared/dailyNote.ts`, `client/src/sidebar/dailyNote.ts`, `App.openDailyNote` / `openDailyTemplate`, `settings/DailyNoteControl.tsx`): one switch, `settings.dailyNotes` (off by default, D12), with `dailyNoteFolder` (root-relative, the `newNoteFolder` rule), `dailyNoteFormat` (default `YYYY-MM-DD`) and `dailyNoteDayFolder`; all four travel. On, three doors open today's note: the calendar button after the % chip in the sidebar footer (D7), ⌘D while `goTo` is `{ kind: 'daily' }` (D1; with the switch off a stored daily place goes to the Files tab), and File › Open Today's Daily Note (D11). **Today's name** is `dailyNoteName(format, new Date())`: the Mac's local day at the press, tokens `YYYY MMMM MMM MM M DD D dddd ddd`, `[text]` literal; a style needs `D` or `DD`, no `/`, no leading `.` (`dailyNoteFormatProblem`, also the store guard). A style with no year is the person's choice (D19). **The vault** (D15): the window's vaults in order, the one in front first; the first that holds the folder (`dailyNoteVault`); none → a notice, and the main folder is never made (D17). **The note** is found by its `title` in the index records, not its file name (a vault with IDs builds the name), flat or in a day folder that carries today's name, both layouts asked with the current one first (D3, D18). Missing → `makeDailyNote`: the day folder when it is on (made when missing, D9, D16), then `createNote` with the daily notes folder's `.template.md` (`templateAt`, D6); never over a file. It opens as a sidebar click opens a file, and its row shows after a fresh tree. A ⌘-click on the button (YAZ-3776 D1, D2) opens it as a ⌘-click on a row does: `openBehindSidebar` (`openBackground`, or a Files window's `filesDoors.background`), and the sidebar does not move; a note already open in a tab stays where it is. The button's `title` names the ⌘-click (D3). App holds the one being made for a key (vault, folder, layout, name), so a double press makes one note; it counts only while its file is in the tree, and a failure clears it. **Open template** (D13) opens that folder's hidden template in a tab, made empty first (`api.writeFile`, atomic); `useVaultTree`'s missing-file checks skip a hidden path, so the tab stays (D14).

## View modules

TOMBSTONE: this heading was "Bases modules" until YAZ-858.

Everything under this heading serves ONE surface — a folder's page (YAZ-2290; YAZ-844 retired `.base`, Editor rule 19's tombstone). The name no longer stays: YAZ-858 renamed the machinery to match what it serves — `client/src/bases/` → `client/src/views/`, `baseFile.ts` → `viewSchema.ts`, `BaseView` → `ViewsPane`, `.base-*` → `.view-*` — a mechanical rename with zero behaviour change. The property index, the query engine, the view chrome and the cell editors were still BUILT for Obsidian Bases and were not rewritten — they were re-pointed, then re-named. Where an entry below still says "base", it is a tombstone naming something the format took with it (or a stored key kept for compatibility, see `baseGroups` under App state); the surface that mounts them is "Folders are the pages", and the config they read is "Folder settings: `.folder.md`". Nothing here reads or writes a `.base` file any more, and no entry may describe one as current.

### Properties (YAZ-835, under the LOCKED rulings of YAZ-816 — `<root>/.yaseendocs/properties.json`, succeeding the Bible A registry)

**What it is**: vault-wide property DECLARATIONS — the ONE registry concept that survived the type system's deletion (YAZ-836). `{ version: 1, properties: { <name>: { kind, target?, required? } } }`, keyed by BARE frontmatter key — never a canonicalised `note.x`. `kind` ∈ `PROPERTY_KINDS` = text / number / date / checkbox / list / link / multi-link (`shared/types.ts`), `target` is a link/multi-link column's picker constraint (an opaque string here; its meaning is `belongsToBasenames`' — a wikilink to a FOLDER, see "Links": Links to folders), `required` is report-only metadata that gates nothing, exactly as it did in the registry. Read and written in main through the vaultConfig plumbing (`desktop/src/main/properties/`, Electron-free like the vault index); the IPC half is `desktop/src/main/ipc/properties.ts`.

**The version rule, unchanged from the registry** (LOCKED, R2.5): `version: 1` is readable AND mutable; a numeric `version > 1` reads best-effort (known fields consumed, no `error`) but refuses every mutation — writing a v1 shape over a newer file would destroy fields this version does not know. An ABSENT file is empty declarations with NO error, and reading NEVER creates anything: the file is LAZY, the first successful mutation writes the `{ version: 1, properties: {} }` skeleton along with the dotfolder. A MALFORMED file (unparsable JSON, non-object root, missing/non-numeric `version`) reads as empty + an `error` string, and every mutation rejects `INVALID_CONFIG` — the file is never overwritten and never moved aside, deliberately unlike `store.ts`'s `.corrupt-<epoch>` policy: app state is disposable, the user's schema is not.

**Surface**: `getProperties(root)` / `setProperty(root, name, decl)` / `removeProperty(root, name)` / `subscribeProperties(root, listener)`, over channels `properties:get` / `properties:set-property` / `properties:remove-property` / `properties:changed` (`CONTRACT.properties` in `shared/ipc.ts`), reaching the renderer as `window.yaseenDocs.properties.get/setProperty/removeProperty/onChange` (bridge table above). Targeted mutators, never a whole-file PUT (the state door's anti-clobber shape); every mutation is a serialised per-root read-modify-write (the store's write-chain idiom, so two can never interleave reads) that preserves unknown fields at every level for forward compat, and removing an unknown name is a no-op that never creates the file. `subscribeProperties` re-reads through the SAME chain, so notifications deliver in order; main holds ONE subscription per open-vault root (`rootsOf(state)` — every vault of every window, YAZ-2602 S77 — dropped with the last window that shows it) and broadcasts the fresh declarations to EVERY window, which filter by their own root.

**Validation** (strict at the IPC boundary — a write is config, not content): names must match `PROPERTY_NAME` `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$` (snake_case, ONE definition in `shared/types.ts` so no mirror can drift), a declaration must be an object whose `kind` is in `PROPERTY_KINDS`, `target` a string and `required` a boolean — everything else `BAD_REQUEST`. Reading is deliberately laxer than writing: an unknown on-disk `kind` string stays on disk and reads back as `text`. `page_type` is now an ORDINARY name that declares like any other (`properties/index.test.ts`) — the identity rule that reserved it died with the type system.

**The clean break** (LOCKED, YAZ-835): `.yaseendocs/types.json` is NEVER read. No migration, no converter, no read-old-write-new — a vault carrying one simply starts with no declarations, and the file is left untouched on disk. Pinned by a test: *"an old types.json is simply not read — properties.json is the only file this module knows"* (`desktop/src/main/properties/index.test.ts`).

**Not ours** (TOMBSTONE, ⚡ YAZ-815 — ruled by Yasin): `.obsidian/types.json` is another app's file — a different folder, a different owner, a different shape — and we no longer touch it AT ALL. It used to be read fresh per `index(root)` call (never cached), ride `IndexResponse.types` and hold a rung in the typing ladder one BELOW our own declarations; nothing ever consumed that rung, because the one surface that mounts cell editors reads the window's link snapshot instead of fetching an index. A stale foreign artifact feeding a rung with no feed is worse than no rung, so the whole chain — the read, the field, the parameter and the rung — is deleted. `.yaseendocs/properties.json` is the vault's schema; we never wrote `.obsidian/types.json` and now we never read it either.

Files: `desktop/src/main/properties/index.ts`, `desktop/src/main/properties/index.test.ts`, `desktop/src/main/ipc/properties.ts` (+ test), `client/src/views/useProperties.ts` (+ test), `client/src/views/propertiesStub.ts` (+ test — the in-memory `YaseenDocsApi['properties']` the client tests install as `window.yaseenDocs.properties`), `shared/types.ts` (`PROPERTY_KINDS`, `PROPERTY_NAME`, `FOLDER_NAME`, `PropertyDecl`, `PropertiesResponse`).

### Property index (GRO-2127 contract, GRO-2128 index — now in the Electron main process)

The query engine behind a folder's views reads notes through `IndexRecord`, never the filesystem. Transport: bridge method `index(root)` (Desktop D10), no HTTP anywhere — the index (`desktop/src/main/vaultIndex/`) is transport-agnostic (tests call `getIndex` directly); it moved, not rewrote, from the retired server process (GRO-2157).

Files: `shared/types.ts` (`IndexRecord`, `IndexResponse`), `shared/frontmatter.ts` (`splitFrontmatter` — moved from the client, which re-exports it — and `parseFrontmatter`), `shared/noteId.ts` (`isNoteId` — what `id` holds), `desktop/src/main/vaultIndex/scan.ts` (`walk`, `scanFile` + pure `extractAliases` / `extractTags` / `extractLinks` / `extractEmbeds`), `desktop/src/main/vaultIndex/live.ts` (`getIndex`, cache + watcher), `desktop/src/main/vaultIndex/idSweep.ts` (`sweepIds` — "Note ids": The sweep), `desktop/src/main/vaultIndex/index.ts` (barrel), `client/src/views/testRecords.ts` (`TEST_RECORDS`).

`IndexResponse { root, records: IndexRecord[], folders: IndexRecord[], generatedAt, ids: boolean, letters?: string[], ask?: { notes, folders, foreign, letters? }, unfinished?: true }` — `ids` says whether the vault gives its notes IDs, and `ask`, present only while the vault's answer is not yes, counts what a yes would write and carries the letters its `ids.json` already holds; `letters` and `unfinished` go out only when `ids` (YAZ-2523, YAZ-2677 — "Two kinds of vault": What the index hands out); `records` is every `.md`/`.markdown` file under `root` (dot-entries and `node_modules` skipped, exactly like `tree(root)`), sorted by path; `folders` (🔒 D8, YAZ-2290) is every folder's settings file `.folder.md` — the ONE dot-entry the walk and the watcher let through — as the same `IndexRecord` shape, sorted by path, its `folder` naming the folder it configures, and NEVER among `records` (`getIndex` splits one record map by file name; pinned by `vaultIndex/folderSettings.test.ts`). Images and everything else are never records — nor were `.base` files while the format existed (YAZ-844), which is why retiring it cost the index nothing: no field, no `CACHE_VERSION` bump, no rescan.

| `IndexRecord` field | Value |
|---|---|
| `path` | absolute |
| `id` | OPTIONAL (YAZ-2293, YAZ-2677): the frontmatter `id` when it is an ID of this vault (`vaultNoteId`, `shared/noteId.ts`), as the app writes it — a number ID with the vault's CURRENT letters in capitals (`YAZ-12`; one the file holds in another case, or with letters the vault had before, goes out so too), or an old 12-character ID — the note's permanent identity, see "Note ids". ABSENT when the note has none or its `id` is anything else (another tool's, another vault's letters — which the sweep replaces, YAZ-2420 D30), and on EVERY record a vault that does not use IDs hands out (`plain`, YAZ-2523 V12). The key is not removed from `properties`: it stays there as written, like any other. |
| `name` / `basename` / `ext` | `VSL-v1.md` / `VSL-v1` / `md` (`md` or `markdown`, lower-case, no dot) |
| `title` | what the app shows (YAZ-2420 D14 — `titleOf`, `shared/noteName.ts`): the frontmatter `title`, trimmed (a number is read as the text it was written as), else `basename` — for a folder's settings file, the folder's own name. Every screen reads this one value. In a vault that does not use IDs it is ALWAYS the `basename` (a settings file's: its folder's name), whatever `title:` line the file holds (`fileTitle`, YAZ-2523 V12). The key is not removed from `properties`. |
| `folder` | root-relative, `/` separators, `''` at the root (`Content Pillars/1. Agentic Agency`) |
| `size` / `mtime` / `ctime` | bytes / mtime ms / birthtime ms (ctime ms where the platform has no birthtime) |
| `properties` | frontmatter parsed with yaml's default **core** schema: `null`/booleans/numbers typed, dates stay strings (`date: 2026-08-01` → `'2026-08-01'`), `pillar: null` is present with value `null`. `{}` when there is no frontmatter, the block is not a map, or YAML fails — the latter two also set `frontmatterError` (one-line yaml message or `frontmatter is not a map`). Files over `MAX_FILE_BYTES` are stat-only (`{}`, empty lists, no error). The reserved `comments` key is DELETED right after the parse (YAZ-1472, 🔒 D5 — a note's comment stream is content, not a property), so it never reaches a record, the cache, a view column or a link source; see "Comments". |
| `aliases` | frontmatter `aliases` — extra NAMES the note answers to (Links E2, GRO-2214): a list → each string item; a scalar string → ONE alias (never comma-split, the deliberate contrast with `tags`); trimmed, empties and non-strings dropped, de-duplicated (first appearance).
